Do you know why there are names engraved on the abandoned turrets here?
Why?
I don’t care.
Many years ago, the battlefield was filled with smoke as the Jinzhou Garrison regiment fought bravely and successfully pushed back the TD tide, reclaiming a small portion of the front line.
In those times, the majority of soldiers were ordinary people, and the demands of war were such that not everyone who departed left something behind.
Engraving the names of fallen comrades onto stone monuments might just be a way of commemorating their sacrifice and creating a sense of unity.
The group then devised a method to engrave the names of the deceased soldiers onto the turrets and continue the tradition.
The engravings here are their names.
You weren’t even born then, were you?
Do you know them?
I didn’t know any of them, but my grandpa said them so many times that I just remembered them all!
When I was a kid, he barely mentioned his war experiences. Lately, he has become increasingly forgetful and tends to reminisce about his younger days.
Grandpa was probably scared of forgetting, so he wanted other people to remember in his place.
Anyway, I’ve heard it a million times and can’t forget it even if I tried, and even if Grandpa forgets, I’ll remember it for a few more decades.
I can recite the names engraved on the monument backwards now.
Really?
No need.
Look, this is Shenyin, he’s nicknamed the Divine Eagle because of his incredible marksmanship.

He stuck to the front line with his gun for two whole days so that the others could retreat without harm. When he eventually returned to rescue him, he discovered that his leg had been shattered, he had lost a significant amount of blood, and yet he had managed to stay in his firing position until his last breath.
This is... Little Bean, she doesn’t have a name, that’s what everyone calls her.
She died as the first one to rush out and pull the alarm when the TD wave suddenly erupted, getting the TD’s attention and giving the others a chance to react.
Do you still want to hear more?
Tell me more.
No need.
This one is Yuandong... next to this one is Beimo...
Yuandong was a military doctor, and when the TD wave broke out, he died fighting without any medical support.
Beimo was discovered in a cave-in after a week-long battle, and he rescued around twelve soldiers from starving to death beneath the sealed ground.
Here is Ziyu, and this is Xiaohua...
Do you still want to hear more?
I'll pass.
Well, then I’ll stay here a little longer.
Dong's just got a sharp tongue.
He really knows about play. But he has to learn how to deliver it in a less outright way and let the young ones figure it out themselves.
When will he learn to restrain his complaints? We'd have no play to see if he scares those performers away.
I hope Qinghe's new play can satisfy his appetite, so he can stop nagging all day long.

The universally agreed terms for special Echoes, like names for humans. They are named based on their characteristics, abilities, and places of origin.
My denomination... It's... It's... I don't know. Do I not have a name at all?

I didn't have time to think. I just had to show up and reach out for it.
So... maybe Abby's power activates automatically under certain circumstances? Perhaps Abby can’t control it yet.

Hey, hey! Stop looking down on me! Like I said, it was just a little slip, really!
But think about it! I just stood there and did nothing and ended up beating a THRENODIAN! Imagine what I could do if I actually tried!

You're so real for that, Abby.
You bet! I said I'm super strong. I'll protect {Male=him;Female=her}!

Let’s take our time. There's no hurry.
We'll still need to figure out my past first.

ABSOLUTELY NO!

I'll make it clear. I am to stay with {PlayerName}.
I agree. Abby cannot leave {PlayerName}'s side, but we can't just trap {Male=him;Female=her} here for research.
Where did you absorb Abby, what are Abby's powers, and what exactly happened between you two... There are so many questions we can't figure out yet.
Our Sentinel Jué can look into the future. Nothing ever deviates from its predictions. It has already sort of guided you to the Norfall Barrens through Madam Magistrate's messages, right?
Now that the Threnodian crisis is over, perhaps you can consult our Magistrate and our Sentinel again. I’m sure they can offer you some more useful guidance.
I'll pay Jinhsi another visit once she returns.
We'll have to wait for now.

Our Sentinel protects every one of us. Of course it's cool!
But... why are you talking about food again. Didn't you just stuff your face? What? Is your stomach a black hole?

Great food, great value! Come take a look!
Come again if you need anything. Since it's your first time here, here's fresh treats on the house, all handpicked.
Everything here is fresh and carefully selected. We take pride in our produce and proteins, handpicked and prepped each morning.
They taste amazing even without any seasoning!
Just make sure to cook everything thoroughly to avoid an upset stomach!
Oh, also. Please don't try to cook weird meat. Like... Gulpuffs.
A young girl visited my store with her sheep dolls, looking for ingredients for a dish she was making. She asked for Gulpuffs, claiming to have had them before without any issues.
I mean, no one in their right mind would think it's a good idea to give a child Gulpuffs to eat... If I ever find her parents, they're in for a helluva lesson on food safety.
You've been visiting quite often lately. Bet you cook a lot in your free time!
Me? I happen to know a thing or two about cooking.
Has Panhua been talking your ear off about proper seasoning techniques? Well, let me give you the real secret to delicious food: preserving the ingredients' natural flavors.
Take Milky Fish Soup for example. It only requires simple ingredients, but with care and dedication, you'll get incredible results.
The fish becomes tender and melt-in-your-mouth, while the soup retains its fresh taste. No need to drown it in seasonings!
In fact, I'm going to bring her a bowl right now and show her how it's done. I'll make her see the difference!
Great food, great value! I've got a wide variety of produce for you to choose from. Hello again. What brings you in today? Or would you like to chat? I'm all ears!
Don't have enough credits yet? I'll hold these for you.
Thank you for shopping at Mahe's! Your order is ready.
I see. Do come again if you need anything.
If you want authentic Jinzhou cuisine, you've come to the right place.
Hmm, I've been trying out a new recipe lately. Well, somewhat new-ish.
Life used to be tough for us before coming to Jinzhou. We had to do whatever we could to feed ourselves.
Our Ma Xiaofang was just a child then, but she was always so kind and selfless. She gave as much of her food to the elderly as she could.
It broke my heart to see her go hungry at times. But one day, I managed to catch a wild rabbit and made a stew with some fresh greens for her. I still remember that smile on her face to this day.
And now, our Xiaofang... Should I call her Chixia now? She's all grown up and even works as a Patroller! She dropped by recently and told me how she missed that stew.
How to make food taste better? Well, buckle up, you're in for a treat.
Heat control, choice of spices, when you should turn up the heat for stir-fry, when to slow cook your stew... Every detail matters.
Mahe would say it's important to get fresh ingredients, and he's right on that, but seasoning is even more important.
At my restaurant, nothing less than perfection is acceptable. Seasoning is crucial for a good dish! Mahe... He just won't get it.
Well, he does make some good fish soup, though...
You're here for some grub? Finally found the time to drop by today, huh?
What are you in the mood for today? I'll fire up the wok!
How was that? I hope you enjoyed it.
What's the matter? Are you low on appetite? Tell me what else you'd like to eat. I'll fire up the wok for you!
Welcome! We've got a variety of produce here.

I recently received an invitation from the Pioneer Association to explore the culinary delights of Jinzhou. Eager to embark on this food journey, I wandered through the city's streets, savoring every dish the city has to offer. My journey led me to uncover delightful surprises that have now come together to form this unique booklet—a comprehensive food map of Jinzhou. I hope that as you read these pages, you will feel inspired to embark on your own food exploration—then my hard work is worth it. <color=Highlight>Panhua's Restaurant</color>, rating: ☆☆☆☆☆
While writing this booklet, I found myself seated at a small table at Panhua's Restaurant, enveloped by the vibrant buzz of lively conversations. It was here that I witnessed a heartwarming gathering involving a Patroller who had just completed her duty, her friend wearing a blue beret, and another friend in an icy demeanor. Before the Patroller could sit down, she swiftly placed an order for Poached Chicken, Perilla Salad, and Maocai before being joined by her friends. They shared anecdotes with each other, and the vivid expressions and gestures of that Patroller made the atmosphere even more lively. This experience makes me confident that Panhua's Restaurant has the ability to provide a relaxing and spirited dining environment, making it a standout choice for any culinary enthusiast.

As I penned these words, the Poached Chicken arrived at my table. While the chicken itself appeared flat, when immersed in the restaurant's specially crafted sauce, it provides an unforgettable flavor. As I savored each bite, the meat juices burst forth, accompanied by a fresh aroma that lingered in the mouth. The accompanying vegetables, stir-fried to perfection, boasted a vibrant green, complemented by sizzling oil droplets. Paired with tender and fluffy rice, the dish left me with only one word in my mind—"delicious". 

So I couldn't resist having another serving:)
<color=Highlight>Jewel Boba</color>, rating: ☆☆☆☆

If I had a second stomach dedicated solely to desserts, there's no doubt it would be reserved for the delicious dessert soup offered here in Jinzhou.. During my visit, I ordered the new buy-one-get-one-free dessert soup. The owner told me that its launch was inspired by a happy couple celebrating their anniversary at the shop—the owner, pleased with their happiness, presented them with a specially made drink. As the couple highly praised its taste, the owner decided to share its taste to more customers. After listening to this warm story, I, who was holding two cups alone, couldn't shake the bitterness of coming here alone. Luckily, the sweetness of the Jewel Boba somewhat lifted my spirits.

In other words, it's your own Echo, captured or absorbed at some point. Without you, it can't manifest.
That's why Baizhi couldn't confirm just how you absorbed that Echo back then. Was it you? Was it the little one? Or maybe, the two of you together?
And Baizhi discovered more after analyzing your spectrums.
She found a new power source within you, similar to the Crownless but even stronger. This power comes from the Tacet Discord you defeated in Norfall Barrens.

So, the excess energy this little thing had "consumed" somehow ended up in your body, available at your disposal. In other words, there's a deeper connection between the two of you. Or, according to Baizhi, it’s a Convergent Codependency.
Uh, to put it simply... you are connected. While you are two separate individuals, your energies and vitals can affect each other, for better or for worse. You may even feel each other's emotions.
The bond between you and this creature is symbiotic. As it strengthens, so do you. However, if one is harmed, the other suffers.
Fortunately, since it can't ever leave your side, it's not an easy target for attackers. And if they do strike, it can seek shelter inside your body for safety.
Okay, now that's... pretty much it. Baizhi was going to explain it to you herself, but she has to go check on a newly appeared Sonoro Sphere in Zhaozhou...
Wait, wait! This is too much information for me to process! Let me get this straight. So, it helped Rover fight off the Threnodian?
Seriously? This teeny tiny thing could do that? Hmm. Seems unlikely...
Compared to mere firewood, we need brave pioneers to ignite the flames of change.
Don't look back. Join them on this right path, and I've got a scorchingly delightful welcome for you up ahead!
Kneel before these brave pioneers who paved the way for our enlightenment.

No one knew how she managed to juggle the interests of various factions and push forward progress across all sectors with a limited budget.
It was said that Changli avoided electronic media during this time, instead recording notes in a booklet. To this day, people continue to search for this elusive booklet, hoping to uncover the secrets of Jinzhou's past. The honorable Madam Jinhsi, our great magistrate of Jinzhou, was handpicked by Sentinel Jué. Her status as the Sentinel's Appointed Resonator is rare among all past magistrates.
Our Jinzhou was leaderless for years until Jué finally chose her to be the next Magistrate, and she answered the call.
To further elaborate, we must start with the "Battle Beneath the Crescent"...
The Norfall Barrens, scarred by countless wars... Discarded weapons scattered like bones.
Our soldiers had fought to reclaim the land for years, to no avail.
Ovathrax, the dreadful Threnodian monster, fed on the frequencies of "weapons" turning our fallen soldiers into deadly Tacet Discords...
General of the Midnight Rangers, Geshu Lin, bravely rose to confront the threat.
As twin moons aligned, General Geshu Lin vowed to vanquish evil, raising his blade against the blood-red crescent that foretold destruction.
His sword blazed with black flames, laying waste to all who dared stand in his way. Victory seemed certain...
...Until the Retroact Rain began to fall.
Raindrops fell upwards as in the past. Monsters raged, loyal souls fell to blood-soaked sands... Infernal carnage!
Sacrificing his body to the black flames for power, Geshu Lin charged at the Ovathrax with all his might... And he was never seen again.

After the fall of their leader, the remaining soldiers despaired... Until a deafening roar of the <ano=Teal Dragon>Qingloong</ano> struck like lightning. A lone youth bravely stood up to lead. A hard-won retreat!
After the battle, that young man who tamed the wind ascended to fame, becoming the new General of Midnight Rangers, selected by Sentinel Jué.
On the other hand, General Geshu was blamed for the massive losses that occurred under his command, earning him a notorious reputation in Huanglong...
That battle struck us hard, but our Sentinel rose from its long slumber to select a new Magistrate who guide us into the future.
Despite the previous disaster, Jinzhou was off to a promising start under our Sentinel and the new Magistrate's guidance. The people held hope for a better tomorrow...
Issuing his last command, Geshu Lin demanded all soldiers stand firm, no matter what happened.

Exiles' Communication Records

...What's so special about the Court of Savantae Ruins? If you ask me, those people from the Court of Savantae were no good. Dead though they may be, their excessive protection measures still got several of my brothers killed. Tsk, I don't get why those people from Fractsidus are so obsessed with the moldy books and scrap metal of the Court of Savantae. All they have done over the last three days is dig up the ground and move the Court of Savantae's junk out of the ruins. I wouldn't humor them at all if they weren't paying so well.
—Yao Shisi

Reply to Yao Shisi
Are you really that crazy about money, or do you have a death wish? The Fractsidus are a ruthless bunch who will swallow you whole. Why not just search Mt. Firmament for something valuable and sell them in Jinzhou instead. That way you'd make a pretty penny, too.
—Kui
Did you bring the stuff?
Yep, all of them, exactly the amount you asked for.
Hold it, man. Be patient. We need to see the money first…
Money? You wish! Go collect 'em in your dreams!
What? You dare to fool us! I'll smack the heck out of you!
Oh no... The box is missing... The bad guy stole it...
Tabbie... Patchie... no...
Meow—
Sounds like there's a little cat in that pile of boxes...
Two kittens?
They're not scared of humans... and look well and healthy. Someone must be taking care of them.
But why are they wandering in this place...
Are they going back home? That looks like the way to Hongzhen.
So you had an ambush all set up? Guess I underestimated you.
You serious? Bring your man here and tryin' to play the victim now? Don't even make me laugh!
Good Tabbie. Good Patchie.
Sorry... it's all my fault.
Meow—
Purr—
Tabbie and Patchie like you very much, {Male=Big Brother;Female=Big Sister}.
Meow, meow meow.
The tabby kitten circles around you and then meows anxiously at Little Tang.
What is it, Tabbie? Hmm, you mean this {Male=Big Brother;Female=Big Sister} saved you from the bad guy?
Meow.
I see. Thank you so much, {Male=Big Brother;Female=Big Sister}.
Come on, you two. Say "Thank you!"
Meow!
Meow, meow!
No trouble at all.
Why did the Exiles take them?
…Granny told me some bad uncles and aunties are doing bad things in the town recently.
Tabbie and Patchie like to sleep in the box. Maybe those bad guys thought there was a "treasure" inside, like others said, so they grabbed the box and took Tabbie and Patchie with them.
I've been looking for them for quite a long time... Thank you for bringing them home safely.
Don’t worry. I’ve taught them to behave.
Wow! You are so cool! I need to be stronger and protect Tabbie and Patchie.
And I made a new home for them using a beautiful new box! I put it in my home, so it's safe there.
You are welcomed to come and play with us at any time!
Are you sure it’s gonna work? I mean… hiding the box in the sea? Underwater?
What else do you want, genius?
Right, let's just carry it and swagger through the streets. Make sure everyone knows we found a treasure box!
If you can't suggest anything useful, then just keep your mouth shut and wait for the ship. Once it docks, you can pull the box up from the water.
Talk gibberish again and I'll toss you into the sea.
Alrigh, got it...
Another blockhead messing around? I'll teach you a proper lesson!
Arrogant Fractsidus Artificer

When "the Genius" Meets "the Ordinary": An Exclusive Interview with the Mysterious Polymath

Q: This is your first time speaking to the public, right? Are you nervous? Everyone's been so curious about what the legendary "genius" is like.
A: Haha, actually, I've interacted with many of you on various topics without you even realizing it. Maybe you would recall discussing proton lifetime with someone named Cream Cat.

Q: That science writer Cream Cat? So it's also you! What a surprise! By the way, does this pseudonym have any special meaning?
A: It's from a little "aha" moment. Let me ask you this: ever accidentally dropped a cream cake? If you have, you've probably noticed the creamy side always hits the ground first, just like a cat always lands on its paws. Now, imagine this: stick the non-creamed side onto a cat's back, and voilà! You've got yourself a cream-cat perpetual motion machine, spinning 24/7—a true scientific marvel.

Q: It must take a whimsical and creative mind to come up with such an interesting idea. I wonder if your research on Automata Mechanics is just as imaginative.
A: To answer that, let's raise our heads and look at the starry sky through the window above. What do you see at first glance? And if you look further, what do you see next?

Q: First, the moon and stars. Beyond that, maybe planets crashing into each other or the starry sky mirroring the world we live in.
A: Now, are these just your imagination or scientific facts waiting to be confirmed? You can't find the answer if you don't imagine it first, right? It's the same with my research: imagination is part of scientification. Researchers today often focus too much on the utilitarian side of science, abandoning imagination to ensure their work contributes to mankind and the world as a whole, even if it goes against their intuition. Applied research is undoubtedly necessary for post-Lament reconstruction, but that's no reason to give up imagination, the breeding ground of science. So, my advice is... just think about how to make the science work. As for what it might yield, well... (smiles)

Q: How enlightening! Speaking of advice, do you have any for your gifted son, Xiangli Yao? As a genius yourself, you must have high expectations for him.
A: That might be a lot for a young boy to handle, <color=Highlight>but... I just hope he inherits my way of seeing things. So that one day, when he steps out of his room and tries to make sense of this world, he can look up at the sky and find the answers there.</color>

Diary II

Dad and Mom always take different paths when we go hiking. Dad likes heading up to the summit, and I enjoy climbing with him. After reaching the top, we sit under a big tree and count the stars in the night sky. Mom, on the other hand, always goes down the mountain. Today, I decided to go with Mom.
I didn't even know there was a village at the bottom of this remote mountain! Everyone there smiled and nodded at Mom like they knew her well. Does Mom come here for her job all the time?
The villagers gathered around and thanked Mom, expressing their praises, just like those mentioned in the newspapers. But I also heard them say something else.
"I wasn't sure if Dr. Xiangli Yan would really give us checkups for free every month, but she did it! And she still does, even after the big disaster..."
"She's so sincere and considerate. But don't you think it's a waste of talent for her to work in our village? I mean, someone of her expertise should be doing more important things!"
On the way home, I couldn't shake off what the villagers had said, even finding myself muttering those words. Mom noticed and took my hand, asking about counting stars with Dad. I told her I could recognize every star, even the faintest ones in the distance. Mom said even though she wasn't up on the mountain with us, she was still gazing at the stars. The difference was that she kept her feet firmly on the ground so she wouldn't fall while looking at the sky. As she spoke, a man came up to her asking for help, so I went home alone. But this time, the starry sky looked different from what Dad showed me back on the mountaintop.

The Academy is experimenting with a new type of technology rumored to be capable of simulating powerful enemies to help with the troops' combat training...

1. In Tactical Simulacra, challenge waves of powerful enemies by using special buffs across different simulation domains.

2. As you complete more challenges, more special buffs will be unlocked to aid you in taking on subsequent challenges.

iii. Technical Points are earned for each successful Counterattack and Dodge triggered. There's a maximum limit to the number of Technical Points that can be earned from each challenge.

Umm... Who are you?
What's wrong?
My stomach hurts... I got food poisoning from accidentally eating the wrong herb to be more precise.
Should I take you to a clinic?
No need, I'm a doctor myself. I've checked my pulse and it's nothing too serious.
I just didn't expect this herb to be poisonous. It was supposed to be safe. I should've been more careful.
What herb did you take exactly?
According to the Supplement to Great Pharmacopoeia, it's a herb called the Loong's Pearl.
The pharmacopoeia says that it isn't poisonous—on the contrary, it can dissolve toxins from plants, wood, metal, and stones.
I suspect there might be some errors in the pharmacopoeia, or maybe I mixed up two similar herbs.
May I take a look at it?
Uh... sure. I've got it with me. Here.
Loong's Pearl... Hmm...
What is it? Did you find anything?
There's a note in the appendix in fine script.

Really? Let me see... "The Loong's Pearl is a fine medicine, but where fine medicine grows, poison also flourishes. Neighboring the Loong's Pearl there usually grows a poisonous herb known as the Yunjiao Gall, which causes unending stomach pain when consumed."
"It resembles the Loong's Pearl, so be careful not to mix them up."
I see... Sorry, I should have read more carefully.
Wait, there's more. It also mentions an antidote: "Loong's Pearl can counteract the poison. The most potent ones thrive under waterfalls and have a strong fragrance."
Sounds credible.
An antidote growing near poisonous herbs... It aligns with the pharmacological theories. Looks like this isn't a mistake.
Could you help me find a Loong's Pearl beneath the waterfall? I'd go myself, but I really can't walk now.
No problem.
Thank you, friend.
You... you're back... Did you find the herb?
Here.
Hmm... the slight blue hue, the faint glow, and the aromatic scent. Yes, it matches the description in the pharmacopoeia.
According to the records, it can be consumed directly if in an emergency, although it might be more effective after processed.
Then just eat it.
You might not have time to wait that long.
Shinong puts the Loong's Pearl in his mouth and begins chewing. His pain visibly eases.
Phew... Much better. It looks like the pharmacopoeia's description of the Loong's Pearl was accurate. Thank you.
Why did you eat the herb in the first place anyway?
Ah, that's a long story. Allow me to formally introduce myself. I'm Shinong, a doctor from Jinzhou.
I've been studying ancient pharmacopoeias and medical books from all over Huanglong.
While the medical practices of Huanglong share the same roots, many ancient texts have been lost over time.
Luckily, Hongzhen has managed to preserve some texts that may have been lost elsewhere.
But over the years, as supplements are made, all pharmacopoeias and medical books inevitably suffer from confusions and omissions.
They even include some superstitions that are completely unrelated to medicine.
Superstitions...?

For example, there's a remedy that involves holding a rooster at exactly noon, jumping three times under the eaves, and then spinning around three times. It's said that if the rooster crows at that moment, it will drive away any plague.
That's actually... kinda creative?
While it might be a fun folklore activity, in practice it doesn't do anything to treat any illnesses.
That's why I wanted to revise these pharmacopoeias—to remove the unnecessary parts and correct the errors.
And the best way to do this is to try each herb personally and observe any reactions.
This way, I can determine their effects and uncover any side effects not mentioned in the texts.
That sounds... quite risky.
Don't worry. After generations of supplements and revisions, I'm certain any herb that poses significant health risks are all highlighted in these pages.
Worst-case scenario, it would just be minor mishaps, like what happened earlier. Such risks are predictable and entirely manageable.
Oh, as a token of gratitude, here's some tonic that I brewed.
...It's not poisonous, is it?
Don't worry. I brewed it using my proven recipe.
Until we meet again, friend. I wish you good health.
Hey, {PlayerName}! Fancy seeing you here!
You didn't eat any odd herbs today, did you?
Of course not—well, not yet.
I read an anecdote in Hongzhen Chronicles about a young man from a few hundred years ago who discovered that Pavo Plums has temporary memory-enhance effects.
He memorized all the texts of Hongzhen with the help of Pavo Plum's incredible effects, earning him the nickname "the Walking Bookshelf."
So... you know. I want to try it.
It's probably just a myth.
You sure something like that exists?
I agree that the story might be fictional. But there might be some truth behind it.
I've always been gathering Pavo Plums from around this area. But according to Hongzhen Chronicles, only those "found near the hot spring and that can slightly heat up" has medical effects.
But I've searched everywhere near the hot spring and haven't found any Pavo Plums like the ones described.
I could give you a hand with it.
R-really? That would be great!
{PlayerName}, did you find any heated Pavo Plums?
Exactly as the chronicles described... I didn't expect it to exist. Interesting... But it could be a mutation.
"Didn't expect it to exist?"
A mutation?
H-haha. Don't be upset. Presumption is the first step toward truth.
I suspect that the surrounding heat might have induced some changes in these Pavo Plums... potentially altering their medicinal effects.
Now, {PlayerName}, could you please say something after I eat the Pavo Plum?
Sure, what would you like me to say?
Anything will do, preferably something long and complicated. I want to test if it truly helps improve memory.
As soon as Shinong finishes the Pavo Plum, his face twists into a peculiar expression.
It's... it's... it's...
What is it? Is it poisonous?
It's so SPICY! I've tasted countless herbs, but I've never tasted anything this SPICY before!
Wait, I think it's working... Say something, Rover. Anything!
How much wood would a woodchuck chuck if—
Oh, my lord, I beg your forgiveness—
You effortlessly recite a passage from a tongue twister.
You passionately perform a monologue from a movie film.
Hm... Hm...
Did you catch all of that?
...None, actually.
Whole thing sounded like a bust from the get-go.
That doesn't mean all myths are false.
After all, it's just a fictional anecdote that can't be taken too seriously. But you never know unless you give it a try.
Perhaps. If I've learned anything from revising these pharmacopoeias, it's never to underestimate the wisdom of those who came before us.
Anyway, these Pavo Plums don't show any special effects, even though they can absorbe heat... and are extremely spicy. Well, that's a small discovery, at least.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. There are still quite a few herbs from the pharmacopoeia that I haven't tried yet. I'll go and search for them now.
Um... It's you, {PlayerName}.
What happened...
I fell off the hill by accident. Luckily I got away with only a swollen leg.
According to the pharmacopoeia, a herb called Elderflower grows on the hilltop, which is far more effective for treating external injuries than other herbs.
However, it appears I overestimated my athletic abilities.
Anyway... Ahem, I'll need your help again, {PlayerName}. Could you go to the hilltop and pick some Elderflowers for me?
Elderflowers grow at the top of that hill, so please be careful. But given your abilities, I'm sure it will be a piece of cake.
Yes, those are the Elderflowers!
According to the pharmacopoeia, simply grind them into paste and apply it to the injury. It takes effect almost immediately.
Shinong applies the paste to his leg, wincing at the sharp sting it causes.
Ah... All right, this should do it now.
Feeling any better?
Much better... I should be back on my feet after a bit of rest.
You must find it strange, {PlayerName}. Why am I out here risking my life instead of treating others back at the clinic in Jinzhou?
Many believe that I'm doing this for fame and attention.
For minor ailments that could easily be treated with injections or pills, using herbs involves a lot of effort, including collecting, concocting, and refining the herbs.
...They think it's meaningless, just a form of performative art and self-satisfaction. What do you think, {PlayerName}?
It's about carrying on the tradition.
Plus, many people still rely on it.
Exactly. These pharmacopoeias are the legacy of our ancestors' wisdom. Yet, nowadays, few are willing to put in the time to revise them.

As a result, the errors in these pharmacopoeias keep piling up, making them less and less trustworthy. Many people who could have been cured end up having their conditions worsen or prolonged due to incorrect treatments.
I'm not doing this for fame. I just want to preserve our ancestors' tradition and help more people avoid suffering.
That's truly honorable!
...No, it's just a simple wish. The wish of a doctor.
Maybe I'm just a humble doctor, but at least I have the courage to see it through.
I wish you all the best!
Thank you for your help, {PlayerName}. Don't worry, I'll get back in town soon.
Hello there, can you hear me? Hello?
Um… I feel terrible...
...Yes, I believe it's a type of migraine.
Migraine?
You're just in time, {PlayerName}.
Based on my observation, he has a rare disease that is only documented in a pharmacopoeia.
Can you treat him?
...It's tough. The disease can't be completely cured, and can only be alleviated with medication. However...
What is it?
I found a prescription in a medicinal book... The note says it has little effect on this kind of migraine, but I think there is a flaw to it.
The prescription uses Silver Lotuses as the main ingredient, but it's not effective for the symptoms.
I recall from the Complete Interpretation of Lost Prescriptions that regular Silver Lotuses and those that are over ten years old have opposite effects.
After observing the migraine's symptoms and checking his pulse, I believe Silver Lotuses which have bloomed for over ten years should be the correct remedy.
In conclusion, the medicinal text likely mixed them up.
It's possible. There's a chance that a minor omission occurred during the transcription. Unfortunately, this small mistake was enough to render the disease untreatable.
I've administered some relieving medicine to the patient. {PlayerName}, could you go to the nearby hill and collect some Silver Lotuses that are over ten years old? I'll wait here for you.
You can count on me.
Thanks, {PlayerName}.
This is it! It fits perfectly with the description in the pharmacopoeia. Well done, Rover!
I'll start concocting the medicine now... Please wait.
After a while, the patient takes the medicine and quickly regains consciousness.
...Um. Wh-what happened? Did I... Oh right, I passed out again.
It's because of your migraine.
Did you help me? It's an old ailment. I've been managing it with medication, but I often...
...Huh? But I feel so much better than before. How is that possible?!
I'll write you a prescription. Take the medicine as directed for a week and you should fully recover. If you still feel unwell, feel free to contact me anytime.
Fully recover? But my doctor said my condition is incurable. Are you... some kind of miracle workers?
...I'm just a regular doctor.
Where is your clinic? I'll make a banner for you and send it over as soon as I get home!
No, no, there's no need for that. {PlayerName} is the one who gathered the herb. I just...
Wrote a prescription?
Brewed the medicine?
...I just did what any doctor would do.
Nevertheless, please accept my deepest gratitude and respect for both of you.
I've made a lot of progress recently and have finished revising the  pharmacopoeias in Hongzhen.
I'll send them to the clinics. Hopefully, what I'm doing can benefit more people.
Where's your next stop?
Next? There's a long journey ahead. The world is vast, and there are countless pharmacopoeias to rectify. I'm not sure how many I can complete.
But I will do my best.
Then, good luck.
May our paths cross again, {PlayerName}.
Rover

Sell? You mean like the herbs you found and gathered on your trip?

Yes... yes, and quality stones for sculpting at that! We offer all kinds of them! Here's a sample... for you to... take a look.
It does look nice, both the texture and color... But this is not from Mt. Firmament, is it?
No, it isn't. I brought it with me from Jinzhou!
Wait, is there something wrong with it?
Not in the slightest! Our company has been in the stone business for over 10 years in Jinzhou. And we... we've always offered the best there is at affordable prices...
Sounds a bit suspicious. If the rocks are fine, why are you so nervous?
This is his first crack at sales. Please understand.
I see. That explains a lot. When I first worked here, I couldn't even get a whole sentence out. It's okay, you just need more practice.
All right, then let's get down to business. What's the price?
Yongxin gives an irresistible quote.
That really is pretty cheap... I've heard that they have to rely on heavy-duty machinery to mine rocks out there, but this...
Do you find the offer appealing?
It's really a great deal.
Sorry, I can't do it.
Is the price too high for you? That's fine, I'm sure we can work something out...
It's not about the price. These statues were carved out of Mt. Firmament rocks.
Mt. Firmament rocks...? Are they different from the ones in Jinzhou?
Of course. Every rock in Mt. Firmament had been blessed by our great Sentinel.
Well, I'm not joking with you. Don't believe me? Just take a look at that!
Out the window? Is that... the Loong's Crest? Wait, the shape... Don't tell me...
That's right. Not just Loong's Crest, the appearance of the entire Mt. Firmament was hand-chiseled by the ancestors of Hongzhen to resemble our Sentinel!
It's okay, you're not the first to be blown away by this marvel. Like I've always said, the story of Mt. Firmament's Sentinel statue really should be included in the tourism pamphlet...
All right, I got to get back to work. Hongzhen's been bustling with visitors lately. Catch you later, {PlayerName}.
I guess I still got a lot to learn about Hongzhen... I'll hang around and see if I can get new clients. If I work hard... I can definitely...
You still have to conquer your anxiety first.
My mind just... goes blank and I don't know what to say.
Say what you say best, of course.
Just repeat the words you were typing before.
That's it...? That does make sense... Let me dwell on it. Thank you, {PlayerName}.
There you are, {PlayerName}.
Your face is glowing red.
And that's a lot of sweat.
It... it's too hot here for sure. That's hot springs for you. Even the air feels hot...
Hello... I am...
Here you are, finally. Tongchuan Pharmacy sent you, right? Do you have any idea how busy I am today, and you just got here? Where's my shipment?
Shipment...?
The medicine I ordered for spa therapy. Wait, why are you empty-handed?
And {PlayerName}... when did you start working for Tongchuan Pharmacy?
We're here to make sales.
You got us mixed up with someone else.
Yongxin quickly explains his intent.
Oops, my mistake. He didn't look familiar to me so I thought he was from Tongchuan Pharmacy.
But I don't have time for that right now. As you can see, I'm swamped here... And the fact that the medicine from Tongchuan Pharmacy still hasn't arrived yet makes it even worse.
Oh, right! Can you check on the delivery for me, {PlayerName}? If I don't have the spa ready soon, I'll get complaints.
No problem.
Yes! I knew I could count on you!
You're a rare sight, {PlayerName}.
Here for some herbs? I just got a fine batch in from Jinzhou. They work wonders for both internal and external use.
I'm here for the herbs for Spring's Taste.
Oh my, can't believe that slipped my mind.
I was going to send someone over this morning, but the guy called in sick. Xinyang must be getting impatient by now...
Let me see... Yeah, should be these. Thanks for delivering them, {PlayerName}.
You're back, {PlayerName}?
Yes, this is it. I spent a lot of money on this new recipe. Now, all I have to do is put it in the hot spring.
Dip in the hot spring just for fun, twice to dodge the flu and run, thrice for muscles feeling fine, four times to make sickness decline!
Oh, the fellow over there... What did you want to see me for again?
Excuse me, but... do you need stones for your hot spring?
Stones? You mean for renovating the pool? No, because we're in peak season so it will cost me a lot of money to renovate now.
How about rockery, got any of that?
Yes, yes! We... do...
Tell me about your best product.

...Well, our rockery comes in a variety of styles, such as the Jinzhou border style, the Mengzhou garden style, and the newest luxury style from Huanglong capital. We also offer customization based on your own design, dear customer!
Dear customer, you can order now for free shipping to Hongzhen, plus a three-year warranty! If you have any questions or need more information, please leave a message and I will...
Ahem. You can stop right there.
...Is this how people from Jinzhou sell stuff nowadays? Sounds a bit weird... but it's actually kind of appealing?
The best bang for your buck, dear customer.
Your hot spring deserves the enticing look, dear customer.
Hm... Indeed, I do think the spring is missing something, so if I added this...
Phew, I guess that's one deal closed. Now I can face the boss.
You seem to be under a lot of stress.
Well, my boss was never optimistic about Hongzhen, or he would've never sent a low-man-on-the-totem-pole like me here.
But I did it... I've taken the first step, and that's because I have your encouragement and help...
So, what's up with the "dear customer" thing?
Didn't you want me to say what I say best? That's all I know...
I still came off a little nervous, but much better than before.
Then I'll have to keep working at it. Thank you, {PlayerName}.
It's simple, really. If we create a macroscopic node with Resonator A, we can use that as the coordinate to perform a three-dimensional expansion through inverse anisotropic frequency...
So you want us to build a three-meter-tall marble control station from your model?
No, no, I said three-dimensional expansion. It means, uh, taking apart the model's original four-dimensional structure...
You need a four-legged stand, too? No problem. It can all be done as long as we have the blueprint.
Am I interrupting anything?
{PlayerName}! I was just telling this gentleman here about our latest project, but he... seems to be proposing a bolder, more profound approach.
To be honest, some of the suggestions are quite inspirational, like the four-directional magnetic restraint he mentioned, despite the lack of practical proof...
...How did you two manage to communicate?
(Thank heavens you're here, {PlayerName}...)
How much of that did you get?
This'll be a great learning experience.
(Frankly, it's like a foreign language to me, except he's not a foreigner.)
Do you know each other, {PlayerName}?
Yeah, but actually...
He's here to make a sale.
Oh, right, I remember now. Pardon me. I've been knee-deep in the new project...
Phew... Thanks, {PlayerName}. Now we can finally get back to business.
You must be the hunter we hired to collect Scarefrost Deer samples, right?
Huh?
He's the stone merchant you were looking for.
Ha.. haha... Oh, is that so? Oh right... I think I did mention something like that.
Actually, we've been working on a new project that mainly focuses on the impact of the Sentinel's time barrier on Mt. Firmament's ecology.
As you can tell, even though the time barrier is gone, the residual effect caused the snow to be permanent, leading to the unique ecology you have now.
The environment may appear stable now, but who can guarantee it won't collapse or become disastrous for Mt. Firmament in a few years or decades?
What's that got to do with stones?
The people of Hongzhen believe that Sentinel's power has seeped into the rocks of Mt. Firmament.
Therefore, comparing the frequencies of the rocks of Mt. Firmament to those from other areas could give us a clue to what's really going on.
Ahem... but there's a... big hurdle.
We're running out of budget. It's the director's fault. No matter how miraculous Mt. Firmament is, we just can't afford all these projects at once...
So... can you give me a discount? Please, the future of Mt. Firmament is at stake.
But what I'm offering is already really low... We still have to haul the stones all the way from Jinzhou, and we might even run into Tacet Fields on the way...
This is a very crucial study, so please...
It's your decision to make, Yongxin.
What, me...?
But I... I can't make the call. I'm a nobody... I'm not even a professional salesman.
Your opinion is very important.
*sigh* I must be out of my mind... Fine, I'll sell them to you at cost price.
Really? That's wonderful! I'll put in a budget request right now!
This probably isn't going to work out for me... The boss might fire me on the spot when I get back.
Having second thoughts?
I don't know. But they seemed so passionate... and committed.
I looked into the research station before I came. They declined generous offers in Jinzhou and other places to work in these makeshift conditions.
I don't understand exactly what they're studying, but I know it's important.
You made the right decision.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. I feel much better now.
I'm still a little bummed-out about it, though... It took me so long to get to this point.
Your hard work will pay off.
Hope so.

We have Uncle Fu to thank for resurrecting this ritual by studying ancient texts.

The stone wall before you is called the Water Shadow Screen. It is naturally formed by years of continuous erosion from the waters of Sagaci Springs.
What's notable is that it inspired the ancestors of Hongzhen to invent a delightful form of entertainment—the Water Shadow Play.

All you need to do is gather some maple leaves that are scattered throughout the mountains and cut them into various shapes. Then, by using small twigs to manipulate them, the shadows of the leaves will dance in the water, bringing fascinating stories to life.
And that's why brewing and sipping tea while watching a Water Shadow Play became the favorite pastime for the folks of Mt. Firmament.
Since you don't come to Hongzhen often, {PlayerName}, how about we shoot the breeze for a while?
Hello, Uncle Fu.
Pardon me, but do I know you...?
It's been a long time, hasn't it, youngster?
The last time we met was in a secret chamber here...
Hahaha, you young people sure are blunt. It's okay. There's nothing to remember this old man by, anyway.
But you can call me Uncle Fu like everybody in Hongzhen does, if you don't mind.
The last time I saw you was in a secret chamber here...
Mt. Firmament was in dire straits back then. It's hard to imagine it being peaceful again in such a short time, let alone more prosperous.
All this just feels surreal, like a dream.
There were a lot of people opposing my decision to step down as the Mayor of Hongzhen.

I get it. Even though Xinyi's ancestors were from Hongzhen, she came to the mountains later on. While her abilities are impeccable, her way of doing things is still a bit different from the locals here.

But back then, I kept thinking, what if Mt. Firmament could open up to the outside world again? After staying in isolation for all these years, Hongzhen has already fallen behind the rest of the world.
For the sake of future generations, Hongzhen needs some fresh blood. Clinging to old ways just isn't sustainable.
And it all worked out better than I ever imagined. See, Mt. Firmament's door is opened again, and Hongzhen is still running smoothly in every aspect.
Letting Xinyi take over was the smartest move I've ever made.
Uncle Fu gazes into the horizon, too lost in his thoughts to notice anyone around him.
No idea what happened to the young ones who ventured outside of Mt. Firmament... I hope nothing bad happened to them.
Hopefully, they'll come back once in a while. This is their home, after all.
Oh, it's you.
I appreciate what you did last time. I think I got a lot better since then.
Now everyone loves to hear my Mt. Firmament stories, and quite a few want me to be their guide.
Congrats.
You did it all on your own.
Well, I couldn't have done it without your suggestions and encouragement.
Of course, I can't be complacent. I learned much of Mt. Firmament's history from these documents.
The more I learn, though, the more I realize how little I knew before.
Have you given more thought to what we talked about before, Yucang?
I thought about it, but... I'm sorry, I want to stay here.
What can you do here? You have to go out, get yourself to Jinzhou to accomplish great things, or the Magistrate saved your life for nothing.
Sigh. I'm staying exactly because the Magistrate saved me.
If all of us young people leave, what will become of Hongzhen?
I feel since the waterway is open now, there will be plenty of opportunities for me in Mt. Firmament, too.
The Magistrate almost traded his life for the peace we have in Mt. Firmament now. I want to defend it to repay him.
You sure you're not coming?
Sigh... Never mind. I know I can't talk you into it.
Hey, what is a little cat doing in the pool?!
Don't panic, kitty-kitty. I'll get you out of there right now!
Please keep it down. The cat doesn't like loud noises when it's enjoying the hot spring.
Oh, and its name is Tiger, not kitty.
Enjoying the hot spring? Stop messing with me, little girl. All cats hate water.
I'm not messing with you. Cats in Mt. Firmament don't.
Well, that's not entirely true, I guess... They don't like the streams. Maybe they just prefer Sagaci Springs...
Hey, look, Tiger heard us and is swimming our way!
This is odd. The cat does seem fine and well...
Interesting... I wouldn't believe it if I didn't see it for myself.
I wonder what makes Sagaci Springs so special...
Maybe I should try it myself sometime?
Don't forget the soil samples.
I won't. You keep the rest safe for now.
Mt. Firmament is rich in geothermal resources thanks to its unique geological and soil composition.
The water supply is also a factor as well, of course.
I had read about similar cases in research files before, but seeing the plumes of steam rising in the frigid wind in person is still quite marvelous.
The scenery here is gorgeous. Make sure to get a full-body shot of me!
Three, two, one... Done.
Wait, let me switch up my pose. Snap a few more pics of me.
Why do we need so many photos? We're not here to sight-see.
Well, I want us to have some mementos. Who knows when we'll be back?
Besides, I want to give some of them to Yuanzhi. If her family doesn't allow her to study in Jinzhou, it may be long before we see her again.
That is true...
You'll miss Yuanzhi too, right, Xunwei? Why don't I take a photo of you, too?
No thanks, I really don't look good in photos. I'm better off leaving it to Yuanzhi's memory.
Color, transparent, slightly blue.
Temperature... 41.
Characteristics...
The sample vials and containers are ready. As for specific traits, that's for lab analysis to determine.
Take a break while I sort out the data from today.
Sure. I'll text Wei. I wonder how he's doing over there.
Hey, the scenery is pretty over here, too...
"Snowflakes dance among the silver trees"... Can't believe I'm seeing what I read in books in real life.
I'll send the samples to the lab later. We should get a report back in two days.
Also, I checked out the test results. We're still missing several key data for building the spatiotemporal variation model...
Okay, I'll sort that out, too, when I get back. Wei can handle the survey as normal on his end. We'll focus on the missing data tomorrow. That's more efficient this way.
You did well today.
Just doing my job.
Oh, when the survey is done tomorrow, let's grab Wei and visit Yuanzhi.
Sure. Let me leave Wei a message.
Mom, why is that lady holding a white board?
Uhh... I don't know...
That board has so many words and pretty pictures on it! I wanna go take a look! I wanna talk to that lady!
Be good, Sibao. She's busy. Let's not bother her.
Hmm... Okay then.
No, no...
Or maybe yes? Let's just do it this way.
Are you guys interested in Mt. Firmament tea?

I heard it took seven steps to make tea outside this mountain: preparing teaware, warming teaware, putting in the tea, brewing the tea, discarding the first batch, pouring the tea, and then serving the tea.
It's not much different from our local tradition, though we're a little more particular.
Just on warming the teaware alone, we don't use boiled water but a scoop of the Sagaci Springs water, heating it with the spring's natural heat.
The teaware would get an earthy aroma from the heat, so when you pour the tea, your nostrils are greeted with a scent as if the leaves were freshly plucked from the snow.
Here, I just made it with the premium Firmament snow tea leaves. Try it.
Let's agree we want safety over adventure on this trip.
I have too little information on Mt. Firmament, so let's focus on scouting this time.
You're the expert, so of course I'll follow you.
But, I'm not going to skip any nice scenery we come across, either.
The two of us are among the first to sign up for a visit to Mt. Firmament. I've worked hard for a long time to get us this opportunity.
The magazine has saved a spot for us, so we've got to offer something unique.
Worry not, I'll make decisions accordingly.
Since we're traveling together, I'm responsible for your safety.
Oh no, none of the tricks work anymore...
Anyone who has signed up can get a pamphlet about Mt. Firmament here. It contains detailed information on lodging and travel.
If you haven't signed up but are interested, please come and sign up here.
The Pioneer Association is an open organization. We welcome everyone with an adventurous spirit.
Whew... Now the crowd has died down. I can finally take a breather.
Is Pioneer Association this popular?
Mt. Firmament is still a mystery to outsiders, after all.
So when the news of the open waterway broke, all of our signed adventurers, photographers, and reporters wanted to come.
Naturally, business has picked up as a result.
On top of that, with the association just setting up shop in Hongzhen, everything's getting mixed up. I have to tackle issue after issue, and I haven't had a proper rest in days.
I need to get back to my business now. I still have some documents to file. Talk later.
Say, would you be interested in checking out Mt. Firmament's famed Sagaci Springs?
Other than the Sagaci Springs, we also offer medicinal, floral, and alcohol baths.
Need a place to rest? We have accommodations too.
There's nothing more relaxing than enjoying a soak in the Spirit Sand Spring and then having a good night of sleep.
Judging from the size of Hongzhen, everyone probably knows each other. It's only a few steps to drop something off, so why would they need Lollo Logistics?
What about places farther away, like Loong's Ridge or Loong's Crest?
I don't think anyone lives there. Even if there were people, I never learned any skills to survive in outdoor snow, so it would actually be faster for the locals to deliver for themselves.
Forgive me. I was too occupied to notice you were here!
Are you receiving or sending a package? Oops, never mind. I forgot we just opened in Mt. Firmament and haven't received anything from the outside yet...
I'm just checking the place out.
No problem. Let me know if I can help.
Sigh, this is still not interesting enough. Got to work on the hook some more.
Huh? Hey there, are you looking for a story?
Unfortunately, I'm still getting a new script ready... I didn't expect the people in Hongzhen to be so enthusiastic. I see I still have a lot to learn.
Not to mention everyone would get bored if I kept telling the same stories. I must figure out how to make them engaging!
Yinyu suggested that I should add some details to attract younger audiences, and I think that's a good idea.
You are not from around here, right? If you're not in a hurry, try the Spirit Sand Spring. It's wonderfully relaxing. Throw in the scenery and I wouldn't trade places with anyone.
But you do look kind of familiar. Where have I seen you before...?
Where, indeed... My memory these days...
I didn't know it could be done that way...
I guess I made the right choice.
I must thank you.
What for?
I saw how much the local girl you helped has blossomed. You know, the one named Yinyu. She's now a famous guide in Hongzhen.
Her story doesn't have much to do with me, but I'm truly motivated by her growth.
When Lollo Logistics decided to expand into Mt. Firmament, I volunteered for the job, only to run headlong into a bunch of messy problems.
I even considered transferring back to Jinzhou or quitting altogether.
But then I saw Yinyu making us locals proud and building herself quite a name as a guide.
And it made me think, maybe I could ship Mt. Firmament's specialties to Jinzhou using Lollo Logistics and help local sellers reach new markets.
I don't know if it will work, but Mt. Firmament is a different animal. Instead of sticking to traditional logistics services, it might be better to incorporate some local flavor.
I won't be quitting anytime soon, at least.
Mommy, these grown-ups... I've never seen the outfits they're wearing before...
Well, Zhichun, that's because they come from outside Mt. Firmament.
What... What's it like outside Mt. Firmament? Is it scary? Grandpa said it's full of monsters...
Grandpa was talking about a long time ago. It's similar to our town now, with lots of people living there.
Hey, kid. Where are your parents?
It's dangerous there. Get down now!
My parents are working.
I always play here.
Or else I'd be bored out of my mind since I don't have anyone to play with...
Then why don't we build a snowman together? Come down first. Let's build a big one.
Well... I guess it has been a while since I last built a snowman... Okay then.
Here, let's give it a nose.
Done!
...Still feeling bored?
I've made tons of snowmen before, so I'm kind of over it...
I think it's more fun to climb up to higher places...
Hi, friend! Can you help me with something?
Are you talking to me?
Can you help me borrow one of those self-moving suitcases? You know, the ones that have four wheels at the bottom and can follow travelers around.
What do you need that for?
The stuff on Mt. Firmament can hardly interest Yanning anymore.
If I don't step in, I'm worried that the kid will do something dangerous again when her parents aren't around.
That's why I want to find something interesting for Yanning.
Leave it to me.
Thank you so much!
What's up? You need a hand or something?
You tell the young traveler in front of you about borrowing the self-moving suitcase and the whole story behind it.
That's it? Sure, no biggie.
But you'll have to wait until I've unpacked everything from the suitcase. I'll head to the hotel first. Let's meet here at sunset.
Alright.
Well? How did it go?
You tell Gulan about your progress.
Perfect. We'll meet you at the spot you mentioned at the agreed time.
I can't thank you enough.
Hey, what's that? It looks amazing!

Jinzhou, on the borderlands, often conjures images of desolate lands and barren mountain ranges.

Once a merchant was tasked with a journey to Jinzhou. "I'm not well," he promptly refused. "I would die halfway if I were to go there." His colleague smiled and responded, "You'll know what it's like once you see it for yourself."

Reluctantly, the duo set out for Jinzhou. They traversed countless barren wastelands and perilous jungles until they finally reached a picturesque place embraced by lush mountains and clear water.

Standing at the end of the forest path were towering city gates. Soldiers on guard gave them a friendly welcome, granting them entry after a quick check of their papers.

A lively tapestry of life unfurled before them as they ventured into Jinzhou. Contrary to expectations, the city was a bustling hub of activity and lacked any trace of desolation or bleakness. Amidst well-designed buildings and serene ponds teeming with colorful carp, they discovered a captivating scenery that rivaled even the lush landscapes of inland regions. Lost in the lively atmosphere, they sampled Kungfu Tea at Liuxian Teahouse, savored the specialty dish at Panhua's Restaurant, and immersed themselves in the shows at Jinzhou Theater. With each experience, their weariness faded away, replaced by the invigorating energy of Jinzhou and the warm hospitality of its people.

"Unbelievable! Who would have thought a borderland city could thrive like this? It feels like a utopia. It must have taken a lot of hard work to create such beautiful structures in here." 

"Our magistrate always preached the value of hard work. No matter your circumstances, with determination and effort, you can achieve your dreams. So despite the barren mountains and Tacet Discords, we built our homes and savored the good times before hardship struck."

"It's amazing how you all pulled it off. It couldn't have been easy, but each of you made it happen. Truly impressive."

"Well, it's not as tough as it seems with our great magistrate leading the way. We just follow her lead, and she takes care of everything here."

"Yeah, she seems really wise and capable. I bet she has years of experience too?"

"Nope, she's still young, only in her teens!"

"Teens?!"

When Jinhsi became the Jinzhou Magistrate, she was young and inexperienced. The people of Jinzhou placed their trust in her decisions, but she knew it was not her alone, but also her role as the Sentinel's Resonator, that earned their faith.

Taking on this great responsibility, Jinhsi felt determined to guide Jinzhou towards a better future, despite her initial challenges. She also understood that trust had to be earned through hard work and dedication.

Despite the skepticism she encountered, Jinhsi was more troubled by the weariness etched on the faces of the people—a weariness born of life's hardships and a lack of hope.

She realized that beyond addressing tangible issues like material shortages and external threats, her true challenge was to restore the hope and confidence of the people of Jinzhou, who had been worn down by life.

In such times, what the people needed most was a reliable source of hope, regardless of who provided it.

During a reconstruction event, the young magistrate performed a "miracle" known as "Sentinel Granting Wishes." The remote village had been plagued by weather anomalies for years. Even though the Tacet Discords had stopped, villagers still suffered from extreme cold and gloom.

Jinhsi asked the villagers to voice their wishes. At first, silence hung heavy until a sneeze broke the silence. A timid voice then followed, "It's so cold… I wish it was a bit warmer here."

Standing amidst the crowd, Jinhsi held a Loong Scale, closed her eyes, and nodded, "I will convey your wish to the Sentinel."

Right after her words fell, loong horns sprouted from her head, and a Sentinel-like light pierced the dark clouds and the snow on the ground—just in an instant, the ice thawed, and the land once again sprang to life.

Witnessing this spectacle, the crowd exclaimed, "The Sentinel... the Sentinel has shown itself!" People observed the loong-shaped light in awe, with hope rekindling in their eyes.

News of the young magistrate's wish-granting ability spread rapidly in Jinzhou. Wishing became a popular custom, with people submitting their desires to her at City Hall. She meticulously examined each one and devised effective strategies to fulfill them.

"Dear Magistrate, I'm worried about Tacet Discords infiltrating our city."—Taoqi, director of the Defense Division, was then tasked with fortifying the city defense walls.

"Dear Magistrate, I pray for my father's safe return and an end to the war."—Jinhsi prioritized research on Tacetite weaponry and material engineering, pushing for new weapons against Discords and faster upgrades for defense.

"Dear Magistrate, the Exiles have been spotted in the city. I'm scared."—Jinhsi expanded Patrol Stations, added Patrollers in the city, and assigned more Midnight Rangers to guard outside.

Within three years, the city defense walls were renewed, new weapons were created, and Tacet Discords were repelled. Jinzhou finally ushered in peace and prosperity.

As time passed, people came to realize that the so-called "Sentinel Granting Wishes" was just a white lie from the young magistrate.

However, they also discovered her true dedication to addressing their problems and concerns, always being on the spot at lightning speed.

The lights in City Hall never went out, even on holidays. Jinhsi worked tirelessly until midnight, developing feasible plans to fulfill people's wishes. 

And eventually, they came to understand that she possessed an incredible power - without a Loong Scale, she could summon a dazzling light that could pierce through ice and turn the tide of time.

...

Today, making wishes has become a habit for Jinzhou people, an unspoken agreement between them and their young magistrate.

"Dear Magistrate, I hope you can take some time to relax and come watch our latest show." This was the last wish of the year.

Smiling, Jinhsi closed the file in her hands, leaned against the window in her office, and listened to the melodious singing from Jinzhou Theater, where the new Hero Play, Loong Maiden and Wishes, was being performed.

In any situation, Jinhsi always wears a gentle smile, reassuring those around her, "There's still much to do, but rest assured, I'm here to guide you through it."

Back then, Tacet Discords ravaged the lands, and warriors fought for every piece of land. People dreaded the thought of bidding farewell to loved ones heading to the front lines, uncertain if those farewells might be forever.

After witnessing the despair and anguish in her people's eyes, the newly appointed young magistrate couldn't bear to add to their sorrow. She understood that revealing her own distress would only weaken the hard-earned confidence and hope they held onto amidst adversity.

Thus, she never let a hint of despair show, always exuding composure.

Despite her unwavering smile and gentle demeanor, Jinhsi was aware that without tangible results, her actions may be perceived as insincere or ignorant of the people's suffering. To counter this, she resolved to be a proactive magistrate, tirelessly working to address their concerns and guide them towards a life of happiness and peace.

While the Midnight Rangers valiantly fought to protect Jinzhou, a different yet equally difficult battle raged within the city walls.

Families of soldiers grappled with anxiety. Their worries for their loved ones' safety had disrupted their daily lives.

Unfortunately, interference in the Tacet Fields hindered real-time communication with soldiers. In response, Jinhsi implemented a speedy delivery service in collaboration with the Ministry of Development and Lollo Logistics. Free letters were quickly delivered to families of soldiers, thanks to Lollo Logistics, while the Ministry of Development built shortcuts for efficient transport. This helped ease the worries of families wanting updates on their loved ones serving in the military.

Another pressing issue Jinhsi tackled was comforting families who lost loved ones in battle. She worked with the Ministry of War and Ministry of Development to create a thorough plan. 

The city honored fallen soldiers by increasing compensation for their families and building a wall of remembrance in Knell Square. Tablets bearing their names were made from the finest ore, able to withstand the elements and provide solace for centuries to come. The Midnight Rangers may not have fought for honor, but their sacrifices deserved to be remembered. With the completion of Knell Square, people had another place to commemorate and seek comfort in their loss.

In all these efforts to console and address the aftermath, Jinhsi always led by example. Whenever people saw her gentle smile, they knew she would introduce policies that cheered them up just like her smile did. Such warmth served as a balm for the wounds of war, helping the people of Jinzhou endure difficult times.

Jinhsi possesses an exceptionally good temper; no matter the circumstances, she always maintains a graceful and gentle smile, and hardly anyone has ever seen her get angry. 

"Does our magistrate even know how to get angry? She's always so calm, no matter what." 

"Seriously, I've wondered about that too. How would she look when mad?"

"I've seen it," replied Shi, a typically solitary miner who stays focused on his work.

It was an exceptionally bitter winter. The contractor, citing supposed excessive equipment usage, claimed a hefty sum from a mining project, leaving the miners with nothing to show for their labor.

Fresh from the aftermath of battles, chaos reigned. With the surge in demand for civil construction, the need for ores skyrocketed. However, the Ministry of Development's exploration equipment fell short, forcing them to resort to renting privately owned tools. However, the contractor proved to be a profiteer, reneging on payment when the time came. What's worse, as the president of the Chamber of Commerce, he wielded a monopoly over exploration equipment in the market and paid little heed to the officials. 

After a year of hard work, Shi had been counting on the payment to spend a joyous New Year with his family. But now, that simple wish seemed out of reach. Looking at his calloused, weathered hands, Shi recalled the words of his colleague, Debiao: "…Honesty won't fill our pockets. Let's take action and get back what we deserve—our own hard-earned cash."

Under the cover of night, Shi and his fellow workers sneaked into the merchant's mansion. Pressing his ear against the door, Shi listened intently for any signs of movement, ready to seize the chance to burst in.

"Mr. Zhu, I'm here to deliver some news," a young girl's voice sounded from within, gentle yet tinged with an unsettling chill. "You have been removed from the Chamber of Commerce, and your business license has been revoked. Henceforth, you are forbidden from engaging in any commercial activities in Jinzhou."

"Huh? That's funny. We're in Jinzhou, a city renowned for its adherence to the law. Since you're new to your role, dear Magistrate, I'll turn a blind eye to your ignorance. Let me tell you: expelling a Chamber of Commerce president takes a minimum of two weeks here, and as for revoking my business license, I demand evidence! No evidence, no revocation. Simple as that."

"Since you mentioned the law, then let's discuss it. Per Article 180 of the Jinzhou Commercial Law, expelling a Chamber of Commerce president requires over half of its members' signatures, as well as those of the Minister of Commerce and Director of the Ministry of Development. Obtaining approval from the magistrate can be time-consuming. Therefore, I am here to inform you personally in order to expedite the return of wages for our workers."

"Regarding the evidence you requested… The Patrol Station has already collected and submitted it to the Decree Council. I am always prepared."

"As I leave, know that your monopoly on exploration gear has ended. The Ministry of Development expedited production and new equipment arrived today. Your monopoly was never going to last."

Lost in the noise inside, Shi missed the rest of the conversation. It seemed like someone was defending themselves, but Shi knew it would be useless against overwhelming proof and careful planning.

Soon, they were notified of their rightful payment on their Terminals. Finally, they could ring in the New Year with happiness.

Following that, such occurrences ceased as Magistrate Jinhsi enacted new laws prohibiting monopolies and amended payment settlement procedures: workers' wages are settled before contractors receive their payments.

As winter faded into spring, a new era dawned.

"C'mon Shi, spill the beans! What was the Magistrate like when she got angry?"

"Well... She wasn't scary. She looked very dependable. Reassuring."

"What?!"

Many praise young Magistrate Jinhsi for her remarkable intelligence and perceptive nature. There seems to be no realm of knowledge beyond her grasp, nor any challenge she cannot surmount.

Since taking office, she deftly navigates Jinzhou's complex affairs, implementing policies that have brought about peace and prosperity for its people, ushering in an era of peace and prosperity.

As the Magistrate of Jinzhou, Jinhsi's responsibilities extend from matters of great importance, such as military and political affairs, to seemingly minor issues. However, she believes that even the smallest details can greatly impact people's lives. This is the standard she holds herself to.

Though well-informed, Jinhsi still faced mysteries unknown to her. Lately, a person of great significance to her city had arrived, surrounded by elusive secrets. This only piqued her curiosity and concern for them even more.

According to historical records, a legendary hero in Jinzhou was said to possess the power of absorbing Tacet Discords with their bare hands. This person left an unforgettable mark on the history of Jinzhou and even the entire Huanglong region. Now, a new individual with unique abilities was about to appear in the world. Jinhsi suspected they may be connected to the fabled hero. Knowing the significance of this distinguished guest, Jinhsi planned a careful welcome, fully aware that they would be drawn into conflicts and conspiracies. Thus, she crafted a meticulous plan to greet them in her own distinctive manner.

She recorded a message to be broadcast throughout the region, extending a warm welcome to all visitors to Jinzhou, ensuring they felt warmly welcomed. She then purposefully left tokens to find her awaited guest, and to uncover hidden threats in the shadows.

Worried about her distinguished guest's safety, she sent her personal bodyguard to protect them in secret. Mobilizing all available resources, she provided just the right amount of assistance to help her guest unravel one puzzle after another. Jinhsi remained determined to return to Jinzhou in time for their three-day agreement, despite hardships.

Once a serene haven, Mt. Firmament bristled with instability, its tranquility disrupted by the Sentinel's peril and minions of the Fractsidus. Driven by a desire for Jinzhou's peace, the young magistrate ventured alone into the fray, confronting various difficulties while seeking information about the Sentinel. 

Emerging unharmed from such adversity was challenging for even someone as strong-willed as Jinhsi. But whenever she felt discouraged or lost in self-doubt, she'd remember a certain person. Upon waking up, that individual swiftly grasped the intricate circumstances, exhibiting patience as they awaited her decision. Jinhsi was sure they would lead Jinzhou to a brighter future, together.

On the City Hall's terrace, Jinhsi, the returning magistrate, gazed at esteemed guest with relief and joy. With a nod of greeting, she uttered the words she had rehearsed a thousand times over:

"It's been three days."

"We've both made it on time."

"Allow me to formally introduce myself. I am Jinhsi... It brings me great joy to see you, Rover."
