If someone wins a prize and spreads the word, it could be the next big thing!
The Pioneer Association really needs a makeover. We need more appeal to get new recruits, you know?
How about giving it a try yourself, {PlayerName}?
A full moon hangs in the midnight sky...
Waves crash and echo, cliffs stand high...
Excuse me, is this for the lantern riddles?
You're in the right place! See these lanterns? They are all set for the game!
The Moon-Chasing Festival fuels my brilliance! It ignites my creativity, setting the stage for my next masterpiece!
Don't worry about running out of riddles. I'll keep up with your guessing speed...
A promise made is a promise kept!
By the way, your name sounds familiar. {PlayerName}... Aha! You must be that legendary hero! The one as knowledgeable as I am!
Eyeing the prizes? Haha, solve the lantern riddles and they're all yours!
...Peel the shrimp, leave the tails, coat them all with bean flour... Once that's done, arrange them in the shape of a fan...
What are you making?
Shrimp tails?
Oh, look who's here! Good to see you, {PlayerName}. Been hearing all about your adventures at the tea house. Must be pretty busy, huh?
See what I'm making? It's a secret, ancient recipe! This one's called Shrimp Fan.
See this? They're all handwritten recipes I've collected from people. Careful! The paper's thin.
I travelled the world collecting them when I was young man. As a gourmet, I can never refuse a delicacy.
Since we're celebrating the festival now, I thought it would be nice to whip up some new dishes.
Panhua and Mahe have their own business to attend to and can't be here in person, so I brought some of their dishes along.
Some are new to me.
Heh! Those are mine.
Not bad, hm? I prefer eating over cooking, but it doesn't mean I can't cook.
Golden Sesame Tofu, Roasted Stuffed Chicken, Osmanthus Pork Stew... All traditional dishes! Try some, won't you?
A sharp mind is all you need to solve the riddles. Come on, you can do this!
Ling from the Academy usually organizes these activities. But this year, she wanted to join in on the fun, so I asked Professor Bosong to take her around.
Ling is a student at the Academy. Something happened to her family... and ever since then, Professor Bosong has been looking after her.
They get along great, but they hardly ever get a break at the Academy. So I stepped in and let them take off to enjoy the festival.
Besides, for a poet of my talent, writing a few riddles is a piece of cake!
Would you prefer landscapes or calligraphy on your fan?
You see, the brushstrokes in this landscape capture the essence of these towering mountains with such precision.
My uncle used to say that mastering just one aspect of a painting takes a lifetime.
Now I see what he meant.
I guess I'll have the chance to appreciate more artwork at this year's Fair.
Hi, {PlayerName}! Remember me?
You're a researcher from Huaxu Academy...
Sorry, I don't recall.
Yes, that's me. I'm glad you still remember.
Oh don't worry, I'll introduce myself again. I'm Zhixiu, a researcher at Huaxu Academy. We met before, remember?
Long story short, interested in trying out "Swim, Gulpuff, Swim"?
In this game, participants race as Gulpuffs.
Jinzhou's Echo technology might not be as popular as Rinascita's, but I think it has great potential.
Entertainment is key here. Plus, it's good for collecting research data.
Besides this swimming challenge, I've got some other events lined up. Hope you enjoy them, {PlayerName}.
Gulpuffs are so soft... Hmm, they do have an interesting texture.
Using Echoes for entertainment could be pretty cool.
At Huaxu Academy, we focus on what works best in practice.
But… not everything we study has to be practical, I guess. Research that brings laughter also has its value.
What do you think, {PlayerName}? Aren't Gulpuffs just adorable?
Welcome! What can I get you? You can't enjoy the festival with an empty belly.
Combine the Silver Dragon with this one… and the Thunderstorm…
Oh, {PlayerName}, it's you! Welcome! Just give me a moment to check the inventory here.
Take your time.
So many different kinds of fireworks.
You know what, I'll sort them out later.
Yep, and some experimental ones too, hehe…
Sorry for the wait, {PlayerName}. See any fireworks you like? I've got pretty much every type here.
Skyrockets, sparklers, smoke flares… you name it.
Oh, I also provide recipes for making your own custom fireworks.
Who knows, maybe yours will steal the show at the Moonlit Fair!
Come on up, come on in! Have a look at the fireworks!
Hmm… so sleepy. Eh, what's new?
With the hours I've been pulling, it's a miracle I'm still awake. Reminds me of my Lollo Logistics days.
I promised my daughter we'd set up the firework stall at the Moonlit Fair. Gotta keep that promise.
I'll design the patterns, and you deal with the hands-on stuff. Together, we'll create something memorable!
All this work… Well, as long as my girl loves it, it's no trouble at all.
…Let's see, we've got 21 fireworks and the full moon on the 15th. Together, that makes 36! Six times six! Such a lucky number!
A good omen for a lucky life!
...I don't understand a word you're saying.
Hehe, it's numerology. It's a bit of a mystery, so don't worry about it.
How about you draw a fortune stick, {PlayerName}? These are Sentinel Fortune Sticks, each one corresponding to a specific Sentinel prophecy.
A good draw will bring you luck and fortune.
What if I get a bad one?
Just laugh it off! It's only a divination, no big deal.
Besides, with the Sentinel's blessings on this special day, how could you possibly get a bad draw?
... Don't tell me they're all good draws.
Well, well, if you say it out loud, the luck might not work.
Draw a fortune stick for luck and blessings! See into the future, see for yourself!
I got into divination from watching those plays about our heroes.
You know, they always start as nobodies until they meet a divination master who sets them on the right path.
An opportunity, isn't it? That's why I decided to learn divination myself.
I thought I was getting pretty good, so I tried using divination to find my lost glasses.
First try said they were under the bed. The second try, on the rooftop. The third try, in my pocket.
So where were they exactly?
Well, I couldn't find them anywhere, so I just bought a new pair.
That's when I realized divination isn't as magical as in those hero plays.
It's mostly for fun. No need to take it too seriously. But hey, it's not bad to believe in something… Maybe I just need a bit more practice.
Back in my Pioneer Association days, I was quite the young adventurer.
But as time flew by, I settled down here in Jinzhou. Life's good now, but sometimes I find myself dreaming about all the wonderful places I once explored.
Even in the furthest of lands, there's people. And where there's people, there's food.
Take the different regions of Huanglong, for instance—no Wuthercake is the same. They've each got their own unique taste!
Try this one. It's the Jinzhou Wuthercake! It's authentic, I promise.
Right on time, {PlayerName}.
You watched the show, right? What did you think?
You're very talented!
It was a stunning show!
Hehe, sweet of you to say.
Most of my puppet shows were missions before. One wrong move and my target could escape, or worse.
But now, I can just relax and perform as I like. Feels kinda nice, to be honest.
Opportunities like this are rare. Duty calls, and I must answer. Sometimes, you might not be able to reach me.
I know you won't, but don't feel lonely when I'm away.
I pity the next criminal who gets in your way.
Fighting crime is everyone's duty in Huanglong.
You work hard to maintain the hard-won peace. Admirable.
Of course. After all, I've got... certain people to protect.
Well said. The safety of everyone is important to me.
Hehe, it feels good to have my efforts recognized.
Anyway, thanks for inviting me to the Moonlit Fair, {PlayerName}. I'm glad you did.
...Hello, {PlayerName}.
Hello.
Do you know me?
You're a household name in Jinzhou, and undoubtedly a strong warrior.
In the name of the Ghost Hounds, I present my respect to you.
If you ever need my blade, or require some... clean and discreet work done, feel free to come find me anytime.
Thanks, I'll consider it.
Thanks... but I don't think it's neccesary.
...Ready to assist at any time.
You know where to find me if you change your mind.
Hello, {PlayerName}!
Hi, Verina.
These riddles are so interesting, especially the ones about plants.
Mr. Xieyang must be really dedicated to this activity.
For sure he is.
He even set aside his favorite poetry for this.
Looks like the visitors are enjoying these riddles too.
I might try writing some myself to introduce more plants to everyone.
Good idea.
Just make sure they're not too difficult.
Understanding plants is crucial for an adventurer!
Don't worry, I'll make them easy and fun!
Watching these young men practice reminds me of my days as an apprentice.
Back then, all I cared about was strength and victory. Every drop of sweat I shed held such significance.
How about now?
Now? Hmm, I realize the world is much more complicated than I thought.
But if I had the chance to do it all over again, I wouldn't hesitate. After all, I learned a lot from the mistakes of my youth.
Hello, {PlayerName}. Here for the Moonlit Fair too?
Yeah.
Hehe, in that case, let's make sure we soak up all the fun.
So much to see and do at a grand festival like this. If you're not careful, these moments slip away like whispers in the wind…
You're right.
Can't believe how fast time's going!
Yes, so it makes perfect sense to enjoy the Moonlit Fair to the fullest.
If you're tired, maybe sneak in a little nap. Speaking of which… Hmm, I'm feeling a bit sleepy myself now…
Hello there. You must be {PlayerName}. Your name is often spoken of throughout Jinzhou.
Allow me to introduce myself. My name's Danjin. I'm currently visiting all the different regions of Huanglong.
Nice to meet you. What are you doing here?
Oh, I'm sending off a lantern.
Lantern?
Yes. You see these delicate lanterns here? People say they'll carry your wishes to a faraway land.
In that land, free from pain and evil, wishes will manifest and eventually return to us here.
A beautiful story.
Hope it's true.
Yes. Maybe you can try sending off a lantern yourself. You must have wishes to make, right?
{PlayerName}! Good to see you here!
Hey! What brings you here?
The Liondance Troupe performed on the Main Street earlier, on those Plum Blossom Poles, and the crowd loved it.
So I was thinking, why not do it again at the Moonlit Fair? Everyone could give it a try.
After all, festivals are all about having fun, right? The more, the merrier!
Have you ever met Xiuyi, {PlayerName}? He used to perform on the Main Street.
We're both in the Liondance Troupe. If you've seen his performances, you might recognize the Plum Blossom Pole dance.
We haven't celebrated the Moonlit Fair in so long. This year is our chance to set up a stall to promote our troupe's services.
Ahem... It's not just about business. It's also about introducing more people to the Liondance.
When I get some free time, I'll show you the dance myself! I need to keep my skills sharp.
Seek salvation from where all began... What's that supposed to mean?
Yeah, could you elaborate?
Is there anything else you'd like to know about Ragunna? I'll do my best to answer your questions.
About the Sentinel...
About the Order...
About the Carnevale...
About Common Echoes...
Our Sentinel embodies peace, justice, modesty, and mercy. They are the lord of the sky and seas, protector of the land.
They freed us from division and conflict, treating all equally and uniting us as one.
Legends say the Sentinel's breath becomes a gentle breeze, blessing Ragunna's ships and guiding them safely to their destinations.
Their radiant gaze pierces the darkness, illuminating the way forward. In reverence, people built lighthouses across the island.
The Sentinel never boasts of Their deeds but bestows miracles in subtle ways, as it is written.
"I am the gentle breeze that caresses you in green meadows. I am the unseen guardian as you walk in the valley of shadows."
"I am with you, steadfast and unwavering, from the past, through the present, and beyond the future."
The Order of the Deep is Ragunna's de facto authority, handling everything from city management and disputes to diplomacy.
We revere our Sentinel and act on Their behalf, overseeing all Common Echoes.
The La Guardia, the armed Echoes you saw before you entered the city, are part of the Order, working alongside us to keep Ragunna safe and orderly.
By the Sentinel's will, all citizens of Ragunna can use Common Echoes by simply registering their information with the Nexus.
If you face any issues during your stay, please report them to the Order. We are here to ensure your stay is comfortable.
The Carnevale is Rinascita's grandest annual festival, lasting seven days. Its theme is said to be "transcend the flesh to the divine realm."

The outer seas of Rinascita were once plagued by Tacet Discords and Lament occurrences, making sea travel impossible. Isolated on the island, the Ragunnesi found solace in the epics recited by limping poets and ballads sung by blind singers.
Stories from many lands were shared, forming a cradle of culture and art. The people mingled, dreaming of the world beyond, envisioning a different life for themselves.

These dreams came to life during the spring rite in honor of the Sentinel. People dressed in costumes, setting aside their positions and prejudices to come together for a grand parade—this is the origin of today's Carnevale.
Sounds fun to me.
Can I join it?
A stage will be set on the first day of the Carnevale. Wear a mask, and you can be part of the show.
The masks set people free, allowing everyone to shed their usual roles and revel in the celebration. We haven't had a Carnevale in many years, so this one is poised to be pretty special.
The streets will be alive with spectacular performances. Vendors from far and wide will showcase unique items.
Even without a mask, you can still take in the atmosphere and pick up some souvenirs.
In Rinascita, anyone can summon Common Echoes from the Nexus, whether they're a Resonator or not.
It has been modified by our Sentinel to allow Echoes to appear in physical forms.
However, not all Common Echoes are available for personal use. For example, La Guardia are armed guards managed exclusively by the Order.
Echoes affiliated with the Order are identified by their halo and respond only to its members, so please be aware of this.
That's it for now.
If you have any further questions, please feel free to ask. It's our duty as Acolytes to assist every visitor.
Okay, where to next?
Let's go get our money first.
The invitation mentioned we could pick it up from Averardo Bank.
Follow this road and you'll reach the Nexus.
To the Ragunnesi, the Sentinel is the Divinity, a holy beacon guiding our way.
We hold the Sentinel and all Their gifts in the highest reverence, especially the Echoes, which bear profound significance to both the Order and the people of Ragunna.
(...You've been hiccuping for a while. Do Echoes get indigestion as well?)
Wow... are they all Echoes?
Yes. Most newcomers to the city are amazed by the spectacle.
Now we're talking! This is what the Land of Echoes should look like! I thought all of Rinascita's Echoes were like that grumpy poker face we met at the docks...
...Hmm?
Eh... Hi! I'm Abby. Nice to meet ya!
Ah! Hello, I'm Phoebe! Nice to meet you, too.
Ah...
A little Echo holds up a gift and presents it to you.
They look different from the Echoes we just saw.
You don't like Echoes?
Yes, thanks to the Sentinel's blessing, most of the Common Echoes in Rinascita are friendly and approachable.

Welcome to Trattoria Margherita!
Ciao, Zani! Knocking off early today, huh?
Not really... still on duty.
Is that so? You seem alright, considering. So, what will it be today? The "Adios, Workdays" or the "Thank Goodness It's the Holiday" platter?
Here's your food. Enjoy!
(Wake up, Abby. Food's ready.)
*Sniffs* Oh what's that smell... it's so good!
You're... Abby, right?
Hi there... Gosh, this tastes amazing...
Zani. Nice to meet you.
Did not expect to see an Echo residing in a Resonator's body... Interesting.
Even someone from the Land of Echoes finds it surprising?
Have you ever seen Echoes like Abby？
Well, foreign Echoes aren't exactly a daily sight here.
...Can't say I have. Why do you sound like you're helping a lost kid find their home...
Told ya! I'm always the most special one! Mmm, this is so good!
Alright, let's dig in.
You will enjoy the food, of course. We Ragunnesi take pride in our food traditions.
For instance, never overcook seafood, or you'll ruin its natural taste. Always serve freshwater fish before sea fish, or its tender flavor will be masked.
I'd start with this appetizer. It complements the main course—hearty but not too heavy, perfect for those burning the midnight oil.
And don't forget the aperitif. As we say, "If you can't appreciate good wine, you don't deserve good water."
Now, try the Nectarwine from Egla Town. It's aged in oak barrels from the Fagaceae Peninsula, known as the "Harvest Spirit" or "Gocce di Divino" for its exceptional flavor.
So this is the Gocce di Divino.
(Raise the glass.)
To you, guests from afar...
...and my vacation that never seems to come.
Phew... nothing beats a good meal... Wait, what's the buzz over there?
Probably the Montelli's Echo show. They've been rehearsing for days, getting ready to perform it for the Sentinel at Carnevale.
Intrigued, are we? The formal event will be even more spectacular.
Watch out!
Command...
Unify...
Ascend...
Converge...
Thou hast come at last... I am the Imperator. Aid me, O Arbiter... that we may return the Lost unto the earthly realm!
The other one's gotten loose... Hey! It's getting away!
After it!
Are you okay?
The Vitreum Dancer suddenly lost control... Luckily, no one got hurt.
Actually...
You brief her on what you just saw.
Now that I think about it, the frequency vibration I sensed felt a lot like... empathy.
Empathy…?
Well, maybe telepathy? Not sure. It's hard to explain…
Telepathy… Yes, according to legend, the Sentinel speaks directly into the mind of the Laureate. Could that be what happened?

So the "Imperator" is the Sentinel. But who's the "Lost"? Plus, it said it needs your help, but… a Sentinel shouldn't need to ask for help, wouldn't ya say? Eh, something's not adding up, what a headache...
We need to learn how the Sentinel talks to people.
That Vitreum Dancer was trying to tell me something…
(The Sentinel has countless ways to send a message, and through the Order is apparently the most convenient one, but why did they go through all the trouble...?)
(Maybe I'm wrong. Maybe calling for help was the only option?)
(With that message left on Tethys… Could the Sentinel here be in a situation similar to Jué's?)
(But it seems like the locals haven't laid eyes on their Sentinel. Everything feels off. That Echo might be our only lead right now.)
Was the Echo performance hosted by the Montellis?
...I see.
Sorry to keep you waiting. That was Mr. Alberto from the Montelli family. Also my employer.
Come to think of it, that Echo... it was looking at you. It seemed to target you.
You've got sharp eyes.
Hmph, I won't pry into my ward's privacy. I only remember what I need to get the job done. Anything else I accidentally overhear just slips my mind.
My orders are to guard and to guide. I do my job. Nothing more, nothing less. So if you want to investigate, I'll stick with you until you're done.
Thank you.
You're very professional!
Don't thank me, thank the family who hired me. Their generosity is beyond what you can imagine.
Thank you for trusting in my abilities.
So, what's our next move?
Let's find that Vitreum Dancer first.
It was complete chaos, but I spied the direction it fled… We can try our luck at the Pioneer Association.
I know someone there whose Forte might help us uncover some details we missed.
Sure, let's head to the Pioneer Association first.
Dear Sentinel above…
Excuse me, do you know anything about the Echo that lost control?
Oh, the Sentinel is in a great rage! They are warning us, reminding us of our follies.
We shouldn't have forgotten... Ten years ago, it was our unbridled indulgence that brought about divine punishment!
We should have heeded Primus Fenrico's words…
What do you mean?
What happened ten years ago?

Oh, dear visitor from afar, you may not know. Ten years ago, the Carnevale angered the Sentinel and brought forth divine punishment. Primus Fenrico foresaw the shadow beneath the revelry and halted its spread!
Simply put, many terrible accidents happened during that Carnevale, like Echoes losing control. Since then, the Primus ordered the Carnevale to stop.
Most Ragunnesi don't like to talk about that tragedy, so it's understandable you haven't heard of it.
Echoes are messengers of the Sentinel. They lost control and attacked people because they were corrupted, reflecting our transgressions against the Sentinel!
This year, the Order has approved the Carnevale. We will return to our traditions… Dear visitor, please join us in praising the Sentinel. Only then can our misguided souls be forgiven…
How will that Echo be handled?

It may be a divine blessing, but it has committed an assault against the Sentinel's people. The corrupted will be purified under the holy light of the Genesis Nexus. As for the one that escaped, the Order will retrieve it as soon as possible to prevent further harm.
Here's to a world of discoveries and wonders! Welcome to the Pioneer Association!
Ms. Zani! It's been some time! Have you finally decided to join us?
No, I'm here for something else. This is Mr. Fulmine from the Pioneer Association.
Oh, hello! You've brought a new friend! Pleasure to meet you. I'm Fulmine, head of the Wutherium Film Studio under the Pioneer Association in Ragunna. How should I address you?
Nice to meet you, I'm {PlayerName}.
Your name rings a bell… Oh! Y-you're the legendary Rover?!
Savior from a foreign land, the dark thunderbolt streaking across the world… I've longed to meet you! By the Sentinel, let me seize this extraordinary moment!
They're just titles, not worth bragging about.
Let's get down to business.
Wait, you're actually some kind of celebrity?

Ha, indeed {Male=he;Female=she} is. Ragunna's routes have only recently opened, so {Male=his;Female=her} feats haven't made it here yet. Should you perform a great deed, trust me to ensure your name echoes throughout Ragunna!
I had a nagging feeling I've met someone important... But let's get back to what matters.
We're here to ask a favor. We're investigating a Vitreum Dancer who caused a scene around Trattoria Margherita.
It fled in this direction, and we're wondering if you can recreate the scene for us.
Ah, I know the one you mean. Saw it streaking out of the city with a few Order fellows in tow.
As for recreating the scene… C-MOSS, my friend, it's time to get to work!
Hmph.
Alright, where is it? My memory of that Vitreum Dancer… Ah, I've found it!
Mr. Fulmine's Forte is Celluloid Chronicle. He can convert events into film, recording all that happens within a span of time.
His partner, C-MOSS, uses a "Memory Projector" Forte to show these captured moments.
There it is! Take a look!
So it did leave the city… This complicates matters. The area beyond is too vast to search effectively. Plus, Tacet Discords are hampering our investigation. We can't start searching just yet.
(Abby, can you sniff it out?)
(…What do you think I am? Not a chance! And I'm too sleepy to help, just wake me if there's any progress…)
I'm sorry. I can only record what is plain to the eye.
Don't be hard on yourself, Mr. Fulmine. You've been a tremendous help. At least we're not flying blind anymore. But {PlayerName}, we need a new plan.
Can you think back carefully?
Was anything unusual?
…Give me a moment. Ah, yes! Look at this!
How could this be...
His garb suggests he's from the Montelli family. Could they be involved in this turmoil?
It's too soon to tell.
He wore an unusual mask.
Indeed. But it's rare to wear a mask before the Carnevale. He must have wanted to hide his face.
Speaking of, the mask is not the typical Montelli style, and wearing it now is unusual.
With their eagerness to promote Reserved Terminals, the Montellis would be the last to invite trouble now. If he's tied to the disturbance...
Then perhaps we should seek Ms. Nyarla's expertise. She's known for her intricate masks, and this one seems custom.
Good idea, but nobles are secretive. Direct questions might lead to unwanted attention.
I have a plan.
I'll arrange for a custom-made mask myself.
Ah-ha, Excellent. Let's make for the Masked Reverie.
Thank you for your assistance, Mr. Fulmine.
Good luck!
We're here to ask a favor. We're investigating a Vitreum Dancer who caused a scene around Trattoria Margherita.
Has the perfume, compact, and jewelry set arrived?
Yes, they have. Would you like them now, or shall we deliver them to your residence before tonight?
Tonight… No, I'll take them now.
…Of course. I'll have someone fetch them immediately. It won't take long.
Welcome to Masked Reverie. From masks to elegant garments and splendid stage props, we craft it all to order. How may I help you today, my dear?
...Who's there?
Hehe, so eager to skip the pleasantries, are we? I'm right here. Do I seem invisible, or are you simply ignoring me? I am... right behind you.
Madame Nyarla, I saw you. Your mask gave you away.
Hehe, don't spoil my secret so soon. It's not every day I get such a charming visitor.
Besides, only by "hiding" oneself can the true beauty of a mask be revealed, don't you think?
But scaring the guests is just your twisted sense of humor, isn't it?

I hope this didn't bother you. <ano=Ombra Elusiva>Invisibility</ano> is Madame Nyarla's Forte. Madame Nyarla, this is the distinguished guest invited by the Montellis, {PlayerName}. {Male=He;Female=She} is very interested in Carnevale masks.
Yes, I'd like a custom-made mask.
You elaborate on the mask design you saw in Fulmine's memory to Nyarla.
Hmm? That's quite a detailed description, even covering the smallest intricacies... I admit, I'm surprised.
Not long ago, we customized a mask just like the one you've described.
If the Carnevale is a dream shared by all Ragunnesi, then a well-crafted mask is the key to it.
When faces are hidden, souls break free from the shackles of everyday life. That's why we love balls and plays, eagerly awaiting the Carnevale.
Masks liberate our spirits. We believe they reveal what lies within. It is our honor to help our customers express their innermost selves.
So, are you certain you want to custom order this particular mask?
Well…
(She's suspicious... Will I be forced to reveal my hand...?)
That's a very fine mask.
If I remember correctly, the one Mr. Gilberto picked up last week looked very similar. If it's your first mask, a unique design might be more fitting?
You have an impressive memory.
I'll be on my way now.
Ahem, we spotted a fellow on the street with a mask that caught our eye… I didn't expect it to be Mr. Gilberto from the Fisalia family.
The Fisalia family?
Yes, they're one of the oldest families in Rinascita. Their ancestors once ignited a war here, but they were defeated and driven out of Ragunna.
The Fisalias are a mixed lot—while some hold honor, others bring disgrace to the name.
They show new ambitions. Lately, they've taken to more prominent roles in the city, flaunting their mining ventures and acting with increasing arrogance.
Speaking of which, I revised Monsieur Gilberto's mask twenty-three times…
I see why it's left a deep impression…
Anyway, given your standing with the Montellis, I'd advise against this design.
Why's that?
Rumor has it the Montellis plan to push for Reserved Echoes at the Carnevale. It's stirred tension with the Fisalia family. Best avoid any association.
That incident with the Montelli's Echoes going berserk... Unfortunate timing. Who knows how this will affect their promotion.
I see…
So, the trail leads to the Fisalia family.
Thank you for the lead, Madame Nyarla. Oh, and we will reconsider the mask's design. Thank you for your time.
Hehe, you're too polite, Mademoiselle Zani. You're my special guest, after all.
Isn't it interesting how a small mask can both hide and reveal? I can't wait to see the "face" you'll choose to show.
I look forward to your next visit. This splendid reverie is always open for you.
Nyarla

Hey, no sneakin' bites! Well, maybe a nibble, but leave some for Jiyan, okay?
Oh, it's you, {PlayerName}.
Are you here for "Swim, Gulpuff, Swim"?
What? Oh, not really… So this is the stall for that Gulpuff game? My apologies. My eyes aren't as sharp as they used to be.
My son is a Resonator. He might like this, I guess...
Your son?
Yes. He's a Midnight Ranger. They gave him a few day off. When he comes back, I plan to visit the Moonlit Fair with him.
Haha, I'm sure he'll have a lot of fun.
Ha, Antonio, surely you know how things work here. It's always about who pays more. Is there a problem?
Do you Fisalias even honor contracts?
Ha, since when do Montellis fret over such trivialities?
Instead of whining, maybe focus on cleaning up the mess your Echoes caused. Ha ha ha...
The Fisalia man walks away, leaving Antonio fuming.
And you are…?
Greetings, Sir Antonio. I'm Zani from the Averardo Bank.
This {Male=gentleman;Female=lady} here is a distinguished guest of your family, {PlayerName}. {Male=He;Female=She} was attacked by a rogue Vitreum Dancer while dining, and we're investigating.
Ah, so you're… Please accept my apologies! It's a relief to see you unscathed. We're as puzzled as you are about the Echo's behavior.
It's okay, but there's something else I want to know.
Miss Carlotta asked me to hold nothing back, so ask away.
Tell me about Reserved Terminals and Reserved Echoes.
Well, before I do, a little context first.
In Ragunna, the Order controls all Terminals for Echo use. They store Echoes in their Data Bank and only grant access after thorough screening.
Only a select few Resonators are permitted to carry a Reserved Terminal.
You see, most Ragunnesi rely on the Genesis Nexus and Common Echoes, with little need for the special access types.
However, things have changed with Ragunna opening up to the greater Solaris. People want to travel, making Reserved Terminals essential for safety outside the Order's reach.
You see why demand is up. The Montellis saw an opportunity and started to develop them. After all, necessity is the mother of invention, hm?
It should be celebrated, but some think we disrespect the Order's authority or even the Sentinel by doing this. The path forward has been... resistant.
Heh, if you ask me, I suspect the Fisalia family has been spreading slanders about us.
We back the Carnevale to showcase our Reserved Terminals to the people. It's our chance to prove their worth and attract investors.
And the Fisalia family has been standing in your way?
Sigh… The Fisalias have coerced our miners to break their contracts, seizing our largest vein and cutting off our Terminal supply.
And it gets worse. With the Carnevale nearing and our Echoes malfunctioning, the family's Executor might have to step in.
The Carnevale is at risk. While we hope it brings fortune, the festival itself is what truly matters to us, just like the rest of Ragunna.
We must uncover why the Echo lost control. We cannot let the Fisalias use this to tarnish our reputation any further!
I can help you with the investigation.
That would be good for us, but it hardly seems proper to involve our esteemed guest in our troubles...
I have my own reasons.

Ah, understood. Thank you! But I'm afraid we can't spare any of our own to assist you. Rest assured, the Montellis are always generous. Here's an advance. Once the matter is resolved, you'll be well-rewarded.
Take it. In Ragunna, if you want help, you must offer a reward and one only declines a reward when they refuse to help.
Yes, that's right. Please accept it. If that's all, I must be on my way. There are many matters to attend to...
Antonio departs with a sigh. The weight on his shoulders seems heavier than before.
From what we know, the Montelli family has no motive for such incidents. They've been anticipating the Carnevale's arrival.

But the Fisalia family is another story. They've been against the celebration from the start, perhaps they could be behind everything? But I don't understand, what could they hope to gain by stopping the Carnevale?
The mystery continues.
Maybe it's related to the Sentinel?
Why do I feel like I've gotten myself into something above my pay grade…
You... have a hunch, hm?
They say the Fisalias have been seen frequenting the Cathedral of Mercury. They must be in league with the Order. How else would they dare to seize our mine so boldly?
Only investigation brings us answers.
Ciao, we need to get to the Cathedral of Mercury.
Got it! Please, come aboard.
We are now in the Fisalia Residencies territory. We should... Wait, look over there…
He looks like the man we saw in Mr. Fulmine's memory. Isn't that Gilberto?
Let's follow him.
Ah, more seekers. What brings you to these halls?
We're here to visit Sir Gilberto.
Sir Gilberto...? Oh, Gilberto from the Fisalia family.
A pious soul, frequently here in prayer. But not today, it seems.
I've heard whispers of you. An Acolyte mentioned your desire to meet the Sentinel. I assume you must be interested in following Their path.
But I don't think you truly understand the significance of the Carnevale. Allow me to explain.
I'm interested.
If you must.
You've probably heard about the connection between the Carnevale and the Sentinel, but do you know why the Carnevale hasn't been held for years?
I have a general understanding.
Is it because of the accident a decade ago?
In the last Carnevale, a sea fog shrouded the entire city. Echoes paraded like lost souls, a dragon roared above, and a beast in the sea stirred up towering waves…
It was sent as punishment and warning against our indulgence and division.
This is our Primus, Fenrico, the Enlightened One.
Amidst that chaos, he stepped forward and quelled the Sentinel's wrath.
Ragunna's greatness was forged from its battles with the sea. It inspired a common goal in all our hearts.
Without everyone working together, land cannot be cultivated, islands cannot unite, and dams cannot be built. A nation's strength lies in its unity.
You see, this is why we preach restraint and control over our desires. Only through rituals can we strengthen our resolve, our unity!
This is why we must banish those who stray from the right path and impose restrictions on those who threaten the common good.
We've dedicated ourselves to this cause.
It seems like you disapprove of holding the Carnevale.
Hehe, you misunderstand me.
I simply mean that the Order's actions are always made with great deliberation.
Guided by the Sentinel, we strive to unite and lead the people. We hope to build a kingdom on high, a land of the blessed… As it was in the beginning, and ever shall be.
I trust you'll have faith in the Order's judgment. We handle all matters that come to our attention.
...What did you say? How could the Montelli family...
Forgive me, I must attend to pressing matters.
If you have further questions, seek answers in the cathedral. We are always open to those in search of truth.
But I remind you to keep your distance from the sacred relics and honor our customs. Otherwise, we will have no choice but to address any act of disrespect.
What's got him so rattled that he'd leave us like that?
He's hiding something. We saw Gilberto enter the cathedral with our own eyes. He couldn't have vanished into thin air.
Could there be a hidden chamber or secret passage within the cathedral?
Now that you mention it, something's not sitting right.
I didn't expect the Order to have such a grand garden hidden here.
But where could Gilberto have gone? Let's split up and see what we can find.
Step forward.
What burdens weigh upon your soul?
I carry no burdens.
Bless me, for I have transgressed.
Are you certain? Search your heart.
Truly, I have nothing to confess.
What do you wish to confess?
I sleep too much, eat too much, and squander my days in idleness.
May the Sentinel grant your absolution. Go in peace, and transgress no more.
Now, I shall open the path to your ascension.
The weather is so good today. You're my Jewel Boba!
Huh? Hahaha, so I'm a boba tea to you?
Sure, let's go have some boba tea then.
Jewel Boba has released a limited-edition boba tea for the Moon-Chasing Festival. Let's try it out.
Your plan for the Moon-Chasing Festival events was so perfect.
It's all because you gave me such good suggestions.
It's because you had such good ideas in the first place.
Wait, someone is coming.
Hello, can I help you with anything?
Were you guys talking about the Moon-Chasing Festival?
Nothing.
Yes, the Moon-Chasing Festival is an important festival here in Huanglong.
It is when families in Huanglong come together to celebrate their reunion and enjoy drinks under the moon.
The Magistrate said she hoped everyone would have a joyful Moon-Chasing Festival this year.
So, besides taking care of the Moon-Chasing Festival event registrations, I also volunteered to help with the event planning, hoping to make the festival even better for everyone.
Luckily, Dingfeng shared a ton of great ideas with me, and everyone really loved the improved plan.
We all just want everyone to have a great time!
I told you that the Liondance Troupe's Liondance would be popular. I've heard there's been a massive crowd lining up at the Plum Blossom Pole stall at the Moonlit Fair lately!
Was it also your idea to set up the stall?
Not exactly. I just mentioned it when I was chatting with everyone in the Liondance Troupe.
I suggested that they could let the audience experience the Liondance from a different perspective, and they gladly accepted.
It's thanks to their careful and detailed planning that the event is doing so well right now.
Sigh, the weather looks bad. It feels like it's going to rain soon...
It won't stop us from chatting though. Want to do something together later?
Shall we go to the Moonlit Fair? I've heard it's very lively there, with fun things to do.
A new day means another day of hard work!
The city really does get a lot more crowded during the Moon-Chasing Festival...
I need to be more vigilant to keep the people safe. That's what Chixia said!
Ah... I'm really a bit worn out after a full day's work.
After work, I'll grab a bite at Climbing Flower Eatery, then head to the teahouse to chat with the boss before...
Oh, right! I need to watch the Hero Play. How could I forget that?
I heard that the special performances for the Moon-Chasing Festival have been announced. I've got to check them out as soon as I'm off work!
Hehe, the Moon-Chasing Festival just isn't complete without reuniting with your loved ones...
My grandson who's been away at school is back home!
I'll look for those missing stuff later. After all, it's just more important to spend time with him.
He doesn't get to come back often, so I'm going to make lots of Loong Whiskers Crisp for him and take him out so we can enjoy the festival together.
I'm so glad he still cares about me and came back just to see me... Hehe... This year's festival is simply perfect.
Hey there! Be sure to check out the lanterns on the street when you get the chance!
Hehe, all the lanterns at the Moon-Chasing Festival have been improved based on my idea!
I experimented for ages, but it wasn't until I studied the devices from the Ministry of Development that I found the inspiration I needed to create a special exterior for the lanterns.
The people at the Ministry of Development acknowledged my skills and actually put my little invention to use! They even said that one day I would be even more amazing than them!
And now these lanterns can withstand any weather without getting blown over all the time!
People might not notice this detail, but I know my invention was a huge success! Hahaha, I'm so happy!
The winding river flows so free, by cypress tall and evergreen. With a basket on my back, I return home to the joy that awaits...
What are you singing?
Hehe, this is a folk song from my hometown. I've loved singing it since I was a young man living in there.
For some reason, I can't seem to find my strength unless I sing a few lines while working. If I finish my work early, I can head home sooner to celebrate the festival with my family.
This is my tenth year here in Jinzhou. I left my hometown to come here because of a disaster that struck, so this year is especially special to me and my family.
I really want to spend more time with my family during this year's Moon-Chasing Festival. Well, I've rested enough, so it's time to get back to work.
With a basket on my back, I return home to the joy that awaits...

Happy Moon-Chasing Festival! The Moonlit Fair will be held in Taoyuan Vale this year, and special performances will take place at the theater on the east side of the city. Make sure you don't go to the wrong place!
I'm here to help if you can't find the venue for the Moon-Chasing Festival's events!
Your delivery is so smooth.
With the festival upon us, more and more people are coming in and out of Jinzhou every day because of the festival, and naturally, more people are asking for directions too.
Many people visiting Jinzhou for the first time don't know their way around and end up asking for directions. Well, I'm usually the first person they come across.
I've repeated the same things so many times that I know them by heart now, hahaha.
Oh, right! This is your first time celebrating the festival in Jinzhou, isn't it? Let me know if you need any help finding a venue!
Thanks, I'll definitely ask you if I need any help.
Great! I hope you have a good time!
This is wonderful. With all the leave I saved up by working overtime, I can finally spend some time with my baby now.
I bought him the toys he asked me to get him ages ago and took him to eat his favorite foods...
Hehe... I haven't seen him this happy in a long time...
I should take him to see the lanterns again tomorrow. I need to make it up to him after letting him down during last year's Moon-Chasing Festival.
After that... I'll find a way to spend more time with him.
Combat isn't just about strength. You need skills and wisdom too when facing enemies on the battlefield.
You there, looking to put on some training? Good training keeps you sharp. The enemies won't go easy on you out there.
Greetings.
What can you teach me?
Combat skills and tactics. Or anything you're willing to learn, as long as I have it.
Practicality is key on the battlefield. Years of combat have taught me that. If you want fancy tricks, go elsewhere.
I'll teach you how to survive, and how to win.
Is surviving more important?
Is winning more important?
Absolutely. But let me be clear, I am not condoning cowardice.
I will give my life for Huanglong anytime, but I've also witnessed too many pointless deaths.
I do not want to see our new recruits make the same mistakes. My purpose is to teach you how to avoid them and give you a better chance at life.
Do not rush blindly into battle like those before you. You deserve more than that.
While winning is important, the battlefield is constantly changing.
Avoid rushing for success and making costly mistakes. Focus on improving your skills and knowing what actions to take.
Remember, you have many years ahead of you. You should prioritize staying alive.
Hello, Hello! I'm here! Hello?
Hi? Hello? I'm RIGHT HERE, can you see me?
Excuse me? See me here?

A set of paintbrushes Zhezhi purchased during her first solo shopping trip as a child, after fumbling for words in front of the shop owner. Wherever Zhezhi went, so did these paintbrushes, recording her artistic growth along the way. Though now too old and fragile to use, Zhezhi still regards them as a source of encouragement, handling them with great care.

A luxurious birdcage left empty for a long time.

As a reward for Zhezhi's obedience in using her Forte to paint and help save the family business, her parents bought her a pet bird as a surprise. Every day, Zhezhi watched the bird beat its wings against the cage until it was exhausted. After much hesitation, one day she boldly defied her parents and released the bird from its captivity.

After her parents disappeared, Zhezhi sold off the family's remaining belongings, keeping only the birdcage as a memento. Whenever she looked at it, she didn't see the bars but the bird that had long since flown free.

New desserts, art exhibit tickets, trips to new cities... Struggling to pay off her family's debt while barely making ends meet, Zhezhi took the habit of jotting down things she wanted to buy or do on a wish list. She often checks this list, but can only fulfill one or two of these smaller wishes on rare occasions when she has a bit of extra money.

Xiangli Yao's work ID card reads "Xiangli Yao, Researcher, Huaxu Academy," neatly printed. 

It took Xiangli Yao an extra year to wear this simple, plain card with a built-in ID chip on his chest compared to his peers at the Academy—a year ago, he had chosen not to take the Academy exam, instead leaving Jinzhou in search of answers to life's deeper questions. A teenager at the time, he stood at a crossroads, uncertain whether to follow in his parents' footsteps or forge his own path. However, a year later, his heart led him down a path entirely different from theirs...

On his first day as a researcher, Xiangli Yao placed his ID card neatly on his desk, opened the window, and let the bustling sounds of Jinzhou City drift in.

"Huaxu Academy. It's a nice place."

Affectionately named Beep-Boop, this lovable machine eventually found a home with one of Yao's lucky classmates. From that point on, Xiangli Yao devoted much of his free time to crafting models, robots, and other fascinating gadgets for his friends.
Whether in school or now at the Academy, Yao's generosity in dedicating time and effort to those around him remains a constant. His selfless nature has always been, and continues to be, an integral part of who he is.

The girl proudly presented her painting to her mother, eager to share her achievement. The woman, absorbed in selecting jewelry to wear, stole a fleeting glance at the artwork. "Impressive, Zhezhi," she murmured with a brief smile. Delighted by the praise, the girl inched closer. "The people in this one are—" Her words faltered as her mother turned, absorbed in wardrobe choices, oblivious to her daughter's attempt at connection. "Well done. Now, why don't you paint a few more before the guests arrive?" Zhezhi blinked, at a loss for words. Her mother grew impatient, sighing as she marched Zhezhi to the door. "Buy whatever supplies you need, dear. The price doesn't matter, we can afford it. Now, I need to dress. Be a good girl. Off you go.” As the door closed, Zhezhi stared at it, wanting to say more but unable to find the courage to voice the sinking feeling in her chest.

Later that evening, Zhezhi, dressed to impress, nervously clutched her skirt in the corner seat, silent amidst the bustling room of guests. The woman noted Zhezhi's unease, the sight of it triggering memories of their family's past struggles and humble beginnings. She strode forward, taking Zhezhi's hand and leading her into the center of attention. "Didn't you know? Zhezhi was gifted from the day she was born. Her paintings were chosen for exhibitions even before we hired a tutor." With a painted smile, she mimicked the grace of the upper class. "Would you care for a painting too? Zhezhi can finish one in a day." Zhezhi shrank inwardly, wishing to disappear, only to be thrust forward. "Show everyone your skills, Zhezhi." All eyes turned to her, leaving Zhezhi trembling, unable to paint a single stroke.

Later, as the mansion fell silent, Zhezhi gathered her courage again. Holding the day's painting, she approached her parents' bedroom door. Just before knocking, she overheard their conversation inside.
"Did you know? That painting sold for 400,000 Credits today. With this money, we can fulfill the paused order."
"Right. Are the paintings for the guests ready for this weekend?"
"Not yet. Zhezhi mentioned wanting to go to the theater. That girl, always seeking diversions, never thinking about what's best for this family..."

Zhezhi looked down at the happy family in the painting, her grip tightening until it crumpled, distorting her mother and father's faces.
"...I'm sorry."

Zhezhi realized something was amiss in her painting only after heading out for a sketch. As she took in the idyllic countryside, a new idea struck her like a ray of sunlight. Glancing around to make sure she was alone, she stretched her arms, and for a moment, let go of her parents' demands.

As her bare feet met the grass, its prickly, cool softness awakened a sense of nature's healing vitality. She broke into an impulsive run, shedding worries about upholding the refined image her family demanded. A distant voice abruptly interrupted her frolic.

"Hey, who are you? What are you doing in our field?"

Startled, Zhezhi immediately looked down at her feet in embarrassment. Realizing she was trespassing on private property, she apologized as she tried to leave. "I'm so sorry! I came here to paint. I didn't know this was someone's field..."

The girl laughed, seeing the panic on Zhezhi's face. "Don't worry! These veggies are tough. You don't need to run!" She laughed as she continued gathering the vegetables with her sickle. "A painter, huh? That's different..." Zhezhi hesitated for a moment, seeing the girl hard at work. "Let me help you with that..." The girl met Zhezhi's eyes with a twinkle. "Sure! Thanks for offerin'! Here, use this sickle, I'll go grab another one!"

Zhezhi stared in confusion at the sickle promptly shoved into her hands. But she soon squatted down among the tall vegetables, mimicking the farm girl's movements. "Wait, wait. You won't get anywhere doin' it like that. Here, lemme show ya!"

Under the hot sun, the two girls worked together to harvest the field until they reached its end. Exhausted, they lay under a tree to rest. Zhezhi forgot about the mud on her shoes and the dirt on her expensive dress, lost in the joy of spending time with her new friend. The carefree laughter between them filled her heart with ease and brought a true smile to her lips.

The mood was suddenly cut by a sharp voice. Zhezhi turned to see her mother watching, her eyes squinted in anger. Zhezhi could see her disdain for her new friend. Sprinting to her feet, she ran to explain and apologize, transforming back into the child her parents demanded she be.

A few days later, the girl received a scroll. She unrolled it carefully, gasping softly at the sight. The painting showed her and Zhezhi in the sprawling fields of her home, picking vegetables together.

A letter fell from the painting.

"I'm sorry I didn't say goodbye. I had so much fun harvesting the field with you! The sickle, the sun beating down on us, my sore hands... It made me realize what my paintings were missing. This is my best work, and it's for you! I hope you like it! Maybe next week, I can sneak out to help again."

Reading the letter made the girl smile, but she couldn't help being confused by Zhezhi's last line.

Next week? Did she think the vegetables would grow back that fast?

Zhezhi stood a short distance from the art supply store, eyeing the tall, gruff-looking clerk who was frowning and scribbling something in a notepad. She hesitated, taking a few steps back.

"Maybe I should go to another store..." The thought had barely crossed her mind before she dismissed it. "But... this is the only store with the latest supplies..."

Zhezhi stopped her pacing and pulled out a coin, a habit she had developed for situations like this. She tossed it into the air, caught it, and thought to herself, "The usual. Heads, I go in. Tails, I come back another time..."

She slowly opened her palm, peeking briefly before quickly squeezing her hand shut. "No, wait. Best two out of three."

The coin went up and came back down. "Heads again," she sighed.

Clutching the coin tightly, Zhezhi took a deep breath and steeled herself. "Oh well, I guess this is a sign. I can't keep running away."

Taking a deep breath to gather her courage, she marched to the store and pushed the door open with all her might. The sharp ring of the bell above the door sent her nerves into overdrive. She rushed forward with a lowered gaze and blurted out the lines she'd rehearsed countless times, as if her tongue was on fire.

"H-Hello! I'd like to buy some new paint! Six cans of Malachite Green No.3, five cans of Azurite Blue No.3, five cans of Vermilion, three cans of Indigo, three cans of Ochre, three cans of Gamboge, and two cans of Golden Yellow. Thank you!"

Relieved to have finished her sentence smoothly without a single pause, Zhezhi inhaled deeply to catch her breath. When she looked up, she met the eyes of a surprised-looking clerk who was just coming out from the back room.

"Hello there. How can I help you?" The clerk's gentle voice was a stark contrast to what Zhezhi had imagined.

Realizing that her earlier words had gone unheard, she froze. "Uhh... I..."

"Are you looking for any specific art supplies?"

"P-Paint... I..."

"The new releases? They're quite popular."

"N-No... I think I..."

"No rush. Feel free to look around."

Zhezhi, sweating and nervous, walked over to a shelf. "O-Okay..."

The clerk's detailed and professional introduction of the products gradually eased Zhezhi's nerves. She relaxed and was able to name what she wanted, even chatting about her painting.

"If you're using White Jade Paper, these new products would pair nicely."

"Perfect, that's just what I needed. I'll take these too."

Walking out of the store with her new supplies, Zhezhi felt light and confident.

"I guess I can talk to people when I'm not feeling anxious. Next time... I'll try it without flipping the coin. Maybe it'll work out again..."

Unsuspecting, Zhezhi was thrown out of her home, her belongings strewn across the courtyard like discarded memories. As she gazed at the mess, it dawned on her that she herself was just another discarded item, abandoned by her parents like the rest.

Desperate for shelter, she first sought out places familiar to her. But those once kind and welcoming turned cold when they learned of her plight. Behind their polite excuses, Zhezhi saw the distaste in their eyes as they pointed her to an old hotel on a street corner.

The hotel's decaying corridors teemed with unfamiliar fights and loud arguments. Sitting on the bed, she wrapped herself tightly in the musty covers, eyes fixed on the flimsy wooden door barricaded by a table. She longed for sleep, hoping to wake from this nightmare, yet fear kept her awake, afraid the door would shatter if she closed her eyes.

Her descent from luxury to hardship stretched endlessly, each day a painful reminder. The staggering figures of her parents' debt seemed to flicker across the ceiling in the dim light of her windowless room. Her hands, covered in worn bandages, trembled from painting non-stop for two days, but she dared not rest.

"It's a big order... I can't mess this up," she murmured, her weary eyes blurring the landscapes on her canvas.

Suddenly, harsh shouts pierced the night, jarring her awake from an unintended nap at her desk. She stumbled to the door, slipping on something wet at her feet.

Aching from the fall, she stood nervously at the door of her leaking room, apologizing repeatedly to her neighbors. The biting cold seeped through her wet clothes, and the neighbors' complaints echoed through the thin walls. She stared at her painting, ruined by the water, and a heavy sigh escaped her lips, compressing the room's thin air, almost crushing her fragile frame.

Zhezhi's exhausted figure stood motionless in the cold puddle. After a long pause, a faint light glowed in the cramped room. With paint-stained fingertips, she scrolled through her Terminal, "First, shut off the water valve... then replace the damaged parts..."

She had made a habit of looking up solutions for life's unexpected challenges. 

"I think I've got it... I'll give it a try..."

She waded through the water, slowly making her way to the source of the problem.

"This painting is a reflection of me. Everyone needs to see at first glance that it's an expensive masterpiece."

"If this is the best you can do, I'll take it. But only at half the price."

The client's words echoed in Zhezhi's mind. She wandered the streets with her bundle of paintings, feeling a sense of numbness begin to creep over her as the festive preparations around her started to fade into the background. It wasn't until she tripped, her paintings scattering, that she snapped out of her daze. Without bothering to look for her glasses, at first she scrambled to pick up her work. But as the wind blew some paintings out of reach, she stopped, staring for a moment before deciding to let them go.

"Forget it, they're lousy anyway... What's the point of having them back..."

She dropped the remaining paintings in her arms, letting them fall. Lost in her thoughts, she didn't notice someone stopping in front of her.

A stranger picked up her paintings and glasses, handing them back to her.

"Did you paint these? I've never seen art like that. Remarkable."

Zhezhi, stunned by the compliment, could only accept the outstretched paintings and watch the stranger turn and leave alongside their companions, disappearing into the night.

She fumbled to put on her glasses to catch a clearer glimpse of who it was, but all she caught was a distant silhouette.

"Someone complimented me... "
"They had nothing to gain from it. It was just... simple praise for my paintings."

The stranger's words, simple yet sincere, pierced through her paintings to reach her heart. For the first time ever, it was as if someone saw her creative intentions. It was like a sudden beam of light scattering the dark clouds that had long weighed her down, bringing a sense of warmth long overdue.

Zhezhi stared in the direction the stranger had vanished, clutching her paintings tightly. Until...

"Excuse me... Hello?"

Days later, a familiar voice startled her out of her thoughts as she searched for the perfect spot to paint.

"Don't worry, we're just here to chat."

Zhezhi looked up and saw a pair of golden eyes. The memory of that night rushed back—this was the person who had complimented her work, their voice free of the pretense she had grown to despise from everyone else. That voice had given her strength when she had been ready to give it all up.

The warmth from that night returned, filling a world of pale grey with color once more.

Years later, I found myself standing at that door again.

The Xiangli family had always been a star in Jinzhou's journalistic circles. Back then, doing a piece on the family was considered an honor, and indeed, their scientific heritage continues to produce admirable accomplishments. The last time I stood on this doorstep, I was still a rookie, eager for recognition, and the Xianglis helped me with just that by allowing me to take their family portrait. A piece that ticked all the boxes.

The photo won me a small award and secured my job.

As the door opened, I looked down to see a boy with bright and clear eyes looking back at me. I flashed my press badge, and he ushered me inside.

Xiangli Yao, the "Son of the Genius" and "Paragon's Descendant." His father's brilliance had turned heads across Jinzhou, and his mother's perseverance saved the lives of countless children in the city.

This very house once drew the attention of many, and it remains that way to this day.

I prided myself on conducting interviews, but this young boy seemed more comfortable than I was. Xiangli Yao, like his parents, possessed a natural eloquence, his demeanor gentle and poised. The interview flowed smoothly, and after setting aside my notebook, he offered me a cup of tea. I thanked him, but he shook his head.

"I should thank you for visiting because of my parents," Xiangli Yao smiled, "I've heard a thing or two about what's been happening."

Jinzhou, with its vast lands and rich resources, is not without its share of discord.

The Xianglis had done me a favor in the past, one I felt compelled to repay, both professionally and personally by making sure their son was okay. Xiangli Yao smiled wistfully, his expression hinting at a memory relived. "My parents are always busy with work, so I'm glad someone remembers them. Your reports capture their moments, research results, words spoken, and many other details that I didn't even know about... When I read those news and interviews, I feel like I get to know them better."

I hesitated for a moment but still went on to ask.

"Do you think... it's unfair? That perhaps your parents should have spent more time with their child?"

"They both have their passions, and it's the same for me. I'm happy they're doing what they love."

"...Is that so."

I took a deep breath and prepared to leave, but Xiangli Yao asked me to stay. I forgot the exact reason he gave. However, I'm sure it must've been a good one. Xiangli Yao had a way with words that made refusing his hospitality difficult. I only remember having another cup of warm tea and continuing to chat for a while before finally taking my leave.

As I reached for the door, the boy remarked with a straight face, "If there's anything you want to confirm, it's best to do it in person. When I was little, my mother and I often talked about the importance of companionship—we even exchanged small notes. Though I was still very young then, those notes, with their few simple words... I find them just as comforting today."

I nodded and left the house, ready to pen my next piece.

But before that, I would send a message to my child, whom I had neglected to contact for several days.

Xiangli Yao leaned forward in his chair and stared resolutely at the elderly man in front of him.

The older man held a prestigious position in the education system and had personal connections with Xiangli Yao's father. Today, it was another attempt at persuasion, much like the previous ones.

"I am not attending a separate class. Regular school is fine for me," Xiangli Yao reiterated.
The elderly man tapped on the table, "Your current pace might not fit into the standard curriculum. Moving too quickly can bring challenges. You and your classmates are not on the same playing field."

Xiangli Yao shook his head.

"There's no point wasting resources opening a special class just for me. I already have access to the Jinzhou archives for study. Besides... I'm just like the others," he said, counting on his fingers, "I have a great time watching hero plays with them, and we trade cards... Oh, and when they invite me over for dinner, I get to test my gadgets out on them and get their feedback!"

The elder sighed deeply. "Your teacher has mentioned such things to me. He says you get along well with your classmates. But this isn't just about you, it's about getting you into the Academy faster," he said, staring at the young person before him. "Xiangli Yao, your father also accelerated his studies and had more time to conduct all the research he loved."

"I am not my father."

"Yet you share his talents and temperament. That I've noticed."

Xiangli Yao gripped the textbooks in his hands, as he slowly and firmly shook his head, "But that's not what I want. I want to take things slow, like the way it is now."

"Playing trivial games with your classmates won't do you any good... You'll tire of it sooner or later. It's a waste of time."

The elder stood by the window, looking out at students playing and laughing in the schoolyard. Xiangli Yao went to him, patting his shoulder.

"That won't happen," Xiangli Yao said softly, also looking at the same view. 

They were his friends.

"I want to be like them, going to school, talking about snacks, catching fish in the river, and watching cool Echoes. Hey, they even taught me when and how to smile and compliment someone. That's important to me. I know you mean well, but... I get to decide what's best for me, right?"

Old and young faced each other in the silent office.

The elder sighed again. "You remind me of your father. But the two of you are not quite the same."

Xiangli Yao smiled, "Well, like I said... I'm not my father. I'm not the student you once had."

The door opened again.
 
The next day, Xiangli Yao returned to his regular classes.

"Here. Another package of yours."

His friend placed the box in a forgotten corner of the dorm, then sprawled out in bed, "Xiangli Yao, you should definitely sign up for Lollo Logistics membership. With how often you've been getting these deliveries, it's worth it."

Xiangli Yao turned his chair to face his friend, "Haha. I'll think about it."

"Latest issue?"

"Yeah, they sent me a sample."

"Jealous! I wish I could work that fast, popping out articles left and right while taking classes at the same time. Man." He waved his arms and grinned, "I guess you already have that Imperial Academy exam in the bag. So, where's it gonna be?"

With that, he tossed over a can of soda.

The can drew a perfect arc in the air, landing squarely in Xiangli Yao's hand.

"Too much sugar," sighed the model student, known for his healthy habits as his lips quirked into a smile, cracking open the can anyway. "About that..."

A brief silence followed. Then Xiangli shook his head softly. "I haven't decided yet."

His friend raised an eyebrow, surprised. "Well, that's new. I thought you made up your mind already. Professors must be fighting over you." 

"There are a few things I haven't figured out yet."

"Which are...?"

"Boundaries. The boundaries of truth," Xiangli Yao said slowly, twisting a cube in his hands. "Pascar, do you suppose that humanity will hold itself back in pursuing the boundaries of truth?"

"Maybe. There are plenty of nut job scientists out there, so who knows."

"We chase after the stars, only to fall beneath them. Boundaries limit our scope... but without it, there's no way to tell whether you're progressing."

"Well... you and I have different opinions on this, and I'll keep mine to myself to avoid an argument. But what's all this got to do with your admission? You trying to change the subject on me?"

Xiangli Yao smiled softly. "It does. After my father pursued his own path, I've heard little about him. But I've uncovered some leads... Perhaps they'll lead me to the Court of Savantae, the place he went searching for."

"You sure you're going? After so many years, plenty of people have tried to find even a smither of hint related to the CSC, with little success."

"I feel that I must go. Even if I'll end up finding nothing. I want to know..." 

The young scholar spoke slowly, his voice gradually softened, "I want to know... if my father crossed that boundary."
 
A month before exams, Xiangli vanished.

He left behind a video, revealing his confusion and the sense of emptiness he felt on his path of pursuing the truth. But whichever path he chose henceforth, he would embrace its outcome.

Empty seats lingered in the dorm, as life carried on.

It took over ten days to get inside the ruins.

At every step, remnants of the Court of Savantae's defenses were giving Xiangli Yao a hard time. Despite his meticulous preparations, some supplies and provisions had been lost along the way.

Xiangli Yao assessed what remained, weighing his options, and ultimately chose to press deeper into the ruins.

He had long since departed from the borders of Huanglong, and returning a second time to explore further would prove highly difficult. After surveying the soil upon arrival, the young scholar conjectured that these ruins, like those before, had little time left.

Internally, however, conditions were far better. The bulk of the instruments were well-preserved and intact. Cerulean fluids surged and circulated in the conduits of all the mechanisms with a vitality outlasting their creators. Each mechanism, precise, robust, and elegant, was meticulously cataloged by Xiangli Yao as he discerned subtle deviations from Huanglong's existing technologies.

The more he explored, the more an irrepressible thrill seized him. Like a poet enraptured by fine wine, Xiangli Yao felt drunk on the outpouring of knowledge that surrounded him.

His Terminal had lost its connection to the outside world, but he still did his best to record everything. His fascination with mechanics, a domain where Savantae had made unparalleled strides, led him to wonder whether his father had known of these innovations, and where he was now on the path of chasing the stars.

Yet amid the marvels, signs of a strange intrusion became apparent. Ever since the Lament, most technologies should have reverted back to their rudimentary states. But here, structures once familiar bore alien marks of alteration, defying erosion yet imbued with an elegance surpassing even Savantae's other creations.

The deeper Xiangli Yao went into the ruins, the anomalies intensified. Xiangli Yao's recordings slowed. The need to distinguish between anomalies and original designs demanded meticulous care. Eventually, he landed on a guess: The people here were trying to create some sort of door.

A door. A gateway. A... portal.

For the first time, Xiangli Yao hesitated.

Besides the danger, the doubt was about direction. So far, no alternate passage into the ruins had revealed itself, suggesting his father's departure had taken a different path. Had his father fallen here? Or...

If truth had a path, perhaps this was its nearest gateway.

Later, when Xiangli Yao reflected on his journey through the Court of Savantae ruins, he realized that parts of his memory had become foggy. He suspected it was due to the effects of the ancient mechanisms and force fields—devices that transcended current technological limits and boasted near-unfathomable levels of advancement. Creating them was clearly unwise, at least for the CSC researchers. Since the Lament, exploration beyond had halted due to the warping of the laws of physics. Yet, many scholars still yearned to traverse the skies again and explore interstellar space.

That portal might have been built for that very purpose: to leap into the sky, or perhaps even further, into the heart of the civilization that had transformed these ruins.

Xiangli Yao wasn't sure if they had succeeded, but he paid a steep price for his curiosity—his arm. He could only speculate that he had managed to solve the sequence and activate the mechanism. He recalled the marks etched into the enormous cavity. They were rugged and twisted, as if a huge Tacet mark was carved onto it.

Then, crystalline, delicate butterflies emerged from the fracture. A strange power seeped from the gap, glowing with the mysteries of another civilization. As Xiangli Yao stared into it, past barriers that once seemed insurmountable now appeared solvable within this new framework. The waves of knowledge surged, capable of bending, subduing, and intertwining all frequencies in existence.

He took a step forward, almost forgetting the blood gushing from his torn flesh. The dizziness from blood loss and a faint euphoria blurred his senses.

At that moment, he noticed a familiar object lying dust-covered on the workstation. His childhood memories were hazy, but he recognized it immediately as a gift from his mother to his father. Xiangli Yan had once shown it to him as a child, a father and son photo of them together. Suddenly, he understood. Even at the end, his father held onto a memory of their family. He hadn't abandoned everything.

Beyond that threshold, could he still see himself progressing, at the end of pure theory where no one could observe…?

His father devoted everything to theoretical science, his mother to applied science. Xiangli Yao was like them, always longing to reach for the stars, even willing to burn himself in the process.

They had given their all.

And what about him?

Standing just a step away from the ultimate answer, the young scholar found himself thinking about trivial, unrelated things. He recalled how, after his parents' departure, friends and neighbors had dragged him out to join a Jinzhou festival. It was supposed to be the Moon-Chasing Festival, but the threat from the Threnodian had forced a simpler celebration. Yet, a festival is always a festival, a reminder to celebrate even in hard times. He had demonstrated one of his newest creations, a small gadget, which won applause from the crowd.

He was like his parents.

However, he was not their clone. Even as his shadow followed theirs, he found himself unable to journey the same roads they had traveled.

With trembling hands, the young scholar searched for scattered parts, trying to assemble a device to stop the bleeding. His newly acquired Forte gently surged and began to warp the metal structures according to his will.

As the bleeding ceased, so did the grand opportunity before him.

It was only a few steps away... but Xiangli Yao had already turned his back.

He knew he had found his own answer.

So many paintings... Ah, not that I'm complaining about the commissions! It's just, I keep finding new things that inspire me... Oh, sorry. What I wanted to say is, the sunlight on you right now is so beautiful. Can I... paint you?

I-I saved half of a lemon cake for you. Want to try it? I couldn't help myself and bought it with some of the money I saved up, as a celebration for finishing my commission. I've wanted it for so long! It's sweet but not too rich, with perfect layers. It tastes just as amazing as I imagined!

You mean those phantasms? They're just illusions. They might look vibrant and stunning, but... they're not real. I prefer a flawed reality over a perfect illusion. Even though it's tough and unpredictable, it also has its surprises, like... meeting you.

Do you ever feel lonely when you're alone? I do enjoy my own company, but after a while, I start wishing I had someone to talk to. But... whenever I try, I never know what to say and I'm afraid of saying the wrong thing, so it usually ends up awkward... But talking to you feels different. It's like a conversation I used to only dream about. I really wish we could talk like this... forever.

You know, I started a portrait of you a while ago, but I haven't finished it yet… I feel like I can't capture everything I feel for you on just one piece of paper. If it's alright, I'd like to show it gradually, through what I do and say.
I like… being by myself.
My family's debt… It'll probably take me my whole life to pay it off by myself…
I have a sweet tooth. Sweet things always give me more energy!
When I cook, it feels like the flavors never blend, like the ingredients and seasonings are at odds… Are-are you interested in tasting it? Um, I'll have to practice more before you try it…
I hope… that one day, I can spend all my time painting what I truly want, leaving a piece of the real me in this world.

This brush is called Miaohua. It reacts to phantasms. When I was younger, I had trouble controlling my ability, and sometimes I couldn't tell reality from illusion… The worst time, I was trapped in an illusion for two whole days without realizing it. It was Miaohua's reaction that made me realize everything around me was fake and helped me find my way back to reality.

If your living space feels cramped, try using furniture in a single color. If prices seem unfair, try going right before the shop closes to find a good deal... I've realized that since I can't change everything, changing my perspective can really help... it's helped me find little bits of happiness in life!

Before I came to Jinzhou, I once met her training in the mountains. She had journeyed far and wide, sharing tales of the incredible places she'd been. Her views on nature completely changed how I paint. That deep focus she had while training... I aim for that same focus in my own art.

I often run into her when I'm out painting. I'm curious about the habits of plants, and she's really into what they mean in Huanglong culture. So we end up spending a lot of time just squatting by some plant, chatting.

She's got a real knack for appraising antiques, and knows all about where the rare old paintings are kept. If she hadn't told me where to find those friendly collectors, I'd never have gotten to see the originals with my own eyes. Though she's never told me how she gets her info, I can tell it's not easy. So now and then, I slip some money into her pocket when she's not looking!

Oh! She once invited me to dinner, and I said yes. However, when I arrived at the restaurant, it turned out to be a large gathering with dozens of people… I was quite nervous, but she was super nice, always making sure I was okay. Thanks to that, I actually met a lot of new people... and some of them even became my clients later on.

His lion dancing... it's really something. So precise and yet so full of life. I once walked by a lion dance performance and tried to sketch it quickly, but the movements kept changing... My pencil couldn't keep up. So, I ended up going to the theater a few more times just to watch. Before I knew it, I actually started enjoying the lion dances quite a bit.

As the child of two scholars, I was always drawn to the same path. Perhaps trying to follow in their footsteps. However, my recollections of them have blurred over time. Most of what I know about my parents comes from reading their published research and evaluations of their work by others, rather than personal memories. Their existence feels elusive to me, like a hazy dream. Yet, I am their legacy—a reflection of their brilliance, and... their madness.

I like interacting with people, be it my colleagues at the Academy, or others. At times, I fear losing sight of my own humanity while chasing truth's elusive grasp... In those moments, I step away and seek solace in a bustling crowd. The laughter on their faces reminds me of the warmth of human connection.

Losing my arm didn't bring as much pain as I expected. I was too consumed with excitement, finally discovering the Court of Savantae Ruins, following in my father's footsteps. The achievements I witnessed were beyond imagination. The secrets of a hidden civilization were revealed to me, their inventions harnessing the universe's echoes.
