Writing a report alone, after completing research, is satisfying. My scattered thoughts and inspirations come together during this time, becoming clear and organized.
During back-to-back academic conferences, my focus wanes and I need time to recharge. Being with peers is enjoyable, but a little solitude is necessary for me to stay sharp.
I love all breakfast foods. I prefer to sleep and wake up early instead of staying up late and consuming caffeine. Eating consistent breakfast portions energizes my mind quickly.
Oh, the Sour Soy Milk… When I was a toddler, my mother once convinced me to try it. While most of my childhood memories are joyful, that particular taste was overwhelming for my young palate.

The laws of nature on Solaris have shifted under the Lament's sway, and even fundamental principles are now being questioned across all academic fields. Yet, I find the pursuit of new theories quite stimulating. Deep within the cosmos, beyond the stars, lies a vast expanse waiting to be understood. And there, amidst the barren landscape, truth awaits its discovery.

This prosthetic arm is pretty handy, loaded with helpful features. I don't have to worry about any arm injury while working on risky experiments, and I can even pull a few pranks on my colleagues. Oh, you want examples? Well... I'll definitely show you when I get the chance.

Among the friends I made when I was a kid, Pascar was the one who kept in touch with me for the longest time. Certain actions, when done too late, can lead to lingering regrets. Occasionally, I contemplate how each individual is a complex enigma, similar to the countless scientific theses I have studied.

Mortefi is an interesting person. He's devoted to his work with unwavering determination. It's that kind of intense drive that pushes scientists towards brilliant discoveries. I know he considers me a "genius"—but in a workplace with only "geniuses", many ideas will never be realized. My dear friend has yet to grasp his true potential.

Magistrate Jinhsi has been paying close attention to the battles against Tacet Discords. She often visits the Academy to learn about our latest progress in weapons development. During those visits, she always seems tense. I understand the pressure and weight she carries, with all the promises and expectations placed on her shoulders...

The Midnight Rangers bring valuable insights on Tacet Discords from their years of combat experience. General Jiyan has shared his extensive knowledge and new ideas with us. He possesses a gentle and just nature, but what truly sets him apart is his composure. This is essential for someone in his position.

Aalto once approached me with an offer from the Black Shores, but I declined. Life at the Academy suits me well. Though his manner may seem unserious, Aalto has a sharp eye for valuable information and connections for rare materials. I've frequently relied on his services.

Baizhi is a great researcher. Our work doesn't often overlap, but I've read her reports and they're well-informed and persuasive. She often participates in field research, earning her a reputation among peers for bringing back valuable data.

I'm getting tired. Let's catch our breath here. Honestly, after answering your questions all this time, I have one for you.
This dreamscape in Somnoire, what... is it?
The dream... is a virtual world.
The dream... is an extension of reality.
I see. That's a realistic answer. So, what about everything you've experienced in the previous space?
Those close friends of yours acting and talking strangely in your deep dream—do you think those are virtual?
Maybe that's the "reality." They are free from restrictions in the deep dream, and that's why they look so real and vivid.
Is dream... a virtual world?
Sort of. Some dream to escape, some to compensate, some to pretend… all these dreams are tied to the real world.
If dreams share so much with reality, how may one tell the difference between the two?
Oh, you're confused by that too? Then let's not stop here and venture deeper for more clues.
In the realms of dreams, only the dream itself holds the answers we seek.
I've isolated this space for now, but it won't last long.
The dream is even more chaotic now.
Have you got any ideas about the culprit?
It is. What's behind the next door is getting unpredictable. Be extra cautious when you open them.
I can't reach a conclusion yet. Let's find that obscure chunk we encountered first—what you saw as the Dreamless.
By the way, before I leave, did he ask you any strange questions, like, what on earth is a dream?
He asked me some similar questions before... Whatever your answer is, I hope you mean it.
See? Sweet dreams, bad dreams, ordinary dreams, heroic dreams, empty dreams. They are all here.
If sweet dreams and heroic dreams are born from someone's wish, then what is the meaning of bad dreams, ordinary dreams and empty dreams?
If we rank them by the meaning we discussed, will you ignore the dreams that seem meaningless?
Let's stop for a while. Breathe in the peace here, and take a look at this magnificent dream.
Sweet dreams, bad dreams, ordinary dreams, heroic dreams, empty dreams...
They are all part of Somnoire, and naturally, they bring laughter, tears, and sighs here, just like the so-called reality outside the door.
However, everyone becomes more honest with themselves behind this door. They show what's normally concealed in real life, unreservedly.
Say, if Somnoire took over the outside world and became reality one day...
...Do you want to live in that world?

This song... where is it coming from?
That's Lorelei's song, guiding ships through the mist.
But her singing sounds a bit different today. There are hints of... sorrow and agony...
Perhaps it's merely my fancy. Regardless, her melody will guide us through fog and storm to the heart of the Nimbus Sanctum.
It seems we have some time before the train arrives. How about a little chat to pass the time?
I'm waiting for someone anyway.
Well, then. Where shall we begin?
"The city, an abomination of chaos, claims its first death at birth. Its mortality has become our sustenance, like a whale that slowly sinks into the abyss."
This comment on Ragunna comes from Rosselli, a painter from the past. Tragically, he died in poverty, his work overlooked. Now, ironically, even a mere sketch of his commands over a million Credits.
Now. What is your impression of Ragunna so far?
The people are very passionate.
A profit-driven place full of corruption.
A city of faith.
I'm not sure.
Passionate... Indeed. Passion is a quality the Ragunnesi possess in abundance. It's also why the Carnevale is so eagerly anticipated.
Indeed. Ragunna is not as glamorous as it seems. Beneath the veneer of prosperity, avarice reigns supreme.
Indeed, faith is Ragunna's crown jewel. Our devotion to the Sentinel stands unrivaled throughout Rinascita.
A most prudent response. Perhaps you're still acquainting yourself with Ragunna, or you simply prefer discretion. Either way, I take no offense.
Ragunna has many facets. Most people only see one side of it, but for me—
It's like two sworn enemies are forcibly bound together. That's Ragunna—a city where tradition and innovation, openness and isolation, ceaselessly wrestle for dominance.
That is why the Montelli and Fisalia families are in a constant clash, as you may have seen.
The Montellis champion innovation, staking all on the Carnevale. Meanwhile, the Fisalias cling to tradition, colluding with the shadows that lurk in Ragunna's depths.
Fortunately, this long struggle behind the curtains will soon come to an end. Not because of the two families, but because of you.
Me?
Yes, you. The Fated One. Perhaps you're not merely entangled in Ragunna's conflict, but are, in fact, the very eye of the storm. The city's fate may well rest upon your shoulders.
Are you serious?
I can hardly buy that.
You may have not noticed it yet, but we are... and have been in the same boat for a long time.
Ah. There's the train. It's time to say goodbye now.
I didn't catch your name.
I'll tell you next time. As for now, let's keep it a mystery.
So this is what's become of the seminary? I never expected this.
You've been here before?
No, but I've seen paintings of the seminary in the Cathedral. It had an enormous dome and spires that seemed to touch the heavens.
Then the Order was forced to abandon it when the sea of clouds swallowed it.
Have you also come to repent and seek forgiveness?
The Sentinel has revealed a path to resist temptation and corruption. We need only devote ourselves wholly... to Lorelei.
We're just here to see Lorelei.
Patience. I see your eagerness for enlightenment, like our new brothers. You've removed your masks, but your hearts… they're still veiled.
Everyone here wears a mask. Everyone in Ragunna. Without exception, never unmasked. This is the source of our suffering. The mask veils our hearts.
Like our new brothers, they wear peculiar masks of madness. Poor souls tormented by evil desires. May they find peace in Lorelei's embrace.
Peculiar masks of madness?
Evil desires?
Yes, their masks are filled with madness, but even wrongdoers can seek redemption from Lorelei. The Sentinel granted Lorelei this authority, and no one can take it away.
Follow Lorelei's song and your heart, and you may meet our lady. But if your transgressions are... beyond redemption, you'll be lost in the sea of clouds forever.
So what should we do to see Lorelei?
Do you seek an audience with Lorelei? Sadly, you've come at a bad time. Lorelei is furious, and our mortal bodies can't withstand her wrath. We've sealed the path to her domain.
We appreciate the explanation, but we believe Lorelei is in danger... We're here to help her. Someone's planning to exploit her powers...
The path has been closed. You must leave.
(Sigh) Doesn't look like we'll be talking our way past him. Let's find another way, {PlayerName}.
Oh. I have been cleansed of impure thoughts. I can finally escape from my wrongdoings.
Sing, dance! For we have been granted peace and freedom!
Yes, we only need to relish this moment!
We'd like to see Lorelei.
Oh! You've also come to rid yourself of your misdeeds? Then join us! Sing! Sing with us!
The door has been shut. Simply sing along and it will open before you!
(Just "Sing"? Doesn't look like we'll get more out of them. Let's go check somewhere else.)
But most of these are worn out and don't look like modern Rinascita script. Phoebe, can you read any of it?
Let's see... This seems like an ancient holy script dedicated to recording the deeds of Sentinel Imperator. As for its content...
"I shall grant this power to... the Night... Queen. May she... during the day... sea of clouds..."
Ugh. Much of this text is illegible. However, the adjacent drawing is mostly intact. It shows Sentinel Imperator speaking to a massive creature.
And the creature slowly shifts from an immense, amorphous form into a humanoid shape.
Could it be Lorelei? After all, no other being that large lives above the sea of clouds....
Actually, I'm not sure if the other figure is the Sentinel. It looks a little different from the Cathedral statues. Maybe it's just the lack of clarity in the drawing.
Anyway, does it mean... Lorelei and the Sentinel are somehow connected to each other?
Nothing about the barrier though. Are there any other clues?
These inscriptions and markings on the stela seem to say something.
A veil of mist shrouds the Atrium, radiating an aura of resistance. This must be the entrance that the believers refer to as "the path to audience."
Small words are carved beside it: "We mourn the martyrdom of the Blessed Maiden."
Is this some kind of hint?
Misteltein! You're here!
*growl*—
*chirp*!
This is Misteltein. One of the missing Echoes. They probably followed the singing.
Misteltein, do you know how to remove the barrier?
Now how would an Echo know that, Phoebe—
*growl*—
I guess "singing" is our only option for clearing that barrier.
But which song?
The stela we saw mentioned the Sentinel, and we're in the ruins of the seminary.
Meaning it should be a "chorale"? There are also the inscription in front of the barrier: "We mourn the martyrdom of the Blessed Maiden."
Any chorales you know ring a bell, Phoebe?
The martyrdom of the Blessed Maiden... Could this be the "Aria of the Blessed Maiden"? It's a chorale rarely used these days. I doubt most Priests even know of it.
The Blessed Maiden? We met a playwright named Cristoforo earlier. He shared some stories about her.
Phoebe, if you know this chorale, why not give it a try? It might just clear the barrier.
M-me?
O-okay then. I suppose it's our best option at the moment. I'll give it a try. Ahem...
A song of false nature. Masking... A twisted view... Tear it to shreds...
Did you get the chorale wrong?
I'm sure I sang the "Aria of the Blessed Maiden"...
Not good... She doesn't seem too pleased with that one.
That flower... looks like the petals we found in Whisperwind Haven.
It's the Fractsidus. I've dealt with them before, and I've seen a flower just like this.
How long have I been in slumber... This nightmare... How long was I trapped in it?
Are you also part of the dream?
No, we are not... Might you be Lorelei?
I am. Travelers from afar, I sense… the kindness pulsing in your hearts. You must be the ones who broke the chains of my nightmare.
The oathbreakers, hiding behind their Masks of Madness… They tainted the Nimbus Sanctum with corrupted blooms, drowning me in rage and sorrow. Endless nightmares became my prison.
Masks of Madness... I recall those people at the entrance of the Atrium mentioned it.

Had you not freed me from my nightmare, I would never be able to fulfill the Sentinel's task… The tides of the Nimbus Sanctum would have engulfed the whole of Ragunna, just as they once claimed the sacred temple now lying in ruins beneath you.
Wait. The Sentinel? Does that mean...?
Yes, the Sentinel molded me from a mindless being to the form you see, and bestowed upon me the most precious gift... A soul.
They commanded me to restrain the clouds and prevent the Remnant Energy within it from... dissipating.
Can you contact Imperator? I need to meet with the Sentinel.

Unfortunately, it lies beyond my power. The Sentinel's link to the mortal realm is severed. Only through collective prayer, and a rite, at the height of the Carnevale, only then can mortals briefly commune with Them.
A rite... You mean the Carnevale?
No, that's impossible! The current Primus, Fenrico the Enlightened One, was given a direct oracle from the Sentinel. The Sentinel has always been with the people!
I'm afraid the Sentinel's current state... transcends mortal understanding. Your Primus is no exception.
Should doubt linger in your mind, I implore you to await the rite's completion. The Sentinel will surely answer the people's call—not your so-called… Enlightened One.
One last thing. Those oathbreakers wearing Masks of Madness you mentioned, do you know who they are?
All that I know is that they are not from Rinascita.
In the whispers between dreams, I heard them speak of their leader, a woman they called…
"—the Conductor."
Conductor...
It is time I return to my slumber. Their wicked acts have scarred the sea of clouds, and I must mend it… within my dreams.
The song shall guide you out of this domain. Farewell, visitors.
What a wild turn this job's taken… Seeing the legendary Lorelei up close? Almost makes it worth the trouble.
Hmm? Are you all right, Phoebe?
Huh? I-I'm fine. I'm just… processing Lorelei's words. Forgive me, I… I need a moment to reflect.
In any case, we managed to stop their plot in time and found the missing Vitreum Dancer.
Speaking of that Vitreum Dancer… What brought it here? Lorelei's song, or maybe the Sentinel's guidance?
But those wearing the Masks of Madness... The Fractsidus, right? I'm curious about their role in all this. I think they supplied Gilberto with the flowers to turn Echoes into Tacet Discords.
Yeah, the Fractsidus is behind this.
Their actions remind me of something...
What's our next move, {PlayerName}?
We need more support.
You're right... Those snakes lurked in the shadows, using Gilberto as their fall guy. We can't expose them just by ourselves.
Oh, another thing. Since the Fractsidus is conspiring with the Fisalias, that makes them an enemy of the Montelli family.
There happens to be an auction at Averardo Vault today. The top members of the family will be there.
We should tip off the family about the Fractsidus' scheme. The Montellis can't afford to ignore this threat.
Agree.
What about you, Phoebe?
I intend to return to the Order first. While I believe Lorelei is truthful, I can't imagine the Primus would deceive our people. He is, after all, the <ano=Sentinel's Resonator>Enlightened One</ano>.
According to Lorelei, the Sentinel will deliver an oracle during the Carnevale. That's when the truth will come to light.
Speaking of which, are all Primuses called the <ano=Sentinel's Resonator>Enlightened One</ano>?
No, only Lord Fenrico has ever directly communicated with the Sentinel. Previous Primuses were merely indirect representatives, not the Enlightened One...
Silence and composure are gifts from the great Imperator. I'll keep today's events between us, locked away in my heart.
It's the same Echo boat we were on earlier... Was it also attracted by Lorelei's singing?
*A gentle cry*
It's called Noah.
Noah... Well, I can't understand what it's saying, but it's a perfect timing. We can have it take us to Averardo Vault.
That's a really big waterfall... Is there no way up?
*An expressive cry*
Whoa, really? You can take us upstream?
*A cry of certainty*
Averardo Vault is just up ahead. It seems this is where we part ways, Noah.
*A cry of understanding*
I'm sure it can find its way back to the harbor. Don't worry. Now, we just need to follow this path to reach the vault. Let's go.
Welcome to Averardo Vault. Do you have an appointment?
My name is Zani. I'm an employee of the bank. Here's my ID.
(Present the family's invitation.)
Ah, this invitation… My apologies. Welcome to Averardo Vault. How may we assist you today?
We're not here on business. We've come to brief the family on the Echo incident from the recent Carnevale rehearsal.
I'll arrange that immediately. Please proceed to the main entrance. A staff member will greet you there.
These Echoes... Are they guarding the vault?
Yes. But I've never seen them in action before. The "Averardo Bank Employee Manual" says they can easily take out a whole squad of Resonators.
Of course, this doesn't apply to someone powerful like you, {PlayerName}. Still, their combat skills are formidable. Their mere presence is enough to make everyone feel safe.
This facility houses nearly half of Rinascita's wealth. It serves all of Ragunna's citizens, even including the Fisalias.
Despite our feud, no one in Ragunna can refuse the services of Averardo Vault.
What the... I thought they only responded to hostility!
Steady now. Don't move. It's on high alert but won't attack unless provoked. At least, that's what the Employee Manual says!
Stand down.
I apologize for the small mishap on behalf of the Montelli Family. And...
What a pleasant surprise to see you again so soon.
And you.
Yet your expression betrays no surprise, {PlayerName}.
Allow me to properly introduce myself. My name is Carlotta, Carlotta Montelli.
Montelli… You are the…
The second daughter of the Montelli Family, yes. Please feel free to call me Carlotta.
Also, I trust the renumeration meets your satisfaction, Ms. Zani?
It was you who tasked me with receiving {PlayerName}?
Surely a distinguished guest such as {PlayerName} deserves the attention of our most trusted employee.
I'm aware of your purpose here. On behalf of my family, allow me to extend our deepest gratitude for your endeavors.
Your eyes show curiosity about me and my role in this… drama. However, this isn't the place for such discussions. Please follow me.
Please accept my apologies, {PlayerName}, for withholding my true identity before.
Rinascita's affairs have grown… intricate. The Fisalia family, the Order of the Deep…
You've likely noticed that many desire the Carnevale to fail. We Montellis, having tied our future to its success, became their target.
…But, let's not dwell on that for now.
Here we are. Welcome to Averardo Vault—the Montellis' heart and glory.

What is this place?

The Remnant Clouds from the sea of clouds drew hordes of Tacet Discords here. Now, their whispers fill the air, turning this once holy place of pilgrimage into the "Penitent's End."
This "Dragon of Dirge," is a local Tacet Discord. It grows by feeding on the others.
We were supposed to pick you up like Ms. Carlotta planned, but... things went sideways.
The truth Ms. Carlotta wants to show you lies somewhere on the isle.
But this is not the best place to talk. The mist is thickening... and rain is coming.
The mist is dangerous here. It traps Reverberations, and when it collects enough, they quickly form into Tacet Discords.
The Captain—I mean Brant... He went into the mist to rescue people, but he hasn't returned. We think he might be in danger.

Just in case, take this to mask your frequency and defend yourself.

Come... Play with me... Look for me... I'm here...
Ah... Roccia... You found me.
I'll always find you, but maybe don't do this again next time.
Why? Isn't this your favorite game... I... I wanted to play with you.
I know, but as your friend, I worry about your safety.
My... friend...
Excuse me. Are you Roccia's friend?
Yes, I am.
Not yet, but I think we will be soon.
Ah... How wonderful.
You're not alone anymore, Roccia.
Yes, I have friends now.
I'm... so happy for you...
All is well...
Fly, fly to the high heavens. We are born free, and our souls will soar even in death.
What exactly are these phantoms?
You were old friends, hm?
Golden phantoms are... Reverberations mixed with the frequencies left behind by people who've passed away.
When someone dies, their Reverberations linger. Usually, they merge into the same cacophony of frequencies that spawns Tacet Discords.
But sometimes, a trace of their final will remains, and the mist shapes this into phantoms.
This lingering will helps the phantoms resist becoming Tacet Discords and instead guide the lost through the mist.
If the mist clears, they'll vanish. If the mist lingers, their fate is sealed. It will only be a matter of time before they merge with other Reverberations and become Tacet Discords.
Their final frequencies tend to cling to certain objects... like this Luceanite here. I collect them as proof that they once lived.
A Pilgrim's Sail? Why is it here?
In Ragunna, those who break the law are sent to the Order Tribunal for sentencing. Those who violate the sacred doctrines are branded as Fools and sent away on the Pilgrim's Sail.
Now, the Fools retrace the Primus's journey, reflecting on their mistakes along the way.
There's a strong undercurrent around this isle, likely caused by that first Dark Tide. It drags all Pilgrim's Sails here unless the ship's course is altered.
This ship is empty.
Did the passengers all drown?
Looks like our brief intermission is over. Time to let the "ghosts" have their moment on stage.
Come on, then! Let the flames of battle ignite our souls!
Wait... is that Brant?
Only Brant would call them ghosts with that kind of flair... It must be him, but I can't tell where he is in the mist.
Anyway, let's deal with the trouble here first before we go look for him.
The show's over, ghosts! Time to take your final bow!
Watch your back.
A marvelous shot! You've earned your stripes, First Mate.
You're welcome, but if you'd tilted your head just ten centimeters to the left, it wouldn't have been the Discord's head that got popped—it'd be yours.
Not on your watch. Besides, fortune always smiles on me. Except in bets.
And we've crossed paths with the Rover again! Can't get luckier than that!
We shouldn't have let {PlayerName} get caught up in this mess.
{Male=He;Female=She} was worried about us and insisted on coming.
Is that so? Then our gratitude to you is even greater for your timely aid, {PlayerName}.
I'm here to uncover a buried truth.
We're all alive, and that's what counts.
I wouldn't even be here if it weren't for that dragon.
To find the brightest truth, one must delve into the deepest shadows. Such bravery deserves to be hailed, my friend.
Where is everyone on the Pilgrim's Sail?
I was patrolling the coast earlier when I saw their ship drifting into the mist. Time was against us, so I departed alone without alerting the crew.
T-thank you.
Don't be afraid. You're safe with us. You've got some skill, you know, holding your own for so long in the trial against the Tacet Discords.
Trial? Ha, I don't buy into the Order's nonsense.
I've worked hard all my life and stayed true to the Order's teachings about forsaking earthly pleasures for divine favor. And what do I get in return? Heavier taxes.
When pirates ransacked my merchant fleet leaving me with nothing, I turned to the Order for help. They said it was a divine trial and left me to rot.
I stood before the Sentinel's statue, asking if my suffering was really Their will, but all I got was... silence.
Why should I wait for peace in the afterlife when I could be living for today? How is that a crime?
As for salvation... I don't believe in it, and I certainly don't need it.
Here's a proposal. How about joining our troupe?
We are wanderers adrift upon the seas. Or perhaps you're more familiar with the name—the Troupe of Fools.
The Troupe of Fools? Could it be...
Yes. We are, like you, by the Order's decree... marked as Fools.
Fools on the Pilgrim's Sail often meet their demise in a storm or they're swallowed by the waves... Even if they do survive, they still face hunger, thirst, and the unforgiving wrath of nature.
Maybe it's luck that brought you here so swiftly, and unharmed at that.
Look around. This is all that remains of the Pilgrim's Sail... This is always their final destination, where the Fools meet their end.
Yes. The pilgrimage is nothing but a banishment in disguise. The path to salvation they speak of doesn't exist.
Otherwise, how could this once sacred place now look like such a hellish wasteland?

Wait, sacred place? No wonder the others were talking about it on the ship. They believed the Order's promise that prayers at the Sacrificial Arena would grant them forgiveness... They must be heading up the mountain now.
I didn't expect their faith to lead them that far.
If only they knew it was just one of the Order's lies.
Captain! First mate! We're here to help!
More hands make light work. I called in some help to escort him back to the base once the mist cleared.
Ah, the first mate's foresight is unmatched! Then the three of us can head up the mountain.
But beware my friend, by the end of this pilgrimage, you will witness the Order's cruelest deceit. The dangers ahead will only intensify.
That's what I'm here for.
These are human footprints. Looks like they're heading to the Arena.
This is the only way up. Let's pick up the pace.
Tacet Discords, incoming. Stay alert, everyone.
Begone, you vexing wretches... The Sacrificial Arena is right there. Let's take them down in one blow.
Oh, Divinity above, please have mercy on me...
Is this... some kind of test for me? I-I see. No matter how harsh the punishment, I'll take it. Even if... even if...
Even if... it means death?
We've never done anything that warrants paying with our lives.
I'd wager mercy isn't on the table. However...
In the face of danger and adversity, the stage is set for our grandest act!
Brant, you handle the Tacet Discords. I've got the dragon.
Of course, but with all due respect... shouldn't the Captain be the one giving the orders?
Just playing to our strengths. Take it, or I'll spill the beans about your wine stash.
Aye, aye, First Mate!
Hic...
Abby! I knew you'd be okay!
Abby! I thought I lost you!
Abby! I'll avenge you!
Of course! You think that lil' lizard could take me down? I just took a nap after eating its frequency. Hic...
Uh, seriously? You think that lil' lizard could take me down? I just took a nap after eating its frequency. Hic.
Thanks, but no thanks. You think that lil' lizard could take me down? I just took a nap after eating its frequency. Hic.
But seriously, that was close! The fire it breathed almost singed your hair! Good thing I was here to back you up!
As soon as I realized it was a Tacet Discord, I went for it and ate its frequency. Piece of cake! But I gotta say, it was a pretty hefty bite.
I swear I chewed it up, but it was hard to swallow. It wasn't the taste, you know. More like my digestion's been a mess lately. Hic.
Gehinnom, a wretched soul, mourned by none...
You are reborn to fulfill our sacred rite... Illuminate the path of salvation...
Become the fiery hand of judgment, purging all transgressions...
Cleanse every soul ensnared by their own indulgence...
Here we are, ladies and gentlemen. Allow me to present to you our sanctuary, a haven for all the surviving Fools at the edge of the world.
Pretty impressive.
A base... in THIS place?
It is, my friend. We built this base from the ground up, and I dare say it's a triumph worthy of the ages.

They say the most dangerous places are the safest. Penitent's End has always been forsaken, and now, cloaked in the sea of mist, even the Order's envoys wouldn't dare set foot here. It's the perfect refuge for us.
The mist does shield us from the Order, but it brings its own set of problems.
Precisely why we must tackle its effects without delay.
By the way, if you'd like to speak with Mr. Bardolino, our Laureate, you'll find his tent deep within the base.
Feel free to talk to the others while we handle our tasks. We'll catch up once we're done.
First Mate! What should we do with these stage props?
Load the light boxes on the heavy suitcases. Place the lights on top and secure them with chains. Keep the fireworks well away from the curtains.
And don't forget to check the freshwater reserves and all cabin doors.
Roger!
The first mate has quite the workload.
I'm starting to wonder who's really running the ship.
Usually, the crew handles these jobs themselves.
But since we're prepping for the Carnevale and working on stage setups, it's fair they ask for my advice.
Here, the role of captain is best suited to someone who can ease the newcomers' fears and worries.
Brant is a natural. As for me, I'm more comfortable managing these kinds of tasks.
There, there. Don't be afraid...
The frequencies mixed in the mist are unsettling Lario. I'm trying to calm it down so the crew can board.
Wanna give it a try? Just place your hand on its forehead and channel your Resonance Energy, like this...
(Reach out your hand.)
*Soft, reassured noises*
You really are special... The Echoes here are naturally drawn to you.
Echoes can sense and respond to human frequencies. They reflect how we treat them, for better or worse.
They're like reflections of who we each are.
I've heard Lario's scientific name is Pliosaurus Somnii, an incredible creature first seen in the dream of its discoverer.
It used to escort our ships across the seas, and then, of its own accord, became our stage. It has braved countless storms with us.
Throughout our many travels, we've never found another like it.
It must've been lonely, after so many years alone, drifting... That's why it chose to sail with us.
Why were you banished?
When I was young, much younger than I am now, I performed in a play that was banned by the Order.
And... that was it. I was sent here with all the other performers.
The play was about freedom, love, and hope. How could something so beautiful be considered taboo? I... I don't understand.
Welcome back, Brant! I... I heard a lot of voices coming from the mist. It's scary...
Don't be afraid, Morrias. They're all friends from the troupe, people we've sailed with.
You said you want to be a captain, right?
Sailing has its own trials—sea monsters, storms, whirlpools, undercurrents, you name it. When such challenges arise, you've got to trust your helm and your crew.
They'll stand by you through thick and thin, and your job is to guide them safely through it all, till you reach the journey's end.
I understand... Everyone has been so good to me, always looking out for me. When I grow up, I'll be a great captain and take care of them too!
That's the spirit, kiddo! You've already got the heart of a captain, and that's no small feat. You're the captain of your own ship!
Bravery like that deserves rewards. Here, take this.
Wow, Captain Sparrow's Legends! Thanks, Brant!
And... can I maybe have a sip of the stuff you like to drink? The Troupe Strength?
Ah, well... Ahem! That's a special brew for captains who've faced the fiercest storms. When you're ready, your own glass of Troupe Strength will be waiting.
Really? I'll work for it!
Troupe Strength?
Kids here really seem to trust you.
About the Reverberations in the sea mist...
It's a drink made of Waterlamps, fermented, distilled, and aged to perfection. Not for young ones, of course.
We brew it ourselves, each of us with our preferred strength. It's not worth much, but it's one of the few pleasures we can have here…
As the captain, it's my duty to be the crew's compass. This face must not show any fear or sorrow.
This isle is fraught with hidden threats. Many who were banished never made it to join us, claimed by the Tacet Discords. Their Reverberations became part of the mist...
Those who did make it have their own dreams to chase.
Some will eventually leave to follow the call of their hearts, their silhouettes forever etched into the mist.
We hope they find their promised lands. The troupe may be a safe harbor, but it's certainly not the final destination of their journey.
We honor their names and stories in our plays, passing their legacy down through the crew.
Beriarti the Fire Eater, Toscanini the Night Watcher, Fernando the Fish Killer... Their stories remain vivid in my memory. One day, I'll compile them into a book. Mark my words.
Over the years, we've bid farewell to many and welcomed countless new faces... It seems this cycle will never end.
Why were you banished?

When I was a boy, I saw the Sentinel's statue in the Cathedral of Mercury. Curiosity led me to point at the statue and ask, "How can you say it's the Sentinel when no one has ever laid eyes on it?" I didn't know the consequences that would follow.
That question earned me a pilgrimage. At the time, I thought it was some grand adventure.
On the Pilgrim's Sail, I was cared for by other Fools who shared what little they had and shielded me from the grim reality with their kindness and smiles.
But all I could do was watch... as they passed away, one by one. From that day forward, I swore to wipe away the tears of the innocent.
Every adventurer needs a rest, and every ship must find a port. For us, that meant finding a sanctuary.
C'mon, fish. Come to my net.
What are you doing?
Why were you banished?
Did you borrow some of the Cloudcaster's parts?
Me? Just prepping dinner. The storm's passed, so it's the perfect time for fishing!
The captain once told me a secret: the fiercer the storm, the more fish it brings. Sometimes we even see fish swept up by the wind, raining down from the sky!
Only fish on the menu?
Uh, are you sure this is legal?
Usually, yeah. But when we dock on an island, the captain and first mate will buy some other food from the locals.
Legal? Ha, who cares! We're not even a legitimate troupe according to the Order.
Back in Ragunna, I was just a fledgling fisherman when I accidentally caught an Orastie.
Turns out it's a sacred fish, only meant as an offering to the Sentinel. Mortals aren't allowed to catch it… but it swam right into my net! Not really my fault, was it?
Though, the Order didn't see it that way. They banished me here, like tossing a fish onto dry land.
Luckily, the troupe found me. I can still fish like I used to. Otherwise, I'd probably be dead or living as a pirate.
Arragh!
Ha! Eat this!
What are you doing here?
Hey! No fighting!
Who are you? A new recruit? Can't you see we're trying to have a fistfighting contest here? Back in the day, a brawl like this was the pride of the streets!
People from every district used to gather on a certain bridge over the river. And first one to toss their opponent into the water got the bridge and the bragging rights.
The victors were hailed as champions, their names sung in the streets. They earned titles and glory beyond measure.
It's a shame the Order banned it. What was their excuse again? Oh, right—"breaking solidarity among citizens."
It's madness! A good brawl was a way to blow off steam and ease some of the hostility between the people before it grew into something dangerous.
And look where we are now. No more epic matches, just a simmering pot of trouble. Can't make sense of it...
Why were you banished?
I got caught smacking someone with a stick in the street.
Yeah, I gave him that stick.
And I'm that someone.
Eh... that's the reason you were all banished?
You all seem to get along well now.
Whether it was for a good reason or not, as soon as you break the Order's doctrines—fraternity, Ragunna's "unity," or whatever—you're sent off on pilgrimage.
Once on board the Pilgrim's Sail, we only had each other to rely on. Out here, sticking together is the only way to survive.
Speaking of which, we never did settle who won that fight, did we?
Hmm, now that you mention it, we didn't.
Then let's do it now! C'mon! Let's go!
Again? But you're friends now!
I certainly won't interfere...
Haha, don't worry, they've been at this a hundred times before! How about a wager? I'll put up my lucky half-coin!
Sailors cheer as hearts ignite, soon we'll break these chains so tight. Set the course, embrace the storm, sailing on 'til light is born...
What are you doing?
Why were you banished?
Did you borrow some of the Cloudcaster's parts?
Oh, hello! I'm writing a sea shanty!
Did you know, Ragunna gondolier's songs are usually in 3/4 time. It matches the flow of water perfectly.
When they row, their strokes go "slow dip, quick lift," which fits that rhythm.
But for our troupe, we use a 4/4 signature with strong and weak beats. It's catchy and perfect for sailors to sing along to as we work together to tackle the waves.
Actually... boarding the Pilgrim's Sail was my choice.
I used to compose hymns for the Order. Sounds prestigious, hm?
But the same old rhythm and lyrics started to wear on me. Music should be alive! So I decided to take the pilgrimage, believing I'd find new inspiration from the divinity.

Hmph, you probably already know what the pilgrimage really is. I was foolish to believe the Order's lies, but luckily, the troupe found me and brought me in. Ah, have you seen any of our performances perhaps?
We don't do those lofty soliloquies that give you existential dread. That doesn't mean our plays are shallow—they're just more hopeful and speak directly to the heart.
We do Commedia Improvviso, a style of play that's all about those fleeting, beautiful moments of everyday life.
We sing of love that endures, enemies who become allies in the fight against evil...
Relax, young man. Life's only just unfurling its sails for you. Why sit there like one of those dour statues in the Order's halls? Don't be afraid to show a little spark!
I... I was just thinking about my future. Is Ragunna truly lost to me forever?
Ah, some have found their way back, but under the Order's watchful eye. Is that really what you want? A life without freedom?
Listen, you don't need a grand stage to leave your mark. A true Ragunnesi can turn even a ragged tent into the finest theater. That's what I'm preparing to do.
I might be an old man now, but don't let that fool you. I was once crowned with the Laurel, you know!
You? A-are you... Mr. Bardolino?
In the flesh! Hahaha!
Did anything unusual happen to you when you had the Laurel?

As I took my final bow on stage, a bright light pierced through the clouds, shining down from the sky. And then, a radiant Laurel descended upon me. And I heard a voice—it was the Sentinel's voice, ringing in my head.
I asked Them a question that had puzzled me since childhood, the ultimate philosophical riddle—"What should I eat tonight?"
And They answered, "The body is the temple of the mind. To keep your mind sharp, do consume healthy food, such as the Laurus Salad."

But why Laurus Salad? I was baffled, and the meaning still eludes me to this very day. I've never been quick-witted though, and the Order's doctrines never quite took hold. Acting, however, that is where my true passion lies...
Perhaps that's just the Sentinel's personal favorite...
I must say, your question is rather interesting...
But why did a blessed Laureate like you get banished by the Order?
Back when I won the Laurel, Ragunna was led by the Holy Maiden. She promoted all sorts of grand celebrations during the Carnevale, an unceasing tide of revelry...
Stages sprang up on every corner of the city, performances dancing through the streets, and shops adorned in vibrant hues. Even on rainy nights, you could still hear music playing in the square.
Some performers wove their critiques into their acts. Sharp as she was, the Holy Maiden noticed. She refined city policy with each whisper of dissent.

Ah, those were the golden days, my friend. The Holy Maiden once said that if she were to leave this world, she'd want no majestic tomb or a solemn funeral, but the grandest Carnevale as her final farewell.

And then... she really did leave us. The current Primus took her place, and in the name of "mourning the Holy Maiden," issued all sorts of bans on the Carnevale. But is that really what she would have wanted?
The Order's grip tightened, and the Carnevale performances were reduced to dull, monotonous shadows of their former selves.
One year, I strung a wire from a Gondola to the top of the clock tower in Liberty Square, and another from the tower to the Fisalia's mansion.
Then, I disguised myself as one of the La Guardia to fool the Acolytes and climbed to the roof along the wire...
Midway through the Order's performance, I hopped on a Wingray with a Cloudcaster, showering the entire city with flowers.
Yes, it was a magnificent sight. The Wingray soared higher than the Acolytes could reach. They couldn't do anything but watch golden-pink petals rain from the sky for three whole days.

They struggled to clean up the flowers from the streets, and it took a downpour to wash them all away. That Cloudcaster, adapted from a music van, became the prototype for the one we use on stage today.
Exactly what I'd expect from a Laureate.
No wonder you got banished by the Order...
But that's all in the past! To this day, I'm still not sure what crime they pinned on me. Maybe walking the wire without protection? Ha!
Anyway, I'm just an old relic now. But you lot, you're the main characters of this era, facing down every obstacle with fire in your bellies!
But isn't our fate already sealed? Without the so-called "salvation" the Order preaches, we're doomed to our banishment. Just lost souls, dying in obscurity...
Life is short, and we weren't born just to atone. The Order may banish us, but they can't take away our right to sing.
Death is one of many possible ends, but it's certainly not the worst. Perhaps being forgotten is what the Order wanted for us.
They want to erase all traces of our existence, grind us into dust, and drag us into the abyss... But we'll fight the tide and live our lives to the fullest.
Members of the troupe may come and go, but they've never truly left us. Their deeds and songs are passed down through the ages.
Is everything going smoothly with your family, Ms. Carlotta?
Yes, thank you. The Order's scheme was uncovered as planned. Uncle Capollo was rescued, and <ano=Head of the Montellis>Grandfather</ano> has handled the rest.
I still owe you thanks, {PlayerName}, for improvising with me in front of that Priest.
That's what I should say. You've always been helping me, with or without my knowing.
Don't worry. Your help has more than repaid your debt.
You've got a sharp mind. No pain, no gain, as Grandfather used to say. I'm pleased we're on the same page.
Your kindness is much appreciated. The Montellis won't forget this. In return, I'll share everything I know.
So, the Order has been targeting the Montellis.
No need to thank me, we share a common enemy.

I believe you've noticed that the Order has been undermining the family under the guise of its doctrines. Alienation, monopolization—just a few tricks up their sleeve. Their true motives, however, run deeper.
Their alliance with the Fractsidus speaks volumes. While we don't know the full extent of their conspiracy, one thing is clear: their sights are set on this year's Carnevale.
Legend has it that the Sentinel, Imperator, has been secluded in the heavens, cut off from the mortal realm. The last record of the Sentinel is from the Carnevale a decade ago.
At that time, the entire city was shrouded in mist. Ghosts roamed the streets, a dragon roared from the sky and a sea behemoth raged, summoning towering waves... Do any clues come to mind?
(Sort out the clues about Queen of the Night)
(Sort out the clues about the Vault Guards)
(Sort out the clues about the Dragon of Dirge)
(I've already figured out their schemes)
The mist might be coming from the Remnant Clouds in the Nimbus Sanctum. Lorelei has the power to purify and control them, but the Fractsidus interfered…
Remnant Clouds corrupted by evil will disrupt Echoes' frequencies. If the mist had spread to the city, it would have stirred the Echoes into chaos.
We are lucky that you and Zani, along with that Acolyte, awakened Lorelei in time. You prevented the mist from spreading and averted the Waveworn. The Fractsidus must still be licking their wounds.
The Montelli traitors used Lycoris in experiments to turn Echoes back into Tacet Discords... If they were successful, the "ghosts" seen ten years ago may have also been created this way.
"Ghost" is just a dramatic name given by the Ragunnesi for Tacet Discords. They look nearly identical to Echoes, especially in the mist.
With your help, Grandfather has thwarted their plan. No corrupted Echoes will appear at this year's Carnevale.
The Order has allied with the Fractsidus to control the dragon... From what I saw when I connected with its frequency, they might be planning to command it to attack Ragunna during the Carnevale.
After the Tacet Discords took over this isle, the Order used them as an excuse to forbid any entry. It might be their way of concealing the dragon's existence.
But without the Lycoris, the Dragon of Dirge is now off the table.
The Remnant Clouds spreading, experiments to turn Echoes, and the dragon's manipulation... The Order plans to recreate these disasters at this year's ceremony.
The Order and the Fractsidus are allies. To prevent the Carnevale's sabotage, we must stop them. But... what is their motive?
Let's consider the implications. If the Carnevale proceeds unhindered, how would it affect the Order?
(Bring up the prophecy about the Holy Maiden's coronation)
(Bring up the Sentinel's inability to communicate with mortals)

The current Primus claims to be the Enlightened One, the Sentinel's Resonator. However, based on the prophecy we found in the ruins, this role is meant for the young maiden who is destined to heed the divine oracles during the Carnevale.
The Carnevale is the only time humans can directly communicate with the Sentinel. Normally, it's the Primus who conveys the Sentinel's words.
A successful Carnevale offers a chance for citizens to meet the Sentinel in person. But for the Primus, and possibly the Order, it poses a threat if they've been fabricating the oracles.
The Primus called it a divine punishment and took the opportunity to appear as a savior. A perfect way to build legitimacy.
The Order relies on the people's faith in the Sentinel. With the Sentinel's ten year absence, faith in the Order has waned. They must be desperate to restore that trust.
It is for this reason that the Order has been forced to revive the festival.
To sabotage it while still maintaining their authority... they partnered with the Fractsidus.
The Fractsidus will cause chaos during the Carnevale, and the Order will swoop in as the saviors, restoring public trust just as they did before.
So far, you've helped us crush three of their schemes, but one remains...
The sea behemoth summoning towering waves...
Cetus the Tidebreaker?
We have evidence that the Cetus is being manipulated, and the Fractsidus are setting up their final plan. With their whereabouts unknown, we'll need to adapt our strategy as the Carnevale unfolds.
{PlayerName}, the Carnevale is likely where you'll find clues about the Sentinel.
From what I've noticed, you're not one to act passively or pin your hopes on others. You prefer to strike first and steer events in your favor.
Winning the Laurel might give you the chance to talk with the Sentinel. The Sentinel's Resonator may also be present. So...
You've guided me this far for it.
You want me to join you in stopping the Fractsidus.
You want me to join the troupe's performance at the Carnevale.
Our aim has always been clear—to restore the Carnevale to its former glory with a performance for the ages.
If the divine truly exists, would they wish to see their people living without freedom or witness a festival twisted into a tool for tyrants?
If we win the Laurel, we'll show that such punishment is absurd. But if that's truly their design... we shall break those divine shackles ourselves.
Whether divinity exists or not, we will fight for Ragunna's freedom, where everyone has the right to live and pursue a future of their own choosing!
The Montellis share this vision. Only in a free society can a fair and open market thrive.
However, the troupe alone is too weak, the family is under close watch, and our enemy hides in the shadows... We need your strength to find our way forward.
I agree. Count me in.
We're united by the same goal.
Seems there's no other way to meet the Sentinel than at the Carnevale.
Thank you. I'm pleased we've reached an agreement once more.
Our rehearsals are rather straightforward. No scripts, just pure intuition and our senses guiding us! That's what makes Commedia Improvviso truly come alive!
For our improvised comedy, we start with a theme. From there, we build our lines and act on the fly, responding to the unfolding show and audience reactions.

But with the limitless capacity for human creativity at play, the plot can sometimes veer into the... well, unconventional. To prevent things from spiraling too far, we set an "anchor" for the performance.
Pardon my interruption, but I'm quite curious. What sort of bizarre plots have you encountered?

Well, something like "A humble craftsman from a small town sets sail on a rainy night, stumbles upon ancient ruins, is reincarnated with super powers, and then decides to conquer the galaxy, becoming the Emperor of the Stars..."
So, we draft a basic outline that assigns roles and guides the plot's direction.

And this time, our outline is: "A kingdom is attacked, monsters run rampant, and the Demon King has kidnapped the Holy Maiden. A few brave heroes accept the minister's quest to defeat the Demon King and rescue her."
A real classic, no doubt.
Sounds a bit cliché...
So, a classic adventure story.
This outline holds special meaning. We want to pay tribute to the play once performed by the Blessed Maiden herself, which was also about a hero facing a Demon King.
Good people have their wishes fulfilled, heroes appear in a time of crisis, justice triumphs over evil, and united friends are undefeatable.
This is the tale the Blessed Maiden once told, and it's a universal story we want to portray.
To me, the world is a stage, and performing is much like combat. Coordinated movements, quick thinking, sharp reflexes, and, above all, trust in your allies.

[About]
The Moon-Chasing Festival is a Huanglong traditional festival that features various origin stories, with the most popular being the tale of The Fox and the Moon. On this special night, families and friends come together to admire the moon and make wishes, expressing their hopes for a brighter future.

[Eligibility]
Reach Union Level 17. For the best experience, complete "Thaw of Eons" before participating in this event.

[Event Rules]
1. Help Xiangli Yao prepare for the Moonlit Fair to boost the festival's Popularity.
2. Increase Popularity by fulfilling Wishes and building stalls.
3. Invite Companions to assist in preparations by completing the corresponding Side Quests, and earn higher Wish Ratings and Funds.
4. Achieve the festival goals to claim and redeem rewards.
5. After the event concludes, unclaimed rewards will remain available for 30 days and will be reissued via Mail when you log in during this period (Note: Rewards that have not been redeemed will not be reissued.)
Popularity

1. During the Moon-Chasing Festival, you can increase Popularity via the activities in <color=#8c7e51>Lodge Wishes</color> and <color=#8c7e51>Fair Stalls</color> to make the Moonlit Fair more lively.
2. Popularity ranges from Level 1 to Level 6.
Fair Stalls

1. Build or upgrade stalls to increase Popularity, gain buffs, and unlock Companions.
2. Building or upgrading stalls requires Funds, which can be earned by completing Wishes in Lodge Wishes.
3. Stalls can be upgraded multiple times, with higher levels providing greater buffs.
4. After building a stall, you can participate in the stall's activities and may earn unexpected rewards, with additional daily rewards for Thus Says the Moon, Hsin's Fortuity, and Riddle Twiddle.
Lodge Wishes

1. You can spend Preparation Credits and Funds to fulfill people's Wishes in <color=#8c7e51>Lodge Wishes</color>. Each Wish has its own resource cost.
2. Fulfilling Wishes will earn you Funds and Wish Tags. Setting new records will boost Popularity.
3. Send the right Companions to fulfill the Wishes in <color=#8c7e51>Lodge Wishes</color>. You can view their detailed stats on the Companions page.
Lodge Wishes Rules

There is a preferred Companion Stat for each Wish. Selecting your Companions accordingly will earn you a higher score.
To boost your Companions' stats, interact with them on the Companions page.

Preparation Underway: Your Companions act in turn, earning scores based on their stats.
Scoring Rules: Scores fluctuate each round, as your Companions can't always perform at their absolute best. Nevertheless, Companions with higher stats have the potential to earn higher scores.
During preparation, Companions may experience a "Eureka" moment. The likelihood of this occurring varies for each Companion.
"Eureka" allows for additional investments. Higher risks yield greater rewards. Make your choice wisely.
Results: A Wish Rating depends on the combined scores of your chosen Companions. Higher Ratings earn you more Funds and Wish Tags.
Companions

1. Companions can help you fulfill Wishes in <color=#8c7e51>Lodge Wishes</color>.
2. They have three stats: Knowledge, Action, and Teamwork. Higher stats and better matches with the Wish's recommended stat lead to higher Wish Ratings.
3. Build and upgrade <color=#8c7e51>Fair Stalls</color> and complete the <color=#8c7e51>Festival Journal</color> quests series to unlock more Companions.
Interacting with Companions

1. You can interact with Companions to boost their stats and Bond Level.
2. Each Interaction has its own cost of Wish Tags. A higher cost results in greater enhancements.
3. Complete Wishes in <color=#8c7e51>Lodge Wishes</color> to earn Wish Tags.

The kernel used by the Tethys System appears vastly different from our current terminal systems. The primary difference is that Tethys's hardware layer is completely invisible to us, and its software language seems to be from an era beyond our own...

...However, my observations have revealed a few intriguing details. While Tethys's code remains tightly guarded, I detect the presence of a stored-program logic architecture - a tried and true computer structure. This design relies on a central processor to access stored data and instructions and carry out computations...

In other words, the Lament data, which is visualized as stars in Tethys, must flow through a system capable of reading and processing it...

Similarly, Tethys shares the same bottleneck as traditional stored-program architectures: its efficiency is limited by the central processor's read/write speed. Just as insufficient fuel limits a spacecraft's performance...

However, it seems Tethys employs another logic structure that integrates the entire central processor physically, allowing it to handle all instructions and data simultaneously. This necessitates a processor of unimaginable power, one capable of managing the data throughput of something as massive as the Black Shores... Why would Tethys incorporate such a complex logic structure?

Investigation Report on the Black Shores' Portals

Applicant: Gardner, Monica
Application Type: Clearance Application

Body Text: 
A causality assessment of the collected data confirmed a normal distribution, with no significant anomalies detected. However, during real-time regional information monitoring, unnatural frequency fluctuations were observed, specifically associated with the access doors.

To verify these findings, a 48-hour real-time data investigation was conducted. Access to the Black Shores system database enabled the correction of anomalous entries and the isolation of a dataset exhibiting characteristics linked to the access doors. Hypotheses were subsequently formulated, followed by a regression analysis and re-simulated modeling based on historical data and relevant theories.

For comprehensive details, please refer to the appendix. Key conclusions from the data analysis include:
1. The intensity of abnormal frequency fluctuations of the access doors is strongly correlated with the sequence in which they are activated.
2. The peak frequency band of these fluctuations bears a high similarity to the high-frequency range of the overlapping section in the current Necrostar frequency history.
3. The transient model of these peak frequencies shows some resemblance to the transient model of an Overclocked Resonator connected to the Black Shores' Terminal.

Based on this, the report confirms that the rumors hold some validity. Among the filtered data, the highest correlation of abnormal frequencies is linked with the grouping of <color=Highlight>Lower Levels of the Hall of Foreign Affairs—Haven of Sprouts—Platform of the Hall of Foreign Affairs</color>.

While no field tests have been conducted yet, further study of the <color=Highlight>sequence and pattern of access door usage</color> may yield significant insights in the next phase.

Additionally, during the on-site investigation, I re-verified the relevant movement path, which was frequently used in past Black Shores debriefing processes. Given Conclusion 3, I suspect this event may be connected to certain historical incidents at the Black Shores.

...In light of these findings, I believe that any potential lead towards locating missing employees warrants serious consideration. Therefore, I formally request higher-level permissions to access historical data for further investigation.

I'm curious to see how you will handle the clash between civilization's greater good and humanity's spirit.

Yes. When Ragunnesi first settled here, they revered the Sentinel. The Carnevale was their tribute—a sacred rite to commune with it.
It seemed the Sentinel Imperator preferred not to flaunt its power overtly to command the people's awe and respect.
Yet, amidst the Carnevale's revelry, it performed miracles, keeping the people aligned with its guidance.
Legend has it that, moved by its grace, the most devout believer braved storms and mists to find the Sentinel—thus was born the tradition of the Pilgrim's Sail.
Should you wish, I have more stories to tell.
Eh, don't worry! We Ragunnesi do not worry over tomorrow. Why not get some flowers for the children? Prices may rise with the Carnevale approaching.
Ah, you just don't understand...
It's okay. Rules are rules.
Can we enter the city now?
Thank you for your understanding. Please follow me.
Certainly. Please follow me.
(H-how am I supposed to know? I haven't had anything to eat since we left for Rinascita. So hungry...)
It's not that... Members of the Order are instructed to maintain a distance from Echoes. We must stay objective to better share knowledge about them and honor our duty to inform the public.
That Echo we saw is known as a Hocus Pocus. Children love its tricks, and they say that if an adult gets its gift, they can relive their happiest memories in dreams... ah...
...Sorry, I got carried away.
I think it sounds interesting.
Is that tower the Nexus?
...Yes. Allow me to introduce to you the Nexus of Ragunna, also known as the Genesis Nexus.
Yes, but the Ragunnesi prefer to call it the Genesis Nexus.
Input your personal information into the Nexus, and you'll be able to use all Common Echoes in the city just like a regular citizen.
Please place your terminal here.
With might and justice, I rule from the throne, silencing ocean's tumult under my reign alone.
For those who refuse to drown in swirling waves, heed this doctrine: Seek salvation from where all began.
A brief history lesson, please?
This inscription tells the tale of Rinascita's founding. Legends speak of a group of displaced people, driven from their lands by the Lament.
Though their origins were different, they followed the same ocean currents to a hidden sea.
They prayed for paradise but were met with a nightmare filled with Tacet Discords. The sky darkened, the sea roared, and towering waves threatened to engulf them.
At that moment, a radiant light pierced the clouds, and a voice resounded from the sky—
"Make the waters your second home, like seabirds nesting along the coast. Build your shelters hither and thither, like stars in the night sky."
"Your fortress is fragile, made only of wickers and planks, but fear not, for it is strong enough to withstand the wuthering waves."
Heeding the heavenly voice, the displaced united. A gentle breeze guided their ships, filling their sails with wind.
Through the storm, they glimpsed a bright light from an unnamed island. This was the light of the Genesis Nexus.

The Nexus granted them knowledge of Echoes and sent them to help build their cities. The people named the island Rinascita and built sanctuaries with inscriptions, honoring the voice that guided them to paradise.
The voice did indeed reveal itself. The faithful saw the true form of their savior, who declared its sacred name—Imperator.
This inscription tells the tale of Rinascita's founding. Legends speak of a group of displaced people, driven from their lands by the Lament.
Guided by the Nexus, they found refuge on this island where they learned the secrets of the Echoes and, under the Sentinel's watch, rebuilt their lives.
This legend is known widely among the Ragunnesi, though the true beginnings of Rinascita remain shrouded in lost history. Scholars of the Order have never stopped their quest to uncover it.
Got it. Now where can we meet the Sentinel?
You wish for an audience with the Sentinel...?
Has anyone done this before?
I heard you can talk with the Sentinel during the Carnevale.
Yes, only one person has received such an honor—the current Primus, Fenrico.
...Yes. The Sentinel bestows the Laurel, through which the chosen one can hear Their voice. Only one has received such an honor—the current Primus, Fenrico.
As the only Enlightened One in recorded history, Primus Fenrico can directly connect with the Sentinel to heed divine oracles.
Meaning they can resonate with the Sentinel?

...Indeed. Primus Fenrico is the Sentinel Imperator's Resonator. As such he bears the title the Enlightened One. You'll have the chance to see him at the Carnevale when he announces the opening of the ceremony.
I hope you enjoy your time here in Ragunna and join in with the festivities.
If you need help with anything, just let me know. As an Acolyte, it's my job to assist all our visitors.
...The last one. Thanks.
And this {Male=gentleman;Female=lady} here... A visitor from afar? It's a pleasure.
I am her guest.
I am Zani's new friend.
I see. You certainly have the air of someone who matters.
Here, look at this. You can order anything you like. The Montellis are getting the bill.
Any recommendations?
I'll have two portions of the platter Zani just ordered.
Bring me all your specials!
How about Steak Margherita and Nuvola Pasta? Both excellent choices!
The woman speaks the truth.
Oh, good choice! Zani's taste will never let you down.
Right away!
No offense but... you sure you can eat all that by yourself?
That's the least of my worries.
Take a seat! Your meals will be ready soon!
Good. Let's go this way. It's right over there.
In other words, the Echo will be reset in the Data Bank. That's how we Ragunnesi usually deal with malfunctioning Echoes.
We deeply apologize for the disturbance caused by that undisciplined Echo… Now, please excuse me. I have other matters to attend to.

The entity at the heart of the Tethys System might... indeed be the Tethys System itself.

Patroller.
Undercover agent.
I'm nobody...
Ask any Patroller if they recognize you. They would only see you as a defector.
You are no Patroller, Yinlin. You never will be.

You are no Public Security agent, Yinlin. Your foolishness has ruined everything.

I'm... nobody...

I have to stop myself!
Something's wrong with this mission.
No, everything's fine.
"Red Eagle" confirmed this mission was a bust.
He's the mole in the Public Security Bureau.
You did nothing wrong.
How could I have known...
No, you knew it all along. Just not in this place.
The mission was a success. You caught the mole and put an end to the Blue Camel's dealings.
As for the Patrollers, you never attacked them.
But I made the wrong judgement...
I put my trust in the wrong person.

You're just too afraid of making mistakes, that's why you dream these things.
You've only ever had yourself to rely on, but still, you never waver.
Think about that question again. Who are you, really?
I am who I am...
I am Yinlin.
You're nothing, Yinlin!
Enough talking, Dollmaker. You've lost yourself.

[About]
Arno, a special agent of the Black Shores, is currently looking for help in gathering Surveillance Datasets on the Lament with the promise of generous rewards. Interested individuals are welcome to speak with him.

[Eligibility]
Reach Union Level 14 and complete Main Quest Act VII "Thaw of Eons."

[Event Rules]
1. During the event, you need to activate challenges across different regions. You can participate in any unlocked challenge as many times as you want.
2. After the challenge starts, Surveillance Datasets will appear. Try to collect as many Surveillance Datasets as possible within the time limit. Once all existing Datasets are collected, new Datasets will appear. The more Datasets you collect, the better the rewards.
3. There are various modules available in the challenges. Utilize them strategically to speed up Dataset collection.
4. If there are any unclaimed rewards after the event ends, they will be automatically sent to your inbox when you log in again within 30 days.

Final preparations are underway. This team will deploy shortly.

I've never regretted the decisions I've made, and I hope this one won't be an exception.
Okay, to tighten the scanner on the Anchor, we need...
A screw, not Drew.
...It's really not funny to keep joking about my name.
But you can't do this without a screw, Drew.
I'm so tired… When are we going to finish clearing all this corrupted data?
Checking every device does take time.

I checked your progress today. You're almost done, so hang in there.
KU-Baski is lying on the ground. It seems to be mimicking humans by resting.
Don't leave the Black Shores with such a weight in your heart.
What I meant to tell you is that you've done an outstanding job.
You've protected many from harm and contributed significantly to the Black Shores' understanding of the Lament's origin.

Please have faith that the things you did have left a positive impact, no matter how intractable at first. The momentum of change you've started will tilt the track of history for the better and leave a mark on your life.
These changes will endure, even if you leave the Black Shores.
Ms. Eleanor...?
Did you notice? The seed you brought from your hometown has fully bloomed now.
Thank you, Artemisia, for everything.
Check this out, Gedao! Pastries from Xiehua Village! Aalto and Encore brought it back from Jinzhou for us.
I've been handling Jinzhou-related affairs, but I've never actually been there myself. All I know is data, just data.

I never expected to get a gift from that village. It feels like the locals are acknowledging my work.
Speaking of which, I wonder how things are in Jinzhou now...
Still under observation, but we don't have time to dwell on it. With Tethys affected by corrupted data, we've got a ton of data to process.
Ha, another day of overtime...
Mmm, the pastries are so good! Want some?

Next time we're on vacation, we should go to Jinzhou and try the local dishes!
Hope I can see it sprout one day...

What did you plant?
I see. Do you enjoy these flowers too?
Every plant here carries the experiences of its owner. Some are pleasant, some regretful. They're like living memories of our past.
Did you plant anything here? If so, I wonder what stories it might tell.
I come here often, praying for my platycodon seed to bloom someday.
It's platycodon, a flower from my hometown. When I planted it here, I didn't realize it would be the last of its kind.
Your hometown...
It was destroyed in the Lament. This seed is all that's left now, the only proof of its existence.
Do you think... the Lament can truly erase everything?
I returned to the ruins of my hometown as an agent, hoping to collect leftover Reverberations, thinking I might uncover the truth of the disaster or find traces of the past.
But I was wrong. Everything I knew is gone, existing only in my memories.
However, what if those memories fade with time? What if I forget them, and start to believe they never existed at all...
No... As long as I have this flower, I'll never forget them.

We should guide these little ones based on their development, not just force changes on them.

"Yet, should that infinitesimal chance arise, I would open my eyes as if newly born, seeing everything one last time before dissolving again into the ceaseless flow of stars."

The Black Shores

Tucked away in the tempestuous Stormy Sea lies an archipelago known for its lavish Tacetite deposits and as a refuge for the world's most talented individuals. With a mission to combat the destructive Lament, the Black Shores has fostered strong partnerships with nations across Solaris-3.

The archipelago cannot be accessed from any known lands. Only those recognized by the Black Shores or who have received an invitation and guidance can navigate their way to this hidden place.

Members of the Black Shores who operate abroad, frequently traversing various lands, are known as "Consultants." Those stationed at the headquarters are referred to as "Bloom Bearers." Apart from these fundamental duties, the Black Shores also accommodates a plethora of other specialized roles.

Though the Black Shores openly shares its advanced technologies with its partners, even its own members remain unaware of the true origins of these innovations.
The Tethys System

Also known as the Civilization Simulation Sand Table, the Tethys System is a supercomputer unique to the Black Shores. By inputting Lament frequency data—collected both manually and via beacon access—into the system, the Black Shores can issue Lament warnings for locations worldwide within a 24 to 48-hour time range. This capability is the cornerstone of the Black Shores' extensive collaborations with countries across the globe.

The results generated by the Tethys System are projected as a starry sky within the underground of the Black Shores, made possible by multiple Anchors and underground Data Hubs. This has earned the underground region the title "City of Eternal Night".

The Tethys System has no discernible energy source, physical infrastructure, or processing core. Its coding language is extremely complex, and it is only known that its terminals take the form of various autonomous robots. In essence, the Tethys System is almost akin to a natural phenomenon, with an origin that remains entirely mysterious.
The Black Shores Robots

These unique robots, found throughout the Black Shores, serve as the physical terminals of the Tethys System. Their construction and performance capabilities remain largely unknown, yet they possess direct access to the system, second only to its administrator. Within the Black Shores, these robots function both as assistants and tools in the daily activities of its members.

Each terminal has a distinct personality, and the study of these robots has advanced the field of cognitive psychology.
Stellar Matrix

Based on the computational protocols of the Tethys System, the Stellar Matrix is a data package format that functions similarly to a highly compressed file. It has the capacity to store immense amounts of information and even simulate a Lament. Certain individuals can access these matrices under specific circumstances, making them an integral part of the Tethys System's operational framework.

Properly functioning Stellar Matrices are projected into the subterranean galaxy of the Black Shores, allowing members to study and observe them. Malfunctioning matrices, however, are collected and isolated in designated areas to prevent data overflow.
The first member to define a Stellar Matrix noted that standards of observing and evaluating one are similar to the astronomical standards of Solaris-3.
Modulation

Modulation is the process of adjusting frequencies. In Solaris-3, frequencies serve as a crucial tool for uncovering the truth about reality. By altering these frequencies, one can delve into the very core of existence.

At the Black Shores, modulating Stellar Matrices is crucial for tracing and analyzing the Lament. Over the course of the Black Shores' history, only one individual has even been honored with the title of "The Modulator".
The Shorekeeper

A mysterious lifeform that rests beneath the Black Shores' subterranean galaxy. Her physical structure and age are shrouded in mystery. In the complicated coding language of the Tethys System, the name "Shorekeeper" also means "Guardian of Secrets". She chose to call herself "Shorekeeper" to symbolize her role in watching over those who venture away from the shores into faraway lands.
