I dodged those pesky "eyes" the whole way here, worried you'd been kept waiting too long. But it seems you've kept yourself entertained.
So the old gentleman was simply hiding from the rain, was he? I see... The Montelli Quarter does attract art enthusiasts. Anyway, I'm glad prying eyes didn't follow.
When it rains in Ragunna, surprises are as common as puddles. A delay is only a small splash.
Calling you here with little explanation and a word of caution... I can only imagine your confusion.
It's taken me by surprise.
You and your uncle both...
The Montellis enjoy their intrigue, don't they?
The Montelli's path is not always paved with roses, but with thorns as well. As the heir apparent, my uncle bears many burdens.
Seeing me work with you on the Carnevale under Grandfather's orders might have unsettled him, leading to a hasty, misguided move.
How do you feel about this?
Will this change your plans?
In truth, I haven't thought about it, and my opinions hold little weight.
The current plan has proven effective. I believe it's wise to trust Grandfather's judgment, as I always do.
Besides, I now have more important duties to fulfill.
The shark in our midst has finally made its move.
Recently, several of our partners claimed to have found a superior seller and ended their dealings with us.
Meanwhile, Benett, our vault keeper, was reported to have embezzled and sold vault assets. It's said that he tried to flee but was killed by Tacet Discords outside the city.
So Benett betrayed the family as well?
I am not so sure... I've worked with Benett before. He was principled, bold but not reckless, not one to easily betray. And...

The night he died, he sent a photo to my Terminal—a blood-stained page of an anthology, marked with three phrases. "Thy eyes guide my course in the tempest," "When forty winters siege thy beauty," and "The planet turns right, twice and a half."
That's rather cryptic.
Okay, but... it makes no sense.
The meaning is yet to be revealed, but he is clearly conveying a message.

The Montelli family is a symbol of liberation for Ragunna. We uphold freedom and equality for all. Our vault is the heart of our family, and if it's corrupted, it threatens not only us, but risks plunging the city back into oppression and isolation.
As much as I hate to suspect family members, I cannot rule any of them out.
You, however, are different. As an outsider who has aided us in capturing the initial traitors... I hope to not be proven wrong, but I feel that I can trust you.
So you're asking for my help.
I suppose this is when I volunteer to help.
My uncle's words were clear. Only those at the table can play the game. To engage with my family, one must have both standing and purpose.
So, I offer you a new identity in our upcoming inquiry—Cat's Eye, a provisional member under my patronage.
But I'm not truly a member of the family.
This... is obviously a lie.
If you wish to join, you must undertake the final assessment and pledge your loyalty to the Montellis.
Oh, don't worry, we aren't harming anyone. It is but a subtle adaptation of the rules.
Why Cat's Eye though?
When it comes to family matters, we like to use codenames, each tied to a unique token. Mine, for example, is Opal.
Opal recommended Cat's Eye. It has a ring to it, don't you think?
Also, have you looked closely at your own eyes? They share the same luster as Cat's Eye gems.
Well, you recommended me, so it's your call.
We must prevent this threat and bring peace to Ragunna.
I want to uncover the true identity of this lurking shark.
I understand decorum is important to the Montellis. But among friends, can't we be a bit more... informal?
What made you say that?
You're always one step ahead. How about we slow down and savor the present?
Hmm, you're curious who I am beyond my role, is that it?
Hmm, I just might entertain that thought.
But for now, my agents just sent me the address of Benett's residence. While his body has been found, what he left behind is still out there.
Let's try our luck at his residence.
All evidence points to Benett being the key to uncovering the shark lurking in our waters.
Now, Cat's Eye, will you stand with me to catch the traitor within our family and avert this looming threat?
It seems someone has acted faster. Those two... They're my uncle's agents, Sage and Acorn.
Codenames?
Those are not real names.
Yes, we address each other by codenames—handy identifiers in a crowd.
I'll keep you updated on the family members' codenames we encounter, along with any other details you might need.
Seems like they are looking for something as well.
It's only natural my uncle wishes to retrieve the lost items... but my presence might raise a few eyebrows.
I'll go have a little chat with them to see what they know.
You can find a way around them and continue the investigation.
Yes, you try and loosen their lips. If memory serves, they are senior members, having served under my uncle for years. Regulars at Margherita's.
Talk business with merchants, and wine with drinkers... Engage their interests, and their words will flow like a river. As for the rest...
I'll improvise as needed.
You tell Carlotta what you learned from the recovered Terminal data.
I see... so Duncan was in the dark about the real cause of Benett's death. He simply wanted to protect his friend's reputation, and Capollo used that.
Duncan gave us a rigged Terminal to cover Benett's "debt", clearing his name.
I can empathize with Duncan, even to some extent Capollo. They are driven by a desire for safety and stability—a tempting future even for me.
But we will never achieve that by surrendering ourselves to the Order.
From the very beginning, our paths diverged. To yield to them now means giving up even more, and once we lose our grip, we'll no longer have the luxury of refusal.
Grandfather and the others have already paved the way. I will follow their lead and chart a course towards a brighter tomorrow. For our family, and all of Ragunna.
An all-out war with the Order isn't a wise move. Rather than blindly tailing Capollo in search of a hidden data module, let's take control and have him come to us.
Scarlet Velvet mentioned they need a formal reply, and we can deliver that.
{PlayerName}, care to help me give them an unforgettable response in two days?
We're taking the initiative. I like it.
Have him come to us... That makes things interesting.

Capollo <color=yellow>couldn't have tampered</color> with the Terminal data himself, or he would have found the information hidden beneath the overwrites. He simply laid a trap at <color=yellow>the dock that Benett visited</color>.
Wealth and power will safeguard our freedom, while freedom, in turn, will nurture wealth and power.

The Montelli family is set to break the Order's suffocating hold and lead Ragunna towards a wider horizon—embracing Septimont, Huanglong, and other countries. And through it all, we will never forget who we are.
The family exists to accomplish what one cannot and withstand the winds of fate. This is the future I envision for the Montellis.
What do you plan to do next?
Like I said, we seize control.
Acorn, Sage...
Hey, that's you they're calling.
No, that's both of us. But I don't recognize this person.
Neither do I. Listen up.
Acorn, Sage...
Okay, you got the names right. Must be family. Who are you?
I'm Cat's Eye, new to the family.
I'm a Montelli.
Cat's Eye? Doesn't ring a bell... Probably one of those new recruits after the Carnevale.
Heh, we are all Montellis here. Remember, when someone asks, use your codename.
Oh, it's Cat's Eye.
A rookie, huh? Learning the ropes with contacts and all. No wonder you look unfamiliar.
So, what do you need? We are just about to wrap up and grab a bite at Margherita's. Still got a lot on our plate today.
(Strike up a conversation about being a newcomer.)
(Strike up a conversation about Margherita's.)
Say, I've heard whispers of your skills. Seeing you here, it's clear you're on an important mission, aren't you?
I haven't faced a true challenge since I got here. Would you accept my help? I'm sure I'd learn a thing or two.
Easy, haha. We've just finished up. So, nothing more to help with.
But here's something I can tell you. Someone tried to steal from the vault recently.
Oh, Margherita's! Nothing quite like it, hm? And the pizza... Oh, it's a favorite in my circle, too.
Ah! Always a solid choice when on the move. Perfect spot for a bit of catching up.
You know, the last time I was there, I heard talk about a thief stealing from the vault. Is that true?
Well, cat's out of the bag now. See that house right there? That's where the thief lived. We came to search for clues.
Did you recover the stolen goods?
No, not yet. We've looked everywhere but found nothing.
To be honest, I doubt we'll ever find them. The thief has probably sold everything off by now, and we are short on manpower. That's a needle in a haystack if you ask me.
Isn't your boss worried?
Boss doesn't seem too worried... is there a plan B?
Well, our boss is the Padrino's son. He has his methods.
Our job is to follow orders, not to ask questions. Just do what we're told and do it well.
That's right. If you spot anything unusual, keep an eye on it. Could be your big break. With a bit more time, I think you'll do just fine.
(That should do it.)
(Time to meet up with Carlotta.)
Your guests won't be showing up today.
Ha, Carlotta… Looks like you've pieced together the whole story. So it was your crew who tipped us off about changing the time and place for the deal yesterday.
Let me guess. You fed the same line to the Order, didn't you? Playing both sides, setting yourself up nicely… But something doesn't add up. You couldn't have pulled this off alone.
Capollo's promises of safety and comfort are nothing but a sham. He has been <color=yellow>using our family as pawns</color>, making them pay the ultimate price. Benett was just one of his victims.
He didn't fall at the hands of Tacet Discords but to Capollo himself. His body was disposed of outside the city's limits... The truth is, Benett never betrayed us.
The path of the Montelli family is one of unity. We stand together, leaving no one behind.
I can't promise there won't be more losses, but I will prioritize the welfare of every member. I do not take sacrifice lightly.
Now, will you continue down this path? Or will you align with our cause for Bennett's sake and your own?
Trust built on deception always comes back to haunt you. You're getting what you deserve.
…You're right, I've crossed a line. But I can still salvage this if I take you out here and reclaim that data module.
Now that you've lost both the goods and your trading partners… this is your last chance to bow out gracefully.
Bow out gracefully? Do you think I still care about saving face at this point?
My only regret is not being ruthless enough… I should've cut you loose earlier, making you pay the price like the others who crossed me.
You've betrayed your family's ideals.
And what of it? You'll never understand!
We lack the power to protect everyone, so what's wrong with seeking a powerful ally? Why not align ourselves with those who share my true goal?
You rendezvous with Carlotta after her investigation and share the information you gathered.
So, they found nothing, but assumed Uncle wasn't concerned?
That makes no sense. Everything that happened recently ties back to the vault. If Uncle wished to protect his position, he'd be quick to retrieve the items and resolve the situation.
Maybe he's hiding something.
Maybe he's in control all along.
Things don't add up.
Curiously, Benett was last sighted in the vicinity of <color=yellow>Liberty Square</color>, where you met Uncle.
Last night, I was investigating the area before I happened upon your private meeting.
That explains why you were there...
But when I brought this up to him afterward, he didn't seem privy to any details.
As for my search of Benett's home, nothing of note turned up, just as the two agents reported.
I found no spoils, not even the faintest trace of them being stored or moved... Everything about his living space fits the profile of a typical junior vault employee.
I've also asked around about Bennet after our previous collaboration. He was ambitious, but never greedy. I was even told he refused the bribe offered by a business associate during an operation.
The Montelli family is ever generous with wealth and opportunities, welcoming all who aspire to make their mark in Ragunna. Mere profit would never make him betray us.
The family protects its members.
Members bring the family glory.
For now, more evidence is required. The entire matter might need to be approached from a different angle...
Shh, hold still... See that man over there, the one that looks like a gray dove?
Without making a movement, you follow Carlotta's line of sight. Not far away, a man, partially hidden, is frequently glancing in your direction. He seems to be observing you and Carlotta.
Noticing your gaze, he immediately starts running.
After him, quick.
The rain's back. I remember telling Grandfather how I hated the rainy season.
I once saw rain as a bad omen in Ragunna.
When it rains, it's easier to wash away blood stains. That's why acts of revenge usually happen on such days.
But today's rain feels different. As it falls, the troubles of yesterday are washed away. I feel calm, like I've found my true self again. My present and my future are now in my own hands.
Well done, Carlotta. And thank you, {PlayerName}.
My girl could not have accomplished this without your assistance.
She personally invited and vouched for me, after all.
She is capable enough in her own right.
I had faith in you two, but you surpassed my expectations.
It appears I underestimated the potential that you possess when working together.
What he just said... Looks like someone has been keeping secrets from me, huh?
I've been curious, you entered that Sonoro and delivered his gun to me. How did you earn my grandfather's trust so soon?
That's a story between the two of us.
I'll tell you next time.
Hm, the nerve... Fine, since we make such a good team, I'll let it slide for now.
Capollo and his lackeys will face the consequences of their actions. Our code is simple—vengeance for blood, death for life. No one is exempt.
There's a lot at play here. It will require some effort and a true Montelli at my side to handle it.
I see. I'll take care of the rest.
But before that...
Are you leaving?
Yes. What, miss me already?
Of course not.
Yes, I'll miss you. Who knows when I'll see you again.
Well... maybe a little.
"No need to feel sad about parting, for each goodbye brings us closer to the next hello."
That's my favorite way to think of it—a countdown to our next reunion.
With Capollo ousted, the family needs someone to fill his shoes. I must assist my grandfather through this tumultuous transition. There is no one else to do it.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. As my grandfather said, things couldn't have gone so smoothly without your help and support.
Now that the dust has settled, you no longer need to stay with me as Cat's Eye of the Montelli family, but still... I want you to have this.
As I said, every member gets a token that matches their codename.
Though you already have a pair of Cat's Eyes, please accept this as a token of my appreciation. No, this gem wasn't crafted by my Forte. I chose it just for you.
I know someone like you won't stay just for me, and joining the Montelli family might not be in your plans just yet.
But I'll keep this codename for you, Cat's Eye—the first and only member to receive my personal invitation.
Nowhere to run. Now it's time for a proper chat.
Hah... These old, creaky bones of mine.
Did I offend you? Or are you just chasing down every passing soul... Never thought the Montellis would grow so aggressive.
No running, no chasing.
Just a glance and you can tell we're Montellis?
He had no choice but to run, to escape his past and sever any ties with the Montellis.
No one knows the family's ways better than its members, even though... he is no longer one of us.
Right, Old Duncan?
Ha, hahaha... I must admit, you have an annoyingly good memory.
It's remarkable that someone of your rank would remember a man such as myself.
I will never forget that <color=yellow>stormy</color> night, nor any of the members who were caught in it.
Sadly, I've no desire to be remembered. To me, Montelli is only a name of the past.
There were moments of joy, but they cannot make up for my loss... now I only feel tired.
If that's true, why are you here?
You say one thing, but do another.
Why go back to what you claim to have left in the past? Unless there's something you can't ignore.

You were standing across from Benett's doorway, and your clothes are still damp from the rain... You weren't simply passing by, you were watching. What were you looking for? Or should I ask, what did you hope to find?
I don't know.
To grieve for my last friend in the family? To blame him for being so reckless and greedy?
Or to figure out how this fool ended up in such a mess, hoping to find the lost items and settling his debts, so he may rest in peace?
I tried to persuade him to leave with me, but failed. In Ragunna's game, the Montelli family has only two options.
We either play to win, or are forced to leave with nothing.
Every Montelli has a chance at their desires, but what's the price... They stake everything they hold dear—family, love, faith, principles, and even their life.
Now... his ambition and greed have cost him everything.
But you can decide when to leave the table.
Is that why you left the family?
Most people find acceptance easier than change, as change demands the bravery to face uncertainty. No great endeavor is without its perils.
So yes, if the Montellis are to drive the change and push past current barriers, the path ahead will be anything but easy.
The family exists to withstand what an individual cannot, and accomplish what might otherwise be unattainable.
But within the family, each Montelli still enjoys the freedom of choice. Your leaving is a testiment to this, is it not?
If you're willing, there is still much to be done for Benett. His Terminal, the alleged stolen goods... everything but his body remains missing.
Given your familiarity, you might help us in locating these items...
Benett's death may not be as simple as it looks.
We were also looking for more clues in his home.
...In that case, you might want to speak to Scarlet Velvet.
Who is this Scarlet Velvet?
The leader of a network of commoners seeking freedom in Ragunna City. They had close ties with Benett. If he was really stealing, I'd wager they were complicit.
That said, with their recent fallout with the family, I can't guarantee you'll find them, let alone talk to them.
We have little choice but to try.
Now... let's go, {PlayerName}. We're off to the most reliable source of information in Ragunna.
This is the place.
The best place for information... is a pub?
I don't think Scarlet Velvet would hide somewhere so public.
She may not be here, but I have my ways of reaching her people.
In Ragunna's market, they say fortune seldom favors those who lack a taste for fine drinks.
Among traders, there's a secret <color=yellow>"code"</color> in the way drinks are mixed.
A base of bitter almond and mint, for instance, usually signals danger and death. But some have devised their own, more private codes.
So they send messages by what they order.
So it's not just a drink, it's a conversation.
Yes. This area is essentially a neutral zone in the city. No affiliations, no restrictions.
With the ongoing feud between Scarlet Velvet and the Montellis, finding her will be difficult. But I've heard they have eyes and ears here.
So all that remains is to order the right drink, watch the crowd, and let their reactions lead us to Scarlet Velvet's contact.
Greetings, what will it be today?
A Scarlet Velvet Ribbon, please.
Scarlet Velvet... An uncommon choice. Perhaps the one you seek is waiting just as patiently. May you both find what you've come for.
The wild desires, they swallow me like the roaring waves. Oh, how maddening is your tender love! I'd forsake all, just to be forever lost in your embrace...
Hello.
But is this amber drink... a deadly poison, or a healing tonic?
Excuse me...
No, leave me be! Don't bother me!
The void... the endless void has consumed me. I want no part in anything... Who are you, and who am I?
Montelli, Fisalia, the Order, the commoners—without these names, what sets us apart? But reality is cruel, and we have no refuge!
Seems like the alcohol has brought out his inner bard.
Is he just drunk or completely out of it...
For a moment, you sense a pair of eyes on you from where you picked up your drink. But as you turn to look, the feeling quickly fades away.
Let's go. Clearly he's not the one we are looking for.
With unyielding determination, the heroes accept the challenge!
The Demon King summons its foul army, poised for a climactic battle with the heroes... The victor will soon be revealed.
Amidst the clashing swords and the cries of the minions, the heroes face the Demon King—victory belongs to the righteous and the brave!
And now, we await the Holy Maiden's return...
And so we arrive at the "happily ever after," yes?
But we do not live in a fairy tale. There is no playwright to script a happy ending for us... What lies behind the curtain is but a cruel jest, a dark satire.
Let me reveal the truth behind that idyllic ending. The Holy Maiden has long succumbed to darkness, drawing power from a heretical force and leading her people into depravity.
And the minister, having uncovered this truth, has vowed to root out this corruption himself.
(There are Fisalia markings on these crates. What's inside?)
(Something's being wrapped in these strange frequencies. I should clear them out first.)
The cloud continues to spread. You may be right. This could be Imperator's test, but we must leave.
Do as you please! I'm not leaving. The relic of the Ancient One is here somewhere. I must...
How intriguing. These seem to be Reverberations hidden in the sea of clouds.
Perhaps you've heard that this was once the Order's seminary. It appears that even after the clouds consumed it, the Reverberations of its members linger on.
Maybe the anomalies in the sea of clouds are stirring them to life once more.
You seem very knowledgeable about all this.
Why yes, I've long been fascinated by Ragunna's history and art. After all, to chart our future, we must first understand our past. Is that not true?
We're likely to encounter more Reverberations on our way. They may even contain vital information. You can search for more if you're curious.
Lo! Foul monsters, taste my steel!
"The Blessed Maiden smote the fiends who dared ascend the hallowed stairs. Yet the Dark Tide surged on, as more monsters poured forth from the mist."
"In this fateful moment, the Blessed Maiden beheld her destiny's end. Moved by the Divinity, she chose to yield her life, for the Sentinel's cause and Rinascita's people."
O Imperator. Guide me!
Wait, wait. Your tone sounds a bit off. The Blessed Maiden should be more determined.
Determined? How about this then?
"In Imperator's name! Vile monsters! I swear your behinds shall be met with the end of my boots!"
I meant determined, not angry... You've got it all wrong!

Soft twilight hushes the day,
Moonlight dances, shadows sway.
Tranquil whispers fill the night,
Slumber's veil falls in quiet.

Twinkling stars, a celestial choir,
Sing softly to realms ever higher.
O Fair Lorelei, let your sorrow fade away,
May the good night forever stay.

Before the darkness falls, come sail with me,
Find haven in my boat upon the sea.
For soon the dawn will paint the sky anew,
And peace will find your heart, like morning dew.
(Something's wrong with these Echoes.)
(Looks like someone's pulling their strings, just like at the rehearsal.)
(Need to find a way to stop them first.)

Leave.

If the waterways fall into disorder because of the Gondolas' idleness, surely the Sentinel will be displeased!
Maybe the Sentinel is just giving you directions.
Not trying to control every aspect of your life?

{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, let me accompany you this time!

Follow me, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}—we'll need a Gondola to reach the third location.
Oh, you're offering us a ride? Thank you, Divine Envoys of the Sentinel. See? I told you the Sentinel has been watching over us!
I don't even know what to say.
You literally just told me to drive them away.

How dare they… I cannot fathom anyone so blind to the Sentinel's grace, even before the rise of the Order of the Deep.
Those people... They lived beneath the Sentinel's watchful eye without acknowledging Their kindness. They even claimed the miracles of the Sentinel as their own!
It was this kind of blasphemy that angered the Sentinel and brought forth the Dark Tide! This is why the world needs the Order's guidance now more than ever, don't you see?
Is the Sentinel you believe in truly so unforgiving and cruel?
Remember, these are the same people who composed the Nimbus Chorale.
I... but I... No! This isn't it!

Who wrote this "Tenets of the Deep"? You've been reciting it over and over.
The Tenets are a code of conduct for all who follow the Order with true devotion. They were meticulously refined by the Primus himself to guide us through the ages.

After the Dark Tide twenty years ago, His Holiness Fenrico stated that the Order's leniency toward disorder had invited the calamity. In response, he revised the sacred text and urged all faithful to live by it always.
I feared the book would become worn from constant use, so I memorized every word, every line!
So, the current version of your Tenets...
Is essentially written by Fenrico?
To be honest I don't know myself. The older prints have all been confiscated and destroyed.
Do you still have other questions, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}?
That's it for now.
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, I am not the brightest among my peers, but I do understand what you've been hinting at. You are a kind person, that I can tell.
But let's turn our focus to listening to the Nimbus Chorale. Perhaps the music itself will speak where words cannot. Come, let's listen!
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, something feels amiss... Do you feel it too?
I think it lacks that human touch.
I guess you'll say it needs to praise the Sentinel more?
Human touch? No, it should be praising the Sentinel!
I knew you'd understand!
The Carnevale is a holiday for everyone to gather and give thanks to our beloved Sentinel. I'm certain there's another part of the Chorale that shows our true reverence.
What do you say...
What is this place?
This is the site of the Order of the Deep's Major Forbidden Archive—well, the former site.
After the Dark Tide, it was buried beneath Nimbus Sanctum along with all of its secrets.
I thought you've always wanted to go to the Major Forbidden Archive?
Do you want to go in and have a look?
Me? No, no. I can't go in there.
It holds the most dangerous books and ideas, and only the most devout believers are allowed inside.
I-I'm not ready yet… O Sentinel, please forgive me.
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, would you be willing to defeat the beast within and bring back the Nimbus Chorale's final part? It will surely celebrate the glory of the Sentinel.
Leave it to me.
I'm taking all the treasure, you know.
Thank you, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}! I swear by Lenore—the name given to me by His Holiness the Primus—that I will repay this kindness with all my heart.

Haha, that's all right, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}! As Verse 9, Chapter 1 of the Tenets of the Deep says: "The great Sentinel has scattered Their blessings upon Rinascita, satisfying the needs of Their people in full measure."
You could say the treasures within are waiting for a righteous hero like you to claim them!
I'll pray for you here and ask the Sentinel to guide you, just as They guided the first believers.
It's a miracle! The great Sentinel heard my prayers!
I was the one who heard you.
I don't understand, kind {Male=sir;Female=lady}... Weren't you sent by the Sentinel to save me?
My sense of justice guided me here.
I just heard someone in distress.
I see... Please pardon my rashness, Righteous One. Thank you for your sense of honor.
Farewell, Righteous One!
What is the Forbidden Archive?
The dean of what?
Why do you look like you're getting ready to become a martyr?

It's called the Minor Forbidden Archive. We have two: one big, one small. The Major Forbidden Archive is where we store all the really dangerous books, tales, and ideologies. Only the most devout servants of the Sentinel are permitted to serve there!
As for the Minor Forbidden Archive... well, it's where we keep the expired or incomplete documents, notes, and such...
But of course, it still takes a truly devout follower like me to be assigned to work there!

That's right, I am Dean of the Minor Forbidden Archive! Although, for the past eight years, it's just been me...  But I have read and recited the Dean's code of conduct over and over again. I hold myself to the highest standards a dean can!
Verse 15, Chapter 6 of the Tenets of the Deep declares, "Those who aspire to achieve extraordinary deeds must bear extraordinary resolve."
What I'm about to undertake is the unprecedented restoration of the Nimbus Chorale. I am prepared to give up my life for it!
I will cross the treacherous Nimbus Sanctum, battle ferocious Tacet Discords... and, well, I may have to face the wrath of the Queen of the Night herself... Uhh...
It sounds like a suicide mission.
You don't sound very confident.
But I have to do this. I've spent eight long years working at the Minor Forbidden Archive. If I linger any longer, Phoebe and the others will surpass me. I must set a good example for them!
Oh, I nearly forgot. "Do not gnaw on a fool's worries." Yes, off I go!
Hold up. What if I said I can help?
I cannot accept such a thing! The Tenets of the Deep solemnly instruct, "A trial that is aided by an outside hand is no true trial." Verse 9, Chapter 12.
Consider it a collaboration. The musical records are yours, but the rest of the finds belong to me.
Uh, I mean... I'm sorry, but may I ask why you're offering to help me?
Phoebe once helped me. Think of this as me returning the favor.
I think there will be plenty of treasures to be found on this trip.
Well... I think you're kinda cute.
So you're Phoebe's friend. How time files... That young girl who once hid behind me has grown into a capable Acolyte. O Great Sentinel, is this part of your grand design as well?
Good. We both help each other, that way, it won't feel like relying on outside aid. Let us join hands then! And of course, I will repay you for saving my life once this is over!
Cute? Me? I... I'm just an ordinary woman! If we passed each other on the street, you wouldn't even give me a second glance.
People always say Phoebe's the cute one. You saying that... well, it makes me a little embarrassed. I haven't even...
Ugh! What am I even thinking! Please... forget I spoke of this at all.
Ahem. Well, Righteous One, we still need to discuss how we will recover the Nimbus Chorale.
First of all, please just call me {PlayerName}.
Secondly, what exactly is the Nimbus Chorale?
Ah, silly me, I almost forgot!
The Nimbus Chorale is a symphony that was once played during the ancient Carnevales of Rinascita, but it was lost to time after the arrival of the Dark Tide.

I've been studying all sorts of historical records within the Order for the last few months, alongside journals of our ancestors' lives in Rinascita. With this research, I've narrowed down the possible locations.

Lord Primus just announced the Carnevale is to be revived this year. If I can recover this ancient symphony in its entirety, it will surely add a touch of grandeur to the festivities! The others, Phoebe especially, will look at me with newfound respect, hehe!
Ah, but wait... I'm getting ahead of myself. Sorry, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, let's get moving!
I understand. As the Tenets reveal, "To know oneself is paramount; to overstep is perilous." Verse 2, Chapter 2. I shall remain here, awaiting your return.
May the blessings of the Sentinel be with you, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}!
You're back so soon, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}! I am in awe!
It was easier than I expected.
It was more difficult than I expected.
May I join you next time? I wouldn't want the Sentinel to think me... soft, allowing you to shoulder all the burden.
Forgive me! It must've been when I faltered in my prayers. The Sentinel saw my distraction... I will stay focused next time!
Now, shall we listen to the record you've recovered? It's a part of the revered Nimbus Chorale, after all!
How splendid! So this is the first section of the Nimbus Chorale, "Soil of Abundance"... What a beautiful depiction of the Sentinel's mercy!
Is it?
I don't think it's anything special.
Of course it is!
Hmm... Maybe it's because you're not native to Rinascita, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}.
As stated in the Tenets, "The Sentinel granted abundance to Rinascita, and we must bow low, our foreheads kissing the earth in gratitude."
For believers such as us, a piece of music dedicated to the fertile soil is proof of the Sentinel's boundless mercy!
I don't think this fertile soil was a gift from on high.
Your ancestors worked hard over the ages to make it fruitful.
Wh-where did you hear such audacious words?! How could anyone dare to place the strength of mankind above the will of our Sentinel?
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, please, you must not speak of this in the presence of others!

Long ago, someone dared to profane the Order by spreading rumors about the Sentinel. That's why the current Primus Fenrico has forbidden even private discussions about the Sentinel. It's considered dangerous heresy now!
You are an outlander, but I fear your views might be misinterpreted...
That sounds like an extreme policy.
Are they so strict even with outlanders?

{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, do you know of the Dark Tide? It was a calamity from the heavens, an abyss that consumed all. The tide of desecration destroyed countless families, including my own.
In our darkest hour, it was the Blessed Maiden who gave her life to seal away the darkness. It was His Holiness the Primus who beseeched the Sentinel's mercy. Our unwavering faith saved us all.
As His Holiness Fenrico once said: "Faith is the cornerstone of Rinascita, and any questioning of our faith and the Order will lead to another Dark Tide."
Nobody wants another Dark Tide, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}.
But we have more pressing matters now. I'll send you the coordinates of the next location.
Perhaps you should join me this time.
Oh? Why is that?
I'm getting tired of running back and forth.
The Tacet Discords only seem to target those holding the musical record.
Oh, I'm so sorry for my negligence!
Phew! {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, I was worried to death. Is everything all right?
Easy peasy.
I ran into a little trouble.
Whew! That's great. Seems I was too rattled by the earlier attack.
I see... I must confess, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, in my nervousness, I failed to pray for you just now. But I'm relieved you're unharmed!
Now then, let's listen to the second part together. I believe it's called "Crystal Sky."
Wait, before we continue... According to my research, the correct way to listen to the Nimbus Chorale is to play the multiple parts layered on top of each other at once!
Care to explain?
I'm sure there's a reason, but let's keep it short.
According to the Order's Ancestral Records, the Nimbus Chorale can only be experienced fully through the collaboration of many.
The performers normally hail from various parts of Rinascita and only come together during the Carnevale. It's the one time it's ever performed in full!
Much of the official records were lost during the Dark Tide, but I've painstakingly reconstructed the fragments from every available source to reach this conclusion!
Each record includes just one instrument's part. Only when all of them are played together can the true Nimbus Chorale be heard.
Phoebe would've loved a detailed explanation. If only she were here...
Anyway, let's listen to it now!

Carlow? No, no, we only met him yesterday. It's from the night...
Ahem...
Oh, it's from... it's from a knight who loves the night. He was the one who told us.
This knight you speak of. Where did you meet him? Is he still around town?
Uh... he's already left.
...So, Carlow really did meet a knight. It's just like the day he came dashing over to me, reciting those same words you did.
I thought he read those in a book. But he insisted that he heard it from a knight passing by.
I had a feeling that Korlacchi might be a family name and that the knight's oath reflected his path of service, so I asked Carlow about the knight's livery.
Carlow described how the knight dismounted from a weathered warhorse, clad in silver armor. He removed his helmet and laid his hands on Carlow's head.
Then he pulled a ring from his pocket and told Carlow he would continue his journey into the depths of Whisperwind Haven, seeking distant horizons.
He asked if Carlow wanted to be a knight and gave him this ring as a keepsake, telling Carlow to rewalk his path one day.
To reach the end where he had arrived, and then... to journey even further.
But this ring is made from coarse steel. Nothing like what Carlow described.
So I had my doubts about Carlow's tale. I thought he'd gotten lost in those knightly stories and made it all up.
Where is Carlow now?
He... At this hour, I imagine he's roaming the outskirts of town, searching for the knight's trails.
He intends to find the knight and the family he serves to complete the knighting ceremony in Korlacchi's name and finally become a true knight.
There's a large tree not far from town, where he said he found the first trail. Do you plan to go after him?
Do you think you can catch up with that knight? If you can, please help the poor boy find the knighthood he's been dreaming about.
The young man politely bids you goodbye and leaves in silence...
What a boy... Sorry about the ruckus, outlander. Are you checking in? If not, it's getting late. You wouldn't want to be caught out there during the Night Reveries.
Night Reveries?
Yes. You probably noticed the graffiti, statues, and signs all scattered across town, no?
They all feature a knight.
Now that you mentioned it, we did see a bunch of kids running around with wooden swords and bedsheets for capes.

Ah, those youngsters are just reenacting the knight's play. The Night Reveries are a kind of a performance, too. They can be traced back to the legend of a brave knight who slayed a giant in Whisperwind Haven.
Since then, the legendary knight has become an irreplaceable symbol of humility, honor, and bravery for the town. The oath the boy just recited is one of the legacies the knight left us.
Knights from far and wide would gather here before setting off to the depth of Whisperwind Haven in search of the legend's origin.
As more knights filled our streets, an odd one emerged. These days, folks like to call him the "Mad Knight."
He only shows himself after dusk. Folks say he roams the outskirts, hunting down Tacet Discords. Get too close, and you might find yourself on the sharp end of his blade!
That's how he became the "Mad Knight," the talk of the town. We reckon he's cursed now from wrestling with those wretches for so long.
To placate this restless soul, the town created the Night Reveries—endless dramas of the knight enacted by the Echoes. Townsfolk and visitors alike were advised to stay indoors at night.
But... there's one lad who stands apart. Fancies that the knight isn't mad at all. He believes a true knight would never betray their oath, no matter the cost.
For him, every swing of a knight's sword must carry meaning. To prove his theory, the boy is hell-bent on becoming a knight and challenging the Mad Knight to a duel.
The young man from earlier?
Yes, Carlow. We all thought it was just another childhood fantasy, but he's held onto that dream to this day.
Becoming a knight doesn't sound too bad. Hehe, you get all the cool points plus who can resist that suit of armor?!
True, but those are knights who have earned their reputations. Maintaining <ano=purity>"knighthood"</ano> is a thing of the past now.
Oh, look at the time! Apologies for rambling on, traveler. If you need a place to stay, just let me know.
(They say he's cursed...)
(Could it be a symptom of Overclocking?)
So you're thinking that knight-guy's Overclocked, huh? I don't know, but one thing's for sure I'm picking up a bunch of familiar smells all over this place.
Come on, it's not far now. The Echoes are getting ready for their opening act, all set to welcome the star of the night.
Sheesh. Look at 'em go! They look like they're gearing up for a loony party instead of a proper knightly display.
A Tacet Discord... To its credit, that's not a bad knight impression.
What's all that about? Is it challenging us to a duel?
In the name of Korlacchi...
"Across the rivers of time, wherever my path may lead, I vow to uphold justice and fairness for all..."
That voice just now... Did you hear that, Abby?
And also... What was that in the end...?
TDs usually mumble the stuff they're trying to say. It might've learned it from somewhere, or maybe the frequencies it absorbed had strong emotions and desires.
In the name of Korlacchi... seems like something a knight might say before charging into battle.
I can't wait to see the townsfolk's faces when they find out the legendary Mad Knight is actually a TD.
No one will believe it.
Let's ask Cosimo about those mumblings in the morning. He might know a thing or two.
Sure thing. Come to think of it, I feel like we're being pretty knightly ourselves right now, don't you think?
I, Abby, and the great knight {PlayerName}, two heroes who solved a legendary mystery with humility, justice, and bravery... Heh, a knighting ceremony would make it even cooler.
It's a ceremony, nothing more.
Titles don't hold much value for me.

It's fine. I do appreciate the noble lady's sentiment—a wise investment often bears fruit in the most unexpected ways.
We're simply spreading the truth through a tale. I'm certain it will pique your interest, so consider this a heartfelt invitation to you and your companions.
Join us, pour your essence into this endless play, and use your humble strength to defy the raging current of fate!
I have many questions for you.
How are you holding up?
Where can I find you?
{Male=Lord;Female=Lady} Arbiter… I am ensnared...
Beyond the clouds and among the stars... thou shalt find an inverted tower suspended in the sky—I am there, watching over Solaris from above.
The Lost... doth wander briefly amongst thy kind...
Seek her out… She, too, doth move within the folds of this festival...
I'm sorry, but I can't stay here any longer. I must return...
Can you tell me your name before you go?

The Sentinel led me to a girl just now.
Cartethyia… I'll make a note of it.

Let's not alarm the public just yet.
We should let the Carnevale continue as planned.

I am Fenrico, the Primus of the Order of the Deep. Your deeds have reached my ears, and I have long wished to meet you. Alas, the burdens of this world delayed our meeting until now. I beg your pardon for the wait.
Please accept my respect for you—you and your troupe have shown great talent and ambition, breathing new life into Ragunna.
I ask you to deliver this message to your companions: from this day forth, the troupe shall have permanent rights to perform within the city.
I surely will.
Even if they're all Fools?
All mortals stumble, but through pilgrimage, they have cleansed their souls and atoned for their transgressions. They have earned their right to return to this divinely blessed land.
I understand that questions weigh on your heart. In the presence of a just Divinity, speak freely, and I will answer with all the honesty I possess.
By the great Sentinel Imperator, I swear to you. There shall be no deceit in my words.
I want to meet the Sentinel Imperator.
You have walked a path similar to Theirs. Indeed, you have the right to meet Them.
However, due to the Dark Tide two decades ago, the Sentinel's body was gravely wounded and remains in a state of recovery.
If you wish to meet Them, I will convey your request.
I see the thirst for truth in your eyes. It is clear that doubts still linger in your heart. Please, voice your concerns.
Tell me about the Blessed Fleurdelys.
Fleurdelys... She was the emissary of the Sentinel, and we are grateful for her contributions.
Twenty years ago, during the Dark Tide, she sacrificed herself to seal the calamity. She fulfilled her duties in this world and returned to the <color=yellow>divine embrace</color>.
Returned to the divine embrace?
Do you know how the Dark Tide came into being?
In Rinascita, wars were waged in the name of faith, tearing apart the Sentinel as our faith divided, weakening Their divine power.
The Dark Tide's true essence is the divine blood shed from the Sentinel's wounds.
That tragic past left deep scars, and with Their divine power drained, They could not prevent the Dark Tide's surge twenty years ago.

The Blessed Maiden chose to martyr herself. She <color=yellow>once again</color> resonated with the Sentinel and, through her sacrifice, restored some of Their divine power, bringing an end to the Dark Tide.

Yet, the Sentinel remains in a state of healing and still requires a mortal representative. Following the Blessed Maiden's departure, I was granted new authority to cleanse the aftermath of the Dark Tide.
I received the Divinity's blessing and became the new Enlightened One. By Their will, I fulfill the tasks left unfinished in this world.
Therefore, we must unify all beliefs, ensuring the purity and unity of our will to prevent another tragedy...
(Reflect on the Blessed Maiden's Second Resonance with the Sentinel.)

You're hiding things from me.
I swear, my words are without deceit.
I see in your eyes that you have walked further on the path of justice than I anticipated.
O dear Sentinel… please forgive my transgressions.
The Dark Tide brought us a bloodstained lesson. To keep our people from faltering, I bound myself to silence, locking away what I witnessed on that fateful day.
Fleurdelys, the Unrighteous, deceived us all. She was not the Blessed Maiden chosen by the Sentinel... The true maiden has yet to reveal herself.
Why did people believe she was the Blessed Maiden?
Where did her power to seal the Dark Tide come from?
You must know that a being capable of rivaling our Divinity exists in this world—humanity's eternal adversary, the evil of all civilizations... the Threnodian.
As the Sentinel has Their Resonator, so does the Threnodian.
Fleurdelys was shaped—both body and spirit—by our ancient enemy. Her actions were intended to plunge this city into fear and chaos.
This is the truth I witnessed—Fleurdelys was the <color=yellow>Threnodian's Resonator</color>.
Never before have I seen a day so steeped in both shadow and light.
The birds sing, the flowers bloom… yet this world knows neither true joy nor eternity.
Phrolova, you do have a knack for indulging in... pointless little chores.
Why, there's no rule against an actor making good use of the intermission.
Besides, I haven't disrupted your arrangement, have I?
"The one from a faraway land who discerns the truth dares to raise their sword against the divine. In response, the slumbering gods break free from their shackles, revealing their true forms..."
The possibility of the Second Resonance Awakening is now a certainty. So we just need to see if that special Resonator truly exists.
Was the Blessed Maiden a Resonator for the Sentinel or the Threnodian?
Or both? If so... Oh, a Resonator capable of wielding both powers... I am eager to see how this story ends.
Cristoforo, if you don't want to spoil the next act, I might have to give your carefully crafted plot a little nudge.
Speaking of which, {PlayerName} shines brighter than anyone else in your play. Do you find {Male=him;Female=her} interesting as well?
Phrolova, it seems we walk different paths. I don't share your fondness for that sort of... puppet theater.
I merely place the characters on their stage and they act out their fates, driven by their own volition.
To remain courageous amidst absurdity, to pursue a spark of divine grace—this, to me, is the truest essence of humanity, don't you think?
Even the most pristine cadence of death pales beside the untamed, fervent, and tenacious spirits of the living.
In their journey, they resolutely overcome all obstacles: they pursue, they tear, they burn—simply because they desire to.
I think you should leave your secluded mansion. Take a walk and listen to the voices scattered across the world.
…Perhaps.
From Huanglong to Rinascita, {Male=he;Female=she} has indeed added a few unexpectedly beautiful notes to my symphony.
I am certain that, even without any direction, {Male=he;Female=she} will walk the path that destiny has laid before {Male=him;Female=her}.
All things ascend towards a singular point of convergence, and what awaits at the end is... immortality.
Before the tides of fate, we are all but…
…humble servants.
Raise your glasses! Shout it loud, friends!
To us, to the Carnevale, and to our very own Laureate, {PlayerName}!
A name that echoes through the world, destined to roam the skies before shaking the earth!
Hear, hear! That's me!
Please, stop. You're making me feel embarrassed…
Don't be fooled by how he looks. Brant is already deep in his cups, drunk as a skunk.
Oh, let him enjoy himself. The taste of victory is still fresh, and after such a battle, we should celebrate to the fullest!
Drink your fill, everyone! This round's on me!
HOORAY!!!
Hmm, I see… Someone's been eavesdropping.
Looks like we've attracted some unwanted attention.
Aren't we in your family's safe house?
A devout Acolyte wouldn't enter such a place without a good reason.
The Montelli family is known for its hospitality, but freeloaders... will not find us so welcoming.
Friends, let's keep the mood lively!
Come, let's discuss the information we've gathered so far.
During the Carnevale, you heard the Sentinel's voice and found a girl named Cartethyia. We've dug up some information on her.
In the Order, every high-ranking Acolyte is given a new name.
We contacted the Acolyte, Phoebe. After some digging in the Order's records, she confirmed that before taking on her holy title, the Blessed Fleurdelys was called... Cartethyia.
So, she is the Sentinel's Resonator.
The family will uncover the truth. The only remaining clue is the "inverted tower" you mentioned hearing about from the Sentinel, but even that feels elusive...
Judging by your expression, you must have discovered something new, right?
Do you recall what we learned from the stained glass in the Tower Ruins? There were two divinities at the dawn of Rinascita.
If one refers to the Sentinel, then the other, who could stand alongside Them, might be the Threnodian.
The two are undoubtedly linked, so uncovering one could lead us to the other.
Remember Gilberto, from the Fisalia family? It took a lot to get him to talk, but we finally got some information from him.
As he tells it, the Fisalia family's long-revered deity is none other than... Leviathan, the Threnodian from the sea's depths.
They worship the Threnodian…

We will attempt to establish contact with the Fisalias to build an alliance and gather more intelligence.

Excuse me for the interruption. Greetings, esteemed guest.

I'm merely conveying the Primus' invitation. The choice is yours.
Don't worry, he wouldn't dare do anything to me.
Perfect timing. I have many questions for him.

Very well, please follow me to the Cathedral of Mercury.

You encounter Camellya at the Black Shores' Greenhouse. As usual, she appears nonchalant but pleased nevertheless to chat. Your conversation is interrupted by Beatrice, who needs you to handle a problem at the Error Cell.
A corrupted Stellar Matrix has escaped and could endanger the Black Shores. To retrieve it, you seek out the Consultant who previously accessed the Matrix's data.
At the Hall of Foreign Affairs, you discover that Camellya has already taken Lady Flora's belongings. Now, you must find Camellya.

After catching up with Camellya, she reveals that she is Lady Flora, but like you, she has lost her memories. She appears indifferent to everything except you and proposes a game in exchange for handing over Flora's items.

Camellya enjoyed the game and gives you the bracelet as promised. Recognizing that her help is vital to resolving the current crisis, you ask her to stay. Camellya finds your assertiveness intriguing and agrees to help. In a discussion about self and her lost memories, Camellya claims her instincts define who she is. To gather more of Lady Flora's items, you decide to split up.
You continue searching and find a forsaken Blake Bloom in a cave.

Camellya shows signs of Overclocking from battle, yet she appears unconcerned. She is accustomed to enduring pain and explains that savoring each present moment is her way of coping.

From the Blake Bloom's frequency, you discover that Lady Flora disappeared around the same time as the Black Shores leader. With enough items gathered, you head to the Modulation Hall.
You find Lady Flora covered in vines, struggling against her Overclocking. As her condition eases, she gazes at you with a faint smile and offers you a flower.

Crossing the Stargate again, you meet another version of Lady Flora at the Black Shores. Unlike the previous Lady Flora, she appears healthy and slightly bashful, yet her admiration for you remains unchanged. She mentions that meeting you feels familiar.

Thanks to your timely arrival, Petalfall Village has survived the disaster in this juncture, even though that is not how it truly happened. Like she did before, Lady Flora smiles and offers you a flower.

After passing through the Stargate for the third time, you finally reach the correct timeline juncture.

The Lady Flora you meet resembles Camellya in the real world and, like the others, she does not hide her feelings for you.

Once trapped in a labyrinth of memories and possibilities, Camellya has lost much. But now, she tells you she no longer wishes to recover her lost memories, believing the seal left by Lady Flora will naturally break when the time is right.

What matters to her now is enjoying this reunion with you.

Just as she did in previous timeline junctures, Camellya smiles and extends her hand, offering you a flower.
You learn that Lady Flora sealed her memories because of a choice your past self made. Bewildered, you return to the Modulation Hall with Beatrice's help.
I didn't care. As long as we were both happy when we crossed blades, I was happy.
But now, {PlayerName} wants to leave… and even abandon {Male=his;Female=her} memories?
Doing all of this for what? A so-called better outcome?

Lady Flora explains that the past duties imposed on the one she yearns for led to their decision to leave the Black Shores. Camellya listens to her past self, surprised by her depth of emotion. Through Lady Flora's words, Camellya realizes that you are the leader of the Black Shores.
Rest won't help… I've lost my anchor. {Male=He;Female=She}'s no longer here to rein me in.
I've started remembering things from before I came to Petalfall Village.

The Order warns of sirens lurking in the Stormy Sea's mists, but they don't scare me. I'll show them who the real siren of these waters really is!

We need your expertise.

Have you considered how you're going to get down?

That fight with the dragon probably messed with the mountain's stability. If Bardolino keeps moving around up there, it could get dangerous. We need to find a way to get him down, and fast.
See? I wasn't lying!
The Order found a way to control the dragon.
Tacet Discords' frequencies are perpetually fading, inching toward their end.
Their only way to maintain their existence is to consume other frequencies as food.
The Dark Tide and mist enveloping this isle have drawn in countless Tacet Discords. Their frequencies should have been enough to feed the dragon.
If what you saw is true, then...

That means they could be responsible for why the dragon began attacking all living beings, including humans...

I found this during the previous battle.

You know of the Fractsidus?

Remember Cetus the Tidebreaker, the creature that attacked you when we first met?

This is what we found on its tail... another Lycoris.
Alas, the Tidebreaker slipped away into the deep, beyond our reach. Still, this bloom leaves no doubt. The Fractsidus is behind its strange behavior.
We saw what they did to the dragon. The Cetus's violent outburst must be their doing as well.
They could wreak havoc at the Carnevale.
What if their true target is the Sentinel?

At first, we thought you were merely a curious traveler, intrigued by the Carnevale and our Sentinel. But now, seeing how far you've come, there's more to your quest, isn't there?
Our troupe has always sought the Laurel, and we won't sit back while others threaten the Carnevale. If they're your foes, then our paths align!
Remember I mentioned one of ours who once claimed the Laurel?

It won't be long now. After such an adventure, a well-earned rest awaits.

Alone in the dark, a young girl of untethered spirit, soared against towering barriers with wings of defiance...
The winds of fate brought them together...

Together, they became unshakable allies, standing strong against the tides of fate.
Even if light were to fade from the world, and the stars cease to shine, they would still blaze like the sun, forever...

The game isn't over. Here... Come quickly...

We'll be out of the mist soon.

Journal Page I

Day 15.

Some have begun to question the worth of this endeavor, and the very honor we strive to uphold for Fisalia. Such whispers should have no place here.

We have crossed the ridges of Thessaleo Fells, weathered storms, and dared currents to reach this place, losing a ship on the way. Now, it's time to claim our rewards. The "relic" that has been kept from our family by the Order lies somewhere within these forsaken ruins, and treasures glimpsed only in dreams seem at last within our grasp.

Dario will stay behind. His legs were pierced by a TD and he can no longer walk. We've left him with enough provisions.

The rest of the knights will press on, toward the ruins in the <color=Highlight>southwest</color>.

May we walk ever upon the righteous path.
Journal Page II

Day 16.

The pilgrimage chapel is nothing but another empty shell. The knights smashed windows and overturned altars, but not one sign of the relic has been found.

Renzo seems to have lost his wits, staring at the torches and babbling—perhaps a result of the drowning earlier. We can't afford to wait for his recovery. Ennio wishes to keep him with us, but such sentiment would only slow us down.

Our cause allows no room for the weak. Now, a ruin lies to the <color=Highlight>west</color> of this island. That shall be our next destination.

May we walk ever upon the righteous path.
Journal Page III

Day 17.

We waded through marshland to reach this waterlogged ruin, only to find more disappointment. The knights are losing faith—some doubt we'll ever find this so-called relic. Ennio, who's as close as family to me, stood against my decision to move on. He accused me of straying from the righteous path.

There was no other way to settle it; we dueled, as the knight's creed demands. He cast the gauntlets over to me, his mentor. Our duel ended amidst a strange howl from afar. When he fell, a part of me fell with him.

Ennio... He was set on the ideals of knighthood but was blind to the cold reality facing our branch of the family. I can feel it now—fortune and glory lie to the <color=Highlight>north</color>. Porto-Veno Castle will have to honor our deeds.

At this point, there's no turning back.
Journal Page IV

(The edges of the yellowed page are charred)

Day ██.

Our search stretched on and on, and all we found in the storeroom was a worn-out weapon schematic, probably left behind by the Order. Silently, we gathered anything of worth, not speaking a word about the relic. No one needed to—everyone knew. This quest has failed, and all our sacrifice has been in vain. But I don't accept it. The Order must have hidden something here on this island. Where is it?

(Rushed handwriting follows as if penned in great urgency)

Those damned TDs are coming for us. It's only a matter of time before they break through. But I've finally found it.

How absurd! The relic was always here, right before our eyes.

At the grand altar of ██, circled by towering Tacetites.

The howls are drawing closer. Forgive me.

*Coughs* Bloody Fanatic Shark...
If they've hurt Liel, I'll skin 'em alive...
Feel my blade!
I'm dreaming... this must be a dream!
Friend, we've been here before.
Those specters are right. We're trapped in this maze.
Going round and round in circles. Let's split up and look for clues.
Okay.
Liel where are you, you little brat? Eh?
Who are you?
Ahoy there... You don't look like a Fanatic Shark. Name's Insula. Didn't expect to find another soul wandering these parts...
And I didn't expect Exiles in Rinascita.
Not from here. Live on an island far off the coast.
Took my crew out to sea a few days ago to plunder merchant ships, or catch fish if we couldn't find any ships.
We got close to this merchant fleet, but then the Fanatic Shark ambushed us.
And a storm hit when we were fighting... the kind that could tear ships apart. Waves taller than a mast.
My crew and I were knocked out by one of 'em. We came on to that beach by yonder...
And if that ain't bad enough, those damned Fanatic Sharks also got washed up on this island.
Why the bad blood between you?
What are they like?
They're savages full of bloodlust.
Why, they butcher every sailor on every ship they loot.
Me and the boys' been busy fortifying our encampment, in case the Fanatic Shark attack. Haven't paid much attention to where we are...
You said we're in Rinascita?
Yup.
Welcome to Rinascita.
Small wonder this place's crawling with strange critters and Echoes... I just hope none of 'em get to Liel.
Who's Liel?
You push the bookcase. Nothing happens.
Captain, there's something under the elevator.
That's enough... We can't leave... We can never leave...
Liel? You're not Liel!
Who's Liel?
They're... they're Fanatic Sharks?
What are Fanatic Sharks?
Our sworn enemies... They washed up onshore with us.
Watch for attacks from above!
Hah, those fish nuts are better off dead than alive. Now their specters show us the right path.
Fanatic Shark, charge!
It looks mighty angry.
Friend, help is at hand!
Let it go. We still need to press on, my friend.
Got away again. Ah, blast it...

Are these the specters of the dead Fanatic Sharks? Am I hallucinating?
Ahoy there, young stranger.
Hi, What are you doing here?
Feel the briny wind from the sea? A perfect day for a voyage with the calm waves, eh?
See, that's my Gondola over there. As long as she's with me, there is no place in Rinascita we can't reach.
Ah, where are my manners? Name's Davide, Captain Davide, or... boatman perhaps. Doesn't matter which to me.
I'm retiring anyway.
But you don't look ready to retire just yet.
You've got that right. I can still run a full trip to Septimont, singing shanties and puffing on my pipe the whole way.

Last voyage? That sounds ominous.

I've crossed Nimbus Sanctum, seen Lorelei dancing among the stars, and ventured to forbidden lands, through reefs sharp as daggers.
From the dread lurking in the abyss to the beauty of fantasy islands, I've seen more than enough.
There's only one place left in all of Rinascita that I haven't conquered—the sky.
The sky?
Aye! Now you probably think I've got a few bolts loose, eh? Older and crazier than the lot on Pilgrim's Sails.
But this is no joke. There were nights I dreamed of my Gondola and I gliding on the wind.
We would pass the rainbow bridge and see birds flashing beneath the boat like fish in a coral reef. Imagine that—a voyage like no other.
But can a Gondola really fly?
I've got faith in her. All she needs is the right push, and she'll take me up there.
I know what I'm talking about. In fact, we did come close one time.
We were out at sea when we got caught in a... what do they call it? Tornado? Felt like a giant hand grabbed us and flung us into the air.
A tornado?
Wouldn't that be dangerous?
Ah, no need to worry. That was just a starter compared to the worst I've seen. Now, you seem like a kind soul. Think you can help me find something as powerful as that tornado?
Naturally, there's something in it for you. Whatever treasure I find on this journey is yours.
Treasure? What treasure?
There's a treasure in the sky?
They say, "At the end of the rainbow lies gold." The same goes for the clouds. In Rinascita, there's a tale of a ruin from the Dark Tide, said to be filled with treasure.
But for me, steering my Gondola toward treasures lost to time is worth more than any treasure itself.
So, what do you say? Not a bad offer, eh?
What kind of power do you need?
Let me think... I remember, in Ragunna, there's a TD built like a giant stuffed toy but packed with raw strength.
If we can turn it into an Echo, it should be strong enough to launch us into the sky. Then I'll just leave the rest to my Gondola—I trust her.
It worked! We're flying! Keep it steady, partner! Take us to the clouds!
See that, my friend? We made it! Want to join us for a view of the heavens?
Wait… how do I control this thing… no, no, how do I stop it?
So we meet again, my friend.
Are you alright?
Me? Couldn't be better. The view above the clouds was exactly like what I dreamed.
For a final voyage, it was everything I ever wanted, and deeply satisfying.
Allow me to thank you once more. My dream has finally come true.
Where is your Gondola?
Oh, don't remind me. That Wingray had a mind of its own—it wouldn't change course or land.
Eventually, hunger got the better of me, so I jumped into the sea, watching my partner and the Wingrays fade into the horizon...
I'm sorry to hear that.
What a bittersweet ending.
That's alright. She seemed happy as could be. My partner loved the thrill of adventure as much as I do—we're two of a kind.
She'll continue that grand, mysterious voyage, and I'm sure she'd find plenty of joy along the way.
And, well, I did manage to find a little surprise.
A surprise?
You found the ruin?
It's that chest over there. I stumbled upon a floating platform in the clouds, and it was sitting right on top. No idea who left it there.
No, not really. Just a chest resting on a platform in the clouds. No idea how it got there.
It could be the origin of that tale, even if it turned out, well, less impressive than I imagined.
Anyway, as we agreed, everything in it is yours.
What will you do now?
Me? I'll go back to Ragunna and live the quiet life of a retired captain, telling my tales to anyone who'll listen.
A captain who flew his Gondola to the sky… Well, who'd believe that?
Farewell, my friend. May the Sentinel always bless you.
Time to set sail!
Give it all you've got, big fella!
We've got it this time...
Hold on... these Fae Ignis are acting strange.
Ah-ha! That's the Echo! Thank you, young one!
Ahem... though I do have one more favor to ask.
Go ahead.
I'd like to share with you this moment of thrill as I break free from the earth and reach for the sky.
Would you do me the honor of witnessing my voyage?
With pleasure.
Excellent! Now, eyes on me!
Ugh... guess my old bones weren't ready for that.
Are you okay?
*Coughs*... Oh, it's you. Gave you a bit of a laugh, did I?
But for me and my Gondola here, this is nothing at all. Right, partner?
*A confident whistle*
If you'd seen us take on the raging seas, you'd know this is smooth sailing.
We've ridden down waves taller than mountains without a scratch. This drop's barely worth mentioning.
Oh really?
Anyway, glad you're okay.
It clearly didn't go as planned. What's holding us back?
Maybe Gondolas aren't built for flight, eh? Even with a boost, all we'd get is a short glide.
Isn't that obvious?
Short glide? More like a nose dive.
Alright, alright, I may have put too much faith in my old partner. She's always been unstoppable in my memory.
Hard to believe there are things she can't do...
*A protesting whistle*
Easy there, partner. I'm not griping. Just saying we need a new plan.
Let me see... Ah, yes. There's a flying TD in Penitent's End called Fae Ignis.
If we turn them into Echoes and load them aboard, there's a fair chance they'll give us the lift we need.
Now that sounds like a plan.
Cool, but please stay safe.
So, mind making one more trip for this old man?
Leave it to me!
No problem.
Thank you, young one.
Aye, that's the one!
Thank you. I'll be ready in a minute!
Good luck!
I've got bad feelings about this...
I'll take that blessing!
Rest easy! No storms can get the best of me!
Brace yourself—you're about to see us conquer the sky!
Well, it's good to see you again, my friend.
Are you alright?
Your Gondola exploded.
*Coughs*... No need to worry. Just a minor setback, nothing I can't handle.
Rough landing aside, I'd say things went fairly well.
At least my partner and I managed to fly, though it was not the voyage I had in mind.
Maybe I'm just getting old, old enough to forget Fae Ignis can go off like firecrackers...
Are you giving it another go?
Maybe it's time to stop.
For sure! Even if I wanted to quit, my partner would never allow it.
Not a chance. Even if I wanted to quit, my partner would never allow it.
*A supportive whistle*
Hah! That's right, partner! We'll be above the clouds!
Could you do me one more favor, my friend? I swear this will be the last one.
Alright… so what's the plan?
I believe we are on the right track. Echoes can make a Gondola fly, but only the right ones can make a Gondola soar.
If, just if, we could get our hands on a calm flying Echo like a Wingray...
Come to think of it, there used to be Wingrays here, but they've all vanished recently.
Could it be… those masked fellas in red uniforms?
The Fractsidus again?
Ah yes, the Fractsidus! They've got a camp around here. Haven't been there, but I've spotted them firing at the sky.
Are they… poaching the Wingrays? By the Sentinel, those transgressors will answer for this!
Would you mind heading over to take a look? If they've taken the Wingrays, please save them.
The Fractsidus has locked up the Wingrays.
These doors look flimsy. Perhaps a heavy blow may break them down.
The gate's open.
Let's bring this Wingray to Captain Davide.
A Wingray! Thank you, my friend.
So, you taught those poachers a lesson, eh? The Sentinel will smile upon that.
Now let's see if it would give me and my partner a ride to the sky.
I can feel the wind beckoning us from afar... urging us to start our voyage.
Thank you for everything. Now, I hope you'll stay to witness the moment we take flight!
I'm looking forward to it.
Hope this one goes smoothly.
Off we go, partner!
*A spirited whistle*
Nothing. Just taking a walk here.
You're the one who may need some help.

A Consultant? Why haven't you evacuated yet?
When the Tethys System issued the order to evacuate, everyone else left for the Modulation Hall.
So why are you still here?
To protect the seeds in the Bank of Life, seeds collected from all over the world.
It's imperative that the plants on Solaris be categorized systematically, you see.
Besides, as long as the Tethys System stands, so will we.
Hmm, hmm... The Great Chain of Being...
Sorry, I was miles away. Welcome, Knowledge Seeker!
You look just like KU-Money.
You've met KU-Money, then. He is the robot administering the Black Shores Archipelago.
Similarly, each area of the Black Shores' underground has been assigned an administrator.
I'm KU-Irwin, administrator of the Bank of Life's Center for Species Conservation. A pleasure to make your acquaintance.
Things are hectic at the moment. The fate of the Black Shores' underground is in your hands and the Shorekeeper's now.
We'll talk again in time.
The numbers are a complete mess! They should've been arranged using a phylogenetic tree.
You want to help? Keep yourself safe, that's your first priority.
Oh, by the way, you're from Jinzhou, right?
I hear there is a Jinzhou scholar by the name of Verina who is well versed in botany.
I hope I'll get the chance to meet her soon…

Oh... I'd better be off now! I came to Egla Town to find some inspiration for new recipes. Something with a knightly twist, I think...
I'm glad I could lend a hand! As for that chipper young lad over there, he's been in it longer than you, so it might take him a wee bit to come around. But don't fret, it's not serious!
