At Gourmet Street, you discuss your dream involving the Sentinel and Mt. Firmament. A fellow diner shares insights about the mountain, and Abby senses a strange aura emanating from the southeast. Together, you resolve to seek information about the Sentinel at the City Hall.

In City Hall, Sanhua reveals that the Magistrate ventured to Mt. Firmament days ago, concerned for the Sentinel's safety. You express your intent to follow and Sanhua offers to contact a guide for the treacherous journey. She arranges a meeting with the Wayfinder at Whining Aix's Mire.

In the pouring rain, you encounter Changli, the Wayfinder, at the ferry. She describes the peculiar nature of time at Mt. Firmament, where it flows erratically. She notes your resemblance to a historic visitor who was immune to this temporal distortion and offers to accompany you into this dangerous realm.

You and Changli come to a damaged bridge that leads to Mt. Firmament. You find a Chronosorter in the vicinity, a Court of Savantae creation believed to have the power to restore objects by rewinding time. Perhaps it can be used to repair the bridge?

Upon entering Mt. Firmament, you find that the flow of time has spiraled out of control, with many creatures falling victim to it. Leaving the mountain now could lead to unpredictable aging. Changli finds her Terminal is not working and suggests hurrying to Hongzhen, a town that Jinhsi must pass through in her search for the Sentinel.

Hongzhen resembles a place from your dreams. Changli speculates that your dreams might be a glimpse into your past and a light guiding you into the future. Here, you meet the Fractsidus and discover traces of Jinhsi's Resonance Ability, and you decide to follow them.

You and Changli enter a hidden chamber. Xinyi greets you. She is an old acquaintance of Changli's and once held a prominent position in City Hall before retiring to Hongzhen. She asks you to follow her.

You learn that the Sentinel may be trapped in its resting place—the Mianloong Chamber. The Fractsidus invasion has activated the defenses built by the Court of Savantae, sealing the chamber. Jinhsi left shortly before to go to Truthseeker's Pass to retrieve the Cipher Key needed to unseal it. You and Changli continue to trace her steps.

At Truthseeker's Pass, you find another Chronosorter alongside three Photonvaults. Changli marvels at how the Court of Savantae managed to manipulate time to create such sophisticated mechanisms, noting that no other civilization has been able to replicate this technology. She speculates that this knowledge must have originated from the Sentinel.

In the depths of Truthseeker's Pass, you find the Cipher Key needed to unlock the Mianloong Chamber. Changli tells you that she has successfully fulfilled her mission to bring you to Jinhsi and chooses to stay behind to handle the troublesome Fractsidus.

You and Jinhsi return to Hongzhen, and with Xinyi's help, unlock the Mianloong Chamber. You discover that the Fractsidus has used a Court of Savantae creation to generate a special force field that prevents Jué from drawing energy from the chamber, effectively trapping it.
Upon entering the Mianloong Chamber, you find a body of water frozen in time. Can you walk across the water's surface to get to the other side?

You meet Jué in the depths of the Mianloong Chamber. Jué calls you "Arbiter" and invites you to step in as Jinzhou makes a historical turn and witness the transformations to come. Knowing that it is dying, Jué is willing to use its remaining life force to freeze Jinzhou in time, so that future generations may have a chance to save it. Jinhsi refuses to accept this and decides to fight the Sentinel, even at the cost of her own life.

On the summit of Mt. Firmament, Jué waits in the Sonoro Sphere for a challenger. Jinzhou's fate is in Jinhsi's hands, and she will fight for it in her own way. You support her decision and open the door to the Sonoro Sphere, ready to witness this key moment in Jinzhou's history.

As the dust settles, Jué meets with you as promised. You learn that you were once Jué's master and established Jinzhou with its assistance. Jué notices something usual about your Tacet Mark just as Abby appears and the two confront each other. Even Jué is uncertain of Abby's origins, but suggests that you visit the Black Shores, the starting point of your journey in this world.

The flow of time has returned to normal. Mt. Firmament thrives once more, and you journey to Hongzhen to meet with Changli and Xinyi. All is not what it seems, however. The Fractsidus is planning its next move...

The stone gate, marked with the Flare Crest, has stars that correspond to Flare Stones. To unlock the gate, you need to find and activate the other two stones. Changli discovers traces left by Jinhsi nearby and deduces that she may be on the verge of Overlocking.

The documents show that the Court of Savantae used Chronosorters to test the Second Resonance Awakening hypothesis, which suggests that colliding frequencies can unlock greater potential within a Resonator. You theorize that the prophesied conflict between Jinhsi and the Sentinel is intended to allow Jinhsi to acquire the ability to manipulate time through this Second Resonance. However, the experiments indicate that the Resonator's Overlocking may be necessary to attain this power.

You finally find Jinhsi, who appears greatly weakened. She has learned from the Court of Savantae's records that the Sentinel was injured upon arriving at Mt. Firmament, and its worsening condition is causing the increasingly unstable flow of time. With Jinzhou endangered, Jinhsi intends to verify the Court's claims for herself. If necessary, she is prepared to engage the Sentinel in battle to trigger a Second Resonance, even if it means risking her life.

You learn about Jinhsi's past. Jinhsi is adamant about fulfilling her duty. The prophesied battle between her and the Sentinel was meant for the distant future, but she is willing to confront the Sentinel now if it is the only way to keep everyone safe. She expresses her gratitude for your companionship.

In Hongzhen, an elderly storyteller shares the legend of a hidden Weiqi game on Mt. Firmament that is said to grant immortality. While listening, you notice Changli nearby. She hands you an accessory and a note before quietly leaving. The note hints at a secret meeting, and to decipher its meaning, you decide to ask around.

The people you speak with have varying opinions on Changli, but you deduce the meeting location from their insights. You encounter Xinyi, who identifies the accessory as one of Changli's prized possessions, suggesting that understanding her intentions will require personal involvement.

At the pavilion mentioned in the note, you meet Changli. She shares the full story behind the "unfinished Weiqi game"—an enigmatic visitor once hid the Secret of Immortality in the last Weiqi game she played with her master. This game might be tied to the Temporal Mandate and your lost memory. Changli asks for your help in uncovering the truth.
You meet Changli again and she shares that she has pinpointed the most likely location of the game record. Together, you prepare to search for it.
As you and Changli enjoy the view from the pavilion in Hongzhen, Abby senses the mixed frequencies of Tacet Discords and humans from a cave. Someone may be in danger...

You rush to rescue an adventurer under attack by Tacet Discords. The adventurer, claiming to seek Mt. Firmament's secrets, faints. Changli suspects he is hiding something and plans to gather more information once you return to Hongzhen.

At the hotel, you meet Fuling, the gravely ill girlfriend of the adventurer Wuli. He had gone into the mountains seeking a way to slow her condition but mistakenly believed that the Temporal Disruptions held the key to immortality. Accepting her fate, Fuling pleads with you to put a stop to the dangerous Disruptions.

Through discussions with Xinyi, you begin to question Wuli's motives and his sources of information. You suspect that the Temporal Disruption might be part of a larger scheme and could be connected to the Weiqi record you are searching for.

While investigating Wuli's camp, you learn that Fuling has accepted her fate and doesn't want Wuli to sacrifice his future as an adventurer for her. Wuli's diary reveals ties to the Fractsidus, suggesting someone is trying to connect the Temporal Disruption to the Weiqi game.
You encounter Xuanmiao, Changli's master, across time. When you touch the old Weiqi board, it glows in response, and you spot the Fractsidus Artificer following you.

A portal to the Sonoro Sphere opens, and the Fractsidus Artificer rushes through, convinced that the power of the Temporal Mandate lies within. After defeating his minions, you and Changli enter the Sonoro Sphere together.

You and Changli manage to escape the burning Sonoro and reunite with Xinyi, Wuli, and Fuling. The remaining members of the Fractsidus have been captured by the Midnight Rangers, and the Temporal Disruptions have ceased. Wuli and Fuling understand each other's true feelings and plan to explore more places together, continuing their pursuit of shared dreams. Changli asks you to rest while she assists Xinyi in wrapping up loose ends.

Two days later, you visit Xinyi in the Meeting Room, learning that the Fractsidus was indeed seeking the Temporal Mandate referenced in the Weiqi game legend. However, their scheme was thwarted by you and Changli. The Fractsidus Overseer who had entered the Sonoro has vanished. As for Changli, she awaits you at the pavilion.

When you meet Changli at the pavilion, she reveals everything. You were the "golden-eyed visitor" who played Weiqi with Master Xuanmiao. Back then, you foresaw a disaster striking Mt. Firmament and left the Sonoro as a contingency plan. Changli admits that while she is not concerned about her lifespan, she feels a deep sadness at the thought of leaving behind the world's beauty. Now, she wishes to play that long-anticipated game of Weiqi with you.

Inside, you find a young girl surrounded by Tacet Discords. She uses flames to fend them off but injures herself in the process. She resembles Changli, raising suspicions about their connection. Concerned for her safety, you decide to venture deeper into the Sonoro with her.
The girl reveals her entire village was destroyed during a TD Outbreak. She only survived because some villagers hid her in a fireproof basement.

She confides that despite the toll her abilities take on her life, she uses them frequently to survive. Her dream is to grow up and become someone strong enough to help others. To bring peace to this world, she must find a skilled mentor to guide her.

Changli recalls her master Xuanmiao's farewell before he passed away, during which he imparted wisdom on navigating life and instructed her to assist someone capable of truly changing the world. Seeing this memory, Changli now understands what must be done.

After solving the puzzle, Changli spots you and the girl's mirage from afar. Meanwhile, the girl recalls that she has been searching for something important. She feels an odd familiarity with you, despite never having met before. Suddenly, a missing part of the device needed to open the gate appears in her hand.
You and the girl encounter a mirage of Changli, while elsewhere, Changli sees multiple reflections of her past self. She ponders over it and resolves to find you at all costs.

Outside Panhua's restaurant, the creature within you, drawn by the food's aroma, emerges from your Tacet Mark. Baizhi's tests reveal that the Threnodian energy it absorbed has completely fused with you, forming a mysterious symbiosis, or Convergent Codependency.
This small, rare Echo has no memory of its origins or the events in the Norfall Barrens. Intrigued by the concept of names, it asks you to bestow one upon it, having forgotten its own.

The little one rejects Chixia's grandiose names, prompting you to suggest "Abby." To your surprise, it loves the name, saying it sounds just right. Curious about Abby's origins, you ask it to demonstrate its abilities hoping to learn something.

Abby tries and fails to showcase its abilities. Maybe it has yet to learn how to activate its power. The answers may lie within your lost memories. Perhaps you can uncover hints during your meeting with the Magistrate and Sentinel Jué.
You meet Zhezhi at the entrance of the Public Security Bureau. Relieved to see you, she gathers her courage and decides to speak the truth about the art forgery case during the hearing.

As the hearing unfolds, Baici, the founder of the Shanyun Art Exchange, casts doubt on Zhezhi's statement with his slippery arguments. Nervous and shaken, Zhezhi finds it impossible to refute him. You decide to step in and explain the events of three days ago. Your support gives Zhezhi the confidence to continue, and she uses her paintbrush to paint an image of the scene.
Three days earlier, Gupan had entrusted you with investigating the "Arcane Artist" in the Tiger's Maw. You then decide to track down witnesses and begin gathering information.

Huaijin reveals that the monsters lurking around the mine have been acting strangely, and hints that they might be linked to some painting scrolls. Huaijin also warns you that there is likely more than one person involved in the case.
Jifeng elaborates on more key details of the attacks, leading you to suspect that they are not random events, but something far more deliberate.

While investigating sightings of the monsters and the Arcane Artist, you run into Zhezhi. She explains she is also investigating the chaos caused by the Arcane Artist. Realizing you are after the same thing, you suggest asking a local mineral merchant for more information.

With the merchant Shilang's encouragement, Zhezhi drums up the courage to ask to be your friend and is relieved by your response. To shift the conversation away from Shilang's friendly teasing, she mentions the Arcane Artist. You learn that some suspicious individuals had purchased heaps of leftover ore and even stole from Shilang at night. To confirm the details, you check Shilang's transaction records.

Your discussion is interrupted by Chixia's arrival. Zhezhi, feeling shy and a little awkward, is unsure how to decline Chixia's invitation to return to the city. Just when she is about to give in to Chixia's friendly insistence, you politely excuse both of you from the gathering. Chixia mentions she is also investigating the Tacet Discords that have been acting strangely. Just then, a loud noise nearby interrupts your conversation and you all decide to check it out.
Regretting her earlier hesitation, Zhezhi promises to speak up more decisively as you make your way to the scene.

You learn from Chixia and a researcher that the Tacet Discords had gone wild due to a frequency fluctuation from a painting scroll found at the site. The scroll's power came from the artist's nearly Overclocked Forte.

While investigating Mingyan, the artist in question, you discover she had once studied art alongside Zhezhi. Although Mingyan's fragmented speech suggests that she may be guilty, her expression hints at a more complicated story. However, she is unwilling to reveal more.

From the witness Su, you learn that Mingyan appeared lost, waving her paintbrush moments before a swarm of Tacet Discords emerged from nowhere. It also seemed like she had tried to stop the monsters from harming anyone.
Yinfeng, another witness, claimed that Mingyan created the dangerous painting purely for personal gain.

After piecing together the clues, you uncover the truth. Mingyan used her Forte to create temporary phantasms in her art that attracted Tacet Discords. The "monsters" reported by witnesses were merely distorted phantasms seen by frightened people in the dark. Zhezhi insists that Mingyan was not motivated by personal gain, and asks that you continue to search for evidence to clear her name in her art studio.

In Mingyan's studio, you discovered pieces of "White Jade Paper." Zhezhi introduces its unique qualities with an artist's keen eye. Drawing from her understanding of the paper and Mingyan's habits, Zhezhi begins to build a theory about what happened prior to Mingyan's incident.

Among Mingyan's drafts, Zhezhi recognizes copies of the "Serenity of Xiehua Village," each painted in subtly different ways. As you examine the details, Zhezhi notices pigment stains on her clothes and quickly realizes that the quality of the paint is lower than usual.
A find a stained piece of clothing, prompting Zhezhi to recall how she used to use her clothing as makeshift canvases. She suggests that Mingyan might have done something similar.

You find Mingyan's notes that reveal her struggles as an artist and the pressure she felt while painting against her true desires. Zhezhi reflects on how common this feeling is among creators. Having once faced the same confusion, Zhezhi expresses her determination to uncover the truth and help save Mingyan.

You stumble upon medicinal herb residue. Zhezhi, inexperienced with such materials, initially thinks it is just leftover pigment. Finding this makes you realize that Mingyan had not been feeling well before the incident.

Zhezhi speculates that a Gulpuff might have escaped from the studio. While the theory seems questionable, you appreciate her effort, spurring Zhezhi to try again. Impressed by her Forte use, you learn that Zhezhi rarely uses her Resonance abilities. Zhezhi confesses that her Forte, which closely resembles Mingyan's, may somehow be connected to Mingyan's uncharacteristic outburst.

At an Exile camp, you find piles of ore fragments and handmade pigments. The amount perfectly matches what you saw in Shilang's transaction records. This confirms that these Exiles were the ore thieves and that Mingyan had purchased their low-quality pigments.
The Exiles admit to knowing Mingyan and admiring her exceptional art. They claim they tried to stop her from creating dangerous paintings, but their efforts had been in vain.

Zhezhi senses that neither the Exiles nor Mingyan are being truthful. She notices that some Exiles have blackened hands, a sign they are secretly producing pigments and inks for some unknown purpose. Suspicious of their deception, you decide to sneak into the camp at night to uncover the truth.

During your infiltration, you overhear a conversation revealing that these supposed Exiles are actually employees of the Shanyun Art Exchange. This confirms that the Art Exchange is involved in Mingyan's plight and hints at their involvement in churning out art forgeries.

From their conversation, you discover that Yinfeng, the witness from the crime scene, had signed Shilang's transaction record. Yinfeng had framed Mingyan to cover up their illegal activities. To verify Zhezhi's suspicions about a certain "batch of paintings" mentioned in the Exiles' conversation, you decide to disguise yourselves and investigate further.

During your infiltration, you overhear a conversation revealing that these supposed Exiles are actually employees of the Shanyun Art Exchange. This confirms that the Art Exchange is involved in Mingyan's plight and hints at their involvement in churning out art forgeries. You also learn that Yinfeng, the witness from the crime scene, had signed Shilang's transaction record. Yinfeng had framed Mingyan to cover up their illegal activities. To verify Zhezhi's suspicions about a certain "batch of paintings" mentioned in the Exiles' conversation, you decide to disguise yourselves and investigate further.

You find a recording of Mingyan asking to leave the Art Exchange's schemes, only to be threatened by Yinfeng. It appears that Yinfeng has also been reporting all of Mingyan's actions to Mr. Baici, his boss.

Inside the camp's warehouse, you find countless copies of famous artworks, proving that Mingyan had been coerced into creating forgeries for the Art Exchange. You immediately share this information with the Patrollers. Meanwhile, Zhezhi discovers the original "Serenity of Xiehua Village," the stolen masterpiece. She begins to explain how she recognized it amidst all the forgeries, but is interrupted by a horde of Tacet Discords.

After defeating the monsters, you realize that the painting's frequency had attracted them. Zhezhi laments that her presence must trigger the emotional frequencies in Mingyan's paintings and that her Forte may have played a role in inciting Mingyan's obsession. You reassure Zhezhi that the blame lies neither with her nor the painting.

Yinfeng dismisses the value of an artist's passion and tries to silence you with money. Outraged but resolute, Zhezhi stands her ground, determined to expose the dark side of the Shanyun Art Exchange and save all the artists who are been coerced into producing forgeries.

In the hearing, you present the evidence—the recording, art forgeries, and the low-quality pigments—to prove how the Art Exchange coerced painters into producing counterfeit works. However, Baici defends himself with different excuses. At that moment, Zhezhi gathers her courage and reveals a hidden truth: she is the original creator of "Serenity of Xiehua Village."
Zhezhi faces her past and takes control of her Forte, preparing to use it to back up her claim and embrace the responsibility that comes with her talent.

The painting Zhezhi creates during the hearing, combined with the message you sent to the Patrollers, leaves Baici no choice but to confess. The Public Security Bureau announces they will re-evaluate Mingyan's charges and launch a full investigation. Victory is yours.
After the hearing, Zhezhi thanks you for your unwavering support and expresses her relief at the outcome. Together, you plan to visit Mingyan.

When Mingyan learns about your efforts, she expresses her deep gratitude and apologizes to Zhezhi. She admits that the incident makes her question whether she is truly meant to be an artist. Zhezhi encourages her to follow her heart, gifting her a painting she had once received from Mingyan. Staring at her own work, Mingyan grows emotional, lost in thought.

Happy for Mingyan's change of heart, Zhezhi tells you that solving this case isn't just about helping Mingyan, but also about living up to your expectations. Touched by your reassurance, Zhezhi playfully teases you for the first time. While it may still be difficult for her to open up around others, she has made great strides thanks to your support.
As the Moon-Chasing Festival approaches, you receive a call from Yangyang, Chixia, and Baizhi who invite you to join the celebration at Taoyuan Vale.

After catching up with the trio there, you share your recent experiences at Mount Firmament, while they fill you in on the tale of Moontree Lodge—where every wish made beneath its branches is said to come true. Chixia suspects that an unsung hero might be making these wishes happen and playfully suggests you try your luck under the Wishing Tree before you part ways.
On your way to the Wishing Tree, a peculiar red robot catches your eye.
You ask around and learn that this little robot might have some connection to the Moontree Lodge.

When you reach the Wishing Tree, you encounter the robot's owner, Xiangli Yao, Principal Investigator at the Huaxu Academy. Xiangli Yao explains that his robot, "Patty," is malfunctioning, and its nonsensical speech makes you realize that Xiangli Yao might just be the unsung hero Chixia mentioned. Xiangli asks you to keep that a secret. After learning you are there to make a wish, he suggests stopping by the Wishing Stall for a chat.

Xiangli Yao reveals that Patty has encountered some technical difficulties, likely due to four unreadable wishes, which he believes are causing the malfunction. Wanting to ensure everyone enjoys the festival, you offer to help Xiangli Yao resolve the issue.

The first wish is from a researcher, though you are unsure who they are. Xiang-LEE, a silver robot created by Xiangli, provides a reasonable analysis, helping you begin your search for the wisher's true desire. Just as you prepare to investigate, Xiangli Yao receives an emergency call—a prototype's core has gone out of control, and he must leave immediately, entrusting you and Xiang-LEE with the investigation.

Outside the Academy, Xiang-LEE analyzes the characteristics of the wisher, and they seem to match a young woman nearby. She introduces herself as Zhezhi, a painter, but it turns out she isn't the person you're looking for after all.

You overhear two researchers discussing something called "Nighttime Blues Syndrome" and decide to ask one of them, Shifan, about the wisher you are looking for. During your conversation, Xiang-LEE accidentally detects a connection between the wisher and the syndrome. As the robot processes the information, Shifan seems flustered for a moment and quickly bids you farewell.

Just then, a researcher named Jiuli, who had been eavesdropping, approaches and tells you that Shifan is indeed the wisher. Jiuli reveals that he and Shifan were once close friends, united by their passion for Echo research, but they've since grown distant. Jiuli is eager to understand what caused the rift between them and suggests you pique Shifan's interest by gathering Echo-related research data.
After collecting the necessary data, Xiang-LEE suddenly speaks in Xiangli Yao's voice. It turns out Xiangli Yao is remotely controlling Xiang-LEE to assist you in uncovering Shifan's true desire.

When you speak with Shifan again, he opens up about his true wish, confessing that he has been burdened with guilt ever since Jiuli was injured in a lab accident. At that moment, Jiuli appears, expressing his feelings. Though the two seem to argue, you can tell that their friendship is strong, and you are certain Shifan's wish will eventually come true.
The second wish involves a difficult choice. Following the same approach as with Shifan, you decide to track down the wisher, Ms. Heying, and hear her story.
During your conversation, Ms. Heying shares the promise she made to her late son, Xiuyuan. Wanting to ease her pain, you take her to Taoyuan Vale to experience the festival's joy.
While at the Moon Shooter Stall, you encounter some Midnight Rangers whom Xiuyuan once mentored. They speak fondly of Xiuyuan and his legacy, gradually helping to soothe Ms. Heying's grief.

With the second wish resolved, you hear two children, Li and Momo, arguing over something related to the Hero Plays. From their conversation, you discover that the third wisher, Mahn, is hiding in his secret base.

When you find Mahn, he is in awe of your past victory against the Tacet Discords and considers you the super Resonator from the Hero Plays. As you chat, you come to understand why he made his wish, and you decide to teach him what it truly means to be a hero. Naturally, the best way to do this is by finding a real-life hero to serve as his role model.

You return to the Wishing Stall and discuss potential candidates for Mahn's hero with Xiangli Yao. As you weigh the options, Xiangli Yao suggests that you are the best choice. To solidify this idea, Xiangli adjusts your Terminal to record your daily life, intending to use it as a reference for Mahn.
At Panhua's Restaurant, you receive a call from Chixia inviting you to the upcoming Moonlit Fair.
Back in the real world, Xiangli Yao needs to check on Patty's condition and suggests meeting up later. You decide to spend time at Taoyuan Vale.
You meet Mahn and his friends, who, after watching the reference video, gain a better understanding of what it means to be a true hero.
You encounter Shifan and Jiuli, who reconcile and restart their Echo research.
You find Ms. Heying and some Midnight Rangers, who, having learned to cook from Xiuyuan, make pastries for her. Ms. Heying feels less lonely and lost.
You meet Zhezhi, who is drawing the scenery of the Moon-Chasing Festival. Despite her shyness, she seems uplifted by the festivities.

Under the Wishing Tree, Xiangli Yao informs you that Patty has become a portal to a Sonoro Sphere, and the abnormal data likely hides within the fourth wish. To ensure the Moonlit Fair runs smoothly, you, Abby, and Xiangli Yao decide to enter and investigate this Sonoro.

When you finally meet up with Xiangli Yao, you discuss Pascar's obsession with the ultimate truth. Xiangli Yao worries about being consumed by the same obsession and abandoning everything. You reassure him by emphasizing the enduring bonds between people. To prove your words, you offer your hand to Xiangli Yao and invite him to enjoy the festival together.

Separated from Xiangli Yao by a turbulent data torrent, you and Abby find yourselves in a room resembling a studio. After investigating, you realize the space is based on Xiangli Yao's childhood memories. You encounter young Xiangli Yao, who is waiting for his father while his friends Pascar, Modi, and Ryan invite him to make wishes at the Moontree Lodge.

In the next room, you discover a Wishing Stall with decorations that don't match this year's theme. Xiangli Yao and Pascar, now more mature, discuss the paths intellectuals should take and each makes their own choice.
You uncover Xiangli Yao's connection with the Moontree Lodge and continue exploring to reveal the hidden truth.

After defeating the Twisted Obsessions, Pascar's illusion appears and reveals the truth, surprised by Xiangli Yao's comments about how his research inspired many and laid the foundation for the "Pascar Spectrum" theory. With his wish fulfilled, Pascar's illusion asks Xiangli Yao to witness the world they have protected before disappearing.

Whoa! I knew it be strong, but not that strong.
Does this mean it really is...
Hey... {PlayerName}, Abby...
Phew... We finally caught up with you. You move too fast. What happened just now... Was it another TD?
Hmph, that's right. But {PlayerName} and I took care of it with the old one-two. No biggie.
Well, aren't you two sharp...
Yes, they sure are... Huh? Mr. Millkeeper... did you just say something?
...Are you both warriors drawn here by the knight's legend?
Haven't seen such fools in a long time. Watching you two charge in like that... exactly like the ones that came before you.
You mean there were others? I don't think I've ever seen any besides you, Mr. Millkeeper.
Of course there were. Some choose to move on, and some... well, they just aged out.
Who were they?
The so-called Windmill Keepers in today's language. But back in the day, I... We were called knights too—though more accurately, we were considered fake knights who excelled at deception.
We were outcasts, people in distress, and many ordinary folks who were drawn in by the legend. We'd find an old horse and cobble together some makeshift armor, and fashion a sword.
We clung to our notions of the knight's oath, laughingstocks wherever we went, dreaming of exploring Whisperwind Haven and even venturing beyond its limits.
Legends of knighthood continued to spread, but over time, the knights in these stories grew more noble and refined with every retelling...
When the people of Egla Town finally realized that there were newcomers settling in Whisperwind Haven, the nameless knights had already become the Windmill Keepers.
S-So what you're saying is… the Windmill Keepers weren't protecting the Windmills. They were watching over... Whisperwind Haven.
It wasn't till we arrived that we realized the many dangers lurking throughout the land. Moving forward wasn't as simple as we thought.
Then a knight tossed a ring made of rough steel onto the table and said briskly, "Let's carve out a path ahead."
"Soon enough, others will follow and reach the same place we have..."
My younger self wouldn't dare believe words spoken so lightly. A new path meant risking everything, even our lives.
That knight might have noticed my hesitation. He came over to talk to me and recited his oath.
"In the name of Korlacchi, I hold fast to humility and justice... Across the rivers of time, wherever my path may lead, I vow to uphold justice and fairness for all..."
He was right. This was the path we all swore to... and he stuck to it until the very end, right here in Whisperwind Haven.
B-But how were you so sure that more people would come? What if...
Ha... Remember the ring? We were knights skilled in deception, so why not make it all one grand performance?
He would travel far and wide with those rings, and in the name of Korlacchi, preach the knightly way to anyone who dared dream of becoming one.
Regardless of wealth, title, or position...
So who was he?
Funny you ask. Despite his vigor, he was just an ordinary farmer from the countryside...
An ordinary farmer... A knight of deceit... Korlacchi. Never really existed...
Carlow!
Abby, stop him!
Carlow runs away in a hurry. As Mr. Millkeeper looks confused by Carlow's outburst, you explain that Carlow has been chasing after the knight.
...I see. That must be a bitter pill for the boy to swallow. All this time chasing after a dream only to find out it was an illusion all along.
This wasn't where he lost the knight's trail. It's where his journey ended.
People love to romanticize the past, don't they? The knight in shining armor we saw as children was really just an ordinary farmer in tattered rags riding a frail old horse.
Please, apologize to him for me. We are liars, nothing more. But... once he's cooled off, he will come to understand. He's been seeking what we once sought, after all.
Everyone who made it here left their marks. The trails they walked, the words they spoke, the tales of the ones who explored the furthest reaches of Whisperwind Haven...
These things shine brighter than any life and are more genuine than any knightly title.
Have you... ever felt lonely on this path?
Haha, perhaps this path of chivalry we uphold is always meant to be walked alone. Besides, "he" is always there.
You must have met him, right? The Echo that you used in the battle just now was displaying his sword skills.
You mean the Mad Knight?
Mad Knight? So that's what the townsfolk call him. Not bad... At least he's got a title now.
What exactly is it...
"He" appeared around the same time as the Windmill Keepers. There's no doubt "he" is a Tacet Discord.
But the swordsmanship, the way he speaks, and his stance against other TDs all remind me of him.
People say that TDs can absorb lingering frequencies...
I believe he exists because the essence of knighthood has taken root deep in Whisperwind Haven.

He swings his sword against enemies to protect the things he loves. When he points his sword at the common folk he meets, I think he's challenging them to a duel... He hopes someone will accept his challenge.
He is showing that to be a true knight, one must abandon uncertainty, confront fears, and wield their sword with courage.
Can you tell me your name, and the others?
I'd like your name to remember you.
Names... Hmm, no one's asked that before. What's wrong with using a common title?
Oh, I know. {PlayerName} is great at picking names. Come on, do your magic!
Nameless... Windmill...
Let's call you Whisperwind Knight.
Like the wind, it leaves a trail that's difficult to trace, yet it journeys to distant lands...
Whisperwind Knight...
Carlow has probably made it back to town by now. What are you going to say when you see him...?
He should have had enough time to think things over. Let's go speak to him.
What do we have here? Our little pretend knight isn't out chasing footprints today. Just standing there like he's lost his spark.
By the way, have you received the invitation? We're just about to buy the attire for the ceremony. Why don't you join us?
Not every day you get to have a "real" knight be as your guide, after all...
Come on. We've wasted enough time here already...
Hey... Those are the two we met earlier.
Shh...
Forget it. You may as well be a rock if you've nothing to say. Off we go on...
...(Breathes deeply.)
In the name of Korlacchi, I pledge to show mercy and kindness to the weak...
I will remain true to all that I love and protect until my last breath.
Across the rivers of time, wherever my path may lead, I vow to uphold justice and fairness for all...
What's got into you? Reciting your little fantasy knight's oath now?
Right here, I, Carlow, swear to the knight's code and challenge you to a duel.
Do you know which part of the fish is the best? Can you practice your sword skills with just a simple wooden pole? Do you know the best path deeper into Whisperwind Haven...?
Have you ever truly helped someone without expecting anything in return, or charged toward a giant with no thought for yourself?
This duel... it all comes down to an apology. The loser must apologize to the victor...
Hey, check it out. I think Carlow's got that wannabe tough guy acting all scared.
Let's go.
Huh? What if Carlow gets bullied...
Let knights handle their own matters. In the name of Korlacchi...
So, what does Korlacchi mean anyhow?
Someone needs to visit the library more often.
Huh? No way. Not happening. Reading makes me nauseous. Just tell me the answer already!
Korlacchi, in the Rinascita language, means courage.
You feel a sting. You suddenly feel like you've forgotten something.

Fragments of Distant Memories

...Mom! This building is so tall!
Today, our school took us on a tour. The guide told us that this is the tallest building in the world!
Tonight, the view from the top will be even better! But our class won't get to visit the rooftop until tomorrow night, so we have to wait another day.
Mom, do you think that when I stand on the rooftop, I'll be closer to Dad?
Will he be able to see me from up there as a star?
I asked the guide about it today, but she didn't answer.
The food tonight is delicious. It's my first time eating in a restaurant this high up! The utensils here are different from the ones we use at home...
I didn't expect to cross paths with you here, {PlayerName}.
This place... it's quite amazing. As I walked through, I felt as if I was drifting between past memories and, at times, into the fantasies of others.
We're in the dreamscape.
I see. That would explain a lot.
Is something troubling you?
Dreams always stir mixed emotions in me. For a long time, I was plagued by nightmares.
Sleepless nights filled with images of my people displaced, shivering in the cold, and facing hunger. We were all so small before the might of the Lament.
Yet, those nightmares serve as a constant reminder of the complex challenges our people face, the burdens I bear as the Magistrate of Jinzhou.
It's okay to take a rest sometimes.
Let go of your responsibilities! You're in a dream!
But aren't you working just as hard to protect what you hold dear?
This ear of millet... it holds deep meaning for me, but now, I'd like you to have it. May everything go smoothly for you on your journey.
Ah... that is reminiscing
What happened?
I just had a dream from my past.
Simple dishes—plain noodles and soft steamed buns—but even in the dream, they appeared irresistible.
Really?
Steamed buns and noodles?
Surprised? In my childhood, I wandered the streets, often plagued by hunger. Each time I passed a restaurant or a food stall, my steps felt heavier.
Back then, all I longed for was a decent meal—so much so that it echoed even in my dreams.
That must have been tough for you.
It's behind me now. Look at me, healthy and well, am I not?
When peace is finally enjoyed across the land, no one will have to starve as I once did.
When we wake, let's go grab a meal together.
I'll treat you to a feast in reality.
Hehe, I won't say no to that. Then, it's a promise.
Here, take this journal. It contains some recommendations. I hope you find it useful.
Anything to share with me?
What happened?
Listen.
You faintly hear the sounds of waves crashing against the shore—they seem distant, yet stirring emotions within you.
Those sounds always take me back to the moments we shared—bathed in soft moonlight, with fine sand beneath us, and the rhythm of your breath and heartbeat filling the air.
You really cherish those memories, don't you?
...It reassured me that I have indeed kept our memories for you.
We'll create even more memories together.
Let's explore more of the world together.
Indeed, our connection will only grow stronger.
Let these bright stars guide you on your journey.

{PlayerName}... I-I think I just saw someone else's dream.
It was in a small, dim room. A child, with her parents watching so warmly, blew out the candles on a tiny cake... and smiled.
You seem a bit moved.
Yes... It was such a simple, ordinary moment, but it felt so full of happiness.
Maybe I had moments like that when I was little too.
But I can't remember anymore... I've gotten so used to being alone. And in my dreams, my parents always seem so... stern, so far away.
You've always been strong.
But you're not alone anymore.
N-no... I'm not strong... but if that's how you see me, I-I'll try to live up to your expectations.
Um... t-thank you... It makes me really happy to hear that, b-but... I don't know how to respond...
I've probably taken up too much of your time. Please, take this painting with you.
Even if it was just a dream, it holds a lot of my feelings... a-and I want to share them with you.
Ah, you're here. Speaking of which, I've stumbled upon quite a few... intriguing nightmares lately.
Seriously? Intriguing for nightmares?
Yes. I encountered different dreamers, but they all feared the same figure—though her appearance varied from one dream to the next.
Sometimes she appeared as a stern office worker, sometimes a lowlife street thug, and other times... a lone Exile wandering the wilds.
Ah, I see. That person... it was you, wasn't it?
Those were criminals' nightmares about you, right?
Well, I rarely reveal myself during a mission, but it's amusing when the "lucky few" get a glimpse.
If they're haunted by a little... trauma, it might make them hesitate the next time they think of causing trouble.
But you don't seem happy.
You've sacrificed a lot.
Hehe, trying to console me, are you, darling? Playing these sinister roles is simply part of the game. It's only natural that I appear in their nightmares.
But I see the real you—not the masks you wear.
I always see you as who you are.
You certainly know what to say, don't you?
Then come closer. I want to reward you with... a memory that tingles just right.
So, it really is you. I owe you my gratitude.
For...?
What happened?
I was trapped in yet another endless dream, fighting Tacet Discords alone. No matter how many I vanquished, they continued to rise.
The voices of the fallen cursed my every step, assailing my spirit. Yet, amidst the chaos, a radiant, golden light broke through the darkness.
It was fleeting, but soon after, you appeared.
But I didn't do anything.
You're the one who endured to the end.
Before, such dreams felt eternal, persisting until I awoke.
Yet, ever since we've crossed paths, I haven't been haunted by them again.
That dream will never become reality.
If you ever falter, I'll stand beside you and support you.
Thank you... If you're heading to somewhere perilous, take this lance.
May it grant you safe passage through every trial, and may it help you prevail the lasting night.

Fallacy of No Return: Dream of Desperation
Welcome back, Dreamwalker.
I didn't expect to see you again so soon.
I liked you better as that white cat.
Well, like I said before, there are still many things to handle within the gateway.
Ahem… I'm back in action now, so let's not dilly-dally with all of that
Since your last visit, the Somnoire has stopped expanding into reality and is gradually returning to its normal state.
However, those extra dreams haven't all been released yet…
What happened to those dreams?
The overloaded Somnoire started "packing" those dreams to save space.
Like creating a big "zip file" of dreams?
Exactly! It's a workaround for the space issue, but now those compressed dreams have turned into abnormal masses.
They're wreaking havoc around here. They keep absorbing other dreams to grow stronger, causing even more chaos.
Can't you stop them from merging?
I tried, but I don't have the right clearance. The Somnoire's self-cleaning function is also currently disabled.
Where's the Ebony Gatekeeper?
I'm still searching for him. He may still be in deep slumber, recovering his strength…
Dreamwalker, keep exploring and restoring the Somnoire. Stay alert, there's no telling what you'll encounter.
Of course, you can count on me.
(Pet the white cat)
Thank you, Dreamwalker.
Meow… Hey! I'm not a cat anymore!
This will help you on your journey. Use it wisely.
Is this the Ebony Gatekeeper's work again?
No, quite the opposite, actually. This is happening because he lost most of his power and influence.
I knew you'd come back…
There are many terrifying things ahead. They are devouring every dream they find.
I can see them... all the dreams, both sweet and nightmarish, trapped inside those giant masses...
Free those dreams, just like you did before…
Dreamwalker, may your mind stay lucid, and may your steps be light.
Huh... it seems like we find ourselves together in this dream again.
Hello, Zhezhi.
We just said our goodbyes, and here we are again so soon. Is it because I can't stop thinking about showing {PlayerName} my paintings...?
You said that out loud.
Oh! Um… W-well, actually, I'm really happy to see you again.
Louder, please.
Me too.
P-please don't tease me! Um… By the way, I remember you have something urgent to attend to, right?
Wh-what…? You feel the same?
A-anyway. You have something urgent to attend to, right?
While you were away, I went on a field trip to gather inspiration and do some sketching.
I didn't have time to perfect all the details, but... I-I hope you can take this with you. Maybe it'll be helpful!
Adventure calls!
Hooray!
Adventure never ends.
This time, the big bad guy is the White Cat Demon King! It's taken over the palace in the Kingdom of Grapes and is turning everyone's dreams into a mess!
You do know the Demon King is standing right beside you, right?
Humph! I can't believe the mighty Demon King actually came to the Warrior's Village to stop the hero before {Male=he;Female=she} even sets out!
But don't worry! Mayor Encore was ready for this!
O brave Warrior, take our strongest Echo—it will help you on your quest!
I hear trouble is brewing in the dreams, huh?
That's just how things go in the dream world.
I'm here to handle it.
Looks like dangers are lurking in this dream world, just like in reality…
If you let your mind wander for a second, you never know what might jump out at you.
So, are you here to help?
Of course, darling. We share the same goal, after all.
By the way, I found this nearby. Here, take it.
Let's finish up here quickly, and in return for my little gift... Promise me you'll save some time for me in the real world, okay?
Well, well, I didn't think we could have this kind of fun here.
Do whatever you want—let's make it more intense, more fiery, more electrifying than the real world…
I'll handle you later.
You're next once I've handled things here.
Are you going to keep me waiting again? Why can't we fight right now?
Because I have something urgent to take care of.
Fine… I'll behave. There's still plenty of time for us, hehe.
I can feel it... Those chaotic energies are gathering somewhere. Looks like there's a big surprise in store for you.
I'll be right back.
Hehe, take this little cutie with you and hurry back, my seed of fate.
{PlayerName}, I was musing about their relationship.
Do you mean the dynamics between the Ebony and Ivory Gatekeepers?
Yes, the Somnoire's guardians. Are they rivals or allies?
I think it's a bit of both.
Sometimes they work together, and other times they clash.
Hmm… They're like two sides of the same coin—interdependent yet counterbalancing. The Somnoire reflects that balance.
The recent disturbances were the result of a series of actions that tipped the scales, rather than the fault of one side going off track.
So, we need to restore the balance.
Are you suggesting I shouldn't favor the Ivory Gatekeeper?
Just my humble opinion. No need to dwell on it. Here, take this pouch. It may prove useful on your journey.
By the way, I'd love to hear about your adventures when you're back, if you have time.
{PlayerName}, good to see you again!
Lumi?
Why are you still here?
It's Lumi, the logistics team's good ol' captain.
Why can't I be here? Are you worried that I might be someone else?
There are still lots of messes to clean up, and besides, the dream's not over yet.
You remember what happened before, right?
Of course! We teamed up and took down that big cat, right?
Don't ya know dreams can pick up where they left off? Must be thanks to that Ivory Gatekeeper, huh?
Maybe so.
He helped a lot, didn't he?
Anyway, now that we're back, let's shake things up! No regrets when we wake up!
Oh, by the way, I ran into this quiet lady on my way here. She asked me to deliver this package to you.
A package?
Yep! Just sign here, and—another satisfied customer!
So this is how it is... I see...
What did you find?
What is that?
The dreams of the Black Shores act like a gravitational center, pulling in other dreams to form entities of extreme density.
Those perished members of the Black Shores… Their thoughts linger and evolve within the dreams.
Their unshakable longings and aspirations lie deep within layers of volatile frequencies.
But why are they trying to destroy the Somnoire?
No, it's not destruction they want. They're trying to break free.
They are trying to escape from this space and return to the real world they once strove to save.
…A lost cause.
It's futile to try to bridge the gap between dreams and reality.
…But they dove headfirst into the Lament, fully knowing they were likely to fail. Maybe it was that same determination that drove them to take this path.
{PlayerName}, please release them.
I will.
This is the only thing we can do for them.
We are not here to prove that resistance is futile, but to mark that… we don't go down without a fight…
When those who follow see our gravestones, they will understand… humanity never surrenders…
We won't retreat… ██. This is our final task… Not everyone is lucky enough to bear this responsibility…
We're so close to getting the accurate modeling of ██… Just give me a bit more time, as long as it's before the Lament strikes…
Gravity... is the only pre-Lament law of physics that still holds true today…
{PlayerName}, you've helped them break free from their hopeless quest to return home.
So, that's it? It's over?
Those scattered dreams will still wander this realm, but they won't be burdened by those overwhelming desires anymore.
Do you regret putting an end to those longings and obsessions?
Their spirits still remain.
They will live on in our memories, won't they?
You are right. The time has come.
What time?
The Black Shores in a dream is not where I truly belong… I must go.
With the help of those two Gatekeepers, you will surely surely help to restore this place back to normal.
What's wrong?
It's just… who knows when we'll meet again in our dreams.
Let's meet one day when we wake up.
Yes, when we wake up... tomorrow.
You sorted out those dream masses. Well done.
Why are you here?
Where's the Ivory Gatekeeper?
He's trying to contain those scattered dream fragments.
But it's not an easy job to retrieve them all in such a vast realm as the Somnoire.
You're not to blame for that.
Don't worry, I'll come up with a plan...
Never stop exploring, Dreamwalker. Only in dreams will we find the answers we need.

You accept the bowl of pasta from Tina. The homecooked flavors seem especially comforting in the moment.
Maybe it's because of all the energy you burned earlier, or maybe food just tastes better when enjoyed with company.
You put down the plate and go inside the tent to help.
I'll come with you. I'm sure they'd appreciate the extra hand.
I'll come with you. I'm sure they'd appreciate the extra hand.
What?! She's still alive?
Wait, I didn't mean it like that! Back when we checked the ship's cabins, we thought she was already...
Ugh, I can't believe myself right now!
It's all right. We can still save her.
We should disinfect her wounds before removing the splinters... No rush, nice and steady.
Tina and Roccia manage to treat the little girl's wounds. Her breathing gradually steadies.
Phew... that was close.
She's past the worst part. She'll recover soon.
How about the others, Tina?
All fed and steadily recovering.
Even though they're just kinda staring at the ground.
Well, they've been drifting at sea for so many days, and now they've washed up somewhere completely new.
They're like a sponge that's been soaked in water. All heavy and waterlogged. It'll take a while for them to bounce back.
What do you think we should do...?
Why don't we try talking to them?
Yes. We should see if anyone needs anything.
Hello. How's your arm?
Feeling much better. Thanks for patching me up.
Filippo's hand is now covered in bandages and is no longer swollen.
Those pain relievers you used are from Rosemary's Apothecary, right? My family used to live not far from them. I'd recognize that smell anywhere.
Sometimes I think about home. Other times, I'd rather not.
I miss my soft couch and the smell of herbs wafting from the apothecary. But those Order activities? Those boring plays full of Codex verses? No thanks.
You know, I bet if the Blessed Maiden were still around, she'd loathe this form of penitance.
"A thousand stars light up the air. Freedom blooms like flowers wide." That was her favorite line from an opera.
That's a line from Pegasus.
Exactly. It's about a world where people can choose their own beliefs instead of blindly following some rigid creed.
Mandatory gatherings, worship, enforced codes of conduct... They even dictate what plays we can watch and how we should laugh and smile.
Oh, I want to go home, I really do... but Ragunna isn't the same place anymore.
During our so-called pilgrimage, people played lunachords and flutes. Everyone on board gathered around a "star" to sing opera and uplift each other's spirits.
In those moments, I felt that as long as we could sing freely together, the Pilgrim's Sail could become my new home.
But as we drifted farther out to sea, we faced more dangers, and fewer of us survived. Even our instruments got wrecked.
And now... there's no way to perform again with what's left of us.
I'm lost now. Nowhere to go, and no home to return to.
The brief smile that once graced his lips has vanished, leaving his face shrouded in sadness.
Hello, sir. Are you feeling better?
Much better. Thank you for the pasta.
Oh, that warmth… that taste of home. For a moment there, I thought I was dreaming.
It took me back to Margherita's, having the usual from their brunch menu... Oh, that's something I thought I'd get to enjoy for the rest of my life.
But... here I am, simply because I sang a few lines from Pegasus...
Pegasus. I see...
That's right. Folks on the ship used to perform together, letting the day's mood pick the song. Just had to keep an eye out for the Order.
That one was an all-time favorite.
Would you ever get tired of it?
Get tired of it? No, why would we do that?
It's a real gem, that one. Lifted everyone's spirits during the hard times.
If only the world were like that, where everyone lives freely. I wouldn't have to endure so much at this age...
They called it a "pilgrimage," but Tacet Discords pursued us the entire journey... We lost so many. The truth is clear to everyone now.
Sigh I survived, while so many young souls did not...
I didn't even have the strength to take their cherished belongings with me...
Everyone has been through so much...

I lost the goods Signor Marcello entrusted to me, and it's all because of that Mad Knight... What kind of knight attacks a merchant caravan anyway?
Surely you jest—one wrong move and I'm toast!
Welcome to Burrata Bakery! Would you like to try the most authentic traditional flavors of Rinascita?
I'd like to see the menu.
Is it really authentic?
Do you know Margherita?
Chat.
Thank you. I'm good now.
Here you go! Here's today's menu. Let me know if there's anything you'd like.
Of course! Every bite you take here is a taste of the century-old rich culinary heritage!
Pizza's delicious, and the bread's hearty! However, we do get the occasional customers with sensitive teeth saying it's a bit too sturdy...
Margherita is a childhood friend of mine. Despite her small stature, she's actually a culinary genius!
I used to be upset about her willful alteration of traditional recipes, but then I realized, isn't it a chef's duty to create dishes that everyone loves?
Nowadays, they even consider Trattoria Margherita a place for traditional local food, just like Burrata Bakery... Honestly, do these outsiders even understand?
You've probably heard the saying, "Crownapple has no place on a pizza!"
I'm probably a conservative if these people are considered radicals—I mean, they're radically conservative for me.
"Nothing but cheese and gemberry sauce on our pizza!" That's the creed here!
Feel free to drop by anytime! Burrata Bakery is always ready with flavorful delights!
Welcome to Egla Town, traveler from afar. May you enjoy your time here.
I'm Wicktorio, the mayor. Feel free to ask me about anything related to the town.
Could you tell me about the history of this place?
What do you recommend here?
About the unattended house.
Thank you. See you around.
Certainly, not many young people care about history these days...

The history of our town begins with the first settlers in Rinascita. Later, The Order united the people during the Dark Tide and established a city-state. Over time, Ragunna City became the cultural and life center of the region.
Egla has managed to preserve its original essence due to its relatively peaceful environment, thus placing greater importance on the traditions of Ragunna.
You can find the most traditional Ragunna cuisine at the Burrata Bakery, or immerse yourself in town life at the Sorrentino Inn.
Or... you could quietly hide behind the curtains at night and enjoy the Night Reveries, prepared for the knights.
The house you're talking about... That family left Rinascita nearly twenty years ago.
It's just old news, not worth delving into. Please don't concern yourself with it.
Goodbye, foreign visitor. May the glory of the Sentinel be with you.
If only I had a golden whip. I could double the number of Tumbleyaks with a gentle flick in the morning! Then, in a month—
I'd turn all the Tumbleyak milk into cheese for Giovanetta to make pizzas! Then I could eat as many as I wanted!
Do you think if we doubled the Tumbleyak every day, would we have enough credits at the end of the month to send Julia to see a play in Ragunna?
Do you really know what 2 to the power of 30 is...?
What? What does "power" mean? Sorry, I actually never went to school.
If we have that many Tumbleyaks... Pela won't have to herd them anymore, right?
Lucio's been heading out to distant fields every day lately... They say the grass around here isn't good for the cattle anymore.
It's almost Pela's birthday again. I should buy her some interesting storybooks this year too...
"Beyond Solaris," "Septimont Holiday," "The Legend of Violinist 2000," "Theatre Paradiso"... Pela has read all these classics.
Oh, sorry, I was lost in thought... My friend, which storybook on the table do you think would be suitable for my daughter?
The Montelli.
John Wicktorio.
Pirates of Ragunna.
The Card Rider Guga.
The Holy Echo War.
None of these fit.
The Montelli... a story centered on the upper echelons of the Montelli family, steeped in themes of crime, conspiracy, assassination, and betrayal. It's just too dark.
John Wicktorio... Some bad people destroyed the loyal Echo of a retired Montelli family accountant, who then revenges by exposing the old nobility's shady dealings... I don't like it.

Pirates of Ragunna... Recounts the adventures of a legendary captain with a morally ambiguous nature. The treasure he seeks and the spoils he plunders are, in truth, the smiles of the people. This story has been banned by The Order.
The Card Rider Guga... It tells of a nameless hero who became a knight to stop the suffering of people, battling creatures known as Threnodian... This story is just too far-fetched.

The Holy Echo War... It tells the story of seven Echo controllers who, driven by their own desires, entered a brutal survival contest in the distant past. It's a tale of ruthless battles and deadly pursuits... This is way too cruel.
That's true... I guess Pela has outgrown these kinds of stories. I should think it over myself.
Hello, welcome to Jamie's Farm. If you're looking for Lucio, he should be herding near Egla Town.
Could you tell me about your family?
What's your birthday wish?
Thank you. See you then.
As you can see, the Jamie family is just an ordinary herding family living outside Egla Town. They lack noble status, background with The Order, or any accumulated wealth.
These are Lucio, Julia, and Pela. Their primary business partners are the merchants and the bakery in Egla Town.
Your way of speaking is quite particular.
Pela exhibits certain cognitive impairments, according to Acolyte Wicktorio's analysis.
Julia and Lucio suffered an incident twenty years ago that left a lasting impact on their minds.
Their offspring, Pela, possesses excellent logical abilities but lacks emotional understanding and self-awareness.
Every year on that day, Lucio and Julia would spend a fortune to prepare storybooks for Pela.
The works they are preparing are poised for commercial success. Thus, Pela surmises that Julia and Lucio expect her to write scripts that will generate profit.
Unfortunately, without empathy, Pela can't become a great author.
Goodbye.
Hello there, traveler.
Stay away from the depths of Whisperwind Haven.
Anything there?
Do you live here alone?
Thank you. Goodbye.
Nothing but the Tacet Discords, illusions, and the traces of fallen knights.
Nothing of value remains.
I'm stationed here to ensure no one strays into the depths of Whisperwind Haven.
Sometimes... I also take care of those who slip through the cracks.
Great to see you, {PlayerName}.
Thank you for helping young Carlow last time, hehe... The Whisperwind Knight Conrad salutes you.
So you remember your own name now?
Are you happy with this title?
Tell me about the past of the Whisperwind Knight.
Good to see you. Gotta leave.
Yes, my name's Conrad, once known as the Wandering Knight Conrad, or Conrad who was never recognized as a true knight.
Before the Order had me marked as a fugitive, I was once a farmer, a fisherman, a carpenter, and a soldier guarding Ragunna against the Dark Tide.
Now just an old man bestowed with the title of Whisperwind Knight.
I'm quite satisfied.
Even if the knights fade from the future history of Ragunna, the wind by the water will remember that we were here.
Twenty years ago, we were just a bunch of country folk inspired by the tales of the Blessed Maiden and the Knights fighting against the Dark Tide. We dreamt of becoming knights ourselves.
We were soldiers, craftsmen, and farmers. While we may not stand beside the knights in battle, we hold our positions steadfastly, inspired by their tales.

After the Dark Tide, we arrived in Ragunna, expecting to see triumphant knights. Instead, in the city square, we found the knights on their knees. The Order condemned them for blasphemy, simply because they suggested a journey to the seminary to seek the Blessed Maiden.
The valiant knights stood tall, shouting defiantly against the sharp blade of the Echoes, invoking the name of Imperator... And some people rushed to save them.
...In the end, we were all deemed accomplices and faced retribution. Those who survived banded together and left Ragunna, becoming the first of the wandering knights.
That's the story of the first Whisperwind Knights.
Goodbye, may glory and courage always light your path.
I won, hahaha! I'll be the knight again today!
"Ha! Let's recount your transgressions! Dark Tide Villain!"
"Can you even count how many times that's happened..." Wait! Wait a minute! That's not fair. Why am I always the one playing the villain?!
Well, Carlow said that in a knight game, you usually need knights and villains for a battle to happen!
No way, no way! Isn't there a knight game where someone doesn't have to play the villain?
I'm not sure about a knight game without any villains... Hmm... Do you have any ideas, {Male=mister;Female=miss}?
The duel of two knights fighting for their own justice!
The tale of a knight who betrayed comrades for a greater cause!
I don't really have any thoughts...
Ohhh! You're right! Bruno, I know which script we should use!
Wait... A script for knightly duels? Could it be...
That's the one!
"I'm definitely not going to die... Bruno, if you take a life, there's no turning back! "
"That's just what I wanted! "
Bruno and Golem begin to seriously play out the knightly tale...
Ohhh! You're right! Bruno, I know which script we should use!
Which one? A script about knights betraying their comrades? Could it be...
That's the one!
"Ha—ha—ha—ha! So, there's only one answer! "
"I swear my loyalty to you! "
Bruno and Golem begin to seriously play out the knightly tale...
So, you're out of ideas too... Golem, why don't you play the Dark Tide Villain instead?
That's not fair!
"Golem, The moment you try to be a hero, you're disqualified."
Bruno and Golem begin to seriously play out the knightly tale...
Firus is truly unreliable. I'll probably have to find the shipment myself.
Mad Knight... Hmph, if he was truly a knight, how could he possibly rob the civilians?
Is losing the goods a big problem?
Yes, quite serious. The Order is watching us closely. Losing the goods will lead to financial deficits, and we'll have to address the shortfall in the accounts.

We can't afford to keep showing over 50% depreciation rate on the ledgers. The tax officials will undoubtedly seize the opportunity to scrutinize the family's cash flow. With the pressure being amplified through the ranks, our accountant might just end up being packed off on a Pilgrim's Sail...
Marcello starts muttering some strange phrases.
Sentinel above, I truly wish to know which noble hero drove away the Mad Knight. Now all the lost goods have been recovered!
I am the one!
Maybe just a knight passing by.
The Mad Knight didn't damage the goods at all... Could it be that he wasn't after credits?
Praise you! Without your help, I would have been forced into that labor contract...
A knight! Could it be... that the legendary knight truly resides here in Egla Town?
Making choices driven by short-term convenience, taking high risks... Why did we entrust such a person with the significant tasks?
I'm sorry for the farce you just witnessed.
Welcome to Egla Town, traveler from afar. May you have a wonderful time here.

Despite that... there have been some unusual circumstances lately, so please avoid going out at night unless absolutely necessary. If you need accommodation, please speak with Damian. He'll help you arrange a room.
What do you mean by unusual circumstances?
Thanks. That's all I need.
Have you ever heard the tale of the knight? Once, a knight ventured deep into the area to vanquish a menacing "giant" that plagued the land. Since then, the knight has become a symbol of this place.
Many knights have been drawn to this place by its fame. And one of them had likely become the "Mad Knight."
It is said that he gradually lost himself during the endless fight against the Tacet Discords...
To placate the Mad Knight, the town created the Night Reveries—endless dramas of the knight enacted by the Echoes. Townsfolk and visitors alike were advised to stay indoors at night.
Heh... How many years have we been strolling here every morning?
I can't remember. My memory is not what it used to be. We're just old fools approaching the grave.
Every time I see this house, I feel as if the child's right before me...
Oh Imperator, is her fate also part of your design?
I'm really grateful for your help with Carlow, {PlayerName}.
Now that the Mad Knight is gone, the endless Night Reveries in Egla Town have finally come to an end.
You seem to miss the drama.
Will this give your business a hard time?
Hah, I just never imagined those old tales of knights would still be unfolding...
My only regret is that I'm no longer worthy of bestowing honors upon them.
It may not be a bad thing if it's so. Lately, Damian's been coming around after hearing something from Carlow.
He's taken a two-month leave to visit Ragunna City. If business slows down a bit, I can manage the inn by myself.
How odd, dreaming once more of the days in the Order...
Why... I saw that child and her knightly companions setting out against the Dark Tide again in the dream.
Is a metal ring really the mark of a fake knight? Heh.
