Chixia contacts you to say that several Jinzhou citizens have recently gone missing. She asks you to stay alert for anything suspicious.

You are both questioned by the Patroller, but the two of you conceal what happened. During the conversation, you discover that the woman is actually a Patroller named Yinlin. After the Patroller leaves, Yinlin reveals that "Yuanyuan" is, in fact, a puppet.

Yinlin tells you that the Séance Society is a dangerous organization that lures people in by promising to bring back their loved ones. They appear to be linked to the Fractsidus, and her mission is to gather evidence against them and identify the mastermind behind it all. Currently, she is investigating the prototype puppets in the hope they hold clues about their creator. Eager to recover your lost memories, you decide to assist Yinlin by following Lirong to the puppets' storage location.
Furious with the Fractsidus for their disdain toward the puppets, Lirong breaks their deal and attempts to escape with the puppets. You quickly follow him.

Yinlin explains that the Séance Society is behind the recent disappearances in Jinzhou. They provide lifelike puppets in place of lost loved ones, and many desperate people join the Society for this reason. However, frequent interaction with these puppets greatly increases the risk of Overclocking. Yinlin is on the trail of those responsible and invites you to meet her outside the city if you want to learn more about the case.

Determined to protect the puppets from becoming Fractsidus experimental subjects, Lirong attempts to hide. He reveals that the leader of the Séance Society is known as the Dollmaker. As the Fractsidus closes in, putting them all in danger, you and Yinlin step in.
Yinlin tries to mediate between the Séance Society and the Fractsidus, but the negotiations fail.

She admits she tracked you using a positioning device placed on you earlier, explaining that her undercover role makes it hard for her to trust anyone. With Lirong and Yuanyuan no longer providing new leads, your only hope lies in the prototype puppets, so you decide to gather as many of them as possible.

After collecting all the prototype puppets, Yinlin plans to take them to a safe place for further investigation. She learns from a fellow Patroller that there is a safehouse nearby for undercover agents, and you both head there.

You soon discover that it was Yinlin who trapped you here. She reveals that this is the Séance Society's base and invites you once more to join the organization, offering to introduce you to its members.
You discover that Jinlu met his fallen comrade He Chang here and chose to stay because of their strong bond.

An anonymous email leads you to Lirong and his daughter, Yuanyuan. Lirong is a member of the Séance Society, a group that claims to reunite members with their loved ones. He invites you to join, but becomes agitated when asked about his daughter's fate, refusing to accept that she is no longer truly alive.
You learn that Lianyue, who also reunited with her deceased child with the Society's help, refuses to let anyone disrupt their current life.

Wu Sheng tells you that even the best doctors can't save everyone, just as he was not able to save his wife. The Dollmaker's puppets gave them a second chance, something no doctor could offer. While Wu Sheng understands the dangers of the puppets, he also knows how much they mean to the people here.

Yinlin reveals that she empathizes with these people who just want to see their loved ones again. She reveals that she was once a member of the Séance Society herself. She grew up alongside the Dollmaker and knows that his experiments are aimed at creating two special puppets. However, she keeps the details of this final experiment from you.
When the Patrollers besiege the base, Yinlin takes you hostage but secretly passes you a message: "Trust me… Come this way."

A mysterious woman arrives and convinces Lirong to leave. After he departs, a fight breaks out between you and the woman over Yuanyuan. The confrontation only ends when a Patroller shows up. To uncover the truth about the Séance Society and the missing persons, you decide to cooperate with the woman, starting by cleaning up the scene.

You learn from Chixia that the injured are recovering, but the Dollmaker still refuses to cooperate. She thanks you for your help, and you hint that the real thanks should go to a mysterious partner. However, you make sure to keep the partner's name a secret.

When you meet Yinlin again, she tells you that the Dollmaker attempted to extract your memories but failed. The cause of your memory loss is far more complex than you thought. She thanks you for your help and coyly suggests that your next meeting may be under a completely different guise.

Upon leaving the Gorges of Spirits, you encounter a newly-formed Tacet Field. In its center stands a woman named Baizhi, who appears to be engaged in an investigation. You decide to glide down there to meet her.
As soon as Baizhi sees you, she runs a diagnostic check on you. She urges you to leave the site immediately, but events unfold much faster than you expect...

The Tacet Discord you defeated leaves behind a lingering golden shadow. Chixia explains it is what's left behind when a Tacet Discord is destroyed, and it can be absorbed by a Pangu Terminal as an Echo to help in combat. You try to absorb it with your Terminal, to no avail.

Your ability to absorb the Echo with your own body leaves Chixia in awe. Ancient records, predating the founding of Huanglong and the invention of the Terminal, tell of a mysterious celestial being capable of absorbing the remnants of Tacet Discords. Legends speak of their influence in heralding the dawn of Huanglong's history.
With the disrupting Tacet Field subdued, a holographic broadcast reaches all of Jinzhou. Jinhsi, the Magistrate, awaits an esteemed guest at City Hall and extends an invitation for a conversation.
Your companions think you are the one whom Jinhsi is waiting for. The path ahead beckons towards Jinzhou, where your destiny will unfold.
You attempt to absorb another Echo with your body but fail. Confusion settles among everyone about the nature of your abilities.
As you approach the city, you have an uneasy feeling of being watched. A mysterious girl stands from a hidden vantage point, her gaze fixed upon you.

Awakening alongside Chixia and Yangyang, you find all your memories have been stripped away. You are a rover in this strange land, and this is the name they give you. As you try to gather your bearings, Yangyang invites you to join them just as a foreboding Tacet Field begins to unfurl its dark presence.

As you gaze at the statue, a vision of the Sentinel flickers in your mind. Just when you are about to ask Yangyang for an explanation, a cry of alarm sounds. Chixia is being attacked by an Elite Class Tacet Discord!
Upon arriving in Jinzhou City, the group prepares to part ways. You leave with Chixia for the Nexus Tower and make plans to meet Yangyang at City Hall later.
You overhear the sound of Weiqi pieces clicking against a board from behind a door, but find the door is locked.
You ask Sanhua about Jinzhou, Jinhsi, and the tokens.

You tell Chixia and Yangyang that Jinhsi will meet you in three days and show them the tokens. They recognize the candy, but cannot recall its significance. After deliberation, the three of you decide to seek answers from Baizhi at the Academy.
You ask a little girl if she has seen the candy before, with no luck. To welcome you to Jinzhou, however, the little girl gives you a candy of her own.
Your investigation yields little leads. The three of you head for the Academy to find Baizhi.

Sanhua tells you that Jinhsi will meet you in three days time. When asked why she is certain you are the guest Jinhsi awaits, Sanhua replies that she can perceive frequencies, and yours, like Jinhsi's, is pure and untainted.
Sanhua upgrades your Terminal. You now have permission to travel to any region of Jinzhou without hindrance.
Chixia tells you that the Nexus Tower functions as a navigation, defense, and regional information system. You try connecting your Terminal to the Nexus Tower.
Yangyang has made all the necessary arrangements and is waiting for you and Chixia to join her.

A crowd has gathered outside City Hall. They are all eager to meet Jinhsi, but each is turned away by her bodyguard, Sanhua. With questions swirling in your mind, you bide your time and hope for answers.
Sanhua instantly recognizes you as the guest Jinhsi is expecting. She informs you that Jinhsi is currently away but has left a welcome gift and some mysterious tokens for you.
At the city gate, you encounter Jianxin, a Taoist who is being denied passage. After learning she is searching for a missing person, you use your authority to help her leave the city.

Jianxin explains she is searching for a boy named Zhiyuan. He vanished after leaving the city, and his grandfather tasked her to find him. Sadly, she has no information about the tokens you are investigating.
A Midnight Ranger reveals details about Zhiyuan's disappearance, and you agree to check on the Detection Beacons that have been disconnected.
As you near the first Detection Beacon, you stumble upon some shifty-looking "civilians." You move to confront them.
You offer assistance to the "civilians" responsible for damaging the Detection Beacon, but they repay your kindness with violence. You have no choice but to teach them a lesson.
Upon subduing the Exiles masquerading as civilians, you reclaim the stolen components and head for the next Detection Beacon.

Upon arriving at the Rearguard Camp, you are greeted by a scene of chaos, revealing the grim state of the ongoing conflict. There, you meet logistic coordinator Xiulan and agree to help tend to the wounded.
A severely wounded soldier begs to return to battle, insisting that resources should be reserved for those in greater need. You treat him, despite his loud protests.

The quartermaster reveals Zhiyuan's likely whereabouts. Jianxin leaves to continue her search for Zhiyuan. You show the quartermaster the mangosteen, which he mistakes for a grenade. After the misunderstanding is resolved, he tells you about the dire situation in the Norfall Barrens.
A wounded soldier is in distress. You summon a medic to his side.
With the soldiers tended to, you start looking for the quartermaster as advised.
Inspired by Yangyang's words, you close your eyes and tap into your intuition, pinpointing the last token's location: Qichi Village in the Central Plains.

Reuniting with Jianxin, you learn she has successfully found Zhiyuan and convinced him to return to Jinzhou. This journey has been enlightening for her, and she looks forward to seeing you and Yangyang again.
You recount the visions to Yangyang. She can't explain it but senses a connection between you and something on that battlefield.
You now know the mangosteen has something to do with the war. But in what way? What is Jinhsi trying to tell you? As you ponder these questions, vivid images flood your mind.
You encounter an unusual Tacet Discord chirping out nonsensical phrases. Yangyang theorizes that it must have consumed a human frequency.
Scar reveals the moral of the tale he has spun for you. He believes himself to be the rule-breaking black lamb. It is clear where his allegiances lie, and you decide you have heard enough...
Yangyang can't communicate with the Tacet Discord, but she senses complex emotions flowing within it. A tragic event happened here not long ago, with danger surely lurking nearby.

From cards discovered at the scene, Yangyang deduces that the tragedy is likely the work of the Fractsidus, an extremist group obsessed with merging humans and Tacet Discords. The cards belong to Scar, one of the organization's Overseers.
Following the surprise attack, Yangyang disappears and a mysterious man clad in red appears in front of you.
The mysterious man, whose name is Scar, doesn't attack you. He invites you to investigate the village with your own eyes to uncover the truths beneath the surface.
You demand the truth, but Scar refuses. Clearly, revealing it to you directly holds no thrills for him.

You find a diary page that once belonged to a little girl, a wanderer who finally found refuge in this village. The entries hint at unsettling truths. Scar, with an air of detachment, shares a fable of wolves and sheep.

You find more notes. Scar continues with his tale about a shepherd providing for the lambs in exchange for their loyalty. He asks whether you would bow to authority to get what you want. You tell him that all are equal.
Your investigation continues. The tragedy that befell the village starts to unravel and Scar persists in trying to sway your judgment.
After gathering all the clues, you learn that the black lamb who told the truth about the shepherd met with a tragic fate. The white lambs sacrificed it to continue to have their wishes fulfilled.
You conclude that the white lambs succumbed to temptation despite knowing the cost of their wishes, while the black lamb was sacrificed for revealing the truth.
After Scar's defeat, a mysterious woman in red comes to his aid. You share the events with Yangyang and realize that you need to find the actual location of Scar's tale to determine its truth.

Your adventure in Qichi Village concludes. As an Outrider tasked with keeping the peace, Yangyang is deeply saddened by the village's tragedy. With all the clues gathered, it is time you return to the city.
The Retroact Rain falls in Desorock Highland as Jiyan's forces prepare to advance on the Norfall Barrens.

Shaking off the vision, Jiyan hears a soldier report that the skies look just like they did that fateful battle three years ago. Spotting the approaching Tacet Discords, he suspects a mastermind is orchestrating their actions.
The moon is waxing, an omen of imminent danger. A message from Jinhsi reveals Jinzhou is preparing to face the threat.

You find Taoqi overseeing border defenses. Aalto is also present. The protective barrier against the Retroact Rain is under urgent repair, but the onslaught of Tacet Discords continues. Aalto and Encore must return to the Black Shores to warn of the impending revival of the Threnodian, while those remaining prepare for battle.

After fending off another wave of attacks, Jinhsi contacts you, announcing reinforcements are on the way. The moment foretold by Jué has arrived. She expresses her gratitude for your defense of Jinzhou and wishes you victory and safe passage through the long night.
With Jiyan's aid, you successfully vanquish the Thundering Mephis. Jiyan is aware of Jué's prophecy and has been awaiting your arrival. As the Retroact Rain falls, the group heads back to camp.
You are surprised to find Jianxin at camp. Jiyan decides to allocate roles and tasks for the looming battle against the Tacet Discords.

With your input, Jiyan quickly draws up the battle strategy. The ranged units will secure the high ground to support the close-combat troops in the valley as they break through the Tacet Discords' ranks, creating a passage for you, Yangyang, Jiyan, and Jianxin to launch a commando assault on the Threnodian.
The strategy is set, but the Disruptor is needed to break through the Threnodian's barrier. You and Yangyang assume responsibility for reclaiming it and repairing its power connector.
A Midnight Ranger breathes his last. This strengthens your resolve to finish charging the Disruptor and use it to face the Threnodian.
With the Disruptor now operational, Jinhsi grants permission to fire it, stating that she alone will take responsibility for the fallout while urging you to press ahead.

As the Retroact Rain pours, Jiyan is confronted by the ghostly figure of Geshu Lin, the general from the Battle Beneath the Crescent. The phantom challenges Jiyan, questioning how he intends to honor the lives lost and whether he will follow in the footsteps of the past.

Despite taking antidotes, many soldiers are still haunted by nightmares of the Battle Beneath the Crescent three years ago. The rain has brought to life their fallen comrades who now fight against them. Jiyan strives to boost morale with a rousing speech.

Resonator Verina identifies the black flower in your photo as a specially cultivated variety. This inspires the idea of wearing a Blake Bloom to draw out members of the organization. But how does one go about conjuring a Blake Bloom from thin air?
Verina uses her Resonance Abilities to conjure a black flower that perfectly matches the one in the photo.

You apprehend the mysterious young woman stalking you, only to discover she is a Bloom Bearer from the Black Shores. She shows a strong interest in you and reveals she has been helping you from afar. In a flash, she manages to escape leaving only her name—Camellya.
Yangyang calls to inform you that she and Chixia have spotted a suspicious figure on Main Street.
You meet Yangyang who points out the enigmatic man.

You track them down and discover they are Consultants for the Black Shores. Aalto strikes a deal to reveal what he knows about you in exchange for your help in recovering a Resonance Beacon from the Court of Savantae Ruins, in Whining Aix's Mire.

After Aalto and Encore depart, Chixia and the others arrive. You brief them on your deal. Yangyang warns that Whining Aix's Mire hasn't been visited in ages due to treacherous weather and urges caution.

After meeting Aalto and Encore, you learn that the Beacon is hidden within the Court of Savantae Ruins, a once-revered institution known for its groundbreaking research in Automata Mechanics and strange experiments. Its members vanished without a trace, leaving behind only damaged Resonance Beacons.
You reunite with Chixia and Yangyang outside City Hall, where the tension hangs in the air. Mentioning Jiyan's name prompts Yangyang to recount a tale about him as told by a certain storyteller...
Noticing you are being followed, you decide to send Chixia and Yangyang with the Blake Bloom to search for Black Shores members in the city while you confront your mysterious stalker.
Aalto is amazed to learn that the Court of Savantae had once attempted to recreate Retroact Rain, speculating on what they sought to achieve.

Upon defeating the monster, Aalto discloses shocking truths about you, the Black Shores, and Camellya. You learn this is not the first time you have awakened from a long slumber—the last happened at the Black Shores. Before you can ask more, he suddenly flees sensing something amiss.
After hearing the story, you express your desire to find members of the Black Shores before heading to the Norfall Barrens. Yangyang suggests starting with the Blake Bloom, the organization's symbol.
After a fierce charge, you arrive at the Suspended Ruins. The Threnodian is now within reach.
Massive stone boulders block your path. With the Disruptor ready, you prepare to clear a path forward.

At the final confrontation, Yangyang stays behind to deal with the surrounding threats. You concentrate, sensing the Threnodian's location, then aim at the Crownless statue's chest and give the order to fire.

Yinlin brings you to meet the Dollmaker, maintaining a façade of hostility due to a bug the Dollmaker planted on you. Through a hidden panel, she explains that this factory produces puppets designed to trigger Overclocking for the Fractsidus in exchange for resources. She needs your help to gather evidence against the Dollmaker's involvement in all this.

You speak to the Dollmaker and discover that the two final puppets he intends to make are Yinlin's parents—his former mentors. He captured you to get experimental data, hoping to create perfect puppets with the Fractsidus's backing. Now, with the Public Security Bureau involved, he's rushing to relocate both the puppets and his research data.

The Dollmaker confronts Yinlin after learning of her betrayal. She asserts that, like her parents, she has always been a Patroller and has never forgotten her true identity and duty. She declares she cannot accept the Dollmaker harming others to recapture the warmth of the past.

In the face of the Dollmaker's twisted obsession, Yinlin argues that puppets cannot replace real family and that it is wrong to take advantage of others' happiness to cope with one's own misfortune. The Dollmaker retorts that he has erased her Patroller records, making it impossible for her to prove her identity. But Yinlin asserts that even without this identity, she will continue to fight evil. That is the spirit her parents instilled in her, and the one that motivates her to pursue her goals in her own way.

After the Patrollers secure the scene, Chixia updates you on the Séance Society's other members, but by then, Yinlin has already disappeared. You promise Chixia that you will go to the Public Security Bureau to provide a formal statement of what happened.
Yinlin reminds you to use your Terminal to record the prototype puppet data.

This looks like a recording of an ancient Carnevale celebration. Since there's no Acolyte in sight… could it be from before the founding of the Order of the Deep? This is a marvelous discovery, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}!
Let us raise our thanks to the Sentinel, who has guided us to safety and protected us on this journey!
Yes, that's right! The Sentinel is truly a great and wondrous being!
And let us thank our hardworking farmers whose toil has transformed the soil, bringing us an abundant harvest!
Let us honor the brave warriors who vanquished Tacet Discord and beast alike so that we might sleep soundly at night!
No, no! The Sentinel blessed us with fertile soil. The Sentinel gave us a home.
How dare they claim the Sentinel's blessings as their own!
S-such utter disgrace!
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, you're back! Are you all right?
Is this it?
This... this is the last part for the Nimbus Chorale! Wonderful! I knew you could do it!
Now, the last section should represent our ancestors' reverence for the Sentinel… Wait. It's titled... "Glory to Humanity"?
But… why? Why does the most important part of the Chorale have nothing to do with Sentinel?
Gently express your opinion.
Be direct with her.
Maybe your ancestors knew the Sentinel was important, but they also knew that the ones who crossed the sea, the generations who built all this, deserved gratitude too.
Of course our ancestors are important! Without their devotion, how could we have ever won the Sentinel's favor?
They lived in a time when the Sentinel was closer to us. Why couldn't they see Their grace as we do?
Maybe it's because they understood the Sentinel's true nature better than you do, and they knew what it took to create the kind of life you now enjoy today.
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}… do you think I've strayed from the path of my ancestors?
No, you're just following the Tenets of the Deep.
I'm sorry, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}. I don't understand.

All I know is that the Sentinel gave us Rinascita as a home and the Common Echos that help us live our lives. The Order, guided by the Sentinel, saved me from the Dark Tide and gave me a name, a new life, and a place to belong.
What you've been told has been twisted by the Order to suit its own ends. The true song of your ancestors is locked away, and you, like so many others, choose not to see it.
I still don't understand,...
The Order uses everyone's belief in the Sentinel to manipulate, deliberately erasing the history of Rinascita's first people.
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, this is very serious slander against the Order! According to the Tenets of the Deep...
Hasn't your Primus told you everything he wants you to do in Tenets of the Deep? You've followed those rules without question.
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, why do you speak of the Order as if it were evil?
Twenty years ago, the Order's Acolytes saved me from the Dark Tide, and the Order's orphanage became my second home. They gave me a name, a new life, a place to belong.
Even when I wasn't wise enough to contribute much, the Order established the Minor Forbidden Archive just for me.
They never asked for thanks. Only that I praise the Sentinel, pray daily, and live righteously. If that's the Order's manipulation… then I'm glad to be manipulated!
As the opening line of the Tenets states, "All that the Order reveals is truth, and our duty is simply to follow."
I suppose, to you, I must seem like a blind follower of faith. I'm sorry for taking so much of your time, trying to convince me when I wouldn't listen.
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, whether or not the Nimbus Chorale is heretical doesn't matter. It's not the music I wish to play at the Carnevale.
I will never forget your kindness. If you ever need me, come to the Minor Forbidden Archive. I've had a long day, and now I need some time alone.
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, why…
Because this is the real song of Rinascita's people.
Because this song was always buried deep within you.
O Sentinel, please forgive this humble, wandering servant. Forgive me for being moved by such a forbidden thing.
{PlayerName}, does the Sentinel here care about such little problems?
We'll talk about that later...
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, what should I do? Should I report this music as heretical to the Order? Why do I hesitate? Am I losing my faith?
Why don't you ask yourself this time?
How about we listen to this song a few more times?
Ugh, the crops are all dead.
Grandpa's notes mentioned the soil was too salty, but the pages with the solution got ruined during the TD Outbreak. If only Grandpa had lived longer...
Ugh, why didn't the Sentinel guide us to a better land...
Don't be so ungrateful. If it wasn't for the Sentinel's help, our fleet would have been wiped out.
From here on out, we must rely on ourselves. If one generation can't do it, we'll try with two. The land of Rinascita will be fertile again, I know it!
All-knowing and all-powerful Sentinel, please bless me with smooth sailing tomorrow!
Instead of praying here every day, why don't you go fix the fishing boat?
Grandma, how can you say such a disrespectful thing in front of the Sentinel!
That's not the Sentinel. It's nothing more than a pile of stones you've gathered.
The Sentinel guided us here to build a new home, yet you would dare lay every little misfortune at Their feet. It is you who dishonor the Sentinel.
You don't understand anything, Grandma.
Lenore

Starlight streams through your fingers as you mount the expedition into the depths of the universe.
The gentle twinkles silently chant a song of gratitude, a tribute to the treasured gifts you once bestowed upon them.
You there, Abster?
(Yawns)... What's up...?
(It's taking longer for Abby to react...)
Hey, there's nothing to worry about... I'm just a little beat, that's all... Oh! Earlier when I was half-asleep, I came up with this great idea for finding the Sentinel.
Let's hear it.
Didn't the Sentinel say They're locked up in some kind of tower in the sky?
Well, how about I just fly up there and look for it? Easy as pie!
The tower is either too far to see or it's totally covered by clouds.
Otherwise, we would've seen some sign of it on the ground.
In the shape you're in... are you sure you could fly that far?
C'mon, it won't hurt to try. The cliff at Egla Town would be a perfect launch pad.
(The aroma from these plants... It's the same scent that was in the study.)
These are Violacas. They produce a unique fragrance, wouldn't you say?
Violacas are a vital ingredient for our elixirs. It even has a soothing effect on its own.
This is it.
Just as I expected... The Threnodian "took notice" of you the moment you learned the truth.
{PlayerName}, what you see in this sanctuary is the Sentinel in Their true form.
A majestic steed that galloped with the wind, not a creature of the ocean's depths.
The Order worships a half-horse, half-sea creature Divinity, a form the Sentinel assumed only after being corrupted by the Threnodian.
Although the Sentinel's will has yet to fade, who knows how much longer They can endure.
{PlayerName}. I wish to ask you to persuade the Sentinel of Jinzhou—Jué—to come to Rinascita. To save Imperator.
That's much easier said than done.
What makes you think I can do that?
In return, I will agree to whatever condition or request you make.
Both Jinzhou and Jué owe you their future. That makes you the only person capable of this task.
A Sentinel cannot leave its commissioned region.
Jué leaving Jinzhou would be a betrayal of duty.
Jué is still in the middle of a recovery.
I understand the position you are in. Word has it that you're currently staying at a hotel and are at odds with the Order.
Perhaps a stay at my estate would suit you, for the remainder of your time in Rinascita?
I can offer you a glimpse into Rinascita's past, and you'd be spared the Order's unwelcomed attention.
Don't lose hope just yet. There might still be a path forward.
Carlotta once helped me interpret some stained glass images. The story it told was very similar to what you've described.
Only more biased towards the Order. It mentioned a maiden who would emerge as the Sentinel's Resonator and later save Rinascita.
Do you think that's also a lie?
Care to elaborate?
(Describe to Cantarella what was portrayed on the stained glass.)
The part regarding the maiden isn't entirely fiction.
The Sentinel does indeed appoint a maiden to be Their Resonator, though not in the way the Carnevale would have you believe. No, it's through resonance with a very particular artifact.
That's not how Jué found Their Resonator.
That's because Imperator wields the power to split and manipulate space.
With it, They can withdraw a portion of power. That power's frequency will match the Imperator's own.
This is how the Sword of Divinity—Tyrvine—came to be. A blade sealed with the very powers of the Sentinel, and the artifact used to select Their Resonator.
To resonate with the sword is to resonate with the Sentinel. Only the chosen one may hope to draw it.
Then... what about Cartethyia?
The Martyred "Maiden"...? The nature of her resonance is unclear to me.
Perhaps she resonated with the Threnodian, or perhaps with the Sentinel in its corrupted form.
But choosing her could not have been the Sentinel's will. That's because...
The Maiden was already dead.
What?
Are you saying the real Maiden was already chosen?

In the past, each year the Fisalia family would hold the Divine Trials to select those with the strongest will. These young women would attempt to resonate with Tyrvine's powers—while Overclocked, of course.
Though none succeeded, some saw fragments of the truth hidden within the resonance.
I was one of them... There was a moment, where I glimpsed the Sentinel's corrupted form and the inverted ruin suspended in the sky.
I also learned that only Tyrvine can break the barrier of that Sonoro Sphere.
When I awoke from that vision, I discovered a line of words inscribed onto my hand.
I would never mistake my own handwriting. That is precisely why I am searching for other possibilities.
The words were—"The Maiden is dead."
(An inverted ruin suspended in the sky... her and Cartethyia's descriptions bear many similarities.)
(If Tyrvine is the key to entering the Sonoro Sphere, it stands to reason that Imperator may have played a role in the Sphere's creation.)
(If I can confirm that Tyrvine was truly left by Imperator, at least it would prove that neither are lying.)
(Cantarella said she was Overclocking when she tried resonating with Tyrvine.)
(That's exactly what happened with Jinhsi. Could Imperator be trying to restore Their power through a Second Awakening?)
(If that's the case... my permission should cause a reaction. That's one way to confirm what they're saying.)
Can I get a closer look at the sword?
Would you mind if I tried to pull out the sword?
By all means.
...I suppose all that's left is its symbolic value.
However, do handle it with care. It is a family heirloom... I've heard of your unique methods and formidable strength.
{PlayerName}... Who are you really?
Jué calls me the Arbiter.
There is a cable car in the lower levels of the Fisalia estate that leads directly to the Sonoro Sphere. The mechanism beside that wall can activate the lifts.
Are all these mechanisms really necessary?
Convenience isn't the only reason for having them. Some were specifically built in case an outsider decided to visit.
You seem perturbed. Are you still gathering your thoughts?
Everything that's happened has all lined up so perfectly. It makes me think it's too good to be true.
I'd like to share a different perspective.
Outside, they call me "The Bane." But historically, every head of the Fisalia family has carried such a title.
It just so happens that I am the most potent one yet.
We've reached the old seminary's undercrypt. The gateway into the Sonoro Sphere itself lies at its center.
We shall continue on foot from here.
Music itself holds no emotion. It's the heart that grants it meaning. So, dear listener, tell me. What feelings did my piece evoke in you?
Relaxation and warmth.
Yearning and sorrow.
A feeling of nostalgia?
Wow... A very valuable insight! Thank you, that brings me closer to completing my piece.
Salutations, {PlayerName}. My name is Ciaccona, a wandering bard. I'm glad to have met you.
You're looking for me?
I was sent by Lady Carlotta to find you. As I passed that abandoned house, I suddenly felt this... well, you know, rush of inspiration that just can't be ignored! So, I stopped to compose a piece...
Surprise, surprise, the melody led me right to you.
Well... I suppose this won't count as me getting distracted, right?
If Carlotta asked you to find me, has something happened?
Lady Carlotta told me you encountered the supposed Martyred Maiden—Cartethyia.
She dispatched search teams soon after, but there's been no sign of Cartethyia since.
That's why she asked me to use my Forte to recreate the frequency you experienced at the time, to see if any details you might have missed become clearer.
Recreate the frequency?
Well, it's a little tricky to explain in words... Think of it like being in an immersive portrait. Can you tell me about your meeting with Cartethyia?
The more details the better. Even the smallest things count.
Let's see here... Tweak a few notes here. Some emotions there. Textures... That should do it.
Now then, {PlayerName}. Time for you to "tune in" to your memories.
Strange...
This area was clear of Tacets Discords on my last visit, and there's no Tacet Field nearby.
Could they have come from the Sonoro Sphere itself?
Didn't think there would be Gulpuffs here.
The road ahead will not be an easy one.
What exactly happened here?
The second Dark Tide... It occurred right here, at the Avinoleum. The largest seminary ever built by the Order.
It arrived on the very day the Blessed Maiden passed her trials and was crowned by the Order. A day when belief burned brighter than ever.
And when the darkness came, none escaped.
These days, what most people remember is the seminary disappearing into the sky. But in truth, the Dark Tide that should have spread across Rinascita vanished, along with it.
Yet due to a lack of records, the second Dark Tide slowly faded from memory.
I was there when it all happened. Still an ordinary member of the family, watching it unfold from a boat just outside the seminary.
It wasn't until later when I attempted to resonate with Tyrvine, that I gained a partial glimpse of the Sonoro Sphere's interior.
Sounds like someone inside the seminary did something to stop the spread.
Precisely. It could very well have been Cartethyia's doing. But, as with the first time, there's also the chance it was the Sentinel who turned the tide.
I can sense the conflict within you, the temptation to trust your Maiden. But it's best to keep those thoughts to yourself, for now.
The Threnodian knows where the heart is weakest and it is there it strikes the hardest.
Of course, it's never too late to place your trust when the evidence is clear.
But... now is not the time, is it?
("Tune in" to my memories... Does that mean I'm supposed to see the past from another perspective?)
Laureate?
Our Tacet Marks are glowing again. It appears there is a special connection between them.
What is the meaning of this?
Someone used their Resonance ability to help me relive this moment, but this seems... unexpected.
How did you first come to notice me?
The Sentinel—Imperator's voice guided me to you.
You heard the Sentinel's voice? Then tell me, am I Their Resonator?
{PlayerName}... {PlayerName}...
Hello, {PlayerName}. I received Ciaccona's memo.
To think the head of the Fisalias approached you when I was still in negotiations with her emissaries. Was it meant to be a diversion all along...?
They invited you and you alone. As a Montelli, I'm in no position to intervene.
That being said, if the Fisalias try anything against you, I'll get you out, even if it means storming through their front gates.
In the meantime, I'll keep looking for more information and the person Cartethyia mentioned to you.
I'll call you as soon as I find anything.
Got it.

Impressive work, Dreamwalker. That was quite a formidable foe, but it was still no match for you.
Looks like that's not all of it.
Yes, many more dream masses are lurking in the depths of the Somnoire...
They're getting stronger as we speak, targeting the Somnoire's weak points. It's almost as if they have a mind of their own.
What are they after?
Keep exploring, Dreamwalker. You will find the truth in a dream.
The frequencies I sensed earlier are still there. "They" are hiding in the depths of all of these dreams.
So, that's what a dream mass looks like?
What was that?
It's likely reflecting a form we're already familiar with, or maybe... it resembles a certain "something" inside the mass.
There are things I need to see for myself. This is the duty you have entrusted to me.
Take care.
See you around.
Rest assured, I will not put myself in danger again.
See you soon. You have my word.
Sigh, you must have noticed the Ebony Gatekeeper by now, right? I finally found him.
We were supposed to keep the balance in the Somnoire together… but now, things have spiraled out of control.
There are dream masses just up ahead.
Dreamwalker, please stay vigilant. I wish you the best of luck.
Don't you have anything to say?
These masses are devouring other dreams, threatening the stability of the entire Somnoire…
With what power I have left in me, I'm afraid I can no longer rein them in. I need your help.
You don't sound like you're asking for help.
I know I made a few missteps in trying to save more dreams. I don't expect you to forgive me.
But I am as devastated as anyone to see the Somnoire collapse. You have to believe me.
I'm… sincerely begging for your help.
Alright, but I'm not doing this for you.
Meow three times, and I'll think about it.
I understand. Thank you.
Ugh… Fine.
Meow! Meow! Meow!
Impressive work. These dream masses are disintegrating.
What happens now?
Well, they're breaking down into dream fragments now. In time, they might form something new. I'll track them down, but...
But what?
You really need to finish your sentences.
Our actions had unexpected repercussions. More dream masses are escaping the Somnoire. The boundary between reality and dreams is rapidly deteriorating.
I cannot predict what will happen next.
I've gotten used to surprises.
Don't worry. I can handle whatever comes.
That's reassuring. Please do keep exploring the Somnoire.
Abandoned buildings and platforms… I didn't see anything like this before.
Looks like things are shifting again inside the Somnoire…
An entity like this shouldn't exist in a dream… But now that I'm here, let me be of use to you.

In the Tower of Adversity, your skills are put to trial. Complete the specific challenge goals to earn your Crests. Collect enough Crests to earn hefty rewards.

The Tower of Adversity features four Zones: <color=#c19f51>Stable Zone</color>, <color=#c19f51>Experiment Zone</color>, <color=#c19f51>Hazard Zone</color>, and <color=#c19f51>Overdrive Zone.</color> Each Zone contains one to three Towers and each Tower has multiple Floors, each representing a unique challenge. Progress through the challenges to unlock new Towers and Zones. Clearing all challenges in a Zone unlocks the next Zone.

In the Tower of Adversity, clearing a challenge reduces participating Resonators' <color=#c19f51>Vigor</color> by a specific amount. Once a Resonator's Vigor is depleted, they can <color=#c19f51>no longer take part in new challenges</color>. Vigor does not restore over time, but you can use the [Reset] option on a Floor to recover the Vigor.
In the Tower of Adversity, environmental effects affect your combat tactics. Use them strategically to gain an advantage.

Crest Rewards in the Stable Zone, Experiment Zone, and Overdrive Zone can be claimed only once. However, the challenges in the Hazard Zone are <color=#c19f51>periodically reset</color>, along with your progression, bringing in new enemies, challenge goals, Area Effects, and rewards. Take on the challenges again to earn Crests and <color=#c19f51>claim fresh rewards.</color>

Complete the challenges and meet their challenge goals to obtain Crests. Collect a certain number of Crests to get various rewards, including Astrites and Hazard Records. Hazard Records can be exchanged for Phantom Echoes, Premium Tuners, and more at the Adversity Exchange.

Deal damage to accumulate Sync Energy. When the Link Energy is full, get ready to activate Dream Link.
Successful <color=#ffd12f>Dodges</color> and <color=#ffd12f>Counterattacks</color> provide a lot of Sync Energy.
When Sync Energy is full, cast any Resonator's Resonance Liberation to enter the Illusive Sync state.
The Illusive Sync only lasts 10 seconds. If you don't cast the next Resonator's Resonance Liberation within that time, you'll lose all Sync Energy, and the sync will end.

Casting Resonance Liberation while in Illusive Sync triggers the Dream Link state and activates the Link Field.
When the Link Field is active:
1. All team members' ATK, Crit. Rate, and Crit. DMG are significantly boosted, while Resonance Skill cooldowns are greatly reduced.
2. A Stagnation Zone is generated, immobilizing enemies within the Link Field.
3. Nearby enemies are pulled toward your Resonators upon activation.
4. When the Link Field ends, your team gains continuous HP regeneration.

Ah, call me Ishmael. Well, well! The Laureate, I presume? Have you ever tried fishing before?
The trick to it is a flexible line and a subtle lure.
Fancy trying your hand at deep sea fishing? It's one of Rinascita's many lasting traditions, like the Carnevale.
Sure, I want to become a pro angler.
I'd like to give it a try.
Wonderful, then I've got a good place for you. Riccioli Islands, north of Ragunna. It's right where the currents of the Stormy Sea meet, drawing in swarms of fish.
And if you're alone, angling on a fishing boat would suit you better. A net will just get you tangled up in trouble.
Once you reach the islands, go visit an old captain called Ahab. He'll be more than glad to show you the ropes.
I've got to make my way back to the islands myself. There's a boat at the harbor that'll take you straight there. Just let the boatman know you're off for some fishing!
Hehe... Oh, my sweet...
No one else knows. It's just between us.
Wait for my return, my darling... fiancée...
Er, excuse me, sir? Are you the one who witnessed Cetus the Tidebreaker?
Hmm? Yes, that's me! Are you here to witness our union? Marvelous! Come, according to tradition, a wedding witness must be present.
A wedding witness? Well, the Codex does allow Acolytes to serve as witnesses during weddings.
What makes you want to marry a fish?!
He's certainly not acting like himself...
Hehe... Hehehe...
Is he... under some kind of enchantment? I've read of symptoms like this in the Order's archives before.
O Imperator's blessings, gaze upon this...
W-wait...
Huh? I did what was written in the archives...
Ouch!? You... I'm...
Golden white... Jellyfish... Pitch black... A large fish... Huh? You're human... I'm a fish... No wait... My fish...
Ow, my head hurts... Who are you?
I think it worked!
Mind if I give him another smack?
Where the hell's my boat? And how did I get here... What?
The fish... My, oh, my... From Serene Bay... The fish... Heeheehee...
He's at it again! Here I go!
Oh? It's you.
Is your leg okay now?
You know this little guy?
I treated their broken leg from a Gondola accident back at the market.
Did... Mr. Coffin ask you to come here?
I think they're trying to say that Mr. Starbuck's Gondola might know something. They're stranded on a reef nearby.
And Mr. Starbuck has been like this for two weeks now...
You want us to use these to free the Gondola?
Hmmm, I fear Mr. Starbuck might not withstand any more of the Order's disenchantment tricks anyway.
It does look rather painful.
It's for his own good.
In that brief moment when Mr. Starbuck seemed to recover, he mentioned his Gondola and a place called Serene Bay.
The rescued Gondola appears to be shouting something.
You came across a "siren"? A creature with a human body and a fishtail?
Could it be Lorelei?
Isn't she supposed to be in Nimbus Sanctum?
Could there be another being like Lorelei?
I suspect that the fish we saw earlier is connected to this "siren."
There's got to be a reason it stayed fresh after all these weeks.
This means we need to think of a way to get that fish out of Mr. Starbuck's hands.
Then I propose...
It's time for a little switcheroo.
We catch one that looks similar and call it a day.
Would that work?
We're running low on options here.
They're all fish, aren't they?
Well, only one way to find out.
Hehehe...
Oh? My dear witness, have you seen my fiancée around?
Hehehe... You… What are you up to?
Help! Somebody help!!!
Phoebe! Grab its tail!
I-It's so slippery! Disenchant!
Thieves! You filthy thieves!
Ugh... You... My head...
Who are you? What am I doing with this fish?
Mr. Starbuck? Captain Ahab asked us to come find you.
Old Ahab? Wait, what's going on here?
Do you know anything about this blue fish?
Do you remember what happened to Cetus the Tidebreaker?
All I remember is being out at sea fishing not long ago.
But all I could hear was a song, drawing me in. It felt like my whole body was being beckoned to follow that tune.
The next thing I knew, I was drifting right out of Serene Bay, where the Tidebreaker is said to slumber.
The singing was still there, like it was rising from the depths. I swear I caught a glimpse of the Cetus's shadow... then another shadow of a massive fish.
Oh, the curves of that shadow. A true beauty...
I tossed everything I had into the sea, anything that could serve as bait, but still, it wouldn't bite.
Then, I felt a tug on the line as the singing grew louder... and everything went blank after that.
Did you catch this blue fish?
Yes! That's the one!
Wait, wait! Where is it...
Key! The key... Blast it, where'd that key go?
The key... I used it as bait...
Whoa, whoa! You're not—
Aha! I knew it! Molto bene! Got gobbled up by the fish!
Old Ahab had me keep it. You'll be needing it too, yes?
A key covered in rust. Seems like it's seen better days...
I can't recall much after that, but no doubt the Tidebreaker did make an appearance in Serene Bay.
If you're looking for it, go take a look around the bay. Oh, and thanks for the help...
Are you...
I'm forty-seven years old this year. After all these years at sea, I've caught more fish than you can imagine.
But the right fish and the right person have yet to cross my path.
Oh, but this beautiful lady here—
Ahem.
We should get going, Phoebe.
Farewell, Mr. Starbuck.
I wish you the best! May Imper... May the sea bring you blessings!
Uh, right... Okay then...
Let's light up the lighthouses on this island as Captain Ahab instructed.
After that, we should go visit that Serene Bay Mr. Starbuck talked about.
Phoebe!
Get out of the way!
The octopus Echo waves its tentacles around as it hands you a note from Ahab.
"Once it's safe, Planck can swim over to Serene Bay."
"Since the lighthouse on Starbuck's island is up and running, we can set sail again. We're counting on you and Miss White Hat."
"There'll be monsters swarming in those waters, ever since Cetus went missing."
"Word is, the key to Serene Bay's lighthouse got lost long ago. We only know it's somewhere at the bottom of the sea."
"I'll keep poking around and see what else I can dig up. I'll have Planck send word once I've got news."
Are you the one looking for a ride to Riccioli?
That's me. Let's go.
Take a seat, and we'll be on our way!
Seeking out old Ahab, are you? He should be at the harbor over there.
He's no ordinary man, I tell you that. You'll spot him a mile away.
Zzz... Zzz...
Huh? Hmm... All right, cut it out...
Oh! Ahoy! A fish! We have a bite!
Well, don't just stand there, {Male=laddie;Female=missy}! Gimme a hand with this thing!
Oh, wait! Easy does it...
That's gotta be one hefty fish...
Too bad it got away...
A big fella like that? He won't be gettin' away from me, just a matter of time, no bother at all.
Oh, that? Pah, that was nothing. Back in me youth, I could hunt a whale for a whole day, I could!
You must be that young'un Ishmael mentioned.
Yes, I'm here to become a pro fisher.
Yes, I'm here to try deep sea fishing.
Aye, good! You've come to the right place. The name's Ahab, and I've been tied to this harbor longer than most.
That octopus merchant over there is Planck. It has all you need, from fishing gear to boat repairs.
But... I see you don't have a boat. We can fix that! You can use mine!
A Gondola?

As much as she loved that town, she never stopped wanting to explore the world outside it.

What I saw just now, is it real? Is that girl my Grandma?

Can I come here again?

I always wanted to travel, but I couldn't bear to leave Grandma alone.
This dream showed me a different side of her. She was once a young girl with dreams... just like me.
She dreamed of traveling, meeting new people, and starting a family.

About Tactical Simulacra II

[About]

The Academy is experimenting with a new type of technology rumored to be capable of simulating powerful enemies to help with the troops' combat training...

[Eligibility]

Reach Union Level 14.

[Event Rules]

1. In Tactical Simulacra II, challenge waves of powerful enemies by using special buffs across different simulation domains.

2. As you complete more challenges, more special buffs will be unlocked to aid you in taking on subsequent challenges.

3. The results of each challenge consist of three parts: Monster Points, Time Points, and Technical Points.

i. Monster Points are earned by defeating enemies in challenges.

ii. Time Points are earned based on the time remaining when a challenge is completed. The more enemies that are defeated, the higher the point conversion factor.

iii. Technical Points are earned for each successful Counterattack and Dodge triggered.

[Combat Rank]
Hitting the enemy steadily improves your Combat Rank, while successful Dodges, Dodge Counters, and Counterattacks provide a greater boost. However, getting hit significantly lowers your Combat Rank.

She awoke from her dream.

The interval between unconsciousness and consciousness became shorter with each passing day. Lady Flora was starting to find it hard to tell where her dreams ended and reality began. She couldn't even recall when this disorientation had started.

Memories surged like turbulent waves, crashing into her mind and wreaking havoc on her senses. Pain ripped through her body, relentlessly and unforgivingly. She opened her mouth to scream, but Overclocking had turned her throat into a gnarled, coarse root, silencing her cries. 

After struggling to take just a few faltering steps, she collapsed onto a muddy riverbank, trembling, her fingertips spasming uncontrollably.

How many times had this happened? She stared blankly at the dark night sky above.

A void of chaos swirled within her, yet there was one thing that stood out in sharp relief: {PlayerName}.

She remembered everything now.

Who she was, who {PlayerName} is, the reason for her being, Solaris, and the Lament…

Before the madness of Overclocking engulfed her, those memories were always buried deep, locked in the depths of her being. Each time she awoke, she lost all recollection, left only with an aching void. As time passed and her body weakened under the strain of Overclocking, glimpses of her mission and roots would resurface, only to vanish again in an endless cycle.

How many times had it happened? Lady Flora had no answer.

Civilizations crumbled into dust, only to rise anew; life faded, only to blossom once more. 

She was witness to the ebb and flow of Solaris, yet remained forever a wanderer in her own mind.

"{PlayerName}…" The name slipped from her lips like a prayer. 

They had never truly met or exchanged words, and now, with her memories fading, she couldn't even tell if they were friends or foes. Yet somehow, the next time she awoke she knew her instincts would lead her to seek {Male=him;Female=her} out. It was not a tender yearning. It felt more like the weight of a heavy chain, one Lady Flora could not resist. 

Yet she felt no hatred for this chain. 

The rustle of leaves shattered her reverie. Wearily, she blinked, and the red camellia unfurled, its vines piercing through the Tacet Discords lurking in the shadows. Yes, this was her instinct, her essence, the core of her being... Even as she teetered on the edge of forgetting everything, she could always rely on her instincts.

In truth, beyond her instincts, there was nothing left for her to hold onto. 

"Next time, if only I could truly get to know {PlayerName} and share a conversation with {Male=him;Female=her}."

Lady Flora mused hazily. Perhaps the Tethys System would lead {PlayerName} to her since she had already revealed herself in this mission.

Lady Flora closed her eyes and surrendered to the darkness as the pain peaked.

The lake's cool water swelled across her cheek, the camellia withering as its vines retreated into her body.

The autumn night breeze blew through the leaves, caressing her as she lay by the lake. To the north, the villagers of Petalfall Village would soon awaken from their dreams, calling to one another as they prepared to set out on a new day of fishing.

She awoke from her dream.

The wind howled fiercely at the rooftop's edge as she stretched, squinting down at the lively streets below. Vehicles crisscrossed the roads, their taillights forming a vibrant, fiery chain. Resting her chin on her hand, she began to hum.

It was a song she had learned from {PlayerName}.

Of course, she hadn't heard it directly from {PlayerName} {Male=himself;Female=herself}, she had picked it up secretly. 

They might not be enemies, but their relationship was far from friendly—at best, it was a one-sided acquaintance. {PlayerName}'s presence had caught the eye of various factions, including her own organization. Yet, that hardly concerned her, nor was it something she could afford to contemplate.

She was merely a "chosen seed," a "flower" that bloomed for the sole purpose of hunting {PlayerName} down. Most days, the injections left her in a fog, drifting through a semi-conscious haze, with only her instinctual yearning for a certain person carved deep into her heart.

The substance she was administered had a sharp, acrid scent, dragging her reason into a mire, robbing her of clarity and self.

Her thoughts whirled chaotically, like a bomb on the brink of detonation, forced to reset just before the countdown expired. 

But she didn't care. 

Outside of {PlayerName}, little else piqued her interest. Sometimes, {Male=he;Female=she} felt like a mere silhouette against a blank canvas, an outline of a stranger. The portrait was drawn from fragments of information she had painstakingly gathered—they were so close yet had never truly met. She didn't know what {Male=he;Female=she} looked like.

It was said this distance was necessary to evade the Tethys System's tracking. Contact was forbidden.

But how she longed to meet {PlayerName}!

Perched dangerously on the edge of the building, she laughed at the fantasy. Vines entwined around her arms, climbing higher, their delicate buds slowly unfurling at their tips.

Suddenly, a thought struck her.

"I'll give {Male=him;Female=her} a flower."

The moment the thought emerged, it consumed her entirely. She envisioned the moment she would find {PlayerName} and present this gift—a blossom sprouted from her very being. It would neither wither nor decay unless she perished. But just as quickly as it came, the thought vanished into the chaos of her mind, leaving no trace behind.

Little did she know, centuries later, the scene before her would vanish in the Lament. She would wander endlessly through a labyrinth of memories until one autumn morning, by a lake in Petalfall Village, where she would finally meet {PlayerName}, there to rescue the village from Tacet Discord attacks. From there, she would join the Black Shores and share a few hundred years together before {Male=he;Female=she} would eventually leave her. She, too, would leave the Black Shores, only to be reunited decades later in Jinzhou. All those futures had yet to unfold, just as possibilities slumbered within seeds, waiting for fate to blossom.

She leaped from the building, her vines weaving through the city's structures, searching for {Male=him;Female=her}.

"Tuesday, clear skies. I watched the sunset from Caidong Peak! But Zhangzhang didn't come… She seems to have lost interest in this kind of thing..."

Lumi paused and closed her notebook in the golden light of the setting sun.

It was a thick hardcover notebook—a birthday gift from her parents, one she had chosen herself. Once a diary, it had transformed into an exploration journal as she grew older. As a child, Lumi was content wandering the pebble paths of Changzhuang, but now, those paths felt too small. Her curiosity stretched beyond the borders of the village. She longed for the roads that led to the world outside. 

The only problem was—no one had found those roads in a long, long time.

Her father once told her about the many failed attempts. Over the years, many had tried to find a way beyond the mountains, but all had returned empty-handed, lost, or worse. Eventually, the villagers gave up, their focus shifting to more immediate concerns. Life in Changzhuang was demanding—farming from spring to autumn, then bracing for the long winter when the mountains would disappear under a blanket of silver frost, making exploration impossible.

Lumi understood the demands of life, yet her curiosity and yearning for adventure burned even brighter. She quickly gathered a group of friends and formed a small exploration team, determined to find a way out. But despite their excitement, failure kicked in—the aftermath of the Lament had seemingly twisted the terrain, eliminating every possible way out, just like it had their forebears.

At first, the setbacks didn't bother them. They were kids, after all, full of energy and hope. But as time passed, they drifted away. The older ones joined the labor teams, others lost interest. Lumi's once lively group dwindled, and today, her exploration ended earlier than planned as everyone was eager to hurry home before dusk settled in.

Lumi sighed. 

She knew that for most of her friends, this was just a way to pass the time. 

She stood up, cupped her hands around her mouth, and shouted toward the mountains, her voice echoing against the rocks and trees before fading into the evening air.

The sunset blazed across the sky, casting the horizon in shades of red and gold before melting into the soft kiss of the night. 

Lumi smiled, patting her cheeks lightly. It didn't matter. The thrill of discovering something new, something unknown, still filled her with excitement.

"…Oh! I'll tell Zhangzhang all about the view when we meet for ice pops tonight. And Beihai, Ming…"

She whispered the names of her friends as she waved goodbye to the mountains, then turned and made her way down the hill, alone but content.

"You're awake? Here, drink this."

As her eyes fluttered open, her parched lips met the cool, sweet droplets of water. Her hand instinctively gripped the container, and she eagerly gulped it down.

"Easy now, don't rush," the voice urged, gentle and concerned. "You'll choke if you drink too fast."

As the last drop slipped down her throat, Lumi blinked, her mind finally clearing. She looked up at the faces of her rescuers—a small squad, three of them, dressed in similar clothing. Their leader, a girl with a kind smile, helped her sit up.

"Are you from around here? That's a surprise. We were told there's no one living in these parts," the girl said, a hint of curiosity in her voice. "Guess we'll need to update our map."

"Thank you… for saving me," Lumi whispered, her words faltering. The world she knew was small, confined to the mountains and the narrow boundaries of Changzhuang. "A-are you from the outside?"

The squad exchanged glances, and it was then that Lumi noticed the emblem on their uniforms—a chubby hamster wearing a straw hat, grinning adorably.

A hand reached out, helping Lumi to her feet. 

"Sorry for the late introduction. We're from Lollo Logistics, a delivery squad."
 
Months later, Chengxiao smiled, setting down the comb and patting Lumi's shoulder. 

"Take a look. How do you feel?"

Lumi stared at her reflection, stunned by the unfamiliar face in the mirror. The girl staring back at her had neat curls and wore a clean, fitted Lollo Logistics uniform—looking every bit the city dweller she had become.

Chengxiao, the leader of the squad that had rescued her, had taken Lumi from the quiet of Changzhuang to the bustling city and taken her under her wing. She was quick-witted, reliable, and now Lumi's mentor at Lollo Logistics.

"I look… different," Lumi muttered, scratching her head shyly. "Thank you, Chengxiao."

"None of that formality now," Chengxiao laughed. "I'm off to deliver some documents. Cafeteria later?"

"Sure!"

As the door closed, Lumi returned to stare at the mirror, her gaze lingering on her reflection for a while. 

Having just passed the Lollo Logistics assessment, she was still adjusting to city life. The city was a whirlwind compared to the quiet village she had left behind. The streets buzzed with life, day and night. Even in the dead of night, lights flickered, and voices filled the air. Walls and doors were everywhere, and restrictions at every corner. In Changzhuang, she could run free, straight through the open land for as long as she wanted. Here, every step had to be measured carefully. The crowded markets left her both energized and overwhelmed.

"Take it slow, Lumi," she murmured to herself. "No rush. No rush…"

Grabbing her straw hat, Lumi took a deep breath and opened the door, ready to face the city once more.

"Squeakie, I'm feeling dizzy…" 

Lumi murmured, leaning against the edge of the bed as the ship rocked beneath her. The waves crashed against the hull with a roar, and the violent turbulence made one feel like it might drag them into the depths. She clutched her hamster plushie tightly, closing her eyes, waiting for this tortuous journey to end.

Days later, the port finally came into view, where the sea met the sky. Seagulls squawked in the distance, and Lumi exhaled a breath of relief as she stepped onto solid ground. "Thank goodness," she muttered. Her two companions, Tangtang and Fulei, staggered behind her, still pale from seasickness. 

"You two okay?" Lumi ran her fingers through her curls and led them to a nearby bench for rest.

"Lumi, was it this bad when you first came to Rinascita?" Tangtang, his head still drooping, asked.

Lumi chuckled. "Oh yeah! That's why I told you to stay fit. There are places way harder to reach than this."

Tangtang groaned, nodding. "Why did you recover so quickly? You were just as seasick as us a moment ago..."

Lumi grinned, remembering her first trip here with Chengxiao. "Trust me, I was just as bad. My legs felt weak, I wanted to throw up, and I almost swore never to set foot on a ship again!"

Fulei nodded in agreement, "The ship did rock hard. It was terrifying…"

Tangtang and Fulei were newbies who just joined Lollo Logistics and were assigned to Lumi's team for training. Lollo Logistics had entrusted her with guiding them through the ropes, but leading a team? Lumi wasn't so sure she was ready for that kind of responsibility. It wasn't because she hated caring for others; she was just worried that she might not meet these hopeful newcomers' expectations. Chengxiao had always made it look easy—could she really do the same?
 
"Lumi," Tangtang said, interrupting her thoughts, "You always talk about Chengxiao, but I've never seen her at the branch. Where is she?"

"She doesn't work in the field anymore," Lumi replied softly.

"What? But didn't you say she was an 'Outstanding Navigator' every year? Why would she quit?" Fulei asked, wide-eyed.

Lumi gazed up at the blue sky, the expanse above Ragunna remarkably clear. 

"Because... of life," she explained, as she had once before in her childhood. "Sometimes life leads you down different paths. Solaris is huge, and being in Lollo Logistics means traveling year-round. Chengxiao wanted something more stable, so she moved on."

Tangtang tilted her head. "And what about you? Did your family mind you doing this?"

"They had their concerns," Lumi admitted. "But this is my life, and I love it—traveling, seeing new things, connecting people across Solaris. That's what Lollo Logistics is all about. Chengxiao taught me a lot, and I'll do my best to pass it on to you both."

Her words hung in the air as the two newcomers considered them. 

Lumi smiled. "Life is full of comings and goings," she continued. "Some people get off the ship, others get on. But as long as there are those willing to carry the torch, our 'We Promise, We Deliver' motto will keep going strong."

Lumi stood up and gave a good stretch, Squeakie perched on her shoulder, nuzzling her cheek. "Rest for another ten minutes, then we're off. Oh, you want some famous Ragunna's triple scoop ice cream? My treat!"

"Yes!"

"Please!"

Ever since its connection to the outside world resumed, Changzhuang had experienced a dramatic change. New buildings and amenities were everywhere, yet when Lumi returned home, she felt a deep wave of nostalgia.

Perhaps those who longed for change had already departed, like Lumi once before, while those who remained had maintained their old habits and daily rhythms. The sun was dipping low, and as she walked through the village, smoke from cooking fires curled lazily into the sky, mingling with the sounds of laughter and the hum of evening insects.

Her parents welcomed her home, placing a steaming bowl of noodles in front of her—the meat was generous, the broth rich, supplemented by a spoonful of fragrant chili oil. 

Lumi dug in, the heat making her cheeks flush as she slurped the noodles eagerly. Her mother chuckled softly, passing her a glass of water.

"Slow down, Lumi, no one's going to steal your food," her mother teased.

After a deep sip of water and broth, she leaned back, letting out a contented sigh.

Her father, seated nearby, tapped his pipe. "Been away for a long time, huh? How's your work?"

Lumi smiled. "It's been tough, but things are getting better. Someone really helped me out—a hero from Jinzhou, actually!"

Her mother raised an eyebrow, amused. "Oh? Our little Lumi rubbing elbows with big shots now?"

Lumi laughed, her eyes bright. "It's true! I was struggling with some work stuff, but thanks to {Male=him;Female=her}, I turned it all around. Here's what happened…"
 
The next morning, with the village still shrouded in the quiet calm of dawn, Lumi left home to enjoy the morning landscape of the fields. It hadn't changed beyond recognition. It still bore the vestiges of the place that had shaped her. 

She wandered without aim, lost in thought until a gentle pat on the shoulder brought her back to the present.

"Lumi? What are you doing all the way out here?"

Lumi blinked and turned to see Zhangzhang, her childhood friend, standing behind her, smiling.

"Oh, Zhangzhang! I was just… reminiscing. It's been a while." Lumi's gaze drifted to the newly paved road winding through the hills. "I can't even tell where we are."

Zhangzhang laughed. "Yeah, it just got finished recently—much smoother than before, huh? It was once your favorite place, you remember?" She shifted her gaze to the road and continued, "Not many people come through, though. But I hear your Lollo Logistics team visits regularly." Zhangzhang paused, intrigued, "Speaking of which, have you been to any cool places lately? Anything to share? You see, I've been thinking about leaving to see the world for myself as well…"

Lumi nodded and began recounting her latest adventures, sharing the tales of distant cities and unknown lands with her childhood friend.

When they parted ways, Lumi found a stone by the road and sat on it, propping her chin up as she gazed at the sky. She knew that she had to move forward—only then would she see new things, bring about change, and make a difference for others.

As night faded, the first light of morning washed over the slumbering mountains. 

There in the distance, where the mountain path met the sky, the familiar silhouette of a Lollo Logistics vehicle, glimmering in the sun, was approaching Changzhuang.

My mind has grown numb with monotony for the past decade or so. I handle exciting jobs sometimes, but the fun soon dries up, like tidal marks on the shoal. But you... you're the only one who keeps me on my toes. So of course I'd be paying attention to you.

My stance? Ha! I didn't join the Black Shores to save the world. Just needed a way to pass the time on this island. Justice, truth… Saints spout them, sinners exploit them, all for their own gains. Me? I need nothing and want nothing. Pretty words hold no power over me.
Why did you... come here? Told you not to... Cough cough! Not to visit... while I'm here in the pod... Hehe, a cute girl like me needs her privacy, you know? ...I hate myself like this... don't look.

You know what? I dreamed of you while I was in the medical pod. In that dream… I couldn't get to know you. Your name echoed in my head endlessly as we roamed the same places, but I never saw your face, not even once... How odd...

Saving the world? Couldn't care less. This cage of a world only consumes and binds you with responsibility. But if you believe it's the right thing to do… Go for it! You're staying true to yourself, and I like that. It's beautiful, we both find joy in our own paths! But if you ever get tired of this whole savior business, do let me know… What will I do? Hehe... Secret!
Napping in the sun on a warm afternoon is so cozy, I just need to find a quiet place. Sleeping in the warmth, nestled among branches and leaves...
Working for the Black Shores has been a snooze fest. I tried to spice it up by picking the toughest jobs, didn't help. There's no one worth my time on Solaris now. I'm dying of boredom!
Fruit juice. Fresh, raw, and tangy. That gentle sweetness lingers... You want some?
I don't like boozy stuff. Why? ...I don't know. It just makes me... uncomfortable.

Pick the best seeds, protect them till they're ripe. Then comes the fun—I'll have worthy opponents to fight! I don't care about the rest. We'll all die one day, might as well dance and live it up while we can. Responsibility? Ideals? Those are just lies we tell ourselves to feel better, nothing but a false high.

The Loong Maiden of Jinzhou reminds me of the Shorekeeper, the way they're oh-so-devoted to their duties, all the self-sacrifice! I don't understand, why must they burden themselves so much?
That girl, the Taoist? She's a fun one to watch. She may seem to follow human society's boring norms, but her untamed spirit still shines through every now and then.

Your birthday is the most wonderful day. Without you, my life would be so empty and dull! Being with you again brings me peace. I am content now. Hey, put your Terminal away, great savior of Solaris! I blocked all signals here so we can be undisturbed. Today, you're mine, and no one else's.

This Terminal ringtone? Yeah, I made it! Thought it'd be a cool way to get the Lollo Logistics name out there… It's catchy, right? My colleagues thought so too and all started using it. Now it's ringing everywhere.

This is Squeakie, my plushie. Here, give it a squeeze—isn't it adorable? I made it when I first joined Lollo Logistics. Everything was new, I mean, scarily new… and I was super nervous about the job… So having Squeakie around was such a comfort!

My nail polish is all chipped off… Time for a new color! When I first moved to the city, I tried all sorts of looks so I could fit in, but always ended up looking silly! Now… Now I've found my own style. So, what color d'you think I should go with?

I never left my village growing up, but once I did, I became a restless traveler. Riding my bike with the wind in my ears just feels amazing. I keep meeting new people, and saying goodbye to them… it's all part of the journey, isn't it? I bet you're the same, always on the move. Great way of living, right? I think... we'll surely meet again somewhere down the road. And when we do, let's grab some local food and catch up on our adventures!
I jot down all the interesting sights, people, and events in my travel journal. If words don't cut it, I sketch it out. I've filled up so many journals since joining Lollo Logistics!
There's never enough time! Delivering packages, planning new routes, catching up with friends, keeping my journal... Oh I wish I could be in a million places at once！
Rice noodles are my absolute favorite! Spice it up with chili, a dash of vinegar, sprinkle some green onions... delicious! Next time you're in Yuezhou, I'll treat you!

Hmm... What did they call it? Some local speciality noodle I tried during a delivery, with this golden fish broth and green veggies. Did NOT taste as good as it looked—ugh, it was so bitter! Never again!

Wow, ever since we got a road in our village, things have been crazy! We've built so much new stuff. I've been keeping an eye on my team, making sure everyone's good—some want promotions, some need more cash for their fams, and some wanna travel. Hehe, busy days, but it feels great to be needed... I should keep it up!
This on my head? It's my employee ID badge. Clipped it to my hair to save myself the fumbling when I'm carrying stuff. Now everyone knows my name in a snap. Perfect!

That day, I left my village, hiked over the mountain, farther than anyone else had gone before. I soon found myself in a vast field, the air fresh and damp with dew. I was so pumped that I started to glow, and the light attracted Tacet Discords... Did everything I could to fight them off, then I blacked out. Next thing I knew, a Lollo Logistics team saved me, their lights cutting through the darkness, the brightest I've ever seen.

When I am out delivering packages, I can't always find a place to stay, so sometimes I rest outdoors. Once, I woke up to see Miss Jianxin napping on a boulder on the cliff edge! She seemed... so light, like a feather...
Ma Xiao...oops, I mean Chixia, hehe! Ahem, Patroller Chixia's packages are mostly snacks and hero play merchs. She was so stoked last time she got one, she practically bounced out of the room!
Youhu's packages always come with insurance, full of pricey antiques. I don't know much about these stuff, but the way she handles them, you can tell they're her treasures.
Researcher Baizhi's packages weigh a ton! Mostly stacks of books, thick ones, and a bunch of other weird stuff. Said those are for research purposes...
Actually, I rarely get to meet Miss Zhezhi in person… She's a night owl, barely out during the day. So I've been dropping her paints and paper at her door.

Auntie Panhua's letting me use her stove today. In my village, we celebrate birthdays with steaming longevity noodles like this, topped with two braised eggs! Hey, you gotta slurp it all in one go, no biting allowed! Hehe… Happy birthday! May your journey ahead always be bright.

Carlotta said it's paid.
