Bloom Bearer Field Report

Bloom Bearer Field Report No. 10826 Authored by: Ariosto Attention Rinascita-based Bloom Bearers: Please follow the advice below in the interest of your safe being. Failure to do so may result in unpleasant repercussions. 1. Rinascita has no center of politics, instead a collection of city-states governs the region. The southern coastal city of Ragunna is the recommended port of entry for Black Shores Bloom Bearers. The "Stormy Sea" between Black Shores and Rinascita is treacherous, exercise extreme caution. Stay on the approved navigation route. If found to be deviating, correct course at once. 2. Strange aquatic TDs inhabit the Stormy Sea. Our current understanding of them is limited as they appear incapable of coherent thought. Do not interact, approach, or touch them. Take evasive action at once should one move towards your vessel. 3. Ragunna, a city-state by the sea, is the city with the strongest link to the Sentinel. This connection is maintained by the Order of the Deep, an organization claiming to act as the Sentinel's representative. The citizens of Ragunna equate Sentinel Imperator to "god," and have erected numerous statues in Their image. Bow and lower your gaze when in the presence of such statues. Do not stare at any one statue for over 30 seconds. 4. Ragunna has one cardinal rule regarding pizza: it does not, and will never, tolerate crownapple topping. Do NOT in any circumstance, add crownapple or gemberry to any pizza served at a Ragunnesi restaurant. This rule must—and I repeat—must be adhered to. Comments Comment 1: I knew sending you to investigate the Somnoire was a mistake! If I read another useless do's and don'ts listicle you'll be re-writing the whole thing. And say goodbye to your performance bonus! Posted by: Mistman Comment 2: Living by the sea… Do the Ragunnesi eat rice from a coral bowl? Posted by: SheepGoBaah Everything I've shared above is based on firsthand experience—gathered by shedding blood, sweat, and tears! In all seriousness. Other than its Common Echoes, the city of Ragunna is also renowned for its "faith" centered around the Sentinel, reinforced via mythologies created by The Order of the Deep to justify the post-lament state of affairs. Personally, I find their mythologies not entirely baseless, as the worldviews espoused are similar to that of the Tethys System. The first inhabitants of Rinascita were refugees displaced by the Lament and Waveworn disasters. Guided by the Sentinel to settle in Rinascita, these refugees were of vastly different backgrounds, cultures, and ideologies. Ragunna's religious and political systems were likely structured around a unifying mono-faith to increase civil cohesion. I encourage Bloom Bearers to approach Ragunna's many rituals and customs with a critical but open mind. I was born in Rinascita, but after years with the Black Shores, upon my return, the change was far greater than I had anticipated. Most notably, the Order now holds absolute authority in Ragunna. I advise all Bloom Bearers to maintain cordial relations with the Order, respect their rules, and avoid confrontation. Given the Order's current stance towards the Black Shores, Bloom Bearers must exercise utmost discretion while in Ragunna, To help Bloom Bearers earn the trust of Order members, I've compiled a few useful examples of how to phrase sentences so they resemble clauses from their Codex. Let me demonstrate: -Oh, mighty lord in black, the founder and ruler of the Black Shores! May I one day be worthy of your talents and devote myself fully to your service! -Greedy KU-Money, reflect upon the error of your ways before the lord's altar and seek redemption. -Praise to Shorekeeper, Guardian of the Black Shores! Your starlight scatters the darkness and banishes all evil. With your light to guide us, we are delivered to salvation! And I was wondering why Ragunna City reeks of money and snobs these days.
Some folks are eager to work with us in their pursuit of wealth and self-actualization. We're simply providing them with the platform.
Since we're on that matter, do you have financial needs we can assist you with? I couldn't help but notice the lofts in Fisalia Residencies seem... out of repair.
If you're planning on a renovation, rest assured—I have some connections in construction and design.
Hmph—I would not waste my breath lecturing you on defending the longstanding traditions and principles of Ragunna, and of Rinascita.
We Fisalias would never disrespect our values and beliefs. But you Montellis wouldn't wait to walk away from these for your grand "course", would you?
(It got pretty intense...)
(Best not to interrupt...)
We're simply adapting to the times. Even the Order is willing to guide us toward ascension. Only fools would drown in old dreams.
Oh, forgive me—I nearly forgot.
In the past, it was you who controlled the Order and the path of ascension. But now...
Mind you, though we may have past our prime, our family still stands stronger than yours.
There, you said it yourself, Fisalia is history now.
Please keep your Echoes down, gentlemen, and avoid causing unnecessary disturbances in the restaurant.
Would you like to put away your Echoes, or should I bring each of them a dish to match yours?
Do they do this often?
I've gotten used to it...
Ms. Margherita won't step in as long as they don't disrupt other guests from enjoying their meals.
But, honestly, I'd really prefer if they could take their arguments somewhere else.
Nah. The tuning is flat... Might as well send it back to the "dock" for remodeling.
Huh? Who's there listening in? Are you trying to steal my <ano=Echo tuning>tuning</ano> skills?
Who are you?
Woah, am I being blackmailed?
Do you not know who I am?
Franciscus of Fisalia, chief musician of the Order, a one-in-a-million musical genius, with all Vox Sancti under my command!
Oh.
Oh, wow.
You little uncultured—Oh, calm yourself Franciscus. Must keep it together for the honor of the Fisalia family...
Must keep it together for the honor of the Fisalia family...
Levito, oh... Levito...
Levito, oh... Levito...
You were a true genius. And me? A mere mediocrity... a petty person even. I betrayed you...
Huh? Who's there?
How much did you drink?
I didn't hear anything...
...Never mind. Friend, if you have a moment, could you indulge me in a brief confession?
Do you know Levito? He was once the Order's lead musician.
I saw him as my primary rival for the chief musician position and went head to head against him on every matter.
To ensure I got the spot, I publicly disparaged his work. I stooped so low as to spread rumors that his work broke the Order's doctrines. All the slandering I did... They worked. Led to his downfall.
I did these things because I was simply jealous of his talent. I couldn't compose such beautiful pieces, nor conduct the Vox Sancti to perform in such perfect unity...
To this day, I still cannot surpass him.
Then words came suddenly one day that he boarded the Pilgrim's Sail. I never heard from him again... only later did I learn that the appalling truth of the pilgrimage.
If anything happened to Levito during his pilgrimage, my part in this shall not be pardoned...
You should say these words to Levito yourself.
If I could, I would tell him in person of my remorse...
Every night, I repent and punish myself with unbearable guilt. But when daylight comes, I put on my mask again.
Thank you for listening. As you can see, my arrogance... is just a facet of my self-loathing and guilt...
I fear my secret being revealed, yet my heart can't stop whispering it in the night...
This guilt... it's nearly crushing me...
It's you. I'm currently tuning these Vox Sancti.

We're finally connected, {PlayerName}. Can you hear me?
(What is this feeling... is it... the Somnoire?)
Don't worry, it's just me, the White Cat from the Somnoire. I'm reaching out to you in your dream...
There are things best discussed face-to-face. Could you come to Ragunna City if you have the time? I need a favor from you, meow...
Hello, {PlayerName}... This city is quite peculiar, meow. To be honest, it's my first time in Ragunna.
Meow?
You are a cat...
Ahem... never mind. The reason I contacted you, {PlayerName}, is because I sensed your frequency coming from Ragunna.
I am not a mere cat! Ahem, let's set that aside for now. The real reason I contacted you, {PlayerName}, is because I sensed your frequency coming from Ragunna.
Originally, I couldn't leave the Whining Aix's Mire or collect dreams from other regions due to restrictions placed upon admin privileges and the Resonance Nexus.
Especially in Rinascita, which has been veiled by a network of countless nodes, making any connection impossible... until just recently, when one of its nodes suddenly linked up.
Those special challenge nodes?
Exactly. I believe you've unintentionally picked up a unique frequency, {PlayerName}. With the Somnoire obtaining samples from Ragunna, I was finally able to connect with you.
Ever since the last incident, I've been working on the Somnoire, getting it to resume the task of dream backup.
But I'm completely powerless when it comes to Ragunna's dreams. So, I'd like to ask you to keep completing those challenges, {PlayerName}.
Most of the Dreamscape Nodes should be directly accessible to you, {PlayerName}. Some are special Tacet Discords linked to the Somnoire, while others are corrupted Dreamscape Nexus.
However, in the Fagaceae Peninsula and the Penitent's End, the Dreamscape Nodes appear to be veiled by an unknown force.
That sounds complicated...
I see... so, that's what was lurking deep within the network of Dreamscape Nodes.
There's something actively collecting people's nightmares and negative emotions...
Well done, {PlayerName}. For now, the Somnoire connection has seen some progress. Let's discuss it further in person.
{PlayerName}, do you think that special TD is similar to some of the memory fragments in the Somnoire?
There are some resemblances.
And it reminded me of an old acquaintance...
Yes, if you look closely, it's very similar to those corrupted dreams.
I'm talking about the corrupted dreams, meow.
Dreams are visions from the subconscious. Even when they solidify into memory fragments, they still carry all the joy and sorrow of the dreamer.
But those special TDs... it's as though people's subconscious have been unified by a single concept, carrying nothing but one desire.
I tried to peer into the depths of the network to see what lay beyond. For a brief moment, I saw a single frame of image and almost drowned in the tidal sound, losing myself.
What kind of image?
I saw a pitch-black abyss, where people were neatly lined up, crawling, performing the same gestures, murmuring the same words, trapped in the same dream.
In the next moment, they noticed my presence and turned to meet my gaze... Their eyes... Their pupils were stained with the same substance...
And in the darkness behind them, a pair of enormous eyes slowly opened... I've never seen a dream like this before.
That sounds unsettling...
They all turned to look at you?
Yes. Just thinking about it gives me an uneasy feeling.
It wasn't normal, meow... Just thinking about it gives me an uneasy feeling.
That dream was far too dangerous and unsettling. What could be lurking in the darkness beneath Rinascita's waters? Have the people of Ragunna always been living with such a threat?
So, {PlayerName}, I'd like to ask you to keep eliminating those TDs hidden within the network. Only then will the dreams housed in the Somnoire be safe.
Well done, {PlayerName}. I can feel that all the Dreamscape Nodes are now connected.
The hidden threats have been cleared... I've prepared your rewards, meow. Let's discuss the details in person.
Good job, {PlayerName}! I knew you could do it.
Now the dream frequency in the Ragunna region is stable... Hmm, how should I say this... It feels very... Rinascita.
Just like people from Jinzhou often dream of the Moon-Chasing Festival or Loong Whiskers Crisp, the most common dreams in Ragunna are about prayers, pizza, opera, and the Carnevale.
From these dreams, it seems the people of Ragunna live quite happily... So why is there such a turbulent subconscious lurking beneath the surface?
Are deep-sea monster stories popular lately?
Maybe the Order is hiding something...
I really don't get it, meow, why would anyone like such terrifying things?! The deep sea is so dark, and I can't even swim, meow.
I'm not sure about that... but there are surprisingly few dreams from Order members in these samples... What's going on?
Let's leave that for later. In time, the Somnoire in Ragunna will be fully established.
Thank you again for all your help, {PlayerName}. By the way, in addition to the agreed reward, I want to give you this as a keepsake.
What is this?
This is a unique sample I found in a Dreamscape Node. I'm not sure what it's for yet, but it certainly looks exquisite.
Maybe one day it will come in handy.
How marvelous! I hear the sounds of birth and doom, of everlasting mountains and seas, and the fierce pulses of life!
This is life's symphony, each note threaded by the loom of time, more alluring than any Siren's call!
As promised, here is the first riddle: The Siren's Song.
"Long ago, a group of girls followed the Siren's call out of town. They journeyed to the 'crown' atop the mountain and to the waterfall that cascaded into the depths."
Beyond this riddle, I, Mammon, have yet another gift to offer for your performance.
Please take this music box. It's dusty with age, but it might just sing again with a song like you just played.
That person does seem a bit extra...
It's understandable. Hearing a Laureate perform is an honor, a blessing for everyone in Rinascita.
Even this music box should be humming along in admiration…
Cantarella taps the music box, but it doesn't work as expected.
Oh, so that's why this little thing isn't behaving… Someone must have silenced it, leaving it unable to sing.
Cantarella's fingers move deftly as she tinkers with the music box, but it remains silent.
As Cantarella examines it, you notice the music box has a unique shape.
If you look at this music box from above, doesn't it resemble a big apple?
Hmm, now that you mention it… Indeed, it does.

To your surprise, the Order's "confessional" turns out to be a freight elevator. 
After leaving it behind, you arrive at Whisperwind Haven and meet Zani. Together, you set off to trace Gilberto.

Gilberto's traces end here. Zani speculates that he must have left using a <ano=Flying Echo>Wingray</ano>.
It seems Gilberto never anticipated that you two could also follow his lead and take the Wingray to where he was heading.

You run into Cristoforo, the mysterious playwright, again. He's on a journey for inspiration to finish his script about the Blessed Maiden, "Fleurdelys." 
As for Gilberto, he tells you that a Fisalia member has been frequenting Whisperwind Haven, and Echoes have been mysteriously vanishing. 
Suspecting a connection, you follow the Echoes to investigate further.

Upon reaching the area where Echoes have gone missing, you're attacked by out-of-control Echoes. After quelling them, you notice that they seem to be manipulated, just like the Vitreum Dancers in Ragunna. 
Bidding Cristoforo farewell, you press on and encounter another familiar face—Acolyte Phoebe.

Phoebe reveals that she's searching for a missing Echo. You share your findings, and she realizes Gilberto's actions are blasphemy against the Sentinel, which calls for a punishment. With shared goals, Phoebe joins your team. 
Suddenly, the missing Echo appears, fleeing as if being pursued. You decide to catch up to uncover what's behind its panic.

You finally pin down Gilberto, who is reciting eerie prayers. 
On seeing you, he transforms the nearby Echoes into Tacet Discords with a Lycoris flower. A fierce battle ensues.

Despite his defeat, Gilberto continues to preach a dark prophecy: Lorelei will command the sea of clouds to engulf Ragunna, sparing only the faithful. Meanwhile, an anomaly at the Nimbus Sanctum suggests Lorelei might also be influenced by a Lycoris. 
Zani and Phoebe stay behind to watch over Gilberto until the Montelli members arrive. You head to the sea of clouds alone.

Upon reaching the port near the sea of clouds, you prepare to board a boat to the Atrium of Reflections, but the port's services are suspended due to the anomaly. Fortunately, the harbormaster lets you take a Gondola yourself.
With no other options, you search the port for an available Gondola.

While searching for an available Gondola, you encounter the noble lady you once met at the Masked Reverie.
She asks to travel with you to catch the train in the sea of clouds.

You arrive at the Echo train station and wait for its arrival. 
During the wait, the noble lady shares her thoughts on Ragunna City, the Montelli and Fisalia families... and you.
You reunite with Zani and Phoebe at the Atrium of Reflections。

At the Atrium of Reflections, a masked believer tells you that the path to Lorelei's domain is sealed. Unable to reason with them, you begin investigating the place to find an alternative way forward.

Through investigation, you realize that the key to unsealing Lorelei's domain is a "chorale." 
With encouragement from you and Zani, Phoebe gathers the courage and sings the melody. The song unlocks the sealed passage before you.

You defeat the "Queen of the Night," Lorelei's corrupted form under the Lycoris's influence, and restore her to her true self. Besides, you also find the Vitreum Dancer that fled away, but it is damaged while protecting you. Zani keeps it in the Montelli's Terminal.
Lorelei, a remnant creature enlightened by the Sentinel, reveals a shocking truth: the current Primus of the Order is not the legendary <ano=Sentinel's Resonator>Enlightened One</ano>. The Sentinel's link to the mortal world has been severed, and only the Laureate of the Carnevale gets a chance to communicate with Them. 
Lorelei also discloses the identity of the one causing Echoes to lose control—the Conductor.

Shaken by Lorelei's revelations, Phoebe decides to return to the Order to seek answers and bids farewell to you.
With Lorelei's information, you are certain that Fractsidus is behind the chaos among Echoes.
You and Zani head to Averardo Vault, the heart of the Montelli family, to seek allies and repair the damaged Vitreum Dancer Echo.

Magistrate Jinhsi insists that I take some time off work. The streets tonight are bustling with life. Since I have little to do, I imbibed some... floral brew. My body is warm yet my heart longs for someone to confide in.

It is a common practice to don monster masks as part of a ceremonial dance ritual. Folks here believe their reenactment of monsters from the legends of Huanglong may ward off evil and invite good fortune. As for me... I do not need the reenactment, for I have worked hard to suppress the monster within, which is already a perfect mask for me.

Those strange sights and sounds in the cold wind and snow are the past that I cannot sever. But because of you all, I see the silver lining behind these macabre scenes. You give me the strength to pray for the return of spring.

The fate you've sown will bear fruit in the coming years. Should you leave on another journey, please remember to take my... and our blessings with you.

This year's ceremony is different—it is the first one free of the Threnodian menace. People are finally able to laugh and rejoice from the heart, and I truly enjoy seeing everyone smile.

I've told Sanhua and Taoqi to take a break. After working all year, they deserve leisure time to bask in this hard-won warmth. When I see others happily reunited with their families, I can't help but yearn for your presence. I knew you had matters to attend to, but your absence during the most festive days in a year would have made everyone a bit lonely.

So, when you came back with guests from Rinascita, I was truly happy—you really do miss Jinzhou enough to spend time with me. Perhaps, in your heart, Jinzhou has become your home.

I wrote a song to express my gratitude, and it seems I'll finally get to sing it. Wearing the ceremonial dress still makes me a bit shy, but if you like, I'll wear it properly after I finish work and sing just for you.

Jinhsi

I hope this letter finds you well.

Jinhsi and Sanhua were overjoyed by the glowing reviews of the Hero Play from the guests of Rinascita. After a year of hard work, they can finally set aside their duties and enjoy a well-deserved respite.

Your Rinascitan friends were eager to share thrilling tales of the Laureate with me, and I found their stories about you both delightful and heartwarming. It is truly gratifying to see the profound impact your journey has had on the lives of others.

However, I believe it is time for you to take some proper rest now, after the busyness of the Hero Play and the joy of welcoming your friends. During your absence, several notable events transpired in Jinzhou. If you are interested, I would be happy to recount them to you at your leisure.

The day before your return to Jinzhou, the winter's last snowstorm breathed a delicate layer of snow on our Go checkerboard, on which I wrote a wish.

By the time you receive this letter, it will have already come true.

Changli

When I think about it, we've really been through a lot, haven't we? From Huanglong to the Black Shores and then onto Rinascita. From Loong Buns and Coral Bowl to Pizza Tropicale. Although our trip had its rough patches, in the end, nothing could hold us back.

This is a letter from Carlotta Montelli. I hope this did not come as a surprise.

It wasn't until I lifted my pen that I realized this was not the first time I had written to you. You had known me through my invitation to you to Rinascita, long before we met in person. That was where it all began.

Fate brought you before me. Together, we captured the traitor within my family and took part in Ragunna's grandest Carnevale. Breaking conventions and revealing all to an outsider was a first for me, but with you, everything came so naturally.

This time, when I received your invitation, I did not hesitate to accept. The cultures of those beyond Rinascita are fascinating, and I'm thoroughly intrigued by the Hero Plays of Jinzhou. But what really captivates me are the aspects of you that I have yet to explore.

If my initial invitation led you to reciprocate, then perhaps a heartfelt expression of sincerity might elicit an equally precious response. 

Would you dance with me if I took the first step?

I wrote this letter after watching the play. Pero was happily stuffed after she ate all the petals on stage. She was as satisfied as everyone else.

The waves bring many things—sometimes a discarded bottle, sometimes a broken sail, and sometimes a precious Luceanite. Then one day, you and the captain braved the waves and reached our troupe. At the time, I never imagined you would be such a joy and inspiration to me and Pero.

I took the funny stories you told me and turned them into commedia to give hope and courage to our happy troupe. I hope you will be the first audience for my new play, since it's about your travels. I haven't decided on the finale yet, but perhaps, like your journey, it should have no end.

May the wind always be at your back and the sun upon your face. Next time we meet, regale me with dazzling stories.

Roccia

My dearest friend, thank you for the invitation. I had heard much about Huanglong's Hero Plays, but attending one in person has truly revealed their magnificence!

There's magic to a great performance where actors pour their very souls into their craft. A tale told from the stage can grow to encompass the world! And the audience too becomes part of that world, immersed in the character's joys and sorrows.

I am always fascinated by performances that evoke such feelings. Therefore, the troupe and I have prepared a new play. Care to guess the plot? Well, think back to when we first met—how one hero braved the sea to conquer the storm and be crowned with the Laurel of the Carnevale!

A hero's journey always deserves flowers and applause. We want people to know of your thrilling exploits and to feel the passion and romance of a roving life. Come, my friend! You must not miss the show!
(Enclosed are two front-row tickets)

Brant

What are we betting?

What does being captain actually involve?
Simply put, you chart the course and steer the ship. The crew will be ready to sail on your order at moment's notice.
Might seem easy enough, but there's more to being captain of the Troupe of Fools.

That does get me going.

Everyone's unique talents make this troupe what it is. Each soul plays an important role.
Ah, but duty calls, Captain. Oh, time to scrub the decks before dinner, as promised.
Dinner's at six. Good... there's still time. Until then!
Six o'clock, dinner! Six o'clock, dinner!
There's still some time before dinner. A little stroll could be a good idea.
A bottle of Troupe Strength, just for you! Around these parts, this stuff is as good as gold.
Oh, and look what I found while gutting the fish!
Let me see.
It's… split in half?

Mmm?
Look, there's something there…
May I have a look?

Hmm, yes. On these seas, there is only one legend about "D."
The story of Drake, the Golden Captain.
Captain Drake! That adventurer everyone talks about?
I thought that was just a fanciful story…
Who is Captain Drake?
What do they say about him?
Captain Drake, the famed hero of Rinascita. Legend has it he assembled a crew with naught but a single coin and amassed great riches from the wealthiest of men.
He then embarked on a quest to chart a safe passage across the Stormy Sea. A feat worthy of being remembered forever!
But there was a price. Only one crew member returned, and he had been driven mad. What happened out there is still a mystery.
You seem to know the story well.
Such tales were my bedtime stories.
Back when I just boarded the Pilgrim's Sail, with no family and nightmares that could raise the dead, Toscanini would share such stories to comfort me.
At the time, I swore that if I ever became a captain, every crew member would come back safe. No exceptions.
Ah, Toscanini, the Night Watcher. Hahaha. You're one of the few who still remembers him.
Did he ever tell you the rest? That mad sailor who raved about his captain's coin, saying it would lead to untold treasures.
Perhaps it's the very coin our Captain here is holding.
Untold treasures, eh? Well, aren't we lucky. If we had the whole thing, imagine the riches we'd claim...
Do these treasures really exist?
Any idea where the other half of the coin might be hiding？
Oh, they exist, alright. The Golden Captain conquered every sea known to man. The wealth he amassed could give us all lives of leisure and luxury.
You raise a fine point. Where is the other half…
Half a coin… Treasures… Blast!
Something wrong, Hymer?
Now that I think of it… I lost a half-coin just like this not long ago.
You sure? One like this?
Yes, almost identical! There was a man yapping about its value. I thought he was just bluffing.
Didn't take him seriously... then I lost it to Bella.
Bella… Since the pirates started stirring the waters around Ragunna, she's been hiring us to guard her family ships.
Aye! She's a regular at Trattoria Margherita. Loves their pizzas. I run into her all the time!

What say you? Ready to check it out?
Don't have to ask me twice.
Sailor Brant, lead the way.
Aye, aye, Captain! Our course is set! Ready the sails, and let the wind carry us!
I've had dealings with Bella before. She's alright in my books, but she's got an odd obsession with good luck charms.

Wait, you didn't actually go along with it.

Pirates are strangling our shipping routes, and if that weren't enough—look at this pizza! No olives!

And that lucky coin I fought tooth and nail to get? Stolen! Some wretched thief made off with it. I've been cursed ever since.
Unlike you, Brant. You could disappear into a fog and emerge glittering like a diamond. If only I could borrow just a pinch of your luck…

Still working on that "grand cause" of yours?
Grand…? Oh yes! My grand cause! I'm this close to realizing it, you see. Look! Drake's treasure is right there, so brilliant, so-so dazzling…
But as a man of principle, I could never hoard such wealth all to myself.
So, in the spirit of fairness, I'd like to give you the honor of opening it first. Please go ahead, the first pick is yours!
Leave your bluster at the door.
You're just afraid of the curse, aren't you?
C-curse? Hahaha! Do I look like the kind of man who fears mere legends? No, no, my offer comes straight from the heart.
It's okay.
In accordance with the law of the sea…
This is just a teeny tiny curse. Nothing more, nothing less.
You... you look fine…
Hahahaha! Curse? Turns out it's as harmless as a kitten!
I fretted for nothing! Yes, now all this treasure is MINE!
What about your grand cause?
What about your crew?
Grand cause? My crew? Oh right…
I'll toss a modest pouch to each of my loyal mateys, and the rest? ALL MINE! Hahaha!
When I left the Pilgrim's Sail, there was only one thing that stayed with me—to chase my desires without chains.
And after all these years, I've cracked the code… Money! Hahaha! That's my one true calling. Hahaha!
But everything comes with a price, Aldric.
And now, it's time to pay yours.
Wh-what?!
Watch out, Captain!
Wh-what's happening?!
Curse… This is the curse! My gold… My gold is moving!
No Aldric, this is the price of your greed.
Did you forget? "The law of quid pro quo."
You mean that blasted half-coin?!
You hear no response, only the sound of waves crashing against the shores.
Six o'clock, dinner! Six o'clock, dinner!
Greetings! Captain Brant sends his regards!
Brant lost his bet.
I'm the captain now.
Ooh, Captain! Captain!
Brant lost again! Surprise, surprise.
It happens a lot, doesn't it?
Has he ever won?
Never wins! Never wins!
Captain, Pan Cake at your service! At your service!
We managed to slip away.
I… I never thought he'd pick those treasures over his own life…
Are you holding up alright?
Back then… When Toscanini first told us about Drake's story, I said I wanted to be a captain who led the crew to countless triumphs so that everyone gets to carve out their own destiny.
Aldric just laughed, calling it foolish. He said, "You fool! With Drake's treasure, you can crush anyone and make everyone's life better by force!"
I never bought into that. For me, it's not about riches or power. It's about freedom—the freedom to sail your own course.
That's why we parted ways. He left the Troupe of Fools and became a pirate.
The two of you became very different captains.
Amidst all your theatrics, you always remain true to your code.
As a captain, you're quite different yourself.
Certainly one I'd be proud to follow.
You accept your crew for who they are, understanding and respecting their choices.
I've had my share of adventures, but I must admit—this one with you has been a breath of fresh air.
By the way, look at this.
Is this... Drake's treasure?
What? It looks like an ordinary scroll.
This is Golden Captain Drake's map, a record of his life.
According to this, he and his crew did indeed brave the treacherous Stormy Sea and return with immense wealth, but not without paying dearly.
Heavy fog, disease, getting hopelessly lost, each entry could have sunk an entire fleet. By the time they made it back to the isle, only a handful survived.
Most of them never left. In the end, only one sailor remained with this coin.
Remember what that note said? "Remember the law of quid pro quo."
I believe it means if you want Drake's treasure, you have to offer something in return. The price I paid for this scroll was that coin.
So, you gave away the coin…
And got this scroll in return?
Yes, but isn't it fascinating? A single coin can lead to both dreadful curses and priceless treasures.
Who would have guessed that Drake's most valuable treasure would be a map worth just one coin?
Honestly, when I made the trade, I wasn't sure what I'd get.
You were betting on it?
That was quite the gamble.
Hahaha! I had faith in you, my friend, and the spirit of adventure.
And this story is far more compelling than the saga of the Flaming Returned, don't you think?
Didn't expect that title to come up again…
Tell me what all that is really about.
Ah, you remember those pirates who said I was always on the run?
Every time a bounty was placed on my head, I'd work with my crew. They'd turn me in for the reward, and I'd handle the escape.
The rumors spread faster than I expected. Hahaha…
Anyway, if you're up for it, the trip back is long enough for me to tell you all about it.
So, Captain, the adventure's come to a close. Ready to sail back home?
Let's go!
Ah, what a journey. It feels good to be back.
Seems like my captaincy is over, too…
I'll leave the paperwork to you.
Time really does fly.
Paperwork? Why wasn't I warned about this?
Haha, jokes aside, you can count on me for that!
Anyway, this is for you.
Is this… Drake's scroll?
Exactly! I figured it would be a good memento of our adventure.
Oh, and due to your stellar performance, I'm officially naming you our troupe's "Honorary Captain," as witnessed by this map!
When do we sail again?
That depends on when the next adventure calls! You know that I'll be ready to join you, just say the word.
I'm proud to announce that you are now our troupe's Honorary Captain.
Whenever the next grand adventure calls, count me in. I'll be ready!
Captain {PlayerName}, what's our destination?
Normally, Captain Brant calls the shots, but since the helm is yours, I'm all ears!
Finally! Now this feels like a captain's job.
I'll leave it to the First Mate.
The Fools are always eager to know where we're headed. So a captain must light the way!
The First Mate's opinion does matter, but it's up to the captain to set the course.
For those of us who've left our pasts behind, a guiding star is everything. I don't know what the troupe would do without a captain.
(I see. I'll do my best to live up to that! Then, let us—)
Explore the entirety of Rinascita!
Sail back to Huanglong!
Visit the Black Shores!
Splendid! Brant took us to Septimont once, so we know that route well.
That might be a challenge. We've never gone that far before, but I've heard about Huanglong's famed Hero Plays. Maybe we'll get to see one!
The Black Shores…? I've never heard of that place. What's it like? Can't wait to see it for myself!
Now that I know the plan, I'll go tell the others and get things ready.
No gasps of disbelief?
Just another day in the life of the Troupe of Fools!
Haha! We've braved wuthering waves and stared down every tide! We're seasoned sailors, {PlayerName}!
Captain Brant might be whimsical at times, but when the chips are down, he always pulls everyone through.
Surprises are just part of our life, so we've gotten used to this "improvised" way of sailing.
Speaking of which, we've been busy with convoy assignments lately as pirates have been causing trouble, intercepting trade routes, so we should stay sharp, Captain.
After today's performance, I'll check the sea conditions again.
Tina! Where are you? Rehearsal is starting soon!
I'm coming!
Well, Captain, duty calls! I hope you're finding your footing here. Catch you later!
Hello, {PlayerName}. I heard you're the captain today. Don't forget to wrap up the paperwork!
I thought I was running a ship, not a ledger!
I came for the high seas, not a list of to-dos!
Haha, don't worry. It was a joke. I hope you've been enjoying yourself today.
Leave the paperwork to Brant. Pero will keep an eye on him to make sure it's done by tomorrow.
Brant might not look like your typical captain, but he gets the job done.
He is surprisingly reliable.
He does things in his style.
Hehe, all in a day's work for a captain, right?

On the bridge to the island, you're ambushed by the Dragon of Dirge. You fall off the bridge and land on a beach, surrounded by swarms of Tacet Discord. Roccia, the Fool's Troupe first mate, arrives to help. You find her to be the mysterious person sleeping in her box on the troupe liner.
Roccia tells you that Brant went into the mist alone to rescue survivors. She suggests you wait here for someone from the troupe to pick you up, but you figure that following her might be the faster way to uncover the "truth" Carlotta mentioned. Besides, you can't let a young girl face such danger alone. 
Meanwhile, you wonder if Abby intervened to absorb the Dragon's attack because it detected a compatible frequency. But why did the absorption fail? Fortunately, you can still sense Abby's presence within you.
Following the Golden Phantom, you and Roccia narrowly escape the Dragon of Dirge's ambush in the mist...

Guided by the Golden Phantom, the two of you reach the end of the beach. You realize the Golden Phantom is actually a Reverberation—a blend of frequencies from Roccia's fallen friends. It's here to lead her out of the mist with a game she loves. Once its mission is complete, you and Roccia watch it fade away, and the mist around you thins slightly. Together, you continue forward.

As you journey through the mist, you spot a "Pilgrim's Sail," the ship you saw when you first arrived in the city. Roccia explains that all Pilgrim's Sails eventually end up here, carried by the undercurrents to this island—Penitent's End, a place both destination and grave for every Pilgrim's Sail.
The ship appears abandoned. Its passengers must have ventured deeper into the island. With the mist still thick and danger lingering around, you decide to head toward a nearby lighthouse, hoping to find any scattered survivors along the way.

After battling through swarms of Tacet Discords in the mist, you reunite with Brant, who saved a survivor named Andreas from the Pilgrim's Sail.
Brant and Roccia reveal the grim truth of the pilgrimage: it's a banishment in disguise, and all exiles are marked as "The Fool" by The Order. Brant, Roccia, and their troupe are among those given this title, having been cast out as "The Fools."
Unfortunately, the Order's lies run deep. Andreas tells you in despair that some pilgrims have been misled, believing they will find salvation by reaching the Sacrificial Arena at the island's peak. But that arena is actually the lair of the Dragon of Dirge, a TD that answers not to prayers but devours all frequencies without mercy. 
Determined to save those deceived by The Order and to settle your own score with the Dragon, you all set out for the Sacrificial Arena.

In the Sacrificial Arena, you find a devotee praying for the Sentinel's forgiveness. She is met instead by the Dragon's deadly claws. Fortunately, you manage to save her just in time. Time to make this monster pay.

After a hard-fought battle, you defeat the Dragon of Dirge. Just as you're about to finish it, Abby emerges from within you again. Abby quickly explains that it tried to absorb the Dragon's frequency earlier but something was wrong with its absorption ability—a sign that Abby's condition may be worsening.
Still, Abby says that's not the main issue. During the absorption, it sensed something unusual in the Dragon's frequency. Abby urges you to empathize with the Dragon before its frequency fades.
As you tap into the Dragon of Dirge's memories, a vision unfolds: a man in The Order's uniform places a halo on the Dragon, commanding it to deliver a final judgment to all who approach.

You share your vision with Brant and Roccia. They theorize that the Dragon of Dirge was once a simple Tacet Discord that fed on frequencies. But now it becomes a harbinger of death under The Order's control and attacks anything in its path. During the battle, Brant also found a Lycoris on the ground, suggesting that Fractsidus is again behind this.
Brant explains that his troupe has faced Fractsidus at sea before. After they parted ways with you, they kept tracking Cetus the Tidebreaker and found a Lycoris on its tail as well. You suspect Fractsidus's plans may involve the Carnevale and the Sentinel of Rinascita. Since Brant's troupe is here for the Carnevale, they are determined to confront Fractsidus with you.
Brant also mentions that a member of their troupe once won the Laurel of Carnevale. He might know about the connections between the Carnevale, the Laurel, and the Sentinel. You decide to seek him out for answers.
Then, you head to the troupe's base together for a brief respite.

The troupe's base is, surprisingly, hidden in a cavern beneath Penitent's End. The thick mist provides a natural cover, but it remains a perilous environment. Brant and Roccia tell you how to find Bardolino, the former Laureate, and then set off to handle the lingering impact of the mist. They'll meet you again once their tasks are done.
After talking to the troupe member, you managed to retrieve one of the Cloudcaster's parts.

You finally meet Bardolino, the former Laureate, and learn that the rumors are true: the Laureate has the ability to communicate directly with the Sentinel. 
As Bardolino speaks, he fondly recalls Fleurdelys, the Blessed Maiden, and her reign. He disapproves of Fenrico, and Brant and Roccia join him, using the moment to share the troupe's ideals with those gathered around.

Excited by the conversation, Bardolino suddenly pulls out a bundle of balloons, ties them to himself, and floats up into the air—a recreation, he claims, of his old performance. "Even without wings, we can still soar to the heavens," he passionately quotes. However, he hasn't quite figured out how to land.
Concerned, you start thinking about how to bring him down. Roccia suggests using Cloud Cushions created by a device called the "Cloudcaster." Unfortunately, she admits that some of its parts have been borrowed by other troupe members, so you'll need to retrieve them first.
After talking to the troupe member, you managed to retrieve one of the Cloudcaster's parts.
After talking to the troupe member, you managed to retrieve one of the Cloudcaster's parts.

You assemble the Cloudcaster and generate Cloud Cushions beneath Bardolino. The next task is to pop the balloons and bring him safely down. The Cloudcaster's resonance device responds to songs, so the troupe members sing together to expand the Cloud Cushion.

Bardolino lands safely and bows in thanks. Just then, a piece of rock falls from the cavern ceiling, headed straight for him. Carlotta, who has arrived at some point, steps forward and shatters the rock before it can strike him. 
She approaches you, and you acknowledge each other with a simple nod. The Montelli family's protection extends to all who stand by them.

Carlotta tells you that the Montelli family's trouble is temporarily resolved. She and you then piece together recent events. You realize that The Order intends to recreate the crisis that wrecked the Carnevale ten years ago. 
The Order has maintained its power through communication with the Sentinel, but with the Sentinel's absence for ten years, faith in the Order has waned. Also, Primus Fenrico does not match the description of the "Enlightened One." Desperate to restore public trust, the Order has been "forced" to revive the festival. However, if the Carnevale enables direct communication with the Sentinel, The Order's deceptions will be exposed. 
Their plan seems clear now: by causing chaos through Fractsidus, The Order can then intervene as "saviors" and regain the people's trust without undermining their authority. Although you've foiled some of Fractsidus's schemes, threats still loom. The troupe has discovered that Cetus the Tidebreaker is still under their control, and it's likely that a Fractsidus Overseer will make an appearance at the Carnevale. 
To reach the Sentinel, winning the Laurel—which grants a chance to communicate directly with the Sentinel—may be your best option. 
With a shared goal, Carlotta becomes your ally. Now, you just need to decide how to carry out your plan.

The Order's goal is to disrupt the Carnevale, sowing fear and unrest. But if you confront them directly, you risk fueling the crisis they hope to exploit. 
Carlotta proposes working with the Fool's Troupe to turn any potential disturbance into a staged performance, stripping chaos of its impact.
Brant and Roccia see your hesitation and invite you to join their upcoming rehearsal and get comfortable with the troupe's style. 
Don't forget to bring Carlotta along. If you're ready, take your place on the troupe liner's stage.

Brant and Roccia introduce you to Commedia Improvviso, the troupe's improvisational show. 
Although the performance is largely unscripted, they've prepared a simple outline—a classic story of "a hero's victory over the Demon King," the very tale that Fleurdelys once performed to win the Laurel. 
The world is your stage, they tell you, so relax and express yourself freely. Actions speak louder than words—now, take the stage!

Brant and Roccia praise your performance with Carlotta, expressing confidence that you'll master the art of acting by the time the Carnevale begins. 
But before that, Brant brings up that you still need one final thing to participate in the festival.
Fortunately, Carlotta has it all prepared. Follow her back to Ragunna City.

You even picked up her way of talking.

At midnight, you arrive at Liberty Square, responding to an invitation from Carlotta's uncle, Capollo.
Though the invitation seems genuine, you remain wary of his true intentions. You and Abby suspect he has ulterior motives beyond mere gratitude.

Standing before you is Capollo, Carlotta's uncle, son of the Padrino, and the next head of the Montelli family.
While expressing gratitude for your cooperation, he warns that your deep involvement may destabilize the family's delicate balance and disrupt future plans. Capollo offers to take Carlotta's place as the family's representative in your alliance but makes it clear that, if you decline, you should avoid meddling further in Montelli affairs.
As the tension escalates, Carlotta intervenes, leaving you a cryptic message, "Meet me at the rendezvous. Beware the eyes."
Seeing you off, she brings up the recent betrayal involving Benett, the family's vault manager, who was caught stealing from the vault.

You and Carlotta quickly deduce that the bartender is the contact for Scarlet Velvet. Though he may not understand all of the cryptic messages, nothing of importance escapes him. While the bartender is not optimistic about your meeting with Scarlet Velvet, he doesn't stop you as you followed the rules and found him. It also seems that he has heard of Carlotta's character from Benett. Therefore, he promises to arrange a meeting for you with Scarlet Velvet at Whisperwind Haven at dask.

Realizing that retrieving the Reserved Terminal is impossible, the Acolytes attempt to further sever the relationship between Scarlet Velvet and Montelli before departing.
According to Scarlet Velvet, it is not her group that severed ties but Montelli themselves. The family revoked their rights to purchase Reserved Terminals and weapons, as well as their protection. This revelation surprises Carlotta, as it contradicts Montelli's philosophy of proactive expansion. She asserts her stance to resume trading and assure that Montelli, which once broke the monopoly, will never become a supporter of it.
Regarding Benett, Scarlet Velvet denies the possibility of him stealing from the vault and reveals that Benett foresaw his own death, leaving something behind at the coast, hoping it would never come into handy.

Deciphering the wine code, you and Carlotta piece together the cryptic message Benett sent on the night of his death. The message points to a collection requiring the highest level of authority in the vault. At the same time, you also receive good news from Duncan—he successfully retrieved Benett's Terminal, though it is severely damaged and requires repair. 
A chilling possibility begins to form in Carlotta's mind: all the suspicious details seem to be pointing to Capollo. To uncover the true traitor, you need to return to Montelli headquarters, repair the terminal, and locate the collection indicated by Benett.

Benett's Terminal is severely damaged, so only basic data are restored. The recovered data shows  Benett's movements, and you notice two suspicious coordinates: one points to the Liberty Square that Carlotta previously investigated, and the other is Capollo's private dock.

The collection the message points to turns out to be the family's custom-made Reserved Terminal, and all clues suggest that Capollo was the one who removed the core data module from the Terminal, and Benett was framed for embezzlement.
During communication, Carlotta rejects Capollo's proposal to move past the matter, unable to ignore Benett's death and the hidden threats within the family.
Time is pressing, so Carlotta quickly decides to split up, with you taking Benett's Terminal to an expert named Pierre for a thorough repair, while she heads to Capollo's private dock to find out more clues or retrieve the missing core data module.

Carlotta arrives at the dock as planned. Following a strange energy fluctuation, she finds a stained-glass mirror buried under cargo. At that moment, a hand adorned with a blue-black ornament suddenly reaches out from the mirror, pulling her inside—the coordinates are a trap in disguise.

Standing beside Pierre is the elderly man you once saw admiring the painting—Francesco, the current head of the Montelli family, also known as ""Padrino."" His words are not just about the painting but also about Carlotta. Rather than relying on his own plan, he hopes that Carlotta and her companions can offer their own solution.
Then he entrusts you with a crucial item to be given to her at the right time.
After fully restoring the Terminal, you uncover hidden data—it turns out that Capollo deliberately handed this Terminal to Duncan to lure Carlotta into the trap at the dock.
With Carlotta now missing, you must rush to the location to save her.

You arrive at the rendezvous before Carlotta and notice Montelli members, dressed in the family's attire, quietly departing one by one. Left behind is an elderly man who is appreciating a painting.
When you approach, he reveals himself as an art-loving investor, simply waiting for the rain to stop. 
He explains that now is not the time to cling to the existing balance, but to embrace the unknown and seek change... You feel there is a deeper meaning behind his thoughts on the painting.

When the rain stops, the elderly man quietly leaves the scene. Freed from the watchful eyes, Carlotta successfully meets with you.
She apologizes for Capollo's rudeness and confesses that she has no interest in becoming the family head. Her true concern lies with the traitors lurking within the family. She reveals that Benett, the trusted vault manager, was caught embezzling and subsequently killed by Tacet Discords outside the city. However, on the night of his death, Carlotta received a cryptic message from him.
Once again, Carlotta asks for your help to uncover the truth as you are an outsider that once aided her in capturing the initial traitors. To avoid alarming your targets, she offers you a new identity: Cat's Eye, a provisional member under her patronage.
Believing that Benett's death holds key to unraveling the truth, you decide to investigate his residence.

Outside Benett's residence, Capollo's subordinates, Sage and Acorn, are searching for the stolen items on his order, as Capollo is in charge of the vault.
After some discussion, you and Carlotta decide to split up: she sneaks in through the back, while you confront them for information.

It would be unwise to directly confront the Order, but staying passively behind Capollo and aimlessly searching for the core data module isn't a reasonable choice either.
You and Carlotta decide to force Capollo into handing over the item by giving them an unforgettable response in two days.

You successfully gather information from Sage and Acorn, learning they found nothing in Benett's residence. They express little hope of retrieving the stolen items as Capollo didn't allocate enough resources for investigation and they also believe that Benett had already sold the items off for quite some time.
With the help of a mysterious figure, you disguise yourself as a family member delivering a gift for Capollo and successfully escort Carlotta into the venue.

Trust built on deception will eventually be shattered by reality. You, Carlotta, and Duncan, who decided to help you, change the location and time of the deal without Capollo noticing. Even though both the trading partners and cargo are lost, Capollo refuses to back down. The two Montellis, now on different paths, finally arrive at their confrontation. The key to winning this duel lies in the whereabouts of the core data module.

Sharing this information with Carlotta, you both notice some suspicious aspects: when Carlotta brought up Benett's betrayal, Capollo had remained calm, but the series of recent family troubles seem to be all linked to the vault he directly manages. If he is eager to secure his position as the next family head, he should have put more efforts in resolving these incidents. Besides, Benett was not a man who would be easily swayed by greed...
While discussing these points, you notice an elderly man observing you from a distance. Realizing he is exposed, he immediately flees, and you pursue him.

As the evening rain falls, washing away everything from the past, Carlotta tells you that today's rain brings her peace. She has finally found her true self and feels in control of both her present and future.
When the rain stops, Carlotta bids you farewell. To build a new, true Montelli, she needs to handle the aftermath of Capollo's betrayal. Before parting, she hands you a Cat's Eye brooch, telling you that the codename "Cat's Eye" will forever belong to you, as you are the only member she has ever recommended.

Carlotta identifies the man as Duncan, a former member of the family who had long left. Duncan attributes Benett's death to insatiable lust and ambition. He shares that like Carlotta, he experienced that "stormy night" and believes all those who inherit the Montelli name are doomed to lose everything.
Carlotta respects Duncan's views, but she also sees through his inner conflict—though he wishes to sever ties with the Montelli family, he returned to Ragunna after hearing Benett's death.
You confide in Duncan about your doubts regarding Benett's death and ask him to join your investigation as his friend. After some hesitation, Duncan agrees and provides you information about Scarlet Velvet and her possible connection to Benett as the recipient of the stolen items.

Carlotta explains that Scarlet Velvet and her group not only may be in contact with Benett but had recently severed ties with Montalli, ceasing all transactions with the family.
Growing more suspicious, you decide to contact Scarlet Velvet. Following Ragunna's code, you and Carlotta use alcohol as a signal to find her contact.

The collapsing morph painting constantly devours and absorbs frequencies and energy from its surroundings to sustain itself. Stones, plants, and even animals stripped of their frequencies are left in a silent, frozen state, as if drained of all life and color.

The stolen colors manifest as chaotic color blocks within the painting. Remove the incorrect color blocks to release these trapped colors, restoring the scenery to its original splendor.
The liner continues to glide through the waves. Before long, distant coastlines emerge from the horizon.
You see that?! There's no such thing as divine punishment!
Hah... I see... I'm starting to understand everything...
Did you see that!? There's no such thing as divine punishment. It's all a lie! That sea behemoth from ten years ago? Just a whale!
Yeah... Why didn't we think of that before?
Probably because of the fog that year, and all that strange talk from the Order that had everyone on edge...
So then, the ghosts, the dragon, even the fog... Could they all be something else entirely?
Yeah! What do you say we team up afterward and head out to the sea to investigate? Maybe we'll uncover some incredible secrets. And who knows? We might just become famous!
Oh... Was that all a dream?
I bet it was just some special effects!
Oh... Was that all just a dream? The sky was nothing like it is now...
I think it was just the "special effects" the troupe uses for the show!
Is it...? But the effect felt so... real...
Well, their actors are clearly a bunch of Resonators. And with so many Echoes helping them, it's not impossible to pull off something like that.
Think of it as a dream! And honestly, there's nothing wrong with that. The Carnevale is supposed to be dreamy like that!
Encore! Encore!
Where do these actors come from? They're amazing...
Again! Again! That was a great show!
Where do these actors come from, though? I heard the Montelli family invited them, but I've never seen them at the previous Carnevales!
How many years has it been since we last held the Carnevale? There must've been a lot of people preparing for this during these years, right? It's not unusual to see fresh faces we don't recognize.
Hmm, makes sense.
Oh, this is the kind of photo I'm gonna cherish for life! Gotta send a copy to Rover soon...
Hi Rover! Have you received the photo?
It was me who captured it—the moment of your grand curtain call! I've already sent it to you from my Terminal!
What an incredible show! I could practically feel the heat of it.
By the way, your performance... "Commedia Improvviso," right? What a bold and innovative style of acting...
When I get the chance, I'd love to make a documentary about your troupe... Wait, scratch that—opportunities are what we make of them, right?
I'll be working on the shooting plan soon, and when the time comes, I'd really appreciate your help in reaching out to the troupe.
Carlotta has really found a gem this time, hasn't she? Hehe...
Well, well, if it isn't our Laureate for this year! How did you like the mask?
If you enjoyed it, don't be a stranger. Be sure to visit us more often! Hehe.
We're truly honored that you won the Laurel wearing one of our customized Masks. I must be the first to thank you for that. It's the best kind of publicity we could ask for.
This dream of ours is about to shine even brighter, all thanks to you.
Carlotta has really found a gem this time, hasn't she? Hehe...
This is where the blonde girl stood. Even now, you can sense faint fluctuations in the air. You scan the surroundings, but the mysterious maiden has vanished, leaving no trace behind.
From Carlotta's reaction, it seems that no one but you can perceive her presence.
Who is she? Or what is she? Did she only show up for this year's Carnevale?
The path to answers will certainly be treacherous. But regardless, you possess the will, the determination, and the courage to seek the truth. These qualities will see you through.
Cartethyia... I will have my family find out more about her.
If we find anything, I'll contact you, and we can discuss our next steps together.
Until then, as you suggested…
Ah, I can't be happier than now!
Inspiration! My inspirations are flowing...
It's times like these that make me want to sing!
Hi there! Haha, if it isn't our esteemed Laureate! Finally made it, huh?
It's a celebratory dinner hosted by Ms. Carlotta in our honor. And let me tell you—she's quite generous with her money!
By the way, have you heard? The Order has granted our troupe free passage in and out of the city. It sounds like a good deal... but there's something about it that doesn't sit right with me.
Look, there's an Acolyte over there. He's probably keeping an eye on us... Hah.
But enough of that! Here's to you, my friend! To our new Laureate!
Raise your glasses! Shout it loud, friends!
Gulp... I love this soda...
Drink your fill, everyone!
Remember, you're not alone. If anything happens, just let us know.
Hey, you! Yes, you, the {Male=gentleman;Female=lady} in black clothes! Over here! In the alley!
Yeah, don't look around. I'm talking to you! There's something I'd like to tell you... I'll be waiting for you in this alley.
Hey, you! Yes, you, the {Male=gentleman;Female=lady} in black clothes! Over here! In the alley!
Ah, finally. I can tell at a glance that you are not an ordinary person.
You... You must be a Bloom Bearer from the Black Shores, right?
Who are you? How did you know?
You are a Bloom Bearer, more Bloom Bearer than I.
Mr. Aalto was right. Bloom Bearers attract other Bloom Bearers!
Sorry, I forgot to introduce myself first. My name's Ariosto, and I am the undercover Bloom Bearer sent here to investigate Rinascita's recent issues.
Are you the only one they sent here?
Are there any other Bloom Bearers here?
The Black Shores has also sent other Bloom Bearers to Rinascita, but to keep things under the radar of the Order, we decided to split up.
If you head southeast toward Septimont, you'll likely run into some of our colleagues. Compared to Ragunna, Bloom Bearers enjoy a bit more freedom there—less surveillance and fewer rules to follow.

But... how should I put it? Things aren't quite as smooth in Septimont. Our operations face their own set of challenges, and the Bloom Bearers' work there hasn't been progressing as well as we'd hoped.
As you know, the Black Shores is a neutral organization, so we don't have the right to meddle in their affairs without the consent of the local officials.
Our relationship with Rinascita's city-states is… well, "delicate" is one way to put it. We've been providing warnings about the Lament crisis—Ragunna being the prime example, of course.
By the way... Come closer, gotta keep our voice low for this... Have you run into any... obstructions from the Order during your mission?
Indeed I have.
Obstruction is an understatement...
I see. It happened to me as well. On the surface, Ragunna appears peaceful, but behind the scenes, the Order has been plotting something.
People from the Order was hot on my tail when I was investigating this matter, and even had my Terminal taken from me. Luckily the Montellis extended a helping hand...
It was the same Ms. Carlotta who told me that a member of the Black Shores would be arriving in Ragunna soon. I decided to find {Male=him;Female=her} quickly and share the information I have.
I borrowed this costume and a mask from the Montelli to blend in with the crowd, so I could get back to the city during the Carnevale. Well, at least my hard work finally paid off.
That sounds really rough.
How could they treat us like this!
Us Bloom Bearers, we endure hardship, but the Lament must be stopped at all costs! That's our Bloom Bearer Creed!
You must already have some sense of Ragunna's situation. Now, let me share a wild thought with you...
You saw that Sentinel statue in Ragunna, right? That statue is strikingly different from the appearance of Sentinel Imperator we recorded in the Tethys System.
Now, take a deep breath—because I'm about to say something big. What if, just what if... the people of Ragunna have been believing in a false Sentinel all along?
Wait... Enough talk for today. I can't shake the feeling that we're being watched.
My mission isn't finished. I'll stay in Rinascita and continue digging into their historical records about the Sentinel. My next stop is Whisperwind Haven. If fate allows, we'll meet again.

Flying along the Wind Trail allows you to <color=#ffd12f>automatically</color> follow the wind's direction.
Follow the Wind Rings to stay on course. Pass through them to earn challenge points!

Across Rinascita, you may stumble upon these fragile containers scattered around. Shatter them to uncover hidden treasures within.

Keep a close eye on those bearing the Montelli family crest, as they contain Monnaies—an old currency that can be redeemed for rewards at Averardo Bank.
Smash the floating containers with the Gondola or your attacks and collect the treasures within!

These collapsed morph paintings drain frequencies and energy from their surroundings to maintain their forms, causing the minerals, plants, and even animals nearby to lose their vibrancy and color.
The absorbed colors transform into chaotic color blocks on the Overflowing Palette. <color=#ffd12f>Adjusting all the blocks into a designated color</color> will restore the environment's former vibrancy.
Select a color on the right and apply it to the blocks on the palette to the left. The new color will spread to all connected blocks of the same color.
Different Overflowing Palettes have different move limits. Plan your moves carefully to return the land to its former vibrancy!
The <color=#ffd12f>Resonance Nexus</color> stores information on the surrounding area. Activate it to obtain the corresponding <color=#ffd12f>Map</color> data.

After a <color=#ffd12f>Resonance Beacon</color> is activated, you can open the Map and <color=#ffd12f>fast travel</color> to an activated Resonance Beacon.
Head to a Resonance Nexus or Resonance Beacon to <color=#ffd12f>heal</color> injured or downed Resonators.

<color=#ffd12f>Defeat</color> the nearby <color=#ffd12f>Tacet Discords</color> to ensure the successful activation of the <color=#ffd12f>Sound Emulator</color>. Complete the challenge to receive rewards.

The product of a collapsed Sonoro Sphere, found throughout the world. It records undistorted memories of the past.
Use Grapple to hook and quickly approach the Sonance Caskets in Ragunna. The Plushie Echoes in the Garden of the Lost are collecting them—perhaps a visit will reveal more.
A village of Plushie Echoes in the Garden of the Lost. The villagers are gathering Sonance Caskets throughout Ragunna to unlock the Sonoro Sphere within a morph painting.

While steering a Gondola, you can use Waterfall Surge to swim up a waterfall.
<color=#ffd12f>(Please note that this function can only be used in safe waters. Protect your Gondolas, and protect yourselves.)</color>

A special Gondola that cruises along the most scenic spots in Ragunna City, often called the city sightseeing water bus.
Board the Gondola to relax and enjoy the voyage.
Aim your Grapple at the Wingray. When the visual cue appears, cast Grapple to link yourself to the Wingray. It will carry you upward.

The link will automatically break once you reach the highest point.
The Wingray will return to its starting point after a short time.

You can use <color=#ffd12f>Flight</color> in your Utility after reaching certain heights off the ground.
Flight is a Utility specific to Rinascita regions. Available only while not in combat.

When in Flight, use movement keys (or the control stick) to ascend or dive.
As you dive, you gain momentum for the Echo Wings, allowing you to ascend higher.
Try diving to restore momentum when it depletes.
Once the challenge begins, follow the ground cues to avoid the Vitreum Dancers dashing toward you.

When you reach a Leap Spot, using Utility will activate Echo transformation automatically. {Cus:Ipt,Touch=Tap PC=Press Gamepad=Press} the Utility button to transform into a Cuddle Wuddle and jump.
Aim your camera to the next Leap Spot and {Cus:Ipt,Touch=tap PC=press Gamepad=press} the Utility button to leap again.

When you reach a Climbing Spot, the Utility will automatically become Echo transformation. {Cus:Ipt,Touch=Tap PC=Press Gamepad=Press} the Utility button to transform into a Cuddle Wuddle for the climbing challenge.
Aim your camera toward the next Climbing Spot and {Cus:Ipt,Touch=tap PC=press Gamepad=press} the Utility button to climb again.
Reach the final Climbing Spot to perform the Leap for the Top!
{Cus:Ipt,Touch=Tap PC=Press Gamepad=Press} Utility button to transform into a Cuddle Wuddle and smash the Seamrock. Ready to throw this Plushie Punch!
{Cus:Ipt,Touch=Tap PC=Press Gamepad=Press} the button while the pointer is in the highlighted section to speed up the progress. The rock will break once the progress bar is full.
When the pointer enters the orange zone, activate Powerful Punch mode. Rapidly {Cus:Ipt,Touch=tap PC=press Gamepad=press} the left and right buttons to speed up the smashing.
Press the Utility button to transform into a Cuddle Wuddle and break the Friable Rock with a single punch!

Ordinary Nightmare Clouds can be absorbed into Lottie Lost's picture book, transforming them into beautiful paintings.
Absorb Nightmare Clouds to earn rewards!

Nightmare Clouds of ghostly flames. 

Observe the number of flames and absorb Nightmare Clouds <color=#ffd12f>in the correct order</color>. Absorbing them in the wrong order will reset the challenge.

Nightmare Clouds that keep multiplying.
 
Lottie Lost must use the <color=#ffd12f>Finished Book</color> and <color=#ffd12f>Hold</color> the Enhanced Absorption button to <color=#ffd12f>absorb</color> and eliminate all Nightmare Clouds at once.

Lottie Lost draws power from the stories in the <color=#ffd12f>Finished Book</color>, enhancing her ability to absorb Nightmare Clouds.
 
<color=#ffd12f>Hold the Enhanced Absorption button</color> to absorb all Nightmare Clouds within her radius.
 
The Enhanced Absorption state lasts for a limited time and can be refreshed by reading the Finished Book again.
Lottie Lost can resonate with the Unfinished Book, sensing the trail of its lost pages.

Guide Lottie Lost to collect the lost pages by following the sensed trail as closely as possible.
Once all the pages are collected, the Unfinished Book will be fully restored.
Stand right before the monument base, then use Grapple to pull the misplaced monument back to its base to restore the monument.
Restore all the monuments, and you might uncover something unexpected!

Approach the base and interact with the flickering point to read the <color=#ffd12f>inscription</color>.
Find the painting mentioned in the text and use Levitator to place it on the <color=#ffd12f>matching base.</color>

Dreamscape Nodes gather various dream frequencies, each presenting unique challenges based on the dreams and emotions they contain.

Clear the Dreamscape Tacet Discords and meet all <color=#ffd12f>challenge goals</color> to link the Node to Somnoire. You can interact with the node's core to retry challenges as many times as needed.
Some special Dreamscape Nodes feature <color=#ffd12f>enhanced</color> Nightmare Tacet Discords.

The Dreamscape Nexus serves as a central point for transmitting frequencies and dreams to Somnoire. Protect it from being destroyed within the time limit. Each defeated wave of enemies <color=#ffd12f>reduces the remaining defense time.</color>
Fae Ignis from the Dreamscape doesn't die when its charge is interrupted. However, when defeated, it will always explode and release fireballs at a faster rate.

Cuddle Wuddle enters a prep phase of synergy when its HP drops below 80%. During this time, you can interrupt the synergy by dealing DMG equal to 20% of Cuddle Wuddle's max HP or defeating the other Plushies Echoes.

Once Cuddle Wuddle enters the synergy with other plushies, they will launch Coordinated Attacks. However, if Cuddle Wuddle's <color=#ffd12f>HP drops below 30%</color>, the synergy will end, and Cuddle Wuddle will be paralyzed.
<color=#ffd12f>Counterattacking</color> the Vitreum Dancer's strikes can break its weapon, which makes the Vitreum Dancer enter an Enraged state and become even more powerful.

Questless Knights, Diurnus Knights, and Nocturnus Knights can enhance their weapons, indicated by a glowing effect. Counterattack them three times to remove the enhancement, or they will continue to enhance their weapons repeatedly.
Face the Nightmare Clouds and use Utility to transform into a Lottie Lost. <color=#ffd12f>Hold the button</color> to absorb the Nightmare Clouds with her picture book!
When the Roseshroom charges for shooting a laser, shoot the core at its head to interrupt the charging.
Select a piece to preview its landing point, then select the point to move the piece.
When a black piece lands on the outer circle, it <color=#ffd12f>opens all gates and maze walls in that direction.</color>
You can pause the game at any time, and <color=#ffd12f>all pieces will stay in place.</color>
Press the <color=#ffd12f>Reset button</color> to restart the game.

The game ends when either side's pieces form a straight line.
<color=#ffd12f>If black pieces connect, you win</color>; if white pieces connect, the Lifer wins.
Use <color=#ffd12f>Sensor</color> to locate the Terminals granting buffs to the Lifer.
Submit a <color=#ffd12f>Stake of Imbalance</color> at a Terminal to remove the buffs.
After submitting the Stakes, you can freely <color=#ffd12f>turn The Lifer's buffs on or off</color> through the Terminal.

Each of the three altars is connected to the Discipline Steles around it.
Stand on the altar platform to charge the steles, but <color=#ffd12f>Tacet Discords will appear</color> to disrupt the effort.
<color=#ffd12f>When only the player is within the altar's range</color>, the steles charge most efficiently.
<color=#ffd12f>When there are Tacet Discords within the altar's range</color>, the steles stop charging.
<color=#ffd12f>When the player is out of the alter's range,</color> the steles stop charging, and the energy begins to drain.
In the dark area not illuminated by the Macare Torch, Tacet Discords are enhanced, entering the Shadow state that makes them <color=#ffd12f>immune to all attacks.</color>
The Macabre Torch's light can dispel the Shadow state of Tacet Discords, making them vulnerable again.
There are certain enemies who will try to extinguish the nearby Macabre Torch after taking specific amounts of damage.
Use Levitator to collect the stained glass pieces.

Go through the Tacet Mark protruding from the ground to enter the Tacet Field in another dimension.

After clearing the Tacet Field, you can consume Waveplates to obtain various Echo development materials and collected Echoes of the corresponding Sonata set.
Surveillance cameras are used to scan for suspicious activities. Staying within their view increases Alertness.
Vitreum Dancers patrol the Vault, charging at intruders and dealing DMG on impact.
Scatter Prisms greatly enhance Carlotta's Forte. Shooting them with the "jewelry set" disables the surveillance cameras and Vitreum Dancers within a large area permanently.

Alertness indicates how alert the Vault's security system is to your actions. It increases when you are detected by Vitreum Dancers, spotted by surveillance cameras, or engage in combat. You can lower it by disabling security systems or defeating enemies. If Alertness reaches 100, you will be forced to retreat and restart from the previous area.
Defense Lasers block certain pathways and deal DMG to anyone who touches them.
