A nation of independent city-states scattered across a vast archipelago, with no central administrative center. Legends speak of Rinascita's founders, who fled their homeland and sailed to these islands to escape the Lament. 

As an island nation reborn from the Lament, Rinascita was long isolated from the rest of the world by relentless disasters and vast distances. It wasn't until recent times that the Rinascitans opened new maritime routes. Ships laden with their spices and minerals began to sail across the world, and in turn, new treasures and wealth began flowing back to Rinascita, enriching its shores.

Rinascita is famed for its unique "Common Echo" technology, which allows Echoes to persist in physical form within the radius of the Genesis Nexus. Through this technology, the Rinascitan people have integrated Echoes into every facet of their lives. This is how the nation came to be known as the "Land of Echoes."

Rinascitans place great value on the identity derived from bloodlines, and their society is built upon a deep reverence for family ties. For them, the welfare of the family always takes precedence over individual fate.

Ragunna City, the administrative center of the Ragunna city-state in Rinascita, is a thriving port city by the sea, its districts linked by winding waterways. The Ragunnesi are devout followers of the Sentinel, who believe Common Echoes to be gifts from the Sentinel carrying Their divine will.

In addition to their faith, the people of Ragunna are also known for their love of the arts. The city is adorned with magnificent sculptures and paintings at every turn, and impromptu performances often bring the streets to life. Under the leadership of Fenrico, the current Primus of the Order of the Deep, a series of laws have been enacted to restrict certain themes in artistic expression. These laws have sparked divided opinion among the city's inhabitants.

At present, Ragunna's daily affairs are overseen by the Order of the Deep, while prominent families such as Montelli and Fisalia also hold significant influence over the direction of the city.

The Carnevale is the grandest celebration of Ragunna, where the masquerades never end, wine flows like rivers, and music pulses through the night. During this time, people cast aside the weight of the world and surrender to the wild, unrestrained joy of the festival.

The Carnevale's origins trace back to Sentinel Imperator, who once guided the people of Rinascita. It began as a tribute to Their grace, a celebration where laughter and performance became the purest form of reverence.

At the peak of the Carnevale, the Sentinel is said to manifest and crown the finest performer with the "Laurel." This honor grants the bearer the privilege to commune with the Sentinel and hear Their wisdom.

Yet, a decade ago, the Carnevale was brought to ruin. A monstrous sea beast, rogue Echoes, and Tacet Discords swept through the festival, turning revelry to ruin. Only when Primus Fenrico intervened did the chaos subside. He proclaimed it was Sentinel Imperator's divine retribution for the Ragunnesi's indulgence and forsaking of their faith. Since then, the Carnevale has not been held again.

Those deemed faithless by the Order of the Deep are sent to voyage upon the Pilgrim's Sail, following the ancient path of those who once braved the mist and maelstrom seeking the Sentinel's guidance.

The Order claims that only Imperator can grant absolution to these transgressors. They must endure a grueling pilgrimage, suffering both body and soul until their repentance is complete. At the journey's end, it is said Sentinel Imperator will offer them forgiveness and the promise of new life.

But no one in Ragunna has ever heard of a faithless "pilgrim" returning from this sacred journey. The Order asserts that they reach Imperator's place of dwelling and devote themselves to Their service for eternity. While many still harbor doubts, few dare to openly challenge the Order—none wish to suffer the same tragic fate as those branded Fools.

A common boat-shaped Echo in Ragunna.

Ragunna's intricate network of waterways, coupled with its narrow streets and rugged terrain surrounding the city has made Gondolas the preferred choice for transporting both people and goods. For most Ragunnesi, they offer a peaceful, smooth alternative to the discomfort of navigating crowded streets or bumpy countryside roads.

Beneath their unassuming exterior, Gondolas are highly intelligent and deeply emotional. They communicate through distinct vocal frequencies, expressing their moods or responding to the command of their gondolier. Some, through specialized training, can even climb waterfalls.

The Order of the Deep worships Sentinel Imperator. In Ragunna tradition, the Order's clergy serve as the Sentinel's earthly envoys, entrusted with guiding the people in Their divine word.

The Order is led by the Primus, and the current Primus, Fenrico, has declared himself the "Enlightened One," the Resonator of the Sentinel. After the last Carnevale, he proclaimed to have discovered the way to commune directly with the Sentinel.

Beneath the Primus, the Priests oversee the rites and sacred duties of the Order, while the common clergy, known as Acolytes, spend their days poring over the Codex, spreading the Sentinel's teachings throughout Ragunna.

To uphold divine order, the Order commands three distinct branches:

Order Tribunal: The Order's secular judicial body that handles civil and criminal matters between families and commoners.

Chamber of Discipline: The Order's executive arm that commands the military to enforce the law. The Chamber heavily employs Echoes in combat, and its enforcers are often called "Inquisitors."

Order Penitentiary: The Order's religious court that trials heretics and faithless who question and defy the divine teachings of the Sentinel.

One of the most powerful families in Ragunna, renowned for their pioneering spirit. The Montelli family played an instrumental role in charting trade routes that not only connect Ragunna, but also greater Rinascita to the wider world. As the city opened its doors, the Montellis rose to prominence, amassing great wealth and unmatched influence.

The Montelli family also took the lead in introducing and developing Reserved Terminals across Ragunna. While the Order of the Deep dismissed these Terminals as an inferior mockery of the Genesis Nexus and Common Echoes, the Montellis secured the Order's approval to continue their development in secrecy, offering guarantees of safety and hefty tax payment in exchange.

Unlike the more traditional families, the Montelli family values emotional bonds and shared ideals above bloodlines and social standing. They advocate for the distribution of opportunities and wealth, believing that riches are worth more when they circulate. Though often ridiculed by traditional families as "nouveau riche with Shell Credits running through their veins," the Montellis take no offense—on the contrary, they wear the label with pride.

One of the most powerful, and certainly the oldest and most traditional, families in Ragunna, renowned for their expertise in medicine and poison. Their devotion to Sentinel Imperator is clear to all who know them.

A faction within the Fisalia family believes that the Montelli family's embrace of openness and the privatization of Echoes is a direct affront to Imperator's teachings, threatening to lead Ragunna into an abyss of heresy. They have directly opposed the Montellis through various means, shaking the family's longstanding image of dignified respectability. Yet, the head of the Fisalia family residing in Porto-Veno Castle seems disturbingly indifferent to the repercussions of these bold and provocative actions.

The Sentinel of Rinascita. In the faith of the Order of the Deep, They are often depicted as a being with the upper body of a horse and the lower body of a fish.

According to Ragunna's legends, Imperator guided its settlers to this promised land, offering them sanctuary from the threat of the Lament.

Though Imperator rarely reveals Their presence to the world, They maintain a connection with the people of Ragunna through the Laureate of the Carnevale, delivering divine guidance in the form of oracles.

In Rinascita, most Echoes can exist independently from Reserved Terminals within the radius of the Genesis Nexus. They are known as Common Echoes.

In Ragunna, the Order of the Deep governs the allocation and use of these Echoes. The people of Ragunna revere them as divine gifts, even as envoys of Sentinel Imperator. They treat them as friends and trusted allies, incorporating them into every aspect of daily life. This deep, symbiotic bond with Common Echoes is what has earned Rinascita its name as the "Land of Echoes."

Rinascita's central Resonance Nexus, also known as the Genesis Nexus. According to legend, Imperator revealed the secrets of the Genesis Nexus to the Rinascitans, enabling them to construct other such towering monuments that stand as symbols of the Sentinel's power and sovereignty.

Within the reach of the Genesis Nexus, Echoes can endure in physical form without relying on Terminals.

The Dark Tide is a Waveworn Phenomenon native to Rinascita. It manifests as a dark, swirling mass of clouds that gathers and eventually breaks, pouring down in torrents like a waterfall. Wherever the Dark Tide strikes, it spawns Tacet Discords, and the area around its point of origin becomes a new Tacet Field.

There have been two significant Dark Tides in Ragunna's history. The first, according to the Order of the Deep, was stopped by Napoli II, the first Primus of the Order. The second was quelled by the martyrdom of the Blessed Maiden Fleurdelys.

The Nimbus Sanctum is the only Sonoro Sphere that exists in the physical world, where mist and clouds are formed by concentrated Remnant Energy.

The sea of clouds that envelop the Sanctum is believed to be the lingering aftermath of the first Dark Tide. As the mist rose, it gradually submerged the former headquarters of the Order of the Deep, the Seminary of the Forgotten, forcing them to relocate to the Cathedral of Mercury in Ragunna City.

Local legends of Ragunna speak of a serene, mirror-like area at the heart of Nimbus Sanctum, said to purify the darkest of thoughts and transform them into part of the clouds. Many pilgrims, drawn by this tale, journey here in search of inner peace.

The Remnant Creature dwelling within Nimbus Sanctum. Legend holds that it was Lorelei's power that restrained the violent sea of clouds, sparing Ragunna from flooding.

Lorelei has the ability to cleanse the dark frequencies within the clouds, but she is not immune to their corrosive influence. As they accumulate to a breaking point, Lorelei will eventually become the Queen of the Night, unleashing her wrath upon all life that comes near.

A vault built by the Montelli family on the outskirts of the city. Within its walls lies the family's vast collection of treasures. The vault also provides public services such as secure storage for valuables, appraisals, and acquisition of rare collections.

The Fools who survived the dragon's assault—whom the Order refers to as the "pilgrims"—drifted on the warm currents, eventually finding refuge in a vast cavern on Penitent's End.

There, the Fools formed a troupe, determined to one day expose the truth hidden by the Order and return to their home. To achieve this, the troupe wrote numerous plays and "danced in chains," performing tirelessly across the archipelago.

For years, they have awaited the return of the Carnevale, hoping to expose the Order's secrets through their performance, claim the Laurel, and earn the chance to commune with the Sentinel.

Shorekeeper and Aalto

You receive a message from Shorekeeper about a possible solution to Abby's weakening frequency. Before going into more detail, Shorekeeper insists that you first visit the Black Shores to review a past record stored within the Tethys System...
The giant Plushie wraps you in a bear hug. A peculiar yet friendly energy washes over you.

A mysterious chest on the liner catches your eye. Brant explains that it is the personal haven of the liner's first mate, who seems timid around strangers. Yet, despite her shyness, she gathers the courage to offer you a rare antique coin as a gesture of goodwill.

You finally arrive at the docks of Ragunna. The troupe bids you farewell, promising to make their grand entrance during the opening of the Carnevale.
As you and Abby search for a way into the city, you witness deacons from the Order sending "the Fools" on a pilgrimage. A mysterious playwright named Cristoforo notices your confusion and begins to explain the origins of this practice.

You successfully fought your way through the mist, but Ragunna is still some distance away. Now is the time to get to know the troupe members who offer a glimpse into the vibrant culture that awaits in Ragunna.

In Tethys' data space, you see a projection of your past self who recounts your prior actions and motives. The past you reveals that {Male=he;Female=she} left this projection as a beacon to guide {Male=his;Female=her} future self— namely you.
If you have already resolved the Black Shores data issue and awakened Abby, go find "Imperator," whom "You" made a pact with long ago.

Shorekeeper explains that "Imperator" is the name of the Sentinel of Rinascita, who might hold the solution to Abby's weakening frequency.
Rinascita, known as the Land of Echoes, is famed for its advanced Echo technologies and is home to many Echoes like Abby. This region may also hold vital clues as to Abby's origins.
Shorekeeper gives you an invitation letter from the Montelli family, which allows you to enter Rinascita through the port city of Ragunna.
Even as the Threnodian's revival spreads chaos across other regions, Rinascita remains strangely unaffected and is gearing up to celebrate the Carnevale grand festival. This unusual calm belies what could be a rough journey.

Aalto has prepared your ship on the Black Shores. Before you set sail, he advises you to be mindful of Ragunna's customs—its people worship their Sentinel as a god.
When you are ready, you may embark on your voyage to Ragunna.

Your smooth sailing meets a sudden disruption as you come under attack from Cetus the Tidebreaker. Just when things seemed most dire, Brant, the leader of a traveling troupe, comes to your rescue and brings you aboard his liner.

Brant tells you he and his troupe will take part in the upcoming Carnevale, where the Sentinel Imperator will make a rare appearance to crown the festival's finest performer with the Laurel, an honor that grants the Laureate the privilege of hearing the Sentinel's voice.

As you converse, a Waveworn Phenomenon rises as a mist over Rinascita's seas. Hidden within are many TDs, ready to attack any passing ship. To survive this mist, you fight alongside the troupe.
You greet the behemoth Echo carrying the liner, even though you are uncertain if it understands your language...

Phoebe recounts the legend of Rinascita, which explains why people view Sentinel Imperator as a divine figure.
 
When asked how to communicate directly with the Sentinel, Phoebe mentions that the Primus of the Order, Fenrico the Enlightened One, is the only non-Laureate to have ever talked with the Sentinel. However, he, like the Sentinel, only appears during the Carnevale.
 
With some time before the festival, you decide to enjoy your stay in Ragunna for now.

Following the instructions on your invitation, you head to the Averardo Bank to collect the funds prepared by the Montelli family.

Zani, a bank employee, has been expecting you. Acting on the Montelli family's orders, Zani serves as both your guide and bodyguard during your time in Ragunna.

After some brief introductions, Zani suggests it‘s time to try some local delicacies. After all the twists and turns on the way, it's high time to reward your stomach.

You’re taken to Trattoria Margherita, the most popular restaurant in Ragunna.
Zani tells you to order whatever you like, as the Montelli family’s covering the bill.

As you are enjoying the meal, the cheers from nearby catch your attention. 
According to Zani, it is a rehearsal for the Echo Dance performance prepared by the Montelli family…

During the Carnevale rehearsal, one of the Vitreum Dancers suddenly loses control and charges into the crowd. Amid the chaos, your mind connects with the Dancer's and you hear the voice of the Sentinel. They ask for your help in bringing the Lost back to the earthly realm.

After pondering these words, you suspect that Imperator, like the Sentinel of Jinzhou, might be in a vulnerable state, relying on Echoes to communicate. But all your questions could only be answered by that Vitreum Dancer.

You ask Zani about the Dancer and the rehearsal. She explains that it's not a Common Echo, but a private one owned by the Montellis. They're pushing the use of Reserved Terminals, and this Carnevale is their opportunity to promote them. The incident with the dancer could cause a major setback for them.

The Vitreum Dancer you connected with has already escaped. Zani suggests finding a Resonator from the Pioneer Association if you want to track it down. But if you'd like to investigate the scene first, she's happy to help.

Fulmine from the Pioneer Association has a unique skill: he can turn his memories into special film reels, and assisted by the Echo, C-MOSS, he can project those memories for others to see.

In one of Fulmine's memories, you see someone dressed in Montelli attire, wearing a mask and lurking suspiciously behind the Vitreum Dancer. Since the Carnevale hasn't started yet, it's odd for someone to already be masked up—as if they're deliberately hiding their identity.

With this clue, you decide to head to Masked Reverie, a mask shop, in search of leads…

At Masked Reverie, you pose as a customer interested in bespoke designs, hoping to gather information about the mask you saw earlier. The shop owner, Nyarla, quickly sees through the ruse. Just as you consider revealing your true motive, a noblewoman steps in to assist you.

You learn that the mask in question was commissioned by a member of the Fisalia family—a man named Gilberto. Rumor has it that the Fisalia Family has been at odds with the Montellis family over issues related to Reserved Terminals.

Since the Fisalia estate is near the Cathedral of Mercury, you decide to pay them a visit and stop by the cathedral to gather further insights from the Order.
As you reach the upper level of the Cathedral of Mercury, you spot Gilberto just ahead, slipping inside…

At the Cathedral of Mercury, you're welcomed by Priest Alessio. He denies any connection to Gilberto and instead tells you about the events of the last Carnevale ten years ago: the city was shrouded in thick sea fog, the Vitreum Dancers acted like ghosts, a dragon's roar echoed through the sky, and giant sea monster stirred the waves.

The Order believes it was "divine judgment" on the Carnevale—a warning against people's selfish indulgence. It's clear they don't want you getting involved in the Montellis' recent Vitreum Dancer incident.

Just as you're left uncertain about your next move, news arrives that the Montelli family is making a move. Alessio steps out, leaving you alone in the cathedral…

Since Alessio has granted you the freedom to explore the Cathedral, you decide to take full advantage of this rare opportunity.

With Zani by your side, you begin investigating the cathedral, searching for leads...

Zani's clues lead you to the cathedral gardens where there is a room that resembles a confessional. To gather more clues, you enter the room.

Meanwhile, Phrolova, the mysterious Overseer of the Fractsidus quietly watches and waits for you to uncover "the path to ascension."

At the dock, you plan to ride the Echo boat "Gondola" into the city.
Maybe you'll see a whole flock of Echoes like Abby along the way!
Within the Cathedral of Mercury, you see Gilberto secretly discussing something with Alessio, a Priest from the Order…

Before entering the city, you go through The Order's customs checkpoint. It seems they have additional regulations for Reserved Terminals. Fortunately, the Montelli family has already arranged a guarantor for you.

During the inspection, the Order members' elusive words confuse you, until Acolyte Phoebe arrives to clear up your questions.

With her guidance, you finally step into the city of Echoes.

The scene before Carlotta mirrors memories from eleven years ago, but the events veer in an unexpected direction. The family members who once rejected her as Padrino's adopted granddaughter and opposed her taking the Montelli name now welcome her with open arms. Acknowledged, praised, and elevated—everything she ever craved is within reach if she chooses to stay.
Yet, Carlotta fires a shot at the mirror. The bullet shatters her mirror self, creating a new passage, leading to a different place.
Rivers eventually converge into the same ocean. If a goal is mutual, then it is only a matter of time before they meet.
Our very choices and our will have led us to this situation. Not the wishes of fate.
You are quite different from what the rumors say.
Oh. And what rumors have you heard?
That you're a recluse, a mystic, obsessed with the crafting of poison, oh... and that you poisoned your predecessor. Those kinds of rumors.
A recluse? On the contrary, I've been searching for a solution to the Sentinel's plight and rarely return to Rinascita.
After most of my leads fell short, a friend at Mingting in Huanglong introduced me to the stories they were telling of you.
A friend?
All the affairs of Huanglong's states eventually land in one person's hands. Would you care to take a guess at the identity of this friend of mine?
...Why not put the other rumors to rest?
Because the rest of them are all true.
(Chuckle)... I see it'll take more than that to rattle you, hmm?
I assure you, this is no jest.
We Fisalias have lived under the Threnodian's whispers for generations. Once the soul fractures, the mind will follow until only a puppet remains.
When the soul of the ruling head falters, Fisalia tradition dictates that the successor... usher them into eternal slumber, with a poison of their own making.
My succession ritual… well, an unforeseen incident gave rise to whispers that sparked those rumors.
...How long has this been going on?
For centuries... every generation.

Any recommendations? Isn't the drink you ordered enough for now?
More wine, more secrets.
I'm a fan of good alcohol. Bring me more!
Well, I was just asking...
Ha, well, whether you're indulging in your desires or giving in to them, I'm here for both.

We've got a menu on the table for newcomers. Maybe you'll find something that catches your eye, or you'd prefer to find someone who shares your taste for a <color=yellow>Scarlet Velvet Ribbon</color> first. What do you think?
I still remember the last time I saw him. It was raining, heavily. He gave me his only umbrella with that bright, reassuring smile, told me he was fine, then walked straight into the downpour...
Had he already started stealing the goods and secretly selling them for money then?
Was it really worth it? To betray the family... for money? Was it so tempting that he could abandon the vows he swore and the values he held?
What if... what if there's more to it, though? After all, no one's found the stolen goods yet. Maybe he never sold them...
Don't fool yourself, Adriana. This is the result of a full investigation by Mr. Capollo and the higher-ups at the vault. It's as certain as it gets.
Think about all the other traitors we've caught from the vault. Those tuners. Who'd thought they were hiding their true selves until it was too late?
Does it even matter why he betrayed us?
Something tells me the next head might be someone else.
Ha, well, if you're so sure, how about you tell me if we can get that special Margherita pie? I hear they're only making thirty of them today.
Hey, you should trust my intuition! It's saved me from the reaper more times than I can count!

But seriously, not long ago they caught another traitor from the vault, and then Benett's betrayal hit... It's no surprise people are starting to question Mr. Capollo's ability to lead. And I heard he hasn't been looking too well lately...
Meanwhile, Lady Carlotta's reputation has been growing. She's helped a lot of people in the family with her actions and words.
True, but you're missing the most important point—the will of Lady Carlotta herself.

You know she's never wanted to put her relationship with Mr. Capollo or Padrino at risk. As an adopted member of the family, she's always felt she doesn't deserve a position like that. But, of course, opinions differ on why she's reluctant to take the role.
But one thing's clear—Lady Carlotta has no interest in becoming the next head. If she did, the family‘s balance would’ve been disrupted a long time ago.
So, for now, just save that intuition of yours for the pie, alright?
If only I were Lady Carlotta! I'd love to have the power to create gems whenever I wanted!
They're so dazzling and mesmerizing. If I were her... actually, just giving me the chance to pick them up would be enough, hehe.
But... don't you know those aren't real gems?
Wait, really? They're not?
Nope. Someone who thought they could make a fortune from those "gems" tried, only to find out that they couldn't even sell them, let alone use them for anything useful.
Those "gems" are actually a medium for deconstruction and reconstruction. They're capable of collapsing and disintegrating the target's frequency they hit before the target vanishes completely.
So they just look like gems. When needed, they can transform into the shape of firearms or bullets.
W-well... what happened to those who actually got their hands on them?
Hard to say. Maybe they ended up as sparkling fragments... Haha.
Benett... where could I dig up more of your secrets?
Oh, it's you. What happened? Need my help?
About that rainy night...
About you and Benett...
What's your plan?
That's it for now.
Ask about something else.
Everyone's got things they'd rather not share. For me, it's that rainy night. Not now, not with you. All I'll say is that the night was bitter cold, and the rain—merciless.
Rain like that reeks of rust. It poured down in torrents, smothering cries for help. Convictions we thought unshakable blurred like ink on waterlogged parchment.
Ask about something else.
Ha, it's just a cheesy story.
Benett and I—we were partners. Missions, mischief, even a dog we shared. We knew each other's families. It's the kind of story you hear about anyone who's faced life and death together.
If our roles were reversed, he'd have done the same for me without a second thought.
I'm old, but I've still got a few strings to pull.
Whether it's a casual contact from years ago or the family's next head, I've got to try my luck.
Ask about something else.
Whether you want to look around or head to that shelter, the choice is yours.
But why... why would Bennett betray us?
Maybe, because he was in charge of the vault. Another soul lost to the greed for money...
If Padrino steps down, do you think Mr. Capollo will be our next head? What's your take?
Well, I thought that was already settled, isn't it? Why bring it up now?
But… this is the Order we're dealing with, and it's strictly forbidden by Padrino.
Exactly, which is why we just need to ensure Padrino doesn't find out. Once the deal's done, it'll all be behind us.
Besides, Capollo is Padrino's own son. Following his lead is bound to benefit us in the long run.
I know, but still…
What's the use of worrying now? Everyone involved knew the risks going in.
Why you suddenly want to change your codename? Did you get yourself into trouble?
Trouble? In our line of work, trouble is part of the package. Look at this mess…
*curses* Why is this city such a nightmare? Problems everywhere! Seriously, who cares about the Order or Fisalia?
Anyway, I'm not retiring yet, but I'm burned out. A new codename and a new environment might give me a fresh perspective and keep my passion for my career.
Ah, I see. Sounds like someone's having a midlife crisis. By the way, if you're changing your codename, I'll change mine too. Let's make it a team effort.
What?! I'm not having a midlife crisis!
Sure, sure. Oh, and I hear Septimont is short on people. Maybe we could...
Coming up with new codenames is tough. I'll leave that part to you.
The Montelli memeber before you is deeply immersed in his work of safeguarding, observing every movement around him. He impatiently waves at you, signaling that he has no time to deal with you.
You decide to check other areas of the trading venue.
The Montelli member before you stares blankly at the entrace. A flicker of hesitation and conflict flashes across his eyes, and his finger unconsciously tap lightly.
It's clear that this Montelli member, caught in his own emotional turmoil, won't give you any further response. You decide to check other areas of the trading venue.
Stop messing around.
The deal hasn't started yet. Get back to your post.
Do you think someone will find out what we're doing?
That's the sixth time you've asked in three minutes. Just breathe and calm down. No one's going to find out.
It's almost time, but why did the Order suddenly change the location and schedule?
This isn't just any ordinary deal. The Order is notoriously cautious, always looking over their shoulder. They were probably worried about a leak.
Once this is over, I'm getting myself a new codename.
A new codename? Why? I thought the one you have now suits you.
Hey, {PlayerName}. Good to see you again.
It's been a while.
You're looking cheerful today.
Well, I owe that to you and Carlotta. Thanks to your efforts, we've been able to restart our cooperation with the Montelli family, along with others whose ties had been severed.
The Reserved Terminal is still a sensitive subject in public, but at least now, people here are free to explore in the wild and gather Echoes as they please.

Honestly, I was shocked when Carlotta asked if I'd be interested in joining your plan. I never imagined you'd outmaneuver the Order and strike a deal with Capollo, forcing him to hand over the core data module.
But in hindsight, trusting you, Carlotta... and Benett's judgment turned out to be the right decision.
Capollo's been removed and dealt with by the family. Carlotta's busy managing the aftermath alongside Padrino while also focusing on charting a new sea route.
A new sea route? Where to?
Looks like Montelli's ambitions are growing.
The exact route hasn't been finalized yet, but it's rumored to span three or four countries.

Carlotta told me it was your brilliance that made this possible. Your performance at the Carnevale was so inspiring that more and more people are rallying behind Montelli, eager to explore a bigger, grander world.
We're still figuring out what ventures to take on and what we truly want to achieve. This time, I'm determined to make the right call too.
{PlayerName}, just sit tight—we'll bring you some good news soon!
Oh no, look at the time... Sorry, but I've gotta head home for dinner.
Seriously? Come on, don't be a buzzkill. Your mom's not gonna lose it if you eat out just once.

Maybe not, but she made it clear: no matter what I'm up to, I have to be home for dinner every weekend. If I don't, she'll "break my legs with a spatula and stuff my head into a bowl of spaghetti." Her words, not mine.
By the Sentinel, Gustavo, a Montelli, scared of his mommy! How interesting!
Hey, watch it! I'm not scared of her—I'm respecting her. Family comes first, always. No matter what.
Returning here once again, you finally understand the deeper meaning that Francesco had not directly stated that day.
"They say in art, we glimpse pieces of our own soul... True artistry lies not only in what is painted, but in what is left unsaid."
Glory in Decay is the name of the painting, as well as the motto this elder man has gifted to himself—he feels honored by his own exit.
Passing by Benett's former residence, you discover a bouquet quietly placed at the door.
Looking at the bouquet, with the signature "DC," you almost instantly realize who is mourning Benett—Duncan, the man who had chosen to leave, yet still returns for his dear friend.

He helped deliver the false message about the schedule and location change to the Order and helped you successfully infiltrate the trading venue... In your and Carlotta's plan, he was an important piece.
Now, for his own safety, he must temporarily leave under Carlotta's arrangement.
But no matter when, no matter in what indentity, as long as he chooses to return, Ragunna and Montelli will always welcome him with open arms.
"The rain poured relentlessly, cloaking the world in a shroud of gloom, stripping away its pretense of grandeur to reveal its barren core."

"Under the storm's shadow, people were fighting at each other's throats—fragile yet ferocious, like... like beasts cornered in a cage." No, no, Tornatore, that's far too trite! Think, man! You can craft something better!
You're the playwright of this drama. Give it an ending that lingers, and echo that won't fade!
"As she fell, her trembling hand raised the gun. The old acquiantance, a traitor to his ideals, stared down the barrel. One last shot. Addio." Hmm, does that come across too... passive?

Ah, I see. Rumors, ripe and waiting, a wellspring of inspiration at my fingertips. Let's see... "Can I really trust {Male=him;Female=her}? She wondered. Yet instinct urged her forwar. She clasped {Male=his;Female=her} hand firmly, then turned her back, offering it wholly to her new companion." Yes, yes, that has promise!
The creator in front of you is completely consumed by the tale of storm and betrayal he's spinning. Perhaps it's best to let him remain in his trance.

Enhanced Buff: The Shockwave causes an Explosion shortly after, dealing Havoc DMG equal to 600% of the Resonator's ATK.
Ultimate Buff: Defeating a target with Shockwave or Explosion recovers 20 Concerto Energy for the Resonator.

Justice to be Served
Default Buff: All team members' Basic Attack DMG is increased by 60% and they cannot be downed during the challenge.
Primary Buff: Performing 2 Coordinated Attacks or 5 Basic Attacks grants a stack of Electric Spark. Stacks from each type and each Resonator are counted separately. When either reaches 2 stacks, attacks will consume all stacks to summon 2 Lightning Bolts that strike the target, dealing Electro DMG equal to 200% of the Resonator's ATK.
Enhanced Buff: Lightning Bolts deal an additional Electro DMG equal to 300% of the Resonator's ATK within 3s of hitting the target.
Ultimate Buff: Lightning Bolts trigger a Magnetic Storm, dealing Eletro DMG equal to 400% of the Resonator's ATK.

Crash and Burn

Primary Buff: Performing Mid-air Attack summons a Meteorite, dealing Fusion DMG equal to 300% of the Resonator's ATK. This effect can be triggered once every 3s.
Enhanced Buff: All team members' Crit. DMG is increased by 10% every second while in mid-air, stacking up to 10 times.
Ultimate Buff: The Meteorite explodes on hit, dealing Fusion DMG equal to 200% of the Resonator's ATK and creating a flaming zone that deals Fusion DMG equal to 380% of the Resonator's ATK.

Smash 'Em All

Enhanced Buff: Dealing Heavy Attack DMG 5 times generates an Iceblast (triggered once every 0.1s), dealing Glacio DMG equal to 400% of the Resonator's ATK.

Right of Self-Defense

Play It Safe

With the crisis behind you, you and your companions spend the day basking in cheers and applause.
Later, back at the Palazzo Agrotta, you drift off to sleep, replaying the day's memories from the Carnevale.
I've prepared a shipping plan based on the client's needs.
Can you double-check it? This piece might need special handling, given its dimensions.
A fossilized whale skeleton? You must be kidding...
Looks like we'll need a few extra Gondolas for this one.
Allow me to introduce our latest "Worry-Free Plan."
The best offer you can get at this price! Perfect for families.
Hmm... It does look promising.
Mommy, can I keep my teddy bear in the safe?
Ah, if it isn't the esteemed guest of the Fisalia family.
What, am I not welcome here? Or are you challenging me to a duel?
Haha, you're still as humorous as ever. Averardo Vault welcomes guests from all over the world!
Whatever our differences, as long as you're here...
You are our most honored guest.
Have they delivered the dancer that needs maintenance?
Yep, just arrived.
Great. Make sure they fill out the form.
No problem. Wait... the form... Where did I put it?
Welcome back, honored guest of the Montelli family. It is my pleasure to see you again at Averardo Vault.
Thank you for everything you've done for the Montellis and the Vault.
How may I help you today?
What kind of services do you offer here?
Well, as you can see, the Vault houses a special collection of rare items collected by the Montelli family.
From tangible relics like fine art, precious metals, and advanced technologies, to more elusive assets—Reserved Echoes, Remnants, and even abstract concepts. If it holds value, we store it.
You are welcome to store your valuables in our safes—for a small fee, of course.
Rest assured, the security we provide is well worth every coin.
Alternatively, if you wish to part with any of your items or Echoes, we can assess their value. Should they be deemed worthy, we will make you an offer based on their worth.
By the way, we're currently refining our auction process to align with best practices from other regions.
As such, the auctions will be on hold for the time being.
Sounds... good.
Many thanks.
I'll take a look around.
It's my pleasure. Should you require anything else, do not hesitate to ask.
Greetings. How may I assist you today?
I'm here for the auction.
I'm afraid the auction is temporarily on hold while we refine our procedures.
If there's a particular item you're interested in, feel free to register your preferences on the Terminal. We'll notify you as soon as the auctions resume.
That's a shame. I came prepared with quite a few credits.
You might be losing out on some considerable profits.
We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience.
Yes, but it's a small price to pay to improve the experience for our clients in the future.
Thank you for your continued support of the Ducat Auction. We look forward to your next visit.
Hello, {Male=sir;Female=ma'am}. This area leads to the private offices.
Only authorized Vault personnel are allowed.
I'm Miss Carlotta's guest.
I'm Ms. Zani's friend.
I'm afraid Mr. Capollo has recently strengthened security here at the Vault. Unless I get direct word from Miss Carlotta, I cannot grant you access.
Allow me to confirm your authorization. One moment, please.
Apologies, but Ms. Zani isn't an employee of the Vault. She doesn't have clearance for this section.
(Guess I'll try my luck somewhere else.)
Hello, {PlayerName}.
Heading to the offices? This way, please.
Hello there! Are you looking to sell any collectibles?
What kind of items do you collect?
Oh, all kinds. Literature from before the Lament, old currency, electronics, contemporary art, and precious metals.
Averardo Vault values anything of significance—anything that speaks to Ragunna's past or whispers of its future.
Of course, value is subjective. Different eyes see different worth.
So we evaluate each collectible to determine its value.
Sounds pretty rigorous.
Ha, you needn't worry. A few years back, we paid quite a sum for a sealed metal canister.
What was inside?
Nothing. We believe it's a pet food can manufactured before the Lament, but due to a production error, it was never filled with anything.
I understand your confusion. But that's precisely why we set such a high price. It's one of the last known artifacts from before the Lament.
As I said, we consider value from every angle, often going contrary to popular belief.
To us, these items are unquestionably priceless.
Enough small talk. Do you have anything you'd like us to evaluate? Artifacts? Maybe a Reserved Echo?
What about Abby?
I've got a backpack full of things I don't need.
Nothing at the moment.
...Do you mean the Echo with human-level intelligence and communication skills?
Honestly, we've never encountered something quite like that in the Vault!
If you're willing to part with it... We'll be sure to come up with an offer you'll like!
You tell Ludvika you're just kidding and decline her offer. She looks a little disappointed.
Yes... these are rare items indeed.
But if I'm being honest, they likely hold far more personal meaning to you than they ever could to us.
We'd hate to take something so dear from you. Perhaps you'll reconsider?
Memories of these collectibles flash through your mind. You decide to keep them as mementos of your journey.
I understand. Shell Credits aren't the most important things in this world.
If you ever change your mind, don't hesitate to stop by anytime.
Today's loss... Hmm, twenty-three crates. Cause: Discovered they were past their recommended usage date during inventory.
Oh! Sorry, I didn't see you there. Anything I can help you with?
Crates? Are they used for transporting collectibles?
Yes. We have specially designed crates for transportation.
They're filled with thick padding tailored to the size and shape of the item, keeping everything snug and secure.
This minimizes the risk of damage during shipping.
We regularly discard crates once they reach their recommended life span, just to be safe. Wouldn't want them to fall apart in transit!
Fall apart? Has it ever happened before?
Well, I'm new here. I haven't seen anything like that firsthand, but from what I've heard… it's happened before.
I didn't think much about the whole "discarding crates" thing until Ludvika mentioned all the past accidents—
Everything from minor mishaps like drops to fires, robberies, and even Tacet Discord incursions.
The Vault has learned from these incidents over the years, and our procedures have become much more stringent as a result.
I suppose I'm standing on the shoulders of those who came before me... but hey, better safe than sorry, right?
Hello, my dear friend. Are you here for business too?
Yeah.
Just having a look around.
You're not from Rinascita, right? Where are you from?
Huanglong.
The Black Shores.
The lands beyond the sea.
Ah, such bravery to cross those vast seas, facing the storms and the lurking Tacet Discords...
Haha, reminds me of the Montelli family's motto. I'm not one of them, but as a Ragunna native, I respect their courage.
They sailed far and wide bringing back Terminals, Shell Credits, and mountains of wealth to Rinascita.
The Order wasn't too happy about it, and I doubt the Primus would want people lured by wealth, straying from the path of the Sentinel.
What do you think about it?
Me? I'm not leaving Rinascita. Wealth or legends, none of that matters to me.
Even if I wanted to "fall from grace," there's very little chance of that happening. So I don't think about it much.
As a humble merchant with no great lineage, I'm content with what I have.
Hello, {PlayerName}.
Do you know me?
Ah, yes. I know a few people here in the Vault. I've heard about your generous assistance to both the Vault and the Montelli family.
Speaking of which, have you ever heard about the Vault's secret tales?
Tales?
Yes, stories I picked up from the Vault staff. But don't go spreading it around that I told you.
Of course.
One of the stories is about a mysterious room in the Vault. My friend says it's an area the cameras can't capture.
They say it's like a formless monster, wandering the Vault as though it has a mind of its own.
Every year, some Vault employees disappear in there. The fortunate ones return... but they're never the same afterward.
(Sounds oddly familiar...)
And there's another tale! About the Vault's "hidden treasures."
Don't ask me what it is. I have no idea. A place? An Echo? A collectible? Or maybe... a treasure map?
According to the story, it's been here since the Vault was built. It holds great importance to the Montelli family.
I've never heard of that.
Haha, just rumors. But a Vault with so many treasures and no secrets would be strange, wouldn't it?
...Record the data carefully, Dimitri. I'm going to restart the <ano=Echo tuner>tuning console</ano>.
Right, I need to check for anomalies in the return signals from the third, fifth, and eleventh groups... I've got this.
What's going on here?
Hey, {PlayerName}. As you can see, those damn traitors have messed with our tuning console.
It still boils my blood thinking about it. Turning on the Montellis is one thing, but...
Mind your words, Dimitri!
Ahem, that's not what I meant, Alfred. Betrayal is, of course, unforgivable.
I mean, the tuning console is delicate machinery. I can't bear to leave it on for more than six hours at a stretch.
But those fools... they left it running all day! Tuning bizarre frequencies, no less!
Sorry, {PlayerName}. I got a little carried away.
Anyway, we're adjusting the console now to make sure those traitors didn't cause any permanent damage.
Uh, don't listen to him, {PlayerName}. The console isn't that fragile.
Our main task is to check for and get rid of any remaining Fractsidus frequencies, in case they contaminate our Echoes, like a virus.
The console was designed to run for seventy-two hours straight, so it's not nearly as fragile as he claims.
To only run it for six hours at a time... The Vault would be overflowing with Echoes waiting for maintenance.
Enough, you uncultured fool! You don't understand the elegance of this beautiful machine, nor the finesse of the tuning work!
All right, "great artist"... If you still want to fix this machine, we'd better get back to work.

As the tides receded, a new world and an unexplored adventure awaited you.
Yangyang and Chixia found you unconscious at the Gorges of Spirits. Together, you decided to head to Huanglong's Jinzhou City, marking the beginning of your journey.

Jinzhou, a border city in Huanglong, had long been a battleground against the Threnodian Ovathrax. The Midnight Rangers, led by General Jiyan, fought tirelessly against the waves of Tacet Discords—nightmarish entities created by the Threnodian—near the Norfall Barrens...

Meanwhile, a mysterious organization known as the Fractsidus operated covertly within Jinzhou. They were aiming to resurrect the Threnodian. Somehow, they seemed especially interested in you, going so far as to extend an invitation...

You met Jinhsi, the Magistrate of Jinzhou. She explained the double threats Jinzhou was facing: external attacks from the resurgent Threnodian, and internal turmoil caused by the mysterious disappearance of Jinzhou's Sentinel.
As the Magistrate and the Sentinel's Resonator, Jinhsi resolved to travel to Mt. Firmament and uncover the truth about Jinzhou's missing Sentinel, Jué. A confrontation seemed unavoidable...

The rise of the TD Outbreak unleashed Ovathrax's latest creation: the Dreamless, an incomplete entity. With Jinzhou City under siege, you joined the battle, eventually defeating the Dreamless and absorbing it with your bare hands.
Jinzhou's immediate crisis was averted, but Magistrate Jinhsi was nowhere to be found...
You sought guidance from Sanhua, who directed you to a ferry near Mt. Firmament. There, you encountered Changli, your "Wayfinder" into the mountain.

This secret realm, where the flow of time warped and twisted, required a price for entry. However, you seemed curiously unaffected by the temporal distortion, while Changli seemed unbothered by its effects...

Within Mt. Firmament's Hongzhen settlement, you discovered that many animals and residents had been frozen in time, trapped by the erratic temporal flows. The Fractsidus had also infiltrated the area.

Xinyi, the mayor of Hongzhen, informed you that Jinhsi had only recently departed for Mt. Firmament's peak, in search of the Sentinel. Due to the temporal distortions, what had been days to you was merely moments inside the mountain.

Deep within the Mianloong Chamber, you finally found Jinhsi. Together, you faced the Sentinel, Jué. Jué explained its dilemma: to keep its power from spiraling out of control, it had chosen to remain confined within Mt. Firmament.
If the situation continued, its only recourse would have been to freeze time across all of Jinzhou, hoping future generations could find a solution to undo the damage...

At the mountain's peak, you stood by Jinhsi as she endured Jué's trial, proving the strength of human will. With your help, she stabilized and inherited the Sentinel's power, finally bringing an end to the temporal chaos on Mt. Firmament...
Jué revealed the truth: You were none other than its Arbiter, the founder of Jinzhou.
Jinhsi's unyielding resolve, coupled with the Temporal Mandate granted by Jué with your approval, allowed her to make it through the impossible trial.
Following Jué’s guidance, you set out on a new path, seeking answers to the mysteries of your origins. Your next destination is the base of an enigmatic organization known as the Black Shores.

You confronted a crisis in the Port City of Guixu alongside Yangyang. Shortly after, the Shorekeeper guided you to the Black Shores, a place shrouded in mystery. The Tethys System of the Black Shores had suffered a catastrophic failure, unleashing data-based pollution that corroded everything it touched.
Once again guided by the Shorekeeper, you delved deeper into the Black Shores, determined not only to save this ravaged place but also to recover memories of your past...
The Shorekeeper revealed that you were once the leader and founder of the Black Shores, an ancient organization spanning ages, with her serving as your loyal assistant.
The current crisis, it seemed, was intricately tied to your forgotten past, and the Lament recorded by the Tethys System during the disaster in Port City of Guixu held crucial secrets...
To resolve the chaos caused by the Tethys System, you and the Shorekeeper entered a simulation it had created, reliving the final hour before the Lament struck Port City of Guixu.
As the disaster drew near, the Tethys System tried to absorb you as its new core. In a desperate bid to protect you, the Shorekeeper was sucked into a black hole...

You reclaimed the mantle of leadership, steering the Black Shores toward redemption. You broke free from the mistakes of the past, liberated the innocent trapped in endless suffering, and rescued the Shorekeeper from the Tethys System's grasp.

Now free from the burden of her mission, the Shorekeeper revealed another clue. She suggested that the key to understanding your connection with Abby—and Abby's recent strange symptoms—might lie within Rinascita.
Rinascita is a nation to the southeast of the Black Shores, making the Black Shores archipelago the perfect starting point for your journey...

A confetti pistol crafted from recycled materials by Roccia. Despite her reserved nature, she never forgets to add a burst of confetti for those cheerful, dramatic moments in life—a little surprise, a quick-witted remark from a troupe member, and so on, each deserving its own small celebration.

Ever since Pero saved Roccia, they've been close friends with a shared love for theater. Years of reading plays stored in Pero's box have shaped Roccia's taste for drama, just like how their time spent crafting props and performing together has deepened their bond. And for Pero, after a century of life, Roccia's presence has brought warmth to her world. They've given each other a second life, both becoming better versions of themselves.

A unique prop set crafted by Roccia, made from Luceanites that hold the emotions and memories of those long departed. When brought onto the stage, these lingering feelings glimmer within each line and monologue, casting a light that, as Roccia believes, allows their original keepers to shine once more.

This is no mere collage made of disparate materials but rather an interpretation of inspiration and a concept of constructivist ideals. Its creator started her career marked by striking innovation, yet she remained deeply underappreciated. Carlotta, however, recognized this "hidden gem," describing her work as "an impression of otherness with a hauntingly poetic touch." Now a celebrated installation artist in Ragunna, she crafted this fine piece as a unique token of gratitude for Carlotta's sponsorship and unwavering trust.

A delicate case decorated with intricately carved gemstones, ideal for any formal occasion. They say a lady's bag is where her secrets hide, which is certainly true for Carlotta. The perfume bottle, for instance, is a grenade in disguise, while the glasses are special instruments displaying real-time locations and query results. Beyond their ornamental charm, these items are Carlotta's most reliable allies in her missions.
In beauty, they adorn; in death, they unmake—perfectly suit their owner's needs.

A pair of black gloves, their lustrous sheen reminiscent of the night, adorned with gemstones bearing the same name as the wearer—Opal.
Within the family, there are many unspoken rules, subtle and unnecessary to voice aloud. One such rule is this: those who wear black gloves must quietly resolve any "troubles" to serve the family's needs.
Yet, this is not a matter of compromise, but rather Carlotta's own choice. The family has shown her the wider world, and now she will guide them into an even greater one—both in the name of the true Montelli and her own.
