Review by [Pure Dream] Dorothy the Wonderous Adventurer; Rating: 9/10
 
Ugh, this is too much! The screenwriter is just... too much! I can't accept this ending! Why, why, why?! Jiu promised he'd give Yuehui a happy ending, but then he says, "I don't want to say goodbye, nor make promises with you." What does that even mean?! The final scene, with them reuniting on those big birds, was beautiful, yes... but why can't they just go back to how it was? Noooo! That sucked! I'm knocking off a point for this!

Review by [Wishes Under a Clear Sky] Miss Orange; Rating: 8/10

This is a film about love, and the scene that sticks with me the most is when Jiu and Yuehui finally reunite at that Lollo Logistics station, the place where they first met. Their dialogue there really nailed the essence of love. It's not just about the romance, but the real, everyday life that makes us feel whole. People are unlike the two legendary birds. Sure, Jiu will eventually meet someone else, or maybe try to force himself to forget, but some things will always remind him of her. It's just like that last scene when he's lost in thought at the Jinzhou Teahouse, staring at the painting on the wall.

Review by [Deepsea Solitude] White Dried Fish; Rating: 10/10
 
Although we can't fully understand human emotions, it doesn't stop us from savoring them. A solid 10! Yummy, meow.
 
Review by [Scales of Death] Aurelia; Rating: 8.3/10
 
This movie's editing? Top-notch. The pacing? Chef's kiss. During the slower parts, the handheld shots on Jinzhou's streets really nailed the vibe. That moment lives on in my head rent-free. The transitions and camera choices, especially when following the characters, were so on point. And that reverse shot at the Lollo Logistics station during the rain? Pure brilliance. It hinted at the unexpected twist without giving anything away.

Story-wise, it's a classic: the two leads meet, then part ways, with the plot coming full circle at the end. It's a little predictable and very tidy, but honestly, it works. It's sincere, and that's what makes it hit hard. I'm giving it an 8.3 because it's a true gem in today's world of cinema.

The first page of the New Branch Employee Handbook, distributed by KU-Tata. It provides an overview of the Black Shores ground level.
 
As the think tank for Lament prediction and world salvation, the Black Shores is also referred to as the "singularity for observing the Lament." Over the course of civilization, it has focused on studying the Lament and Waveworn Phenomena. Black Shores members travel globally to collect Reverberation samples from Lament zones, using the Tethys System to reverse-engineer them. Their goal is to replicate the premonitions and processes of the Lament in order to pinpoint its original source. By feeding a large volume of Reverberation specimens into the system, they aim to improve the accuracy of the Lament and Waveworn Phenomenon forecasts, reducing losses for their allies.

The Black Shores Archipelago is built on a massive piece of Tacetite, rich in high-dimensional Remnant Energy, which powers the endless computational cost of the Tethys System. Additionally, the vast energy field generated by the Tacetite's frequency forms a natural barrier that conceals the Black Shores within the seas. For those outside the organization, entry to the Black Shores is by invitation only, under the guidance of the Shorekeeper.

Each area within the Black Shores Archipelago serves a specific function, including personnel management, issuing warnings, hosting international envoys, and providing living and preparation areas for Black Shores Consultants and Bloom Bearers.

Its true core, however, lies deep underground in Tethys' Deep—a highly classified zone off-limits to anyone outside the organization.

For years, the Black Shores has been collecting Reverberation data, recruiting skilled personnel, and liaising with other nations to advance efforts in analyzing the Lament.

As a global salvation organization, the Black Shores aims to minimize the impact of the Lament on civilization, help allies avoid threats, assist with reconstruction, and offer neutral advisory services during disasters. Notably, only the ground level is accessible to international envoys, where visitors are welcomed, daily affairs are managed, and information is exchanged.

Report on Lampylumen The Tiger's Maw Mine primarily produces Lampylumen along with other ore deposits, as well as a minor quantity of Tacetite ores. Following years of joint research by Huaxu Academy and the Ministry of Development, a unanimous conclusion has been reached regarding the formation of the Tiger's Maw. They found that tectonic shifts caused by the Waveworn Phenomenon altered the plate tectonics in Jinzhou, uplifting ore deposits formed tens of millions of years ago to the upper crust and introducing Lampylumen into the domain of human knowledge. The initial survey of the Lampylumen veins has led to the following conclusions: Form: Lampylumen typically has a cubic structure, often found as singular cubes or stacked formations, and its rectangular shape allows for easy extraction. It melts at high temperatures, making it easy to shape. Properties: Due to its unique formation, Lampylumen has an internal structure arranged like an electrical network, making it an ideal material for semiconductor sheets. Application: Lampylumen can be used in chips for Terminals and Resonance Beacons, as well as in the manufacturing of various high-precision components (further assessment required).

Report on Hypothermia Incident The newly surveyed mine, designated T36E8, has developed a freezing fog accompanied by an unusual buzzing sound that spreads with the mist. Until the source of the fog is identified, all survey operations in mine T36E8 have been suspended. Following the appearance of the freezing fog, mining machinery has been unable to reach operating temperatures or issue safety warnings. Multiple health monitors on-site have reported hypothermia warnings among workers. The Midnight Rangers have entered the mine to conduct an emergency rescue. Wounded miners have been transferred to the Medical Division of Huaxu Academy. In response, the Ministry of Development has deployed the Defense Division to secure and lock down the T36E8 site. Symptoms among the affected miners include delirium, hallucinations, and hypothermia. These conditions, along with abnormal vital signs, have not responded to standard medical treatments. The preliminary assessment points to a potential assault incident involving TDs.

A tourism guide penned by the Pioneer Association, featuring reports on the Hongzhen hot spring in Mt. Firmament.

[Tranquility’s Healing Touch] Spring's Taste

Spring's Taste is a centuries-old hot spring inn nestled in Hongzhen, set against the foothills beside a natural hot spring and known for its distinctive architectural style. After the slowed time flow on Mt. Firmament was lifted, the inn has finally opened to outside visitors. Here, snowflakes drift down as steam rises into the warm glow of lantern light, creating a serene atmosphere for guests soaking in the hot spring, with views of the undulating, snow-laden mountains in Mt. Firmament. This experience promises to dissolve all fatigue and stress! Many visitors leave Hongzhen with a lingering sense of awe and wonder, as though they've glimpsed a celestial realm—making Spring's Taste the top hot spring destination in all of Huanglong!
 
[Hot Spring Egg Challenge] Perfect Coddled Egg
 
As the oldest hot spring inn on Solaris-3, Spring's Taste offers food and lodging that reflect the authentic essence of Mt. Firmament, earning unanimous praise from its guests. The owner is a renowned foodie with a deep love for life and gourmet cuisine. Taking full advantage of the natural hot spring, he invented a unique method of "hot spring slow cooking," where food is sealed in jars and soaked in the hot spring to cook slowly.
 
Each year, Spring's Taste hosts a Hot Spring Egg Challenge, where participants compete to cook the perfect egg with a custard-like yolk. The winner is said to earn a year of free accommodations at the inn!

[Nature's Majestic Cascade] Snowy Stream
 
Mt. Firmament is home to many natural hot springs, and the scenic Snowy Stream is the source of Hongzhen's hot springs. A blooming tree's branches cradle the cascading waterfalls from the cliff, nourishing the entire hot spring system of Hongzhen.
 
This tree was planted by Hongzhen's first settlers when the town was first established. Over time, it has grown from a crack in the rock and now stands tall and proud. The waterfalls, constantly beating against the mountain rocks, have gradually polished the once-hard stones into smooth, rounded surfaces.
 
Later, the people of modern-day Hongzhen refined the landscape to replicate the legendary story of Snowy Stream from Mt. Firmament. Several centuries ago, a mysterious figure journeyed through the region when a heavy snowfall sealed off the mountain passes. Seeing the villagers' firewood supplies dwindling, the traveler used Resonance power to carve a passage through the mountains and divert the mountain stream to the village. In an instant, mist and melting ice flowed westward with the stream, creating a breathtaking sight as if ethereal immortals were gliding across the water's surface.

A page of the New Branch Employee Handbook, distributed by KU-Tata. It provides an overview of the Black Shores underground level.

The underground of the Black Shores is where its data space intersects with reality, also known as Tethys' Deep.

In other words, the underground space of the Black Shores is the Tethys System itself. Space Anchors, stabilizing devices positioned throughout the surface and underground levels, act as firewalls to maintain the balance between the data zone and reality, ensuring they do not interfere with each other.

If the Space Anchors malfunction, the data zone within the Tethys System can "invade" reality, triggering anomalies that, according to the records, include but are not limited to:

Regional overlap between the digital space and the physical world, an increased likelihood of Consultants and Bloom Bearers developing spatial perception disorders, and simulated objects from the Sand Table escaping into reality.

The Tethys System consists of two key components: the Data Torrent and the Stellar Matrix, a supercomputational Sand Table that imitates the celestial bodies.

Using the data of the Lament to observe and analyze its mechanisms, and thereby forewarn future occurrences of the Lament, are the duties of the "stars."

However, this is just the beginning of the application and exploration of the Tethys System. The Black Shores Consultants are actively working to unlock its full potential.
 
They say that the one with the highest clearance within the Black Shores was able to harness the Stellar Matrix's full computational capacity to simulate the future of civilization. However, this attempt led to the system's resources being drained to the point of near-total shutdown.

While the Order often lauds water for its tranquility, gentleness, birthing of life, and enriching nature, it can also symbolize instability. Ragunna faces constant threats from tides and floods. Everything in Ragunna arises from the sea, yet everything ultimately returns to it.

Surrounded by the sea, the people of Ragunna live in harmony with the water. Whether driven by love or fear, the Ragunnesi hold a deep reverence for it. In a sense, this also reflects their anxiety and fear of the Final Tide, as foretold by the Sentinel.

They hold various rituals to pray to the Sentinel, hoping that the Sentinel will guide them through the tides of this life and ultimately lead them through the Final Tide.

Scholars of the Order have also drawn inspiration from myths surrounding the Sentinel Imperator, developing an entire set of theories about water.

[Theory I: The Origin of the World is Water]
Water is universally present in everything and encompasses all things, representing infinity. It is an object of infinite nature. Everything originates from water, including the creation of the world itself.

[Theory II: Water is Fluid, Like the Constant Movement of the Tide]
In its movement, water is divided into the contrasting sides of cold and hot, dry and wet, forming the world. The movement of water is the tide. Everything is born in the tide and will eventually end in the Final Tide. However, this end does not signify obliteration. Just as everything originates from water, the end is merely a return to the embrace of water. This movement creates a cycle, ultimately reuniting everything in the sea. From this reunion, humans will again be separated, only to be reborn like spring shoots, in an infinite cycle.

[Theory III: Water is Reflective]
The Ragunnesi believe that water reflects everything without discrimination, allowing humans to see another version of themselves within it.

Water mirrors the appearance of the Ragunnesi, and the Ragunnesi, in turn, see their reflections in the water. If the world is like an ocean, then the frequencies of humans and the world influence and shape one another. The wondrous water has been imbued with the human spirit, symbolizing the cycle of life and death. If water represents the subconscious, it also serves as a harbor for fantasies and desires.

This is why research into the Remnant domain is also prevalent within the Order.

The Seminary of the Forgotten in Rinascita was once flooded by Nimbus Sanctum, which later proved to be a manifestation of Remnant Energy, recording the emotions and memories of humans without distinction, and then reflecting them in reality.

With the old site of the Seminary still present, Nimbus Sanctum holds a special allure for Acolytes of the Order, who visit to pray or salvage ancient texts.
Some scholars believe the Remnant Cloud is a higher-dimensional form of water, while others speculate that another world exists beneath Nimbus Sanctum.

[Theory IV: Water is All-Encompassing]
This all-encompassing nature is why Ragunna, under the guidance of the Order, is a city that welcomes exiles from all walks of life and grants them equal rights. The Carnevale is the epitome of this inclusiveness. Ragunnesi from various isles unite to honor their hometowns and families lost in the Lament. Dressed in their traditional clothing and wearing masks symbolizing ancestors and totems, they perform a variety of dramas. The diversity and inclusiveness lie at the core of the performances during the Carnevale.

[Theory V: Unity]
Taking inspiration from the all-encompassing nature of water, Primus Fenrico, upon assuming power, developed the doctrine of Unity and enshrined it in the Codex.

For the exiled people of Rinascita, formed after the Lament, religion is not merely a practice in the Order but a collection of science, philosophy, politics, individual identity, and the hope for salvation. The civilization of Rinascita is anchored around faith, meaning religion is not just a personal pursuit but a universal truth that explains the world and defines one's place within it.

Any heretical theory that undermines or challenges this faith is seen as a dagger aimed at the heart of truth itself. Such ideas threaten the existence of those around them and risk tearing apart the fabric of society, bringing calamity and destruction to this city by the sea.

The Primus believes that whenever the ideology of Division reaches its zenith, the calamity of the Dark Tide will descend from above, endangering the very existence of Rinascita. For this reason, even the Carnevale, which embodies the spirit of inclusiveness, must be overseen by the Order.

I once joked to a friend that if, one day, you find yourself wanted across all of Solaris-3 for illegal actions like short selling or trading in debts, then, based on my experience, apart from digging your own grave, your best bet would be to hide in Averardo Vault in Rinascita. As long as you can prove your worth, the Montelli family will keep you safe—even if it means turning a blind eye. They'll go so far as to pay your bail out of their own pockets and assemble a professional international legal team for you, with only one condition: that you build strong business ties with them. Trust me on this, I deal a lot with the Montellis. They value the so-called "spirit of the contract" more than most businessmen. Back when I was younger, I couldn't stand those brash islanders. They didn't play by the rules, were full of energy, and always spoke their minds. They were nothing like the Rinascitan people I knew, who were all about dance and performance. But over time, I came to recognize a trait in them that others lacked. They always price everything upfront. The Montellis are by far the easiest businessmen to understand because their world operates on just one principle: the contract. And the only thing driving that principle? Profit. —Excerpt from How to Get Unlimited Shell Credits

As long as projected earnings outweigh the risks, the Montellis will go to any lengths to fulfill the contract. They never turn down a deal that lands on their doorstep and always deliver once the client has paid. Their team possesses a unique, almost magnetic force, uniting individuals driven by ambition and the promise of fame. But don't expect to hear talk of ethics or loyalty—profit is the only metric that matters. It's hard to wrap your head around, isn't it? A family that has its hands in Echo technology, global trade, banking, private arms, and once even currency manipulation, yet they don't rely on bloodlines to sustain the empire. Decades have passed, and the fortune stashed in Averardo Vault must be beyond imagination. To protect it, they've even imported specialized tech and upgraded their Echoes into formidable war machines. Trust me, gentlemen—no matter how confident you are in your abilities, never, ever even entertain the thought of going after that vault. —Excerpt from How to Get Unlimited Shells

In my observation, up until six or seven years ago, most people sent to the Fool's Sails never really believed they'd end up there.

Back then, Acolytes still tried to persuade those who had gone astray, reminding them they had a choice and could still change their ways. If only they knew their fate, they would surely alter it.

I believe that at the time, most Acolytes genuinely preached with compassion, even though they couldn't foresee the consequences.

"Wait not to correct mistakes after they are made. Save the misguided before they act foolishly."

Without the revelation of the Enlightened One, this idea is undoubtedly a paradox: humans cannot decide the outcome before the cause—just as it is impossible for a child to be born before the mother. But this, in fact, is the very greatness of the Primus. This is the grace granted by our Sentinel!

I am simply filled with awe:

O how great you are, Fenrico, the Enlightened One! O how great Thou are, Sentinel Imperator!

The Fools who were sent to the ship are the peculiar outliers marked by Ragunna, unable to understand the principle of Unity upheld by the Order. As the line from that famous play says, "One is all, and all is one." To be "one" is the ideal of Ragunna, and those who cannot shape themselves into that singular ideal can never truly belong to the "all."

As an employee at the Ragunna branch of the Pioneer Association, I rarely bring up my hometown with colleagues.

I come from a small town called Egla, which fits every definition of a "small town"—simple, a bit behind the times, and quiet, at least during daylight hours. Through my business travels worldwide, I've seen many such towns. Most eventually merge into larger, fortified cities for protection from TDs or the Lament. Few people realize, however, that Egla's history as a settlement is nearly as ancient as Ragunna's, and it had stubbornly kept much of its original character.

Within the Order, there's a well-known piece of advice: never anger the elders of Egla.

Visitors to Egla might encounter a few lively elders who seem like humble figures, be it a local mayor or an innkeeper. But behind these modest roles, many were once people of influence, even retired Acolytes or Priests of the Order who served alongside the Primus, interpreted the oracles, or shaped doctrines. When Ragunna was still a city on the rise, these elders—or their forebears—stood on the front lines, helping lay its very foundations. After long, distinguished careers, they returned to Egla, choosing to spend their later years in the place where it all began.

What is it, exactly, that keeps people returning to Egla Town?
 
Honestly, I can't quite understand the mindset of that generation.
 
The last time I left my hometown, I saw a group of elders gathered in front of an abandoned house, almost as if they were holding a vigil.
 
They stood there for a long time in silence before one of them spoke, reflecting on the past:
 
"Old friend, time doesn't turn back. You can't live forever in what might have been. You need to understand that the present isn't necessarily worse than the past. It might even be better... We couldn't save that child in the end. But we should be grateful for the majority we did save."

This is a transcript of an interview that occurred in the Montelli family.

- Good day. I've been assigned as your consultant for this case. You can refer to me as No. 35.

- No. 35? Don't you have an actual name?

- I beg your understanding, sir. Those of us in this line of work prefer to keep our dealings strictly professional, with no entanglement beyond the task at hand.

- Alright, then. What's your plan regarding this employee's contract?

- Termination.

- And...? No emotional support, no severance, no kind words to soften the blow?

- No. Just termination.

- What? Then why would the Montellis need you for this? I could handle it myself, and probably better.

- Are you sure, sir? Are you prepared to look this young woman in the eye—a girl who's worked tirelessly for this family, despite being separated from her own mother—and tell her, without a hint of empathy, "I'm sorry, but you haven't brought sufficient value to the family. We have to let you go." If you're certain you can do that, then be my guest.

- I... I can certainly do that. Besides, there's no need to be so harsh, is there?

- If you're not harsh enough, sir, you may very well be the next to face dismissal. Be too lenient, and you risk failing to generate value for the family and wasting extra compensation. Even if you manage the dismissal, the staff may start seeing you as cold-hearted. The Montellis are a big family, aren't they? Who would do that to their own family?

- So... That's it? I'm supposed to pay a hefty sum to hire you just to let her go? Feels like extortion. But you're right. I can't be the one damaging the family's reputation.

- Or, you could give me a reason why she must be dismissed. Then I might be able to make her understand.

- A reason? Isn't losing the cargo enough? She's not a Resonator. She couldn't resist the hallucinations and failed to protect the cargo... What use is she?

- So, you plan to hire a Resonator or someone with similar resistance at the standard employee wage? Besides, are we certain she actually lost the cargo? My last employer once broke down when he was dismissed, sharing a story about his supervisor...

- You... How dare you bring that up? This conversation is over. Just do it your way.

Notes from the Executor: Initiate a review of this regional manager. Also, arrange a new position for the dismissed girl.

10 Fun Facts You May Have Missed in the Pioneer Association's Historical Documentary: Land of the Sentinel!

1. All scenes depicting miracles and myths were filmed on the Fagaceae Peninsula, the only location abundant with the distinctive Viscum Viride. Interestingly, plant lineage studies suggest that Viscum Viride is most likely not native to Rinascita.
 
2. For scenes featuring Napoli the Second, the Order of the Deep denied the crew access to film within their Cathedral. Instead, the crew used ruins in the Fagaceae Peninsula to complete these shots. The reason for the denial was that the actor portraying Napoli the Second had previously played a merchant who falls in love with an Acolyte in another documentary.

3. The backstory of the Fisalia family's rise to prominence is loosely based on a legendary wealthy merchant from the New Federation, as the Fisalia family declined to share their own history for the documentary.

4. In the documentary, the Blessed Maiden is shown helping villagers pick fruit as a child. However, there are no fruit trees near Egla Town. This scene was actually filmed on the Fagaceae Peninsula.

5. The Divine Envoys featured in the documentary were actually portrayed by the Echoes from Reserved Terminals, as the Order refused to allow the actual Divine Envoys to participate in any form of entertainment filming.

6. The battle scenes involving Napoli the Second and the Blessed Maiden were largely performed by sponsors, many of whom were contractors from Lollo Logistics. Locals from Rinascita only made up a small part of the cast, but they spent an entire day teaching the couriers how to charge into their enemies like knights.

7. In the bar fight scene, the director personally contributed to the fighting choreography due to having consumed too much of the special brew made in the Fagaceae Peninsula.

8. The iconic scene of the first Pilgrim's Sail setting off was filmed in a single take because the crew was only able to lease the ship for half a day.

9. The current head of the Montelli family made a cameo appearance, playing the role of the first family head of the Montellis.

10. The documentary has yet to be shown in local cinemas in Ragunna.

I'm... I'm the traveler without shoes, stumbling down a path to inspiration that's nothing but thorns... *cough*!
Alright, I'll confess. The truth is I just can't seem to write a thing.
I've got a handful of half-baked manuscripts, but none of them capture the life of the Blessed Maiden.
How did she grow up, and what aspirations did she set for herself? How were her studies in the seminary, and how did she pursue her dreams?
I'm at a loss. I can't even figure out the ending for this script. I talked with the captain about it earlier, and he's just as stumped.
Recently, I received a mysterious package. The captain says it's a private collection from the Fisalia family. No idea who sent it, but they must have had a soft spot for me...
After reading, I felt like I was on the verge of piecing it all together. But inspiration's like a shooting star. Every time I reach for it... poof! It slips through my fingers.
I don't know what to do! Perhaps I am just a seaweed. Brainless, drifting with the tide...
What kind of fireworks display would fit the grand spectacle of Ragunna's Carnevale?
Fireworks shouldn't just light up the night... they need to dazzle in the daylight too!
Golden Fleece, burst forth in colorful flames! Wait, that's strange...
What are you up to?
I'm Kasper, the troupe's Fireworks Master. I'm experimenting with this Golden Fleece, you see.
It comes from the sighs of ancient dragons, the remnants of their flames. It was once used to make gunpowder.
But now, it will be transformed into the finest firework material!
No longer will it bring terror, but joy and laughter instead.
It will explode in the sky, lighting up Ragunna's sky!
But... there's still something missing... What could it be? Let me think a moment.
I've got it! I've got it!
Some Golden Fleece, a touch of unstable glazed young rock, and a feather from Pan Cake! I'll get consent first, I promise!
After that, three happy Nimbus Wraiths. I'll use their laughter to catalyze a rainbow of flame.
Then, the grand finale—Boom! My power will set it all off!
Oh, dear friend! Keep your distance, will you? I wouldn't want to blow you up by accident!
What's going on?
I'm working on a new firework invention... Just about to let out a sneeze!
Sneezing?
Oh? Didn't they tell you? Every time I sneeze, it sets off a little explosion.
Before I close my eyes, wherever my gaze lands, boom! That's where the spark happens.
That's quite a special ability.
Aha! That's why I need to pluck a feather from Pan Cake. You see, just a little tickle on the nose with it, and I'll—
Ahhh—Achooo!
Hold it in!
Whoops! Sorry, almost caused another disaster.
Another disaster?
It's a long story. You see, I was just accompanying my beloved Miranda to the Cathedral of Mercury to pray...
When wouldn't you know it, a pigeon feather landed right on my nose. Just as I was devoutly gazing at the Sentinel's statue, too... and then—sneeze!
So that's why you ended up being...
Exactly. The Acolytes thought I was a heretic trying to deface the statue. Without a second thought, they tossed me onto the Pilgrim's Sail.
I've spent years as a fireworks master in Ragunna without a single soul noticing. But one sneeze, and suddenly, I'm making headlines! Guess I finally got my moment.
You see the scar on my nose? The Acolytes were so afraid I'd sneeze on the Troupe of Fools that they actually clipped my nose before I boarded.
If it weren't for Brant saving me, I'd be breathing through my mouth for the rest of my life!
Speaking of odd things... if you manage to climb up to the Sentinel statue, you might find the little hole I left behind. My sneeze mark.
That's a bit absurd...
Absurd? This is Ragunna! At least I'm still alive to tell the tale.
Since I've been with the Fool's Troupe, business has been booming. Got me a solid group of customers.
When I was a fireworks master in Ragunna, business wasn't nearly this good. Now look at me, practically blowing up the competition! Ha!
Ragunna... the false Righteous One... cloaked in divinity, divinity... hmm...
Father... Mother... It's me, Todd... Did you like my performance...?
Don't cry... I'm here... I'm home...
I get what you're saying... but I want a No. 65 Tubpup with Nuvola Pasta...
It's so deep... It's all Troupe Strength in the Tubpup... I can't drink anymore...
Too much Tubpup... bad for your health...
I love you... but I can only see you in my dreams...
Look at our daughter... how adorable she is... Marina...
Can I see her one last time, please... Why... Why can't I see her face clearly...
Marina... Marina...?
Can't sleep either?
What's keeping you up?
As you can see, it's only when I'm fully awake that I can "craft" their dreams.
What kind of dreams do you craft?
Hmm… it varies, really. Most of the time, I create beautiful visions to heal the regrets that weigh on their hearts.
But, from what I've seen, the fear of "boarding the Fool's Sail" appears to be so deeply rooted that the dreams don't always turn out as they hoped.
What are their regrets?
Todd, hailing from an underground theater troupe, was banished merely for using comedy to satirize the Order's tax policies...
Gideon's family was framed by the Acolytes. At his lowest, he could only find solace with a Tubpup. It became his shelter, his only home in the storm.
Knox was sent aboard the Fool's Sail before his newborn child even had a chance to open their eyes. And as kin of a "heretic," the future doesn't look kind.
So that's how it is...
During this Carnevale, we all have to hide our identities and take on roles in the Fool's Troupe as we return to Ragunna City, after so long.
We must suppress our desire to reconnect with old friends while trying to complete the Montelli family's mission. It's... complicated. So insomnia, I suppose, is inevitable.
That's why I need to create dreams for them, to help them get some rest.
Why do you hide your true identities?
Well, the Order doesn't know... but most of the Fool's Troupe are survivors from the Pilgrim's Sail.
The moment the Order uncovers the truth, our Fool's Elysium will burn to the ground. We have to keep our silence, no matter the cost.
In our plays, we sing to condemn the oppression, to shed light on the bloodshed… One day, all of Rinascita will know what Fenrico has done.
Take a break when you feel ready.
Thank you… for taking the time to understand us, for wanting to know the Fools' story.
Who... who are you? How did you suddenly appear at sea? Why are you rescuing us?
I just want to return to Ragunna City… My belongings are still there, left behind in the rush.
Fede... we can't go back.
I understand your panic, Mr. Fede. But remember this—
In the eyes of The Order, a pilgrimage is no different from an execution...
(Narrator: A mere infatuation is far from enough. What Chappell, now fallen to mortality, needs is a heart consumed by desire. Without it, anyone's love is nothing but a delusion!)
(Narrator: The doctrines that sever human desires and the silence, the tasteless laws and divine meals, now only provoke her instinctive revulsion—)
I don't need a sermon, Acolyte Bugatti. Either shut up or join me in enjoying this delicious Golden Crab Pie.
Don't look at me like that, Bugatti. I'm not the Acolyte you once knew.
Call me Chappell... My name is Chappell·Romanya, Lord Bugatti.
Hmm… These botched recreations. But I guess I'll have to finish them off anyway.
The taste and presentation might be lacking, but it's still edible!
Oh my! This one is... Poached Egg with Slug Relish, from "The Merchant of Ragunna."
Seems the slug meat got overcooked. No wonder Gisle's jaw started twitching halfway through his lines...
And here we have the Layered Yak Short Rib Bake... Must be the family feast main course from Act 3, Scene 6 of "The Lady of Camellya."
Ugh, this yak meat is far too fatty. No wonder Heather's aria sounded like it was dripping in butter...
Hello there, {PlayerName}! I'm testing out some new recipes, but I won't invite you to sample them just yet.
All these dishes are...
Yes, inspired by the plays, you see. Though recreating them has proven to be a bit more troublesome than I anticipated.
Golden Crab Pie is one of my few triumphant creations!
I'm Rossini. I didn't get the chance to introduce myself during today's rehearsal. I used to work in the kitchens of the Order of the Deep, preparing meals for the council members.
Why did the Order exile you?
I merely enhanced the council's meals—naturally, in the best way possible.
The head chef accused me of using sinister methods to incite the Acolytes' appetites, corrupting their piety and undermining the Order.
Heretic, he called me...  a laughable but effective accusation.
I suspect we'll head for Lilyland next.
I'd wager that Septimont is more likely.
What are you doing?
We're debating our next destination. We're still on a Pan-Ragunna Tour, after all.
The Captain often says, "Wherever the applause calls, there we'll go to 'capture laughter.' With our craft, our wit, and a touch of our own flair, we'll claim what's rightfully ours."
True enough. But each island has its own tastes when it comes to theater. We'll need to tailor our efforts to make sure everyone feels the journey was worthwhile!
But, whether we head to the Lilyland's Sea of Flowers or the exhilarating spectacles of Septimont, it's up to the captain to decide!
Focus, Doggins.
Look at me! I'm your audience. Break the fourth wall with your gaze!
Madame Nyarla has thrown us another curveball...
The imaginative design of this stage truly aligns with Madame Nyarla's signature style—"a labyrinth of opulent, fevered dreams."
But why do I feel like this "fevered and opulent dream" has left me standed outside the gates?
This new brew's potency should carry us through the entire Carnevale.
If Brant manages to snag the Laurel this year, you can bet Troupe Strength will sell like hotcakes. Heh, heh, heh...
This... this... is yet another baseless slander!
If this religious play actually gets performed, how will my wife and daughter see me? How will the rest of the town see them?
How are they supposed to live in Ragunna after this? Damn it!
Is there really no hope? If we head to Lilyland or Septimont... surely there's somewhere that will take us in...
I... I don't know...
Wake up, Fede. No city-state will take in outcasts without identity, unable to prove their very existence. We've lost our status as citizens of Ragunna.
Even our papers... they've turned to nothing but scraps of useless parchment.
Is there really no one who'll take us in? I still have a few friends... I...
Your friends? Do you truly think they'd welcome "heretics" like us?
What would you have me do, Chantelle? The Order's just left us to die out here, haven't they? How could they do this to us...?
Mr. Federico, please... stay calm. You can stay here while you plan your next steps.
Thank you so much Ahem... Fid?
Y-yes, thank you. I... we don't know how to thank you enough...
Oh, dearest Elisha... what shall our next ballet be?
Who are you talking to?
Ah, {PlayerName}, is that you? I was just asking Elisha what our next performance should be...
See, each island nation has its own preferences, you know.

Take Septimont, for example. They favor plays like "The Three Hundred Knights of Capitoline" and "Assassin's Journey"—you know, action-packed, filled with historical sagas and war. That's their thing.
I like them too, but Elisha doesn't share my enthusiasm.
She prefers heart-wrenching tragedies like "The Shape of the Ocean" or "The Perished Waterworld." You know, those tear-jerking stories that only the Riccioli people seem to appreciate...
But I can't stand that place. And let's be honest, tragedy is not in my wheelhouse. Ugh... it's so frustrating, Elisha, my dear Elisha...
Hey! Want to try my first latest dish?
Your first dish?
Your latest dish?
Ah, yes! This is inspired by a performance I saw. A true Rinascita culinary creation, born from the stage!
Place a Goldcrest Scarab into a pie, baked with Mastic Nuvola and Viscum Berry... then nestle it in a Bell Crab shell, arranging it just so, to mimic the playful movements of the scarab...
Goldcrest Scarab?
Bell Crab's shell?
Yes, exactly! Isn't it fascinating? To help the actors truly feel their roles, I've gone all in to recreate these legendary dishes!
So, what do you think? Want to try this dish—the one that brings "Chappell Romanya" back to the mortal realm, but leaves "Acolyte Bugatti" with a most perplexed expression?
Sure!
Maybe not...
No, no, no! No way! There's just no way!! You eat it, I'm not eating it!
Scared you enough to jolt you awake?
Hey! Are you sure you don't want to give it a try? I can guarantee this dish has a flavor like no other!
What should I do, Mama Jemma? I can't go anywhere, and I can't sing...
It's alright, I can't sing either, and I'm doing just fine here, aren't I?
Come on, let me show you around. Let's see what you might be able to do.
Hello there! Need some help?
What are you doing?
Jemma is comforting those recently exiled by the Order. I'll see if there's anything I can do to help.
The captain said if they're headed to the Riccioli Islands or Septimont, we should arrange for Echoes to help them avoid dragons and safely get to where they want to go.
Everyone's got their own path to walk, after all. Not everyone's going to stay here.

In the past, some have sought refuge with their families in the Riccioli Islands, while others ventured to Septimont, trading honor for a new identity, all holding onto the hope of one day returning to Ragunna.
And then there are those who turned to piracy. That's not really our way.
But that's fine, everyone's choices take them down different roads. Let's just help each other while we can!
One-two-three, perfect!
Woohoo! Yay!
What are you doing?
We're rehearsing. This is Doggins, the main character of our play!
An Echo as the main character?
Ha! Don't underestimate our Doggins. This kid is sharp as a tack!
He sneaked aboard the Pilgrim's Sail, searching for his exiled friends, and ended up here.
But the friends he was looking for... they're not here. They went somewhere else.
Still, our little Doggins didn't give up. He decided to stay with us and join the tour across Rinascita!
This play we're rehearsing is all about Doggin's own journey. I'm sure if his friends see it, they'll come looking for him.
Woohoo! Yay!

Traces of Tides
Wait here
Ugh, what's this smell?!
Nope, I can't take it… Gotta take a break…
Ew, why do I still smell it down here? Wait, this weird frequency… It's coming from that message!
Ugh, my head… so dizzy… I'm gonna lie down. Just... just holler if you need me…
Looks like we've been hit by the weird frequency in that message. I should check out what's going on in Egla Town.
He couldn't use it himself, but sold it for a nice profit!
Then… if we get our hands on it, let's keep it for ourselves!
I want to stay young forever. That way, you'll always see me at my best!
Nah, I want the one that turns stone into gold! Then we can live a wealthy life together.
Perhaps Mammon has offered us a little aperitif.
Alright, I know where we need to go next… The second riddle is waiting for us.
Perhaps the last riddle will give us a clue.
The show begins.
The melody evokes a sense of familiarity, reminding you of that place—<ano=Castle of Fisalia>Porto-Veno Castle</ano>。
It only strengthens your suspicion that the "ghost girl" must be connected to the Fisalia castle.
A sharp headache interrupts your thoughts, the distorted frequencies intensifying. Through the pain, you find a reason to visit the Fisalia castle.
Ugh… what was that…? My head… This pain's getting worse. I need a break somewhere…
You've been under this influence far too long, especially in a place filled with spirits. I should have warned you sooner.
You need a proper rest… and we're not far from Thessaleo Fells.
Come to my castle. I have potions there that can help ease the strain.
This potion is crafted from freshly crushed Barnacle Leaves, mixed with the sap of Violaca, Sea Okra, and Sea Apple, all fermented in a glass vial.
Each of these lovely plants is cultivated here, hand-picked, sorted, and blended by my own hands.
As the poisonous ingredients entwine, their toxins soften over time, like nightmares transforming into the sweetest dreams.
Don't worry, it's perfectly safe and even delightful. Drink up, and rest a while.
Though I may not be able to lift the "curse" binding you just yet, I can certainly help tame it for now.
Ah... Excuse me for a moment. It's time I tend to the flowers.
So, what brings a distinguished Laureate to this ghostly place?
Tired of heavenly views, are we? Hehe, are you here to savor the underworld's wonders and dance with its spirits?
What brings the head of Fisalia here?
Why not? What harm could there be in a ghost of the deep reveling among spirits?
So you're also a ghost of the deep.
"Also?" What are you implying?
You show the strange message to Cantarella.
On the Night of Remembrance, it's only natural that the departed return to the mortal realm for their unfulfilled wishes.
Still, it'd be best if they didn't stir up trouble for the living.
In my humble opinion, lost souls find peace only when their wishes are fulfilled. Then, perhaps, they'll stop haunting people.
Since fate has brought you here, why not offer your aid to those poor, restless souls? I'll join you, of course.
I don't usually do ghost work.
Why would you offer to help me?
Ah, the familiar confusion of a first-timer. But fret not, for I will be your guide through this unforgettable night. Step by step.
Shhh, no need to jump to conclusions. Who knows, it might actually be you doing me a favor.
Every Night of Remembrance brings its own theme. And this year, it's the "Ghost Girl."

Imagine this: an innocent girl lost in the dark sea, fear ripping her apart as her soul drifts away, while her body sinks ever deeper into the abyss. Despair consumes her, bit by bit, until she transforms into a monstrous phantom.

A thrilling story, don't you agree? Like savoring a medium-rare lamb chop served with oysters. One tender slice, and the crimson juice spills, adding just the right flavor to the already exquisite dish.
I like exquisite things, too.
Not sure I love it.
You're making my skin crawl.
Huh… So we share similar tastes. How wonderful.
Oh, really? Then consider it a simple "appetizer" for tonight.
Oh, is it too much for an innocent lamb like yourself? Hehe, my apologies. I hope this doesn't dampen your spirits.
Just look at her dress! Such elegance! She's not even eclipsed by the Laureate. She must be someone of great importance.
I've heard the Fisalias are super secretive. Never thought we could actually see one here.
I know, right? How lucky are we to meet them both tonight!
Wait a second… If people like them are showing up, could the rumor about the elixir actually be true?
Yeah, that makes perfect sense!

On the forty-second full moon of my knighthood, a young man stabbed the right of my abdomen. In retaliation, I took his life. The Order rewarded my killings and celebrated my bloodlust. Yet Sentinel, if my words reach you, I beg for clarity: is mercy the path to saving grace or a swift descent into an early grave?

On the first full moon of my knighthood, I was defeated by a band of Plushies. The big Plushie was more terrifying than I imagined—a slight hesitation almost cost me my life. I was lucky to survive. But Sentinel, I ask you to witness how I conquer my fear and become unyielding. Under your divine gaze, I will forge myself into the very embodiment of the Five Knightly Virtues!

On the hundred and forty-fourth full moon of my knighthood, I was ordered to write a book on an island—despite my illiteracy. I wanted to share my techniques for fighting Tacet Discords, but the Acolytes suggested I center my words around the Five Knightly Virtues. O Sentinel, perhaps you can't hear this, but in all my supposed wisdom, I might be the most foolish of all.

On the ninetieth full moon of my knighthood, I was assigned to duel on the great bridge. Day after day, knights came to challenge me, only to fall again and again—all to hasten my so-called glory of a hundred victories. O Sentinel, do you hear me? The weight of honor grows heavier, yet my sword feels ever more brittle.

On the ninety-fifth full moon of my knighthood, I managed to gather fifteen crates of donations. After giving dues to the Order and the family I serve, only five remained. Even with the three crates I donated... No, it's not enough. It's nowhere near enough! O Sentinel, please enlighten me: why do the greediest souls always hide behind the banner of generosity?
Eek! Who are you?! Leave me alone!
Are you hiding from something?
Plushies! Hordes of them, with pointy horns!
You look like a mighty one. Could you drive them all away, please?
Please, I beg of you! Chase away those Plushies and I'll give you everything I have, even my sword!
Now I understand... I understand it all...
There's no need for thinking whatsoever! I'll simply do whatever they command!
You can call me the {Male=Blessed One;Female=Blessed Maiden}.
The Sentinel's... Arbiter?
No... you're likely a far more special entity.
Well, I have some information and theories of my own. Care to hear them?
Please. Enlighten me.
Interesting. I've never seen such little creatures before. Would you mind sparing a few for me?
(I'd better not ask what she plans to do with them...)
Lady Maiden...
Please. Cartethyia would suffice. I am but a fake after all.
I've waited for this moment, this chance to save the Sentinel... and my family.
I will not turn back, even if this does turn out to be a trap.
If the thought of the final answer troubles you, then I suggest you step aside. {PlayerName} and I will take care of this matter.
Since you are willing to overlook the possibilities of a trap, then there's no reason for me to worry and turn away.
I underestimated your resolve. I'm sorry.
So, how do we get up there?
Simply place Tyrvine on the pedestal behind me and this tower will elevate itself.

A dragon-like Remnant creature haunts the peak of Penitent's End for an unknown reason, devouring all frequencies indiscriminately. Twisted by the frequencies of decay and death it consumes, it now appears as a dreadful, skeletal beast.

Once a sacred place, this island is now a grave of sorrow, and any who come for redemption must face its fire of judgment.

Yet wicked desires have transformed her into the “Queen of Night,” seeking to cloak the Nimbus in endless darkness to clear all sins.

With her final grasp on reason, Lorelei sealed herself within her garden, where she sings a haunting lament, awaiting one who can awaken her from this dismal slumber.

After I get you back, Liel, you'll be eating fish gut rations.
I told him to stay out of trouble, but he never listened. But oh, he'll start listening after a return voyage of nothing but fish guts!
That's really harsh...
A stern lecture ought to be enough.
Speaking of fish, see that gaping hole outside in the sky? Look at all the fish swimming into it.
Sends a chill down my spine... Like a maw that spawns unholy monsters.
Ones larger and more terrifying than what we've faced up till now...
You think monsters will emerge from that hole?
Perhaps those monsters are from inside the tower.
Whatever it is, I'm sure it has something to do with Liel's disappearance.
And I won't give up before I find him.
What do you plan to do?
Not sure if you've noticed, but I'm a Resonator. For some reason, my Tacet Mark reacted when I got close to that monster.
I'll use my Tacet Mark to track the monster down. With luck, that'll lead me to Liel.
We didn't find Liel, but nevertheless, I appreciate your help, friend.
Don't mention it.
A few extra fish and we're even.
I won't forget you. Till next time!
Of course, here you go. Well, this is where we part. Till next time!
What did I tell ya, Itzel? There's our destination.
Shut up... We'd be running around like headless chickens if I listened to you. It was I who pinned that tower down!
Hey, don't make a fuss... Oh, hi friend! You're here!
And so are you two.
Of course. Itzel says she feels the monster's frequencies from within that tower.
Unlike the decoys in the other two towers, this one there is probably real.
Come on. Time to bring Liel back.
That brat had better be in one piece when we find him!
Like the last two towers, this place is filled with poisonous gas. We might see visions of the past here as well.
Let's look at the vision here... Oh crap, the Fanatic Sharks captured Liel.
Those fish nuts... Watch out friend, something's attacking us from above.
Liel, wait up...
That thing again? Watch out, friend!
Taste this!
Out of the way! I'll slaughter you all to get Liel back!
Blasted thing keeps running away.
Argh, the path is broken. Wait, what's that floating in the air? It's Liel's vision!
He got away from the Fanatic Shark? Can't be. When did he learn to fly?
He's not flying. He's running on something... Are those bookcases on the right?
Woo hoo! I'm blazing fast!
You're going nowhere, boy!!!
Look at that little rascal scamper....
Takes after his sister. Hahaha! He might even be a secret Resonator!
These Fanatic Sharks all got skewered!
They were ambushed. Everyone stay alert.
Even if Liel got away, he's no match for that prowling monster.
Don't worry, he's a smart kid, and he's wearing your jammer. He can handle a few Tacet Discords.
I hope so... You'd better not be dead, you idiot...
Those archers again! And look, Fanatic Shark specters... They met their end here!
Oh Liel, I hope you made it out alive.
I don't want to die!
Captain, I'm hit...
End of the line, fish face!
Curse you!!!
Go Liel!
Itzel, you don't look too well. Didn't you see? Liel dealt with that Fanatic Shark.
But how was he getting out?
Sis... Chief... I'm not gonna make it...
Liel...
Liel...
I was kidding about the fish guts. Don't go Liel, I'll serve you the plumpest side of the fattest fish we have.
You know... Liel's love of fish was what got me into fishing.
You can have all my catch once we're out of here. They're meaningless to me now.
But before we leave, that monster at the top of the tower must die.
Liel... I was training him to lead our crew someday.
Come friend, let's go... whatever's in our way will get smashed to a pulp.
Blinky's here. It's summoned a bunch of copies！
Damn, their frequencies show only one copy is real.
Die! Every bit of you!
This one's for Liel!
Go to hell!
Friend...
I can't bring Liel back from the dead, but I've avenged his death by destroying his killer. That's all I can do.
So, you got any questions for me?
About you and Liel...
About this tower...
I don't have any.
We sailed Sentinel knows how many seas. I always thought the ocean would be our grave.
Never thought Liel would meet his end on land... in the depth of an icy tower...
I've got a theory for the tower.
I saw small devices hidden away in most corners back there... much like the fractured halo at the top of the tower.
My guess is the tower is a lab, and those devices were used as some kind of experimental Echo control.
Those controlled Echoes were extremely dangerous... the exact opposite of the cuddly Echoes I heard about in Rinascita.
Someone in the Land of Echoes sought to weaponize them...
The tower's broken halo must have been the largest and most powerful of their devices.
I shudder to think of the horrors that'd be unleashed it ever got completed...
The only thing I have left of Liel is this compass pendant.
It was my gift to him after we divvied the spoils from our first job.
Whenever we got lost at sea, it always guided us back home.
But Liel was so afraid of losing it, so he left it with me for safekeeping.
After we leave this tower, Insula and I will repair our ship and leave this wretched place.
Once we return to familiar waters, I'll throw this compass out at sea.
Maybe, just maybe, Liel will follow our ship's course, find the compass, and let it guide him home...
Thank you for helping us, friend.
Have you spoken to Itzel? She could use a kind ear.
What a day. The life of an island Exile, robbing just to survive... People like us die every day.
But Liel... Liel was different. He was too kind for this kind of life. He did the sailing for us, never the plundering.
I really liked that kid... Had dreams of training him to be the next captain. Ha, an odd choice now that I think about it...
If he became captain, maybe we'd stop being Exiles and turn a new leaf—as legitimate traders and such.
But that's all a pointless dream now... The fate of the crew still rests with me. I have to guide them through this muck.
It's over now, friend. Itzel and I thank you for accompanying us.
What's next for you and your crew?
We'll fix our ship and leave this place of sorrow behind.
None of us want to stay in Rinascita after what we've been through.
I guess we should say our goodbyes. So long, friend!
Oh, and if you're ever on a ship we've captured, you get to keep your stuff, haha!
But Insula's laughter is hollow. His expression is stony, and he sinks into silence.
Itzel mutters to herself while squeezing the compass pendant.
Come home Liel...
Insula appears downcast as if everything he sees and hears means nothing.
You find some fish left by Insula and Itzel, neatly laid in a box on the shore.
You figure they must have patched up their ship and sailed off with their crew.

Carlotta takes you to the "Masked Reverie" shop, where she has customized Carnevale masks for you and Abby. 
As you walk together under the night sky, Carlotta seems to have more she wishes to discuss...

During your conversation, Carlotta mentions the Black Shores, revealing that the Montelli family's intentions are more complex than they seem. 
The family isn't seeking to usurp the Order's power or undermine the faith. Rather, Carlotta explains, they're pursuing a truth about the origin of Rinascita.
As you walk to Palazzo Agrotta in the southern part of the city, where Carlotta has arranged a room for you, Carlotta shares an old story about Fleurdelys, the Blessed Maiden...

After finishing her tale, Carlotta confides her deeper thoughts: "If the Sentinel indeed permitted such a girl to serve as their spokesperson, it suggests that all this joyous revelry is not something They disdain." 
The Carnevale, she says, is meant to be a celebration of people's true selves. Yet now, it has become a tool for those who use faith to control others. But Carlotta believes that this year's Carnevale can will spark a flame fierce enough to burn down that cage.
Tomorrow, you and Carlotta will take the stage at the Carnevale. Tonight, all you need to do is rest and prepare.

Get some rest tonight for the Carnevale tomorrow.
Good night. May your dreams be sweet.

A large crowd has gathered in front of Trattoria Margherita. Curious, you approach and spot Zani, who's still hard at work during the festival. After a quick check, she concludes that the Echo "Bakie" is just overloaded with all the work.
After things settle down, Zani assures you that she and the Montelli members will be on duty here, ready to assist you if needed.

A short distance away, you notice C-MOSS, the Pioneer Association's Echo, looking downcast. Phoebe points out that it's probably disappointed it hasn't been able to capture a photo of itself at the Carnevale. 
Snap a picture of C-MOSS and Phoebe together to cheer it up.

With C-MOSS's wish granted, Fulmine arrives to thank you for your kindness. Phoebe, however, is bound by her duties to the Order. She needs to maintain order at the festival and can't join you for the rest of the Carnevale. 
You can see the excitement and joy in her eyes, though. With her blessings for you in mind, you decide to help keep the Carnevale safe.

Carlotta has been waiting for you. The troupe is set to arrive at the port any moment, and your performance is about to start. 
If you're ready, it's time to join Carlotta and prepare for the stage.

The Fool's Troupe makes its grand entrance to thunderous applause, and the city's excitement reaches a fever pitch. 
Amid the celebrations, you spot Phrolova, one of the Fractsidus Overseers, moving through the crowd.
You follow her trail to a rooftop, where she invites you to join her. Phrolova reveals that you're both searching for the same "special Resonator." As a gesture of goodwill, she offers to exchange a story with you, one that holds a hidden truth. 
Her tale needs a stage, and there is no better stage than Ragunna City at this moment.

With Phrolova's opening cue, your performance begins. 
Each of your allies plays their part to enhance the show, while the main stage is set for you and Carlotta to shine.
Phrolova summons a wave of Tacet Discords to block your path, but you and Carlotta manage to break through the obstacle and press on toward her location.
Once again, Phrolova conjures a deadly swarm of Tacet Discords...
You and Carlotta are surrounded by TDs, but Roccia arrives in time, diving headfirst into the fight to aid you.
Facing Phrolova's taunts, you stand firm and accept her challenge, ready to face the powerful Tacet Discords she has summoned.

At last, you reach Phrolova. It seems like the story should end here, but she has one last surprise. Unleashing her powers, she tears through the fabric of space itself, adding yet another twist to your tale.
You enter the Sonoro Sphere crafted by Phrolova. Here, she intends to tell you a story about a prophecy...

You and your companions defeat Phrolova and free Cetus the Tidebreaker from her control. The gloom that had shrouded the Carnevale lifts, and the crowd erupts into applause for your performance.
As daylight breaks through the clouds, a golden Laurel descends over your head, a reward as promised. The Sentinel's voice then echoes in your mind, directing you to Their location. If you wish to find Them, head to the Inverted Tower suspended in the sky, from where They watch over the world.
You notice a hint of vulnerability in the Sentinel's voice. They leave you with a final clue: a "lost" person, someone connected to Them, is currently among the people enjoying the festival.

Following the Sentinel's lead, you meet a girl named Cartethyia. Something unusual about her frequencies catches your attention, but she disappears into the crowd before you can learn more.
Later, Carlotta arrives and remarks that no one else seems to notice Cartethyia. She offers to have her family members search for the girl in Ragunna, but you urge caution. Too many mysteries surrounding the Order and the Sentinel remain unsolved. Hasty moves could draw unwanted attention from the Order and disrupt the Carnevale. Besides, you need time to piece together the clues you already hold.
For now, you decide to enjoy the festivities.
Hahaha! There you are, my friend! A compliment, if too subtle, loses all its charm!

Carlotta invites you to the Montelli family's safe house for a celebratory dinner. You and your friends raise a glass and share a rare moment of laughter. During the gathering, Carlotta reveals that Cartethyia is actually Fleurdelys, the Blessed Maiden. This new information helps you piece together the clues you've uncovered.
Carlotta also shares a shocking revelation from Gilberto regarding the history recorded in the ruins: The Fisalia family actually worships the Threnodian known as the "Leviathan" from the deep sea, a belief that may date back centuries. Rinascita's Sentinel and the Threnodian are connected, and if the situation demands, the Montelli family might seek a conversation with the Fisalia family.
Meanwhile, the Montellis will keep investigating the mysterious Inverted Tower, the other clue left by the Sentinel.
Soon after, you receive an invitation from the Primus, Fenrico, to the Cathedral of Mercury.

At the Cathedral of Mercury, you meet Fenrico. He apologizes for Alessio and others' deeds and promises to answer your questions as best he can.
In his words about the Sentinel, you catch a mention of the "Second Resonance Awakening." This raises suspicion—such a transfer of power from the Sentinel would require your permission.
When you press Fenrico about the true fate of Fleurdelys, he finally reveals a long-held secret: Fleurdelys was the Threnodian's Resonator.

After leaving the Cathedral, you discuss the findings with Abby. Every clue now seems to point back to the Threnodian mysteries, and you'll have to wait for Carlotta to contact the Fisalia family.
Gazing out over the tranquil sea of Rinascita, you feel a shiver of foreboding. The Carnevale is only a prologue... Everything is just beginning.

Not far away, Phrolova watches your every move. Beside her stands another Overseer, Cristoforo the "Playwright."
It seems his script is only starting to unfold...
Rest in peace Liel.
We'll destroy the real copy to kill it for good.

At the site, you're forced to subdue the rampaging Echo guards by force.

You are stopped by Echo guards at the outer part of Averardo Vault. Just as tensions rise, the noble lady you met before shows up, commanding the guards to stand down. 
She formally introduces herself as Carlotta Montelli, the second daughter of Montelli.

After defeating the Echo guard, Carlotta asks Zani to handle the cleanup.
You both head quickly to the tower ruins.

Arriving at the tower ruins, you find shattered stained glass telling the Sentinel's legend and the Order's founding by the first Primus. 
An ancient stone tablet stands nearby, waiting to be deciphered.

Carlotta successfully deciphers the prophecy inscribed on the stone tablet. 
To fully understand it, you may need to piece together the information from the tablet and the stained glass.

You restore the frequencies of the stained glass using your Sensor. 
With that, Carlotta tells you a legend about Rinascita's divinity.

Carlotta is stunned by the revelation: the legend speaks of two divinities in Rinascita, with the Enlightened One depicted as a young girl—a sharp contrast to the Order's teachings. She suspects the Order destroyed these ruins to conceal this truth. She hints that another secret lies on a northern island, but before she can elaborate, the Order's pursuers arrive.
Carlotta swiftly defeats the pursuers and tries to pry out more information, but Priest Alessio soon arrives with reinforcements.

Unable to persuade you to give up, Priest Alessio shows Capollo's pendant—proof of his capture—and uses the family tie to force Carlotta to "make the right choice." 
Carlotta quickly forms a silent plan. She pretends to aim her gun at you but instead shoots to dislodge debris, blocking the pursuers and opening an escape route for you. 
Now, it's time to head to the northern island and uncover the Order's buried secret.
Enough staring. Come on, let's go.
What happened to her?
I heard her ranting about her {Male=brother;Female=sister}...
You're back. I've been keeping a close eye on her, just in case she gets any... wild ideas about hurting anyone.
Funny enough, she's been holding it together. It's like she really has been waiting on you.
Really? That's good to hear.
You're finally back! Now I won't ever go hungry again! You must be exhausted from that trip, I'll prepare something for you to eat!
Dana takes the fish and quietly begins to skin it with her bare hands.
She's starting to lose her grip again. But now that you're back, no offense, but I'll be taking my leave... Good luck.
Hold on, do you know any of the people she talked about?
Those fancy Mister and Madam types? Ha! You think I know any toffee-nosed snobs like that? You might try asking Ahab, he knows just about everyone!
Got it. Thank you.
Dana serves up a plate piled high with messy fish pieces. She gazes at you like she's serving a feast.
How about we go to Madam Claire's first, Dana?
Oh, she wants to see us? Well, what are we waiting for? Let's go!
Oh, dear Madam Claire. Where could you be?
Do you... not wish to see me?
Ah... Madam Claire went out fishing, Dana.
Oh... How could this be?!
Wait. Is this a note from Madam Claire?
"The folk from the city grow stranger by the day..."
"Why don't you craft a few specimens to sell, Ronald? It could be a profitable venture."
So you've been to see Uncle Ronald, haven't you? Madam Claire. I'm coming for you!
Here, {Male=brother;Female=sister}! I finally caught it! Look how pretty it is!
Best keep your distance, friend. There's something off about her. Best not to get too close.
It's a strange one. She seemed fine when I offered her some food not long ago...
Who is she?
What happened to her?
Haven't the slightest clue. Doesn't seem to be from the Riccioli Islands the way she's dressed. Maybe the promise of adventure drew her from the city.
Something must've shaken her up. She seems all scrambled in the head.
Unusual fish seem to flock to these waters. City folk love coming here in hope of adding another rare trophy to their exotic collections.

These unknown waters are perilous. Those who lack respect for them are sure to invite misfortune. Every day, fools set out, never to return, yet still, the lure of adventure continues to draw in newcomers.
I overheard someone say that she and her {Male=brother;Female=sister} arrived asking about fishing some time ago.
I wonder why it's just her now...
I can't convince her to leave, and I have no idea who her family might be. Perhaps you could try talking to her again.
I can't wait to see the look on their faces once I bring this pretty little fish back, {Male=brother;Female=sister}.
Dana extends her scarred arms, revealing the broken pieces of a wine bottle she was holding.
Huh? {Male=Brother;Female=Sister}, you're hurt.
Oh, marvelous! Do you remember Uncle Ronald spoke of peculiar fish here that are drawn to people's wounds?
Hurry, we need to head out to sea. We must catch one, even if it costs us our lives! Imagine showing it to everyone in the city!
Do you promise to return to the city after we catch this fish?
Absolutely! I shall be the first to present this fish, and then no one will ever be able to deny that I am truly the greatest collector there is!
What does it look like?
You don't remember? I'll make a sketch for you.
The wind is too strong! We're taking on water, {Male=brother;Female=sister}. I need your help!
Dana stamps her feet impatiently, her empty hands seeming to tug at something invisible.
I found the fish you're looking for.
A new fish! A fish no one's ever laid eyes on! Oh, don't you dare die on me now. I won't let you rot away...
Uncle Ronald. I have to find Uncle Ronald, he's the finest taxidermist I know. He'll preserve your beauty forever.
Dana skips away happily with the fish clutched in her hands.
My fish, Uncle Ronald, you promised me you would help me. Where's my fish?!
W-Who in tarnation are you?! Get away from me!
It hurts... My face hurts... Please don't bite my face... Save me, {Male=brother;Female=sister}. {Male=Brother;Female=Sister}?
Dana? What are you still doing on the island?
My fish. The fish you gave me. I can't find it...
You notice the fish you caught for Dana dangling from her waist, exuding a foul, rotten stench.
I'm so sorry! Please don't be angry with me! I'll find your favorite fish and make it up to you!
My favorite fish?
Dana quickly scribbles a drawing of a fish.
This one! You told me it was your favorite fish when we were children! It still is, right? Please tell me I didn't get it wrong.
You don't need to go look for it. I already have it.
What? Where? Did you go out to sea without me? What treasures did you find? Show it to me!
I'll bring you the fish.
No, stop. Don't eat me. Get off! Get off me!
Why are there so many? Ack! My legs... My arms... You're not taking me too!
Dana swings her arms wildly trying to dodge you, as if she's in the water.
Don't you remember me?
Ah. {Male=Brother;Female=Sister}... How are you...? I saw you were... I saw it with my own eyes...
I've found the fish. We should go back.
So you managed to escape from all those fish. Not only that, you also found your favorite fish!
Yes, yes. Now that we have everything we want, it's time to return home and enjoy their beauty together.
Haha... Haha... You... You'll be a better collector than I'll ever be once we're back... I'm so thrilled for you!
Fishy... Oh, fishy, fishy... Come out, come out, wherever you are. I got a little treat for you.
Still here, huh?
Why the long face? There's plenty of room inside this fish tank, and look at all the lovely little fish keeping you company.
Hey... Did you throw your own {Male=brother;Female=sister} into the sea...?
Oh, don't cry. I'll help you find it. Anything for my dear {Male=brother;Female=sister}... Yes, anything...
(Trying to convince her to leave isn't getting anywhere. I should find her family and see if they can bring her home.)
Dana, where is your {Male=brother;Female=sister}?
{Male=He;Female=She}'s still in the sea. It's so cold there... I want to find {Male=him;Female=her}.
In the sea? You mean {Male=he;Female=she}'s...
I can't go home alone! We made a promise! This is what {Male=he;Female=she} looks like. No, more like... this. I must bring {Male=him;Female=her} back.
Dana scribbles frantically on the ground. She draws a fish.
Suddenly, Dana panics and bolts toward the sea. You catch her just in time.
Get your hands off me! Who do you think you are?! I am a noble! An invitation bearer! A true collector! Let me go this instant!
We're here bringing gifts for Mr. Doria. Quick, {Male=brother;Female=sister}. Show him the gifts we prepared.
(If there's a chance she'll mistake that fish for her {Male=brother;Female=sister}, maybe bringing it back will convince her to leave?)
Okay. I'll go get it.
Hmph. Just you wait and see, peasants!
Dana, I found your "{Male=brother;Female=sister}."
Dana reaches out to the fish in surprise and begins stroking its scales.
Oh, {Male=brother;Female=sister}! I'm sorry... I'm sorry... I didn't mean to kick you into the water... They just liked your taste better...
I didn't want to die... You reached out to pull me in, right? It was either you or me...
So your {Male=brother;Female=sister} is already gone.
I saw those fish first! You can't take them from me! I'm the better collector! I'm the one and only genius!
If I bring these back to Madam Claire, she'll let me into her salon, right? No one will ever look down on us again.
(Let's hope she stays in this delusion until she makes it back to the city.)
Dana holds the fish tightly, thrusting it toward the fishermen who recoil in discomfort.
Take a good look at this fish, Mr. Doria. It's a species thought to be extinct! I spent three days and nights at sea searching for it.
Oh, Madam Claire, may I join your salon now? I've completed all the extra tasks you set for me. You promised...
What she got in her hands...? Is that a rotten fish...?
I don't understand a word she's saying. Isn't that just a normal fish?
You gave me your promise! Why would you all lie to me?! WHY?! WHY?!
Whoa! Easy there, miss! Someone find a way to calm her down!
Dana, it's me. Just breathe, please!
As Dana notices you, her frantic energy shifts. Tears begin to stream down her face.
{Male=Brother;Female=Sister}. Oh, {Male=brother;Female=sister}... I'm so sorry... I let you down... I went looking for them, but...
They... They kept changing their promises. They never intended to accept us into the family...
Don't cry. We'll figure something out.
Do you really think there's hope? If we offer them another rare fish... will they accept us then?
They will. What kind of fish do you have in mind?
I-I was thinking... What about this one? You can only find it around the Riccioli Islands. It's extremely rare.
If we catch this fish, does that mean we'll finally bear the family name? Imagine, they might even fetch us in a carriage!
Exactly. I'll go get the fish, and you stay here and wait for me, okay?
Okay. I'll be a good girl. Please be careful, {Male=brother;Female=sister}.

Did you come all this way for me, or are you in search of the secrets slumbering in the deep?
I come for you.
I come for the secrets.
Both.
Oh, I'm flattered… Don't worry, with someone as precious as you here in my castle, I'm not going anywhere.
Hehe, clever little fish… Have you figured it out? The answer has been right here, waiting to be discovered.
Hehe, such greed… Rest assured, I'm here to unravel the secrets with you, as I promised.
What exactly are the Sea Apples and the Jellyroses in the garden used for?

The crimson Sea Apple, also called "the alluring reaper," is a dangerous plant. A single bite can lead to paralysis, suffocation, or the excruciating pain of a burnt throat and torn organs—ultimately bringing its victim an agonizing death.

As for the Jellyroses, their blooms will transform into Jellyrose Medusae. These little ones can produce a neurotoxin that induces intense hallucinations, and in extreme cases, causes the body to seize and twist in a violent, uncontrollable dance of death.
The two lethal plants have been meticulously nurtured by generations of the Fisalia family, flourishing within the gardens of Porto-Veno Castle for centuries.
So my guess was correct. The "Red Apple" in the second riddle refers to the Sea Apple, and the "Round Hat" in the last riddle points to the Jellyrose Medusa.

As for the first riddle, "Siren's Song," the "crown atop the mountain" and the "waterfall that cascaded into the depths below" clearly points here—a crown-like castle that sits atop a jagged cliff, with a waterfall rushing down.
It seems the girls in the riddle were lured into the Porto-Veno Castle.
The strange frequencies coming from the music box probably reflect the suffering of the "ghost girls," who were poisoned and tortured in the castle.
But why?
I don't believe you'd engage in such senseless cruelty or take pleasure in others' suffering.
There should be a reason behind this… Wait, there's one Fisalia tradition that might explain it. The Divine Trials.
It's a ritual to select a maiden of extraordinary willpower, a Fisalia who can withstand the Threnodian's whispers. I assume such extreme methods were needed for the trials.
Well… I never imagined you'd solve the mystery so quickly. You never cease to amaze me.
The truth behind the "ghost girl" riddle is none other than the grim secret of the Divine Trials.
The blood and tears shed in these trials throughout the years have seeped into this castle and concocted what we now call <ano=Sonoro Sphere>the Sea of Ghosts</ano>.
There, past and future intertwine, and Fisalia's ancient secrets cling to the cracks of time like grotesque scabs.
With you by my side, I would relive that trauma, and unfold the layers of forsaken time for a closer look.
And if… you find these scabs have somehow crept unto my very flesh and feel the need to cut them away, I'll place my full trust in you and leave it in your hands.
Why do you trust me so much?
Can I trust you?
Ever since I guided you to the sanctuary… you've seen through me and all that the Fisalia family conceals.
I've witnessed you cleanse the chaos of the Inverted Tower, restoring order to the heavens and seas. If you are the one to pass final judgment on me… it would be the highest honor.
Absolutely. Remember my promise? Whether it's elixir or poison, I'm ready to explore it with you.
I, Cantarella Fisalia, value every promise I made to you and vow to see them through.
Now, the answers we seek lie in the depths of fierce undercurrents… Will you join me and dive into the deep sea?
Sure. I'm good at swimming.
Of course. I've seen it all.
Yes. We must free those ghosts.
Yes. I have to remove the influence on me.
Then let's dive in together.
You're like a pearl from the deepest sea, but… I'd never let such a flawless gem endure even the smallest scratch.
I knew you'd say that.
Your wisdom, courage, and kindness… no matter how deep the waters, always shine through.
Mmm, the strange frequency you carry is indeed from the Sea of Ghosts.
That message with the distorted frequency is no doubt a creation of this Sonoro.
I don't know why it reached you, but the answer is hidden within. After we uncover the truth, its influence on you will fade.
Once we enter the sea, I'll be right by your side, tightly. No poisonous creature shall harm you.
For you are the one I've chosen.
I think I'm ready to go now.
I need some time to get ready.
Excellent. Together we dive into the Sea of Ghosts.
Of course. It's wise to ready yourself before diving into such perilous depths.
I'll be waiting for you in the garden, whenever you're ready.
