Teacher, the Seminary will soon be engulfed. What should we do?
We have to leave… but we can't go without the relic. We can't let it be lost to the sea of clouds.
The Seminary is but stone and tile. It can always be rebuilt. My days are numbered, but until my last breath, I will protect the sage's relic, no matter the cost.
I heard a fascinating tale while we've been here, {PlayerName}. Would you care to listen?
What sort of tale?

It's a fishermen's legend passed down for generations on this island. It speaks of Rinascita during the ancient Age of a Thousand Islands, when the Riccioli Islands were ruled by a sailor driven from his homeland.
This sailor possessed untold riches, yet no one knew the source of his fortune.
He used his vast wealth to build a citadel that brought peace and prosperity to the people of the land.
Just when they prepared to build a monument to honor him, he vanished without a trace.
Whispers claimed he sailed away to seek revenge for a dark past.
Before he departed, he left behind his most cherished treasures on these islands and set forth on a path of revenge, never to return.
I'm curious what kind of treasure a man like that would leave behind. It must've held great significance to him.
Shall we set out to uncover it?
I can hear the treasure calling to me!
I knew you'd be intrigued! Perhaps we could seek out someone well-versed in these legends? They may hold the key to our quest.
The Acolyte? Back again so soon?
Mr. Toretto, we're here to learn more about the "Sailor's Treasure."
Since when did the Order start caring about treasure?
Err. No, actually...
Ah, spare me the details! Treasure hunters come and go, you lot are a dime a dozen. You'll end up empty-handed like the rest of 'em anyway.
Maybe we'll find it. You never know.
Awfully sure of yourself, aren't ya? You know how long ago the Age of a Thousand Islands was. Besides that old legend, there's not a sliver of evidence proving any of it is true.
Without real clues, it's just a wild goose chase. The islands have already been turned upside down by those treasure hunters, and not a single coin has been found.
Are there any other stories about the sailor?
Other stories, you ask? Lemme see... There's the Wandering Gondola. Or there's the Master of the Fish King...
Tell us about the Wandering Gondola.
Tell us about the Master of the Fish King.
I don't have any more to ask.
Legend has it a sailor arrived here in a Gondola. Even after he disappeared, it still drifts among these islands waiting for his return.
The Fish King is a notorious foe for any fisherman. Legend claims that once a sailor caught one in these very waters.
No one has caught one since. They say a Fish King only heeds the call of someone as great as that sailor.
All right, you already know what you need to know. Off you go, then. I'll be watching to see if you can find that treasure, ha!
What do you make of the clues, {PlayerName}?
Finding that Gondola might be a good start.
Good idea. The sailor may have vanished, but if his Gondola is still here we may be able to find some clues.
Phoebe attempts to communicate with the Echo and decipher what it's saying.
They seems to know something! It may be trying to guide us in a certain direction... Shall we go take a look?
Onwards!
I never expected to actually find something... This appears to be...
Looks like a treasure map. A piece of one at least.
There looks to be something inscribed inside the chest. Hmm... It's hard to make out. The script is unfamiliar to me.
Let's ask a reliable local for advice.
Ah, well met, friends! What's this ye've got there?
Phoebe shares the story of your treasure hunt with Ahab and shows him the chest with the inscriptions.
So, ye're telling me this here chest is from that legendary sailor?! Let me have a look.
Hmm... there's a seal coverin' up these inscriptions. Can't get a good look at 'em. Heh, but watch me!
Ahab searches the surrounding area and returns with a unique plant. He squeezes it to extract its sap and applies it to the chest. Almost immediately, the inscriptions become clear.
See that? It's an old trick we used to write hidden messages. Now we can read what it says.
"No victory is instant. The truth must be pieced together bit by bit."
It seems like... we need to gather the rest of this map to find the treasure.
Let's keep our eyes peeled from now on, {PlayerName}.
I wonder what that sailor left behind. Endless riches? Ancient relics?
Or perhaps... a Fish King?
Huh? Hahaha. Never thought I'd hear that from an Acolyte!
Thanks, Ahab. We'll make sure to share the treasure with you once we find it.
That's mighty generous, but I'm content with me lot in life. Whatever you find, keep it for yerselves!
"Someone has surely found that legendary sailor's treasure by now."
"If you can't see it, just try squeezing some waterweed juice onto it."
"What? Any waterweed will do. Do you think a sailor has time to be choosy?"
"No victory is instant. The truth must be pieced together bit by bit."
"Search for all the scraps of that treasure map. Piece it together, and who knows what you might discover?"

[About]

John Wicktorio, a retired Acolyte and accountant of the Order, found his cherished Echo brutally killed by some thugs.
Determined to settle the scores and avenge his old pal, he's stepping back into the game to make the culprits pay.

[Eligibility]

Reach Union Level 14 and unlock the Resonance Nexus in Ragunna City during the Main Quest: "The Sacred Breeze So Often Breathes."

[Event Rules]

1. During the event, you will enter a special sphere to battle waves of enemies within a set time limit, with the aid of unique buffs.

2. You will collect Coins by dealing damage to enemies, but taking damage will cause you to lose Coins.

3. Progressing through enemy waves unlocks more special buffs to give you the support you need.

4. The Coins you have collected by the end of the countdown will be your Coins record of this stage.

5. Defeating each enemy wave grants additional time.

You repel the Tacet Discords, saving both the pilgrims and the troupe members. 
Roccia thanks you and explains the origins of the pilgrims.

Together, you and Roccia rescue the pilgrims. 
Some are badly injured, others are starving, and none are in good shape.

The pilgrims need better shelter, so Tina takes them back to the troupe. 
Roccia volunteers to stay behind for a final checkup, and you decide to accompany her.
Pero discovers a dying little girl in the cabin.

You return to the troupe, where Tina is preparing pasta. 
Meanwhile, Roccia is busy patching up the little girl. You decide to go lend a hand.

Roccia carefully tends to the little girl. She then asks about the condition of the other pilgrims. 
Tina informs you two that the others have been fed and are recovering from their injuries, though they remain mentally drained. 
You encourage the introverted Roccia to ask the pilgrims directly about their well-being and explore how else she can help.

Filippo’s arm has mostly recovered, but he remains deeply depressed. 
He recounts how Ragunna, under the Order's rule, strictly regulated theatrical performances. 
He and others were exiled for performing the banned opera, "Pegasus." 
During their exile, many of their companions perished in perilous encounters, leaving the survivors unable to continue the beloved opera.
Giulio, another exile, shares his longing for the freedom celebrated in "Pegasus" and his deep nostalgia for his departed partner.

After speaking with the pilgrims, Roccia concludes that their biggest wish is to perform "Pegasus" with their companions once again. 
As a stage prop maker, Roccia resolves to collect and repair the objects left behind by her partners so she can participate in the welcoming opera alongside them.
Roccia begins setting up the stage and preparing props for the welcoming opera. You help her inventory the items Pero brought back to determine how they can best be used.

Roccia reflects on the ship debris. These fragments once belonged to a Pilgrim's Sail—a vessel that carried everyone’s fear and confusion, while also recording their resilience and defiance. 
The debris is large and well-suited for use as scene props for the stage.

Roccia shares with you the significance of Luceanites. 
Legend has it that each Luceanite is a soul trapped on the Strand. 
If left exposed in the wild, the stone loses its light and must be collected in time. 
Bright Luceanites are ideal for creating star clusters to decorate stage ceilings.

Roccia tells you about a petal—a fragment of a wreath that once belonged to a little boy who didn’t survive the shipwreck. 
The petals are soft and fragile, and Roccia carefully considers how they might be incorporated into the welcoming opera.

The initial stage setup is complete, but Roccia notices that the stars aren’t shining brightly enough. 
The North Star, a symbol of hope in "Pegasus," should shine even brighter. 
Roccia recalls Filippo mentioning that people sang under a star on the boat and decides to ask him for more information.
Filippo reveals that the star belonged to Luca. Pero, sensing that Luca may have woken up, goes to investigate.

Luca cries upon realizing her star is lost. 
She believes it has always been the star that blessed everyone and that misfortune strikes when the star is gone. 
You and Roccia comfort the weak Luca and promise to help her find the star.

You and Roccia search the ship but find no star-like objects. 
Objects imbued with emotional frequencies resonate with their users, so Roccia decides to use familiar items to help the pilgrims. 
She resolves to create a new "star" to perfect the "Pegasus" ensemble. For Roccia, "possibility" means "hope."

Roccia notices an unusual mist rising around her and goes on guard. 
The play Pegasus warns to be careful in misty conditions. You decide to hurry up.

You discover some clams. 
The troupe isn't high on budget and often has to eat whatever they can find nearby. 
Roccia takes the clams to make a pot of clam soup for everyone.

You find a Luceanite, which Roccia carefully stores away. 
Meanwhile, Pero suddenly perks up, as if it's made an important discovery.

Pero finds footprints that emit star frequencies, though they’re jumbled and hard to decipher. 
You volunteer to investigate further.

As you venture deeper, the rising mist surrounds you, forming a maze. 
The open door seem to invite you in.

Roccia realizes the misty maze resembles a scene from "Pegasus." 
Together, you conclude that the maze must be man-made and decide to explore what lies within.

At the end of the maze, you find a cavern shrouded in mist. 
Inside, the pitch-black cavern is filled with stars and something you can't recognize.

You return to the troupe with the Plushies. 
Roccia suggests letting them to help set up the stage. You tell Luca that her star has been found.
Luca, overjoyed, lets you lend her star for the welcoming opera.

Back at the stage, the Plushies reveal a startling truth: their owners never abandoned them—they were exiled. 
To protect their Echoes from the Order, which sought to erase their frequencies entirely, the owners made the painful decision to leave them behind. 
At the theater, some Plushies are joyfully reunited with their owners, while others discover cherished items their owners once held dear.

After the show, Roccia returns the borrowed stage props to their rightful owners. 
The audience leaves, satisfied with their reclaimed belongings. 
As the stage empties, only one Luceanite remains.
You recognize it as Roccia’s Luceanite.

Roccia, sensing something different in you, invites you to join the Fool’s Troupe. 
Together, you performed the perfect welcoming opera, giving everyone the freedom to bring laughter back to Ragunna. 
Your ideals and the troupe’s ideals align, making them your steadfast allies and support.

Thanks to your efforts, Roccia’s first orientation and return-to-sail event was a success. 
In addition to paying you for lending a hand, Roccia has a special gift for you.

Roccia reflects on a lunachord left behind by the Pilgrim’s Sail. 
Its owner sought to ease everyone’s hearts through music, and they performed till the last second of their life. 
Though the lunachord has lost its strings, Roccia replaces them with something new, transforming it into a stage prop to inspire others.

(A tourism guide penned by the Pioneer Association. But the column about Egla Town hasn't been updated in quite a while.)

[The Next Big Travel Hot Spot]: Egla Town!
For those brave enough to venture to the place that inspired the adventurous plays during the Carnevale, exploring the legendary realm of the mighty "giant," listening to the songs echoing from the sea of clouds by the water, or following in the footsteps of knights in pursuit of honor and justice will no longer be mere fantasies. In Egla Town, travelers can immerse themselves in breathtaking waterside scenery, observe the majestic migration of Tumbleyaks, and watch windmills spin gracefully on the plains, while bathing in the golden light of the setting sun. Alternatively, they can simply enjoy a peaceful afternoon tea and indulge in century-old delicacies, all while being surrounded by the vibrant colors of blooming flowers.

[Dreamy Destinations] Nimbus Sanctum!
In this edition of [Dreamy Destinations], we journey to the mesmerizing Nimbus Sanctum hidden deep within Whisperwind Haven. A highlight of the enchanting Gondola cruise, the sea of clouds has long been a must-see destination, captivating visitors with its ethereal, dreamlike vistas.
Yet, few are aware that the Atrium of Reflections—often depicted in romantic tales—is not merely a creation of fiction, but the ruins of the highest spire of ancient Ragunna. To save its people, Napoli the Second invoked a miracle, turning the Dark Tide into the very sea of clouds that graces the land today.
The forgotten ruins of old Egla Town are now submerged beneath the sea of clouds.

[The Journey is the Destination] Embark Today!
It's worth noting that, although the reason remains unclear, the water level of Nimbus Sanctum has been steadily rising over the past decade, forcing the residents of Egla Town to move to the higher ground in the north.
Once, this area was a barren, undeveloped land, scattered with exposed boulders, and known as the Whisperwind Barrens.
However, the resourceful people of Egla Town began to build windmills that turned day and night, drawing water from the lower regions to nourish the land above. Their efforts transformed this rugged place into the thriving Whisperwind Haven we see today, where crops and flowers now flourish in the breeze.

(A short novel published ten years ago.
"An outrageous best-seller, banned by the Order three times!"
"Only one-tenth of readers truly understand it—are you one of them?"
"Incredible! The Russellian's satire remains as insightful as ever, even after all these years!"
So reads the editor's recommendation page… Clearly, this book stirred up quite a bit of controversy a decade ago.)

Far out across the stormy waters filled with jagged ridges and giant beasts on the surface of Solaris lies a group of small, unregarded islands. On this archipelago, the exiles-descended cultures are so amazing that they still think a unified thought is a pretty neat idea. These islands have—or rather had a problem, which was this: most of the people on them were unhappy for pretty much of the time.

After retirement, I kept thinking back to that afternoon when my friend and I first met.
Ford Percival. He was an alien.
On his first day in Egla Town, he ate ten baton bread without paying anything. Before the Divine Envoys could punish him for theft, I quickly paid off his debt.
Since the prayer, the Oracle of Mercy had wandered in my mind in search of something to connect with—until I met him, the poor outlander. He must have been starving.
"Hi, I'm Ford. I'm an alien. I'm analyzing your weapons. Quite odd components."
He said after I saved him. "And what is this place?" he continued.
An alien? Oh, I'd heard this kind of tale once from someone who claimed to be from a federation. He said Solaris was actually a living tomato—a tomato that could turn, breathe, even dance. And aliens, apparently, were from other tomatoes, living or dead.
"Egla Town," I replied.
"Egla Town, good. Wait, what is that?" He pointed at the windmills in the distance.
"Those are windmills. A cluster of Cyclop windmills, Briareos." Born and raised in Egla, I replied almost instinctively.
"C-Cyclops! Ah, I know about those! I've seen them before! But my stars—you actually managed to kill them? How did you people pull that off? Are those auto-rotating arrays made from their dead bodies? And what exactly is Briareos? A cooling device? A propeller engine? Or something to open up a network channel?"

(Continued)

After hearing my explanation, the self-proclaimed alien Ford seemed completely fascinated by the Cyclops. His emotions became so agitated that he plopped down on the ground, muttering some unintelligible words while pointing at the windmills in the distance.
So it was true—no matter where they came from, no matter what "tomatoes" they hailed from, anyone who laid eyes on the scenery of Egla couldn't help but fall in love with the chivalric literature.
So I straightened up, took three steps forward, and adjusted the nonexistent necktie, then explained graciously, "Exactly! That's right! Once, a righteous knight guided us to defeat the giant. Before that, all the people and Echoes in Egla Town were driven to the high ground in the south, fleeing from the giant's threat. Now, that oppressor lies buried beneath the sea of flowers. We built majestic windmills to irrigate the flowers and the farmlands, and named our past home Briareos, in honor of that knight's heroic deeds!"
After hearing my speech, Ford sat frozen on the ground, as if ten thousand Cetus the Tidebreakers had roared at him all at once, shattering his perception.
After a long pause, he asked me in disbelief, "Do you still have knights here?"
What did he just ask me?
Praise be to Imperator!
I could finally deliver the ranked No. 1 answer in the Top 10 Most Satisfying Moments for Egla People.
Putting on a solemn expression like the Acolytes of the Order, I envisioned a halo of nobility above my head, envisioned the almighty Imperator spreading wings before me, envisioned myself crowning a laurel at the Carnevale, envisioned standing in the grand church, wielding a sword as I was knighted, relishing the reverent gazes of the noble lords of Ragunna!
I replied, stressing each word with great emphasis:
"OF COURSE—"
"However, there are too many outsiders who seek the path of knighthood. Are you confident enough to accept the trial?"
The alien named Ford, whose Tacet Mark was blinking along excitedly, quickly grabbed my calf and shook it furiously, as if clinging to a log in the midst of a drowning. He cried out, "I am! I am! Please guide me to the legendary knight! As long as I can return to the planet Russel and save my hometown, I am willing to pay any price!"

(A feature on the culinary traditions of Ragunna.)

[Top Chef's Super Secrets]
Imagine yourself asking anyone on the streets of Ragunna, "Which restaurant is the best in Ragunna?"
Six out of ten will answer, "Trattoria Margherita!" Three will point to the family restaurant downtown, and the last one will say, "It's the place where the soft-tailed chef works!"
That's right! Such is the clout of Trattoria Margherita in Ragunna!
Amazing!
But what many don't know is that Trattoria Margherita is actually a family-run restaurant inspired by traditional Ragunna cuisine. From our investigation, we found that Egla Town still preserves this classic culinary tradition to this day. To maintain the special flavors of her dishes, Miss Margherita even takes time off to gather ingredients in Egla Town or Riccioli Islands!
Now, you might be wondering: "What? I can understand why Miss Margherita would go to Riccioli Islands for the fish harvest, but Egla Town? Isn't that a backwater town? And can the cuisine of Egla really be called Ragunna cuisine?"
Indeed, life in Egla isn't as thrilling as in the bustling Ragunna. People there live quietly, following the rhythm of nature. The town's trade and logistics are tied to Ragunna City. The people rise with the wind and rest by it, living a life shaped by windmills, wheat farms, and pastures.
But that's exactly why, for hundreds of years, the cuisine of Egla has remained unchanged. Here, the original flavors and cooking techniques of Ragunna have been preserved—using windmills to process crops and cooking food in traditional ways.
"This way, the ingredients and the food are especially precious! The cheese made from local pastures is creamy, and the meat is tender and flavorful! It's the perfect food to fill your belly!"
Miss Margherita commented during our interview.

[Comments from Special Guests]
Former Tax Envoy of the Order: The traditional cuisine is a remembrance of Rinascita's past. To forget it is to betray our heritage!
Orlando the Gourmet: The old man earlier sounded like he was chanting a slogan! What traditional cuisine? The bread from your town is as hard as a lethal weapon!

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part I)
...

At dawn, the Primus and I stood to bid farewell to the Pilgrim's Sail as it prepared to depart. Both the crowd and the acolytes watched with reverence as the believers boarded the ship. Only the most devout and courageous among them were chosen to embark on the Pilgrim's Sail, destined to meet the Sentinel in the distant sea.

For countless ages, Sentinel Imperator has rarely lingered in any one place, choosing instead to roam the seas, aiding vessels on their journeys. The Sentinel's guiding light has always led those lost upon the waves, helping them find their way back home or seek new lands for settlement. The Order believes that to face the storms and tides in search of the Sentinel's heavenly voice is one of the greatest honors a soul can aspire to.

Yet only those with practical experience can grasp the immense cost of each pilgrimage. Taxes and provisions are drawn from the commoners, skilled workers and sailors are taken from prominent families, and seasoned captains and chief mates are hired at great expense. All who embark on these treacherous seas are devout, but only those truly blessed by the Sentinel return with the promised glory and honor. Reflecting on history, the number of such fortunate souls is vanishingly small.

I have never questioned the purpose of the pilgrimage. My only concern is the immense cost it demands. Can we, in good conscience, allow these devoted believers to embark on a journey that burdens both mind and body? And as for our new Primus... What are his thoughts on this matter?

I looked to my side, surprised to find that my former seminary classmate, Lord Fenrico, had his face shrouded in a strange shadow.

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part II)
...

How has it come to this? After a sleepless night, I retreated to a secluded prayer room, seeking solace as I lay my confession before Sentinel Imperator. My hands trembled as I put these words to paper.

For a time, the Order ceased organizing large-scale pilgrimages, and the burdensome taxes were lifted. Though the people of Ragunna still honored the devotion of those who once sought the Sentinel across the distant seas, the Pilgrim's Sails had become a relic of the past. But everything changed after the bloody Carnevale... No, in truth, the shift began even earlier than that...

I still remember when the Primus delivered the order for correction, and I dutifully transcribed it: the Order would send violators of doctrine aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, stripping them of all official identities and setting them back onto the path of pilgrimage. Who could have foreseen that an act once meant to embody faith would come to serve as a form of punishment?

"The power of punishment and indoctrination shall be returned to the Sentinel," the Primus proclaimed to the assembled crowd. "Those transgressors who embark upon the pilgrimage in sincere repentance will, by their journey's end, be absolved of all transgressions and granted the Sentinel's forgiveness."

Yet no one truly knows if transgressors can fulfill their salvation, for no one has ever returned from the pilgrimage alive. "Those who commit acts of foolishness shall be sent to the Pilgrim's Sails"—this has become a steadfast law of the Order Penitentiary. Vandals defacing sacred statues, disloyal acolytes distorting doctrines, and even troupe members crafting satirical comedies—all have been condemned to the Pilgrim's Sails for their acts of blasphemy. Recently, however, familiar faces have joined their ranks, faces of those who had openly questioned the Primus's decrees.

I could have sworn my integrity on their faith and character, yet I stood by and watched as they were sent aboard the Pilgrim's Sails, doing nothing. No, it's no longer fitting to call them the Pilgrim's Sails. The common folk have given them a more appropriate name—the Fool's Sails, a vessel filled with those who have committed foolish acts.

Oh, Primus Fenrico... Is this the dream world you so passionately spoke of in the seminary?

...

Former Privy Councilor's Notes (Part III)
...

I was surprised at how calm I felt upon hearing the sentence from the Order Penitentiary. Perhaps my heart had grown as still as that of a dead person.

At dawn, like others before me, I was escorted by the Executors to board a Fool's Sail. Before the ship set sail, I glanced back at the port, only to find the Primus absent. Just as I expected, that man, now in control of unmatched power within the Order, has no need to concern himself with a fool stripped of his identity.

The Fool's Sails are nothing like the Pilgrim's Sails of old. Gone are the smooth, spacious decks and well-maintained sails. Instead, all I saw were rickety planks, loose screws, and splintered masts. The narrow cabins clearly lacked food and fresh water. I stared blankly at the other pilgrims around me. For now, we still manage to maintain some semblance of decorum and restraint, but I know that, before long, this ship will become nothing more than a cage filled with rampaging desires.

And even if we do reach the so-called destination, what awaits us there?

I once read the investigation reports sent back by the expatriate acolytes. That Penitent's End, shrouded in mist, is littered with the wrecks of Pilgrim's Sails. During those fateful voyages, the Fools who braved the storms never met the Sentinel. Instead, driven by the sea's undercurrents, they were cast ashore on that island, where the eerie glow of phosphorescence mingles with an unmistakable aura of death. I've even heard whispers of something far more terrifying lurking there, and the "Fire of Judgment"—a force so dreadful that even the Privy Council dares not speak of it.

...

Food is running out... Last night, someone lost control again, trying to lock themselves in the cabin to hoard the dwindling supplies...

O great Imperator, if you can hear my prayer, please grant us your final mercy through a storm. Absolve us from our misery, and let us... find peace at last.

(The remainder of the notes has been blurred by the seawater and is unreadable.)
Former Privy Councilor's Notes

Later, with the assault of the Lament, the civilization of the archipelago teetered on the brink of destruction and our family became one of the founders of the Ark, embarking on a quest to find a new settlement. The journey across the sea was treacherous. The fleets of the Ark were either swallowed by thick fog or torn apart by fierce storms. Yet, our family's Ark, guided by a heavenly voice, led the fleet to a lush archipelago, following the faint glow of a distant lighthouse. One of those islands would later become what is now Ragunna. The newly founded Ragunna was still in a state of flux. To strengthen the family's rule, our family head declared that the manifestation of ▇▇▇▇ was a symbol of the deep-sea faith and a response from the marine divinity to our devotion. This proclamation proved to be successful. As the number of believers grew, so too did the stability of our family's power. Later, some fishermen claimed that they had been assisted by ▇▇▇▇ during their fishing trips. This entity, long known as the Giant One, had existed for ages. Its shadow beneath the sea guided Ragunna's fishermen and fleets, helping them weather storms and bringing in harvests far greater than before. The Fisalia family was the original ruler of Ragunna, and we also laid the faith foundation of the Order. Yet, why have generations of family heads chosen to conceal this history? Why can't I remember Its name? Cursed be it, the wound... it is throbbing again. Something must be wrong with the air... I must find a safer place. Excerpts from The Hammer of Heresy (The pamphlet presents several radical opinions that appear to reflect the theories of an extreme school of thought.) What is witchcraft? And what is its true nature? The power of Resonance wielded by Resonators is known as a blessing from Sentinel Imperator. Devout followers of the Order are granted this blessing by adhering to its precepts, allowing them to channel the divine force through mortal bodies. Witchcraft, however, arises from vain desires—faithless souls, drawn by Leviathan, form a contract to practice forbidden arts. In doing so, they forsake the divine blessing bestowed upon them at birth and abandon their humanity, transforming into witches who seek to taint the mortal realm with profane power. The Divinity has shaped our world, and all that we hold dear flows from Their blessings. Yet witches, seduced by the Arch Enemy, pervert these divine creations into impure, disgraceful entities, crafting a false Resonance with them. The enemy's mark upon these witches is proof of their transgressions. With the aid of the Vessel of the Enemy, they can even transform into Tacet Discords, posing a grave threat to Imperator's faithful followers. Caution is essential, for anyone who craves freedom and worldly desires is vulnerable to becoming pawns of Leviathan. Thus, we must regularly cleanse and exorcise such souls. If we allow these heretics to grow unchecked, wielding their tainted power to defile the mortal realm, they will inevitably bring the Dark Tide upon Rinascita. It is the Order's duty to guide and govern them, ensuring they align with Imperator's divine will. Should they refuse to join the Order, swear loyalty to Imperator's statute, or diligently uphold its teachings, their misguided fate will be set right by the Pilgrim's Sails. We shall pray for them day and night, that they may be saved by our Sentinel Imperator. Praise be to Imperator. The Spy Network of the Order the Deep Ah, my friend, my companion on this quest for freedom and truth, I implore you—open this pamphlet only in a secure place, away from prying eyes. What I am about to reveal is crucial to your safety. Learn now how to identify the spies of the Order the Deep and evade their grasp. All Echoes bearing a golden halo upon their heads are spies of the Order the Deep, serving as "Angels." They are always seen alongside the Acolytes, serving as the Order's minions to take out the heretics. Rinascita, the Land of Echoes? Ha... not even the greatest satire could ever truly capture the utter absurdity of the reality we endure. First, you must beware of those lantern Echoes, known as Lucerna. Though they may appear harmless, they possess the ability to reveal so-called heretics hiding in the shadows of the night. Their light can illuminate the path ahead, yet it also serves as a blinding weapon, causing one to lose their sense of direction. There was once an instance where someone used Fae Ignis's Echo ability to remain concealed, only to be exposed under the unforgiving glow of a Lucerna's light. Next, there are the most commonly seen plaster statues, the infamous La Guardia, the most loyal guardians of the Order. Without commands from the Acolytes, they stand motionless, like silent statues. However, if you find yourself pursued by La Guardia, do not waste time fighting them. Instead, focus on locating the Acolyte of the Order Penitentiary who is issuing the command. Among all these minions, the most detestable is Vox Sanctus, perched high atop the church buildings. They serve as the Order's guards of honor. While they cannot move freely, they use their instruments to preach false doctrines day and night. These sermons infiltrate the souls of the Ragunnesi, poisoning their thoughts. Can you imagine that the children of Ragunna are forced to hear this nonsensical preaching the moment they are born into this world? Oppression by force may still leave room for resistance, but in Ragunna, how can one escape the spiritual chains that seep into every corner of life? A Comprehensive Study of the History of Ragunnesi Drama (with Commentary) A Comprehensive Study of the History of Ragunnesi Drama: The Evolution of Tribal Cultural Fusion and Faith Systems Written by: DeLillo Quentin Proposed Grant: Ragunna Dramatic Association Regional Research Project - Aspire Scholars Grant Avinoleum Theological Seminary, Ragunna, Rinascita Abstract: This paper reviews recent research trends and developments regarding the origins of drama culture in the Ragunna and Septimont regions, with a particular focus on advancements in the "archaeology of drama" over the past decade. Drawing on the diverse research and perspective studies from the New Federation in recent years, the paper also incorporates insights from Huanglong's archaeological experience in studying historical relics. The case studies selected focus primarily on classic plays and significant historical events. The findings suggest that Ragunnesi drama culture originated from narrative performances that documented the history and life of island tribes. Keywords: history of drama, cultural studies, review, folklore studies, archaeology ...(Some of the pages are missing) As illustrated in key literature such as Chronicles of Avinoleum and The Golden Bough, the origin of drama is directly tied to the faith of Sentinel Imperator. However, technical studies of stage design, costumes, makeup, masks, and props, as found in both historical and modern literature, as well as translated foreign texts, reveal that much remains to be explored regarding the evolution of drama as a reflection of life and folklore. For instance, the Montelli Culture Foundation's Cultural Characteristics and Cultural Reconstruction in Translation: A Case Study of the Journey to Rinascita Collected in Huanglong examines the transition from folk traditions to their textual and stage representations in drama, focusing on the evolution of the translated texts. Seminary Commentary: Please do not submit the anecdotal piece for Almanacs and the Occult to our foundation. Additionally, food security must be more strictly managed to prevent potential nervous breakdowns among students caused by consuming spoiled bell crabs. ...(Some of the pages are missing) The people of Rinascita during the Age of a Thousand Islands used costumes to represent the origins of different tribes, masks to symbolize ancestors and totems, and various tribal languages to interact and communicate with one another during the Carnevale in the form of drama. This process continued until a fusion and mutual understanding among the tribes was achieved. After numerous adaptations and reinterpretations of folklore and legends, it eventually evolved into the prototype of the Ragunnesi drama, which remains popular today. Mentor Commentary: It is recommended to omit some of the details and avoid excessive research, as the paper will be reviewed by the Chamber of Enlightenment of the Order. A Study on the Evolution of Drama Costumes and Stage Design (This handwritten notebook is almost completely torn, with only a few pages from the Epilogue remaining.) Epilogue: I would like to dedicate this paper to my friends who have supported me, to those who have secretly provided invaluable literature for my research, to the work of my father, DeLillo Quentin, to the exile granted to me by the Order of the Deep, and to the expulsion by Avinoleum Theological Seminary. This paper, titled "A Study on the Evolution of Drama Costumes and Stage Design," has taken four years to complete, from its inception to the eve of my exile, and I have finally finished the first draft. I hope my friends can read it, as I originally intended. Tomorrow morning, I will leave Ragunna aboard the Pilgrim's Sail, just as my father did, in search of the Sentinel—Praise be to Imperator! If I survive, I hope you, the omnipresent Imperator, will guide my way. ...When I was a child, my father, DeLillo, said to me before he left, "Little Quentin, do you know what humans are?" I knew that would be my father's last words to me, so I replied that I didn't know. Father then said, "Keep doing your best, Mario Quentin. Humans are a blade of thinking seagrass." I didn't understand why humans would be compared to a blade of seagrass. But now, I think I understand what father meant—don't stop thinking and don't stop searching. The islands of the past were destroyed in the Lament. Under Imperator's guidance, our ancestors boarded the Ark and voyaged far, eventually establishing Rinascita on the land it now occupies. During the Age of a Thousand Islands, to commemorate their lost homes and honor their tribespeople in the Lament, people began to wear the costumes of their tribes and masks symbolizing their ancestors and totems. As concluded in Chapter 4 of this paper, the culture of drama has never been a blessing promised by the Order. Rather, it is a commemoration and symbol developed independently by the people of Rinascita. But are we truly just a blade of seagrass? If so, there must be a distinction between the seagrass that flows with the waves and those that can think independently, right? People praise the name of Imperator for its mercy and its encompassing nature, for preserving the culture that unites people from different tribes, helping them merge and support one another. They praise Imperator for the will to unite the vast patch of seagrasses to defy the currents of the Lament. Praise be to Imperator! We exalt you! But have the Ragunnesi of today truly executed your true will? Ah, great Imperator! I don't want to die... I really don't... I wish I could attend the Carnevale one more time... I'm truly terrified... Please, don't turn me into a blade of seagrass tomorrow! Laurel and Sword (Part I) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal, Volume 1 Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough The Golden Bough, a Ragunnesi narrative epic rich in history and deeply influenced by primitive religious culture, is renowned for its prominent theatrical elements. The epic begins with pastoral plays that draw on the primitive beliefs and customs of various tribes during the Age of a Thousand Islands. As the story unfolds, these diverse narratives converge under the guidance of Sentinel Imperator. The author employs the perspectives of the Divine Envoys to provide Imperator's view, allowing the characters to assume their roles in classical plays. Throughout the work, recurring symbols of religion and totems appear, echoing metaphors commonly found in traditional plays. The use of these theatrical elements has helped establish the epic as a beloved classic, cherished by both officials and commoners in Ragunna. Furthermore, it embeds the author's profound reflections on the will behind the Oracle delivered by Sentinel Imperator, as well as the social changes occurring in the region of Rinascita. ...(Some of the pages are missing) One of the most commendable scenes in The Golden Bough is the concluding Scene 3, where five storylines dramatically converge at the climax of the Carnevale: the Holy Forest of the Fagaceae Peninsula, the Order of Ragunna, the Keepers of Secrets in Thessaleo Fells, the successor of the governor in Septimont, and the gladiators, all merging in a grand finale. In this scene, the author masterfully interweaves characters and plotlines, capturing the unique allure of a grand historical tragicomedy. This convergence in Scene 3 has served as a template, inspiring countless plays thereafter. The scene's influence owes much to its intricate plot design, which displays a skillful technique that sets a standard in narrative structure. Beyond the theoretical framework of the work itself, this design—where each element reflects the core theme and draws from historical settings—has solidified this epic as a timeless classic, maintaining its relevance and reverence across cultural shifts in literary history. (See Note 23) The Golden Bough is recognized as the earliest work of art to connect tribal folklore with the Sentinel (see Note 24). In the climactic Scene 3 of the Carnevale, the five masks stand together, each pursuing their own faith, when Sentinel Imperator descends from above, bestowing the laurel upon the chosen Enlightened One—the main protagonist on stage. This ritual has since become a lasting cultural emblem in the hearts of the people of Rinascita. From this scene onward, every heroic journey must conclude with the ritual of "being laureated," whether the hero takes on the role of an actor on stage or a playwright behind the scenes during the Carnevale. Laurel and Sword (Part II) Laurel and Sword: On the Divine Imagery in The Golden Bough Journal Title: Ragunna Sea Breeze Drama Society Research Journal Category: Literary Studies, Literary Theory, Theater, The Golden Bough (Continued) The reason for Sentinel Imperator's descent at the climax of the Carnevale in The Golden Bough remains an open question, one largely unexamined in the epic itself or in related research. Historically, the prevailing view in the Seminary held that the Laureate must be the individual who most aligns with Rinascita's ideals and resonates with the Sentinel—not driven by dramatic passion or ulterior motives. For a long time, this perspective dominated studies of The Golden Bough and the broader field of Laureate literature, with the laurel seen as a symbol of immense honor and the embodiment of Rinascita's collective will. (See Note 25) However, following the cultural events after the Seminary incident, the Laureate's symbol and performances are now seen as expressions of the Sentinel's divine will—the guiding force behind delivering the Oracle and unifying the doctrines. The image of laurel has also come to represent this sacred intent. The author raises an intriguing question: given this interpretation, could the selection of the Laureate itself be seen as an indoctrination of freedom—a concept seemingly at odds with The Golden Bough? Can freedom, once indoctrinated, still be considered freedom? ...(Some of the pages are missing) [23] Charlie Welbeck, "The History of Reforms on the Rinascita Drama Aesthetics," published by Avinoleum Theological Seminary Culture Journal. Timeworn Logbook 2
Logbook_Number_#17
Mom, I miss you.
It's pretty misty here, and whenever it's like this, I can't help but think back to when I was little, back when we were together.
We used to live in a house out in the countryside. It was a thatched cottage, and in the summer, I could hear the dried hay on the roof crackling as the sun beat down. In the winter, the walls would get damp.
Inside, the house had a narrow hallway that led to the kitchen, where a broken lightbulb, somehow always mysteriously fixed, hung from the ceiling. The exposed wires were wrapped in black tape.
Along the hallway were two rooms. I slept in the smaller one, the one on the north side. The gauzy curtains, printed with the sacred verses of the Order, always felt a little eerie at night. When I couldn't sleep, I'd sneak out to the narrow hallway. It didn't matter if I kept my eyes open or closed. With my back against the damp walls, it was pitch black, and I couldn't even see my own breath.
The wind tried to sneak in through the cracks, and the door frame seemed to shrink. The old wires were starting to tear, and the damp air pressed against the bricks. My hair brushed against the wall, and behind it, a patch of quilt slowly shifted. All these sounds tangled together in my head, floating from my ears to my skin, then rushing back inside, shaking my bones with a soft, mesmerizing tremor.
I can't shake this feeling of dampness that echoes in my mind. Today, it's here again.
I just passed through the misty barrier on our route. It felt like an unsettling dream.
But don't worry about me. The safety manual says this mist can cause hallucinations, but it's harmless. I've made it through safely. Now, I need to check the inventory again, just in case someone took something while I was dreaming.
I really miss you, Mom. Don't forget what I promised. Once I've made my name here, I'll bring you to Ragunna.

Timeworn Logbook 3
Logbook_Number_#29
Mom, don't worry. I'll be home and see you soon.
The day before yesterday was so cloudy, and I bet the Nimbus Wraiths were feeling pretty gloomy. We weren't supposed to set sail, but with the auction coming up, I have to make sure the item gets delivered on time.
This mission was given to me by the Montellis, and I can't let them down.
It's a bit of a detour, but since all the ships have already left and the Order sent Lucerna on board, I think it should be fine.
Don't worry. The Montelli family added more people to the crew, and with the Order's presence, everything will be okay. Yeah, it'll be fine.
I should tell you something to lift your spirits. Once I'm done with this job, I should have some time off to come and visit you.
Even though my job keeps me in the cabins, I get to see a lot of interesting things along the route.
Here, they don't use words like sunny or cloudy to describe the weather. Instead, they use emotions, which is kind of interesting, don't you think?
When it's "happy," we get to see rainbows, and the Nimbus Wraiths even dance under them.
When it's "gloomy," like today, it's cloudy, and we usually get to take the rest of the day off.
A "forced smile" is when it's sunny, but with a hint of rain. At times like that, the train picks up speed on purpose, and some of my colleagues will start telling loud jokes from the back of the train.
When it's "sorrowful," it rains, and the train moves very slowly.
"Unhappy" weather means thunder or strong winds. On days like that, we definitely take the day off. I just sleep through it.
And then there's "angry" weather, which is the scariest. The entire sea of clouds turns red. If we encounter that in the middle of the journey, our superiors make us wear soundproof earmuffs to work.
According to the route map, we'll be passing through a place called the Atrium of Reflections. I'd never heard of it before, but the seniors say we usually avoid it unless it's absolutely necessary.
I'll be careful, though. Don't worry about me. It's just a small challenge. Tough jobs need to be done, right?
As long as I put in the effort, I know I'll get the reward I deserve. Just wait for me, Mom. I'll bring you to Ragunna.

Cantarella's lips curve into a gentle smile, her eyes, calm as the ocean depths, rippling with a hint of warmth.

Oh, the pleasure is mine, my dear.
With you here, this castle feels… warmer. Your presence may have dispelled the chill that used to linger.
The Fisalia family...
The Divine Trials...
Our family's purpose has always been clear—to resist the Threnodian's spiritual interference and hold fast to our faith in the Sentinel.
The cruel trials were designed to find a Maiden with an unbreakable will, someone who could withstand the Threnodian's whispers and fix her eyes on the true light.
Yet, in pursuit of that "noble cause," innocent lives were sacrificed without question.
I can't accept the so-called "necessary sacrifice," one that tramples the will of others in the name of duty. It's nothing but living off the weak.
Though it's important to kindle the flames, none should forget those burned to ashes—those lives shouldn't have been squandered.
After all, we are more than just firewood.
So, you chose to offer your own strength...
So, you sought a different way...
Yes. When I took up the Sword of Divinity, I felt a <ano=Fleurdelys>presence</ano>, someone far more capable, more suitable. A new possibility emerged.
I asked the Sentinel to transfer my Second Awakening power to that girl.
The Sentinel had always wielded the power of separation, but instead agreed to my proposal to combine our strengths. With that power, she confronted the Threnodian.
We triumphed, for the moment, but the Threnodian proved to be more difficult than we expected.
To stop the brutal Divine Trials and secure us the final victory, I chose to become the family head, drawing on every resource available to achieve our goal.
I pretended to align with the Order to keep the Threnodian off guard, all while searching for a way to fully liberate the Sentinel and end the Threnodian once and for all.
And then... I found you.
So that's why you took me straight to the Sword of Divinity.
You must've gone through a lot.
Hehe… I have been watching you from the moment you set foot in Rinascita.
Now, I daresay I know you inside out.
Just as you chose your path, I've chosen mine. I will see it through, whatever it may cost.
Besides, compared to what you've endured, my hardships aren't worth mentioning.
You defeated the Threnodian in the Inverted Tower, saved the people of Rinascita, and freed those young girls... and me as well.
The girls are now back home, and the Threnodian's whispers have finally faded from this castle.
And with the Order's concessions, the shadows over Rinascita are vanishing. Peace has come to us once more.
Thanks to you, the days of pain and sacrifice have ended. A calm life… that is the miracle you've brought.
As the head of Fisalia, I must offer you a fitting reward for all the efforts you made.

Hehe, this is "our" home now.

Here, a special elixir I've prepared with Albizia flowers—their gentle, lingering fragrance can waft through reality into your dream.
Now, close your eyes... and rest. Good night.

Among the prized treasures of the Montelli family is a morph painting depicting Hadrian, the legendary gladiator, with his blade drawn. In Ragunna, these paintings have the special power to pull anyone who touches them into the sphere within, allowing them to experience it as though it were real.
At the heart of Trattoria Margherita is an oven Echo known as Bakie, tirelessly fueling Ragunna with its roaring flames and delicious aromas.

To be a true performer, one must first learn how to listen. Give your records, sheet music, or any musical medium to the Aria Mummer. Don't be alarmed when it swallows and chews these items—it's simply its way of "listening" to the music.

Passersby are often drawn to the delicate hands reaching out from the Averardo Bank. These hands are perfectly adorned, always gesturing with elegance and grace...
Though their owner is just an Echo teller.

Once a lonely Echo drifting through the seas, Lario has spent years without a companion until it joined the Troupe of Fools. All people know about it is its genus—Pliosaurus Somnii. Though the troupe has sailed across many waters near Rinascita, they have yet to encounter another like it.

C-MOSS, the camera Echo owned by the Pioneer Association's Ragunna branch, acts with all the fine manners of an old gentleman. He captures moments in time with care, often sipping a cup of developer solution between shots.

Before they fall into slumber, the Farceur's Faces of the Masked Reverie fill Ragunna's days and nights with their playful banter. As the shop's iconic mascots, they've garnered their fair share of noise complaints.
An Echo boat that quietly glides through Ragunna's canals, offering a safe and silent voyage to all who hop on it, often known as the Water Bus.

Once, when the Dark Tide ravaged the city and Tacet Fields spread like a plague, Signor Octopus's duty was to sound the alarms. Those days are like a distant dream now, yet he still announces the hour with a gentle horn, guarding the city's peace with quiet dedication.
An Echo lantern that belongs to the Order of the Deep, serving as the Order's watchful eyes to monitor the people of Ragunna.
Originally transformed from discarded dolls, these plushie Echoes have evolved to feel delicate human emotions. For them, these emotions are delicious frequencies to be savored with relish.

Spotted throughout Ragunna's streets, the Tubpups are lively Echoes that serve as faithful companions. Whether they are playing with children, carrying art supplies, or working as handy baskets, they bring joy and energy wherever they go.

Wow, even the clouds here are golden, just like...
…Just like Ragunna's Golden Fried Cutlet.
Keep it down, will you? You're ruining the mood with all that chatter.
Septimont is importing large quantities of Ragunna spices and alabaster. It seems we've chosen the perfect time to enter the market.
Lucky for us, the Order relaxed trade restrictions around the Carnevale. Without that, this deal might've been a gamble.
Who knows how long these good days will last...
Hello, are you here to do business with the Montelli family as well?
Something like that.
I'm actually a member of the family.
The Montelli are sharp with coin, but they honor their word. Good business partners, if you can trust them.
Is that so? Guess that means you're a high rank. Most of the staff are stuck in those drab uniforms.
We're brothers traveling between Ragunna and Septimont. We deal in commodities, art auctions, and, of course, high-stakes competitions.
Perhaps one day, we'll find ourselves working together on a venture.
Well, I'll be! A golden fountain... This place is practically drowning in riches!
What happens if you throw a coin in and make a wish, I wonder?
Oh, that's easy. You'll end up being carted off to pay a fine.
Hey, what's that in the sky?
It's stunning, like a pair of glowing wings...
Quick, snap a shot! Might be worth sending to Wutherium Film Studio!
There are perks to working the front desk, like sneaking out for a bit of fresh air now and then.
Everything really alright? Your schedule looks packed with tasks.
Work's still work, no matter how you stretch it. Only the moments when you slack off truly belong to you.
I really envy your laid-back attitude.
Ah, my friend, come to admire the sunset too? This kind of beauty doesn't come around often.
Tsk, why aren't they here yet? That man has no concept of time.
Ugh, I'm late. Black Alley business. I got held up.
What happened? Don't say our home got raided.
Eh, just a few young bucks fighting, didn't know when to quit. Almost turned into a bloodbath.
On to more serious matters. Find anything useful while you were staking out Montelli's turf?
Shh, quiet down... do you want someone overhearing us?
...The "prime goods" we've been after? Yeah, the Montellis got their hands on them. They're locked up in the Vault now.
Hmph, used to do side jobs for them. Not even a scrap of respect now.
What are you all talking about?
I'm sorry, {Male=sir;Female=ma'am}, we were just discussing the collection auction here.
Averardo Vault at night truly has a charm of its own, doesn't it?
...No doubt.
These stairs just keep going, don't they?
Did you notice the grand building at the top of the stairs? Many see it as a symbol of a new age.
Are you here for business as well?
Of course, I have a rather significant collection item to store—
Only here could I escape those insufferable Acolytes, the pestering editors, and those gatherings of writers full of the same tired clichés.
Recent security reports came in. We need to tighten vigilance.
Is someone really targeting this place? This is supposed to be the safest spot in all of Rinascita.
You're new here, so you might not know, but "breaking into the Vault successfully" is something some folks can brag about for a lifetime.

Sailing Time

1. The fishers of the Riccioli Islands follow a strict tradition of working from sunrise to sunset, believing the night belongs to Cetus the Tidebreaker, who guides lost souls back home.

2. While sailing in certain waters around the Riccioli Islands at night, Rachel's Threat Level will rise. Once it reaches a critical point, Ghost Medusas will emerge and attack. Stay alert and avoid their strikes!

3. The riskier the waters, the greater the rewards. Fish caught in areas where Ghost Medusas appear tend to be of higher quality.

4. Some special species only appear at night. Check the Index for details.

5. Night on the Riccioli Islands spans from 19:00 to 5:00.
Durability

1. As a Gondola Echo, Rachel takes damage upon bumping into hazards on the sea. Steer clear of Bampuffs, Tornadoes, and Ghost Medusas while navigating the waters.

2. Rachel's Durability decreases when damaged. If it reaches zero, it will automatically return to the dock, and all collected catches will be lost.

3. To ensure a safer and more successful voyage, you can use Riccioli Fishery Coins to restore Rachel's Durability before weighing anchor at the dock. Keep a close watch on its Durability to avoid unnecessary losses.

Ariosto
Are you curious about this old ship too? Hmm, seems like I'm not the only one who thinks there's something wrong with it.
See, we've always fished close to shore, that's why we Riccioli fishermen use Gondolas when we head out.
But word is, years ago Captain Ahab and his crew pulled out a wreck of a ship outta the sea, then left it with a strange fella to guard it.
That's not so strange, is it?
You think that's it? Now, don't go getting all scared on me... This ship... it's a ghost ship!
Come again?
There's a fella, Queequeg's his name, who's always mumbling something to the ship. And the damn wreck... it answers him! Mentions a "Flask" an awful lot...
Eh, enough of this! I'm not saying a word more. Get going, quick!
Otherwise, that crazy ol' bastard is gonna be back any minute, mark my words!
What's for dinner tonight?
Anything's fine by me.
Airsailer stew then?
What, Airsailer stew again? We've eaten that for the last week!
You think of something then! That's all you've been catching lately anyway.
Eugh, can we try something else, please?
How about some crispy fried Airsailer?
...Fine, I guess.
Ah... I know you! Heard about you from Mr. Fulmine some time ago.
Didn't think I'd find you out here in the Riccioli Islands, though. Came for a bit of a break?
I'm here to become a fishing expert.
Just here for a vacation.
This place is perfect for that, I'll give you that.
You must've run into my colleague, Clemont, then? He's been wandering the islands digging into the local history.
There are secrets buried here, ones even the ruins of Ragunna City have no record of. Secrets about the Sentinel and that Cetus the Tidebreaker…
Those lighthouses are the key to unlocking them, no doubt. Shame, though, the fishermen won't take us to the other two islands.
There's a legend... Say, ever seen Cetus the Tidebreaker? The creature has three gem-like holes on its back.
They say it wasn't always like that. No, it was a crew of sailors chasing it down who left those three marks on its hide.
Can you imagine… what kind of men would have the strength to leave such scars on a creature like that?
Fresh octopus clams! Just pulled from the water!
Care for a taste, hungry traveler?
Octopus clams?
Absolutely fresh! Look at this one's siphons, still glistening with seawater!
Just pop them open with a knife, squeeze on some lemon, and you're all set!
Eat them raw!?
Oh, they're delicious, you've got to try them!
If you're interested in buying, I've got the freshest stock around, no doubt about it.
Hello?
(The old man stands dazed, staring at the sea as if he can't hear you.)
Pequod...
Hello?
(The old man mumbles the ship's name again, but it seems continuing the conversation won't lead anywhere.)
Strange... So strange!
Got something else to make a fuss about?
My old man used to tell me that Queequeg had been working on this ship for years, fixin' it up with nary a single change!
Now, all of a sudden, the mast is fixed and soon the canvas will be patched up too!
I helped him with the repairs!
That's all thanks to me.
Oh, it was you? Well, that's a bit odd, isn't it?
That fella's been at it for as long as anyone could remember, never seemed to age a day. The ship never got any better either... So what are you, some kind of magician?
This ship's huge, isn't it? But, something about it feels familiar.
It reminds me of the Fool's Sail...
Yes! That's it, it looks like the Fool's Sails used by the Order!
I wonder what this ship looked like before. With all the new parts patched on, and its new shape, can it still be called the same ship?
Speaking of, do you know how to sail this thing?
It's too big, I don't think I could.
I know someone who could sail her out of here.
Imagine sailing a ship of this size... You'd look mighty impressive out there.
Abyssal sea serpents, hell, even a big ol' whale would be a walk in the park.
Maybe that's what it was made for in the first place.
You can take Cetus the Tidebreaker off that trophy list.
Sure, but even though boarding the Fool's Sail isn't exactly something to celebrate... I'd still love to give it a try. Never been anywhere beyond the Stormy Sea myself...
Ah, back already?
I heard the news. The ship has ended up broken again, right?
Ahab has disappeared, and even that Queequeg who's always fixing the ship is nowhere to be found.
Funny. Kind of miss him now...
Take that wretched pile of fish away! The mere sight of it flopping about makes my skin crawl!
Tsk, bothersome city folk… Beggin' your pardon, miss, but do step aside, would ya?
You think this dress is cheap? The cost of cleaning it would buy every one of your... fish.
Cheap? That fine mesh is perfect—for catching minnows. Scrap cloth, really.
Why, you—!
Best you stay away from this place, missy. Don't wanna get fish guts all over your fancy dress. And who knows, a shark might just decide to take a bite on your way back.
Did you say... s-shark?
Big mouth like the doors to your Vault, teeth sharper than knives. One bite, and it could swallow four whole men...
Is that really true?
Eh, might be. Hard to say.
Seems like we get a lotta pampered city folk wanderin' in here, thinkin' this is some kinda vacation spot.
Look at ya. Can't lift a finger for nothin'. Never had to break a sweat or pull a fish out of the water, have ya?
I'll need thirty Pricklecrab, thirty Bell-less Crabs, a crate of Legilimens Shrimp, and three Sunfish, alive. I'll go with you to the boat to pick them up.
By the way, got any Stygian Phantom?
What? All I've got to eat are a few Fried Egg Jellyfish. Why would you want one of those? They're deadly, aren't they?
Don't ask. The lady of the house is expecting a special guest, and that's what they fancy.
I'll check with Old Hart. He's been fishing further out lately. He should have some.
You're talking about that Feshalia family, right? I've heard rumors they're a strange lot. Only eat poisonous things.
It's the Fisalia family. I'm just a cook, don't know much more. If someone dies eating one of thoseStygian Phantom-what-have-yous, it's not my problem!
So, you still want the Fried Egg Jellyfish then?
Yeah, toss me a few.
They don't know how to enjoy a proper Tomato "Egg" Stir-fry... I'll make the most of it myself.
You're telling me... this lighthouse existed even before the founding of Ragunna?
Huh? What was that?
I said... this very lighthouse, it was here before Ragunna was even a thought, right?
Ah, yes, that's right.
They say Imperator built these lighthouses as part of some grand plan, something They laid out long before.
The tale has been passed down through the ages. My great-grandfather spoke of it, too.
That would make it older than the Order of the Deep.
Well, if it's really true, it would make this place an archaeological treasure trove.
Stove? You looking to roast some fish? Head to the market, you'll find it there, easy enough.
Ah, it seems your hearing is a bit...
It's quite alright, old sir! Thank you! Have a nice day!
Aye, sure, you're welcome, kid. If you're serious about diggin' up stories, head on over to Helm Village. Those old codgers are no younger than me. They'll have stories to share.
Don't let it get to you. We'll have the ship fixed and give it another try.
Not every venture at sea ends with a catch, after all…
But I'm out of coin. I can't keep going to the guild for help.
The sails, the nets, even the Gondola—all of it costs.
Why not ask Plank for some help?
You've got to find some way to make a living, one way or another.
Why do they all hold Captain Ahab in such reverence? I've never even seen him sail before.
You don't know? He's not from Rinascita. They say he was once the most renowned captain across the four seas.
I heard that when he scolded his crew, even the fiercest storms would part for him.
Is he really that fearsome? Then why does he still have so many people's respect?
Well, you don't earn your stripes as a captain by being soft with the crew.
If Gulpuffs had less of a temper, they'd all be eaten into extinction by now.
What? Some people eat Gulpuffs?
It's a metaphor, you fool! A metaphor!

[About]

Beside a mysterious morph painting, you find a painter named Claudia, trapped in her nightmares. 
Claudia asks you to investigate the world within the painting and gives you a protective talisman.

[Eligibility]

Reach Union Level 22, unlock Co-op mode, and unlock the Resonance Nexus in Ragunna City during Main Quest "The Sacred Breeze So Often Breathes."

[Event Rules]

Claudia asks you to investigate the world within the painting and gives you a protective talisman. Within the painted world, the talisman transforms into various Echoes to assist you.
Clear all enemies in the investigation area to advance. The Echoes transformed by the talisman will boost your Resonators' power as you progress.
Clearing enemies before the countdown ends earns extra points. Reach the required stage points for Stage Rewards and the required total points for Point Rewards. The Match feature is available for all challenges, allowing you to team up with other players.

※Only specified Echoes can be equipped in this event. The Echo will replace your main Echo Skill, but activated Sonatas remain effective.

{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, I owe you an apology for how I acted that day... I was stubborn.
Rinascita's civilization was planted by our ancestors, and the Order is just one of its many fruits. I shouldn't have been frightened by the ancient music; I should've been delighted!

I'm glad you've found some peace within yourself.
Do the Tenets permit you to speak so freely?

Where are you going next?

Or perhaps I should go further… to the Montelli vault, or even to the Septimont? Hmm, I suppose I wouldn't need to wear my uniform...
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, do you have any suggestions?
I say you should go wherever you like.
I say you should meet the people you want to meet.
Ah, I aspire to have your confidence one day!
"True faith is born from the heart, and Sentinel's guidance speaks through my voice." From the bottom of my heart, I thank you for your help, {Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}.
Which chapter of the Tenets is that from?
Hahaha! I said that. I am quoting myself!
That must be the spot Lenore said the record would be. What are the Vitreum Dancers doing over there?
More of those white phantoms... and Vitreum Dancers.
I, I... I'll go find a place to hide!

I never imagined it would lead us here. Twenty years ago, during the Dark Tide, the kind old Acolyte who took me in brought me to this place—our final refuge. But he returned to the seminary alone and never came back.
Still… now is not the time to dwell on the past. Let's press on!
Huff… How much longer must we keep chasing… Huff... Sitting in the basement every day doesn't exactly prepare one for such exertion.
{Male=Mr.;Female=Ms.} {PlayerName}, Huff… Please, go ahead. I'll catch up soon!
To question the Sentinel in such melodies of blasphemy... A history of insurrection and blind folly... They must be destroyed.
What am I supposed to do…? This feeling within me…
I want to listen to the Chorale again… just a few more times…

Now, back to our topic. Hidden among the stalls set up for tonight are three riddles entwined with the tale of the "ghost girl." Yet, these stalls are rather elusive. Rumor has it that they might even be run… by demons.
But of course, there are no demons in this world, only distorted frequencies or men cloaked in disguise, driven by their unmet desires.
Dealing with them requires no money. Instead, they sift through your desires, choosing what to claim for themselves.
Isn't that enchanting? There's no thrill in simply buying all your heart's desires with mere money.
And now, we have the "main course" for tonight: whoever solves all three riddles and uncovers the mystery of the "ghost girl" can ask the host for an elixir.
Whether to turn stones into gold, grant eternal youth, or even bring the dead back to life… Whichever you want, this potion is here to make it real.
I want the one that turns stones into gold.
I want the one that brings the dead back to life.
I just want to get rid of whatever effect that message had on me.
I doubt it.
Well then, might I suggest we collaborate to secure this reward?
I am after a particular elixir myself.
Well then, might I suggest we collaborate to secure this reward?
Such admirable restraint. However, it's too late to withdraw from this game, as the ghosts have already begun to shadow your every step.
According to that message, bringing those ghosts back to the mortal realm might clear the effects weighing on you.
So, might I suggest we collaborate to win the elixir that brings the dead back to life? I could also use that elixir myself.
In that case, why not unravel the lies and find the truth yourself? It could be quite enjoyable.
Come and join me in this game. I know you won't let go of any potential clues.
Besides, there are certain places that only you may be able to reach.
I happen to need a special elixir myself.
I thought someone as talented as you could make any potion.
Well, it requires more than you might imagine: the finest ingredients, precise procedures, impeccable techniques, and, of course, the proper mood.
But with you at my side, even the most intricate elixir would be a delight to create.
I'd love to explore this with you, be it elixir or poison.

As Carlotta falls from a great height, you reach the depths of the vault just in time to catch her safely.
Her agility raises questions in you, and she finally reveals her hidden identity: she is the family's Executor, tasked with handling disputes and eliminating traitors. 
Just then, traps set by the traitors activate, calling guards to stop you—but none can stand in your way.

Carlotta leads you into Averardo Vault, explaining that her family is aware of the Fractsidus's evil doings and is willing to help. 
She plans to deliver the evidence you've collected to her uncle, Capollo, who will arrange a formal meeting to exchange information about Fractsidus. 
Before the meeting, you take time to explore the vault.

After waiting for Carlotta for a long time, you search for her and discover she's in trouble—Capollo has vanished. 
In private, she reveals information from Gilberto's interrogation: there are traitors in the family who have been bribed by Fractsidus.
Carlotta requests your help to reach the traitors' hideout deep within the vault via an alternate passage. She hopes to capture and interrogate them to gain more information.

Before you enter the alternate passage, Carlotta assigns Zani to create a diversion by drawing attention of the traitors' helpers in the property room. 
With everything in place, you and Carlotta prepare to venture into the depths of Averardo Vault.

You and Carlotta reach the tuning room in the depths of the vault and catch the <ano=Frequency Specialist>tuners</ano> tampering with the family's Echoes using Lycoris. 
Intimidated by Carlotta, they confess their betrayal: they altered the Echoes and sent them to the rehearsal venue. 
While the traitors are taken away, Carlotta suspects an even more dangerous traitor is involved. 
To thank you, she offers to take you to the family's Echo Collection Room, where you might uncover connections between the Sentinel and the Vitreum Dancers.

In the Echo Collection Room, Carlotta proudly presents the family's treasured collection of Echoes, symbols of freedom and the Montelli commitment to developing Reserved Terminals for exploration beyond Rinascita. Common Echoes rely heavily on beacons and can't be used at sea, limiting exploration outside Rinascita.
Here, you find the first Vitreum Dancer, the prototype for all other Vitreum Dancers—the same one that had empathy with you in the city. 
Carlotta suggests this is no coincidence. The Sentinel may be using this Vitreum Dancer to send a message. 
You decide to delve into the archives on Vitreum Dancers for further insight.

Sails of the departed drift on and on, souls above the clouds, hearts claimed by the sea...
Oh, hello, {PlayerName}.
Is that one of your new songs?
It is... this one came from a rather unusual experience.
Tell me, {PlayerName}. What do you think of the sea?
Why do you ask?
Someone once said the sea is a city of the dead. You can hear the endless cries of the wind and waves, but never the voice of anything living.

When you spend days, weeks, maybe even years adrift, loneliness creeps in and twists despair into something monstrous. And yet, when you see a flicker of light out there—something you dare call "hope"…
That's when people stop thinking straight.
Is this from someone from the Fool's Troupe?
No, it was someone who's long gone now.
He died ten years ago in a shipwreck. I wasn't there to see it happen, and his face has almost faded from my memory. But...
But?
On my last voyage, I saw him. He was on another ship. A lively one if I might add. I could hear the laughter and clink of glasses.
Hold on. Didn't you just say it's rare to see anything living on the sea?
Exactly. That's what makes it unusual. When I saw him, he looked just as he was all those years ago, not a single day older. And in that moment, everything I'd forgotten about him came rushing back.
Are you saying… he might still be alive?
Surviving ten years on the sea, without even a scratch? What do you think, {PlayerName}? How likely is that?
Almost impossible, right? My thoughts exactly.
Yet when the light of "hope" is right in front of you, you can't help but chase after it. No matter how violent the waves or impossible the odds, you have to see it for yourself.
Sadly, when we got closer, Battier and Brant reported back the waters were teeming with Tacet Discords.
If another ship were to stumble across that area…
It would end badly. No doubt about it.
That's why I need your help, {PlayerName}.

I'll admit, this seems more of a personal request from my side. But when you're out there dealing with those Tacet Discords or trying to find the man, regardless of the results your safety comes above all else.
What does this man look like?
He had the same blue hair and eyes as me. He used to call it the color of the sea, a blessing from the ocean itself.
After he died, I stopped believing in nonsense like these. Most sailors still prefer to hold onto their superstitions though, as a way to boost their spirits before heading off to sea.
{PlayerName}, I wish you safety... and the best of luck.
{PlayerName}, welcome back. How did it go out there?
The place was overrun with Tacet Discords.
So it's already…
I didn't see the man you mentioned.
Ah, I see... Thank you for trying, {PlayerName}. Can you tell me more about what you saw?
You describe what you saw to Levito.
Sea fog, never-ending tides of TDs, distant voices on the wind... {PlayerName}, it reminds me of an old story I heard as a child.
Sailors, weary and broken after battling storms and endless waves, find their minds playing tricks on them. As I said before, loneliness can evolve into something unbearable.

In those moments, if a door appeared before them. Bright, warm, and inviting. Even if it led straight to death, many would still choose to walk through it. All for a glimpse of happiness that feels so real they'd gladly give everything for it.
So these waters… is a trap. The TDs are luring people in.
I believe so. And the longer those monsters are left unchecked, the more lives they'll claim.
I'd like to ask another favor of you, though I understand you've got plenty of other tasks to tend to...
I do have a lot going on.
But it's not like I can't make time.

I've learnt about your reputation of being quite a busy person. So don't feel pressured in taking on the task. Feel free to come by whenever you have the time to spare. I'll think of other ways to handle it in the meantime.
That said... I do prefer that you make use of that time on some relaxation.
Are you planning on a reward for me?
Of course, if that's what you hope for. I do not want anyone else to have to experience the loss of hope any longer.
Don't worry. I've made my peace with the idea that he did die ten years ago. Maybe that's not such a bad thing after all.
Ten years have passed for me, but for him? He'll stay forever young. I think there's something beautiful about that—it's the kind of ending that belongs in a song.
Thank you, {PlayerName}. I'll leave the rest in your capable hands.
However, if you do lend me a hand, I'll make sure you're rewarded properly.
The TDs have been growing in numbers lately. I'd be grateful if you could lend me hand when you have the time, {PlayerName}.
