If we steer our course by Ahab's example, we might discover things, even treasures he left behind...
Can we catch Cetus the Tidebreaker?
It's a possibility. Captain Ahab always had an obsession with the Cetus, but why remains a mystery.
Well then, let's press on with this as our goal!
The sea feels ever so calm, and the whirlpools have finally settled.
Everything's returned to how it once was… To be honest, {PlayerName}, Captain Ahab and his crew met their fate at sea decades ago.
Their love of the sea and their promise to Cetus the Tidebreaker is what kept their spirits lingering here.
And now, the peaceful waters of Riccioli mark their final resting place. This is their "final harbor."
But the Rachel still sails on, and it seems to have taken a liking to you.
I believe that Captain Ahab also hoped you'd carry on his legacy...
What about you?
Me? I'm just a simple sailor and fisherman. I was born here, and I'll probably get married and have children here too. Eventually, I'll find my peace in these very waters.
So set sail, Captain {PlayerName}! Your journey leads to the very edge of the world.

The Employee Manual for all staff members of the Averardo Vault. Below is the content from the first page:

Welcome to the Averardo Vault. Your arrival brings fresh energy to the Vault, and we sincerely look forward to your exceptional performance.

In keeping with the principle of "the sanctity and inviolability of private property," the Averardo Vault houses a vast collection of priceless Echoes and artworks. It is the safest and most secure place in Rinascita. Your every word and action reflect the Vault's image, and we trust this manual will help you gain a comprehensive understanding of the Averardo Vault.

Vault Overview:

The Vault is located east of Ragunna City, where it stores a vast array of Echoes and artworks. The Vault is divided into two zones: the Upper Management Zone, positioned above a chasm with a commanding view of the sea of clouds, and the Underground Depository Zone, situated beneath the clouds and connected to the upper zone by an elevator tower.

The Vault's security system is comprised of Echoes.

Kindly Note:

Staff and Echo activity take place in the following areas:

1. Office Area (The designated workspace for staff members).
2. Underground Vault Area (Primarily housing Echoes and patrolled by armed Echoes. Do not enter this area without prior authorization and declaration).

As the most secure and reliable place in all of Rinascita, all staff members of the Vault are responsible for ensuring the safety of the items stored inside.

The deposit and withdrawal of all items must strictly follow the prescribed reporting procedures. Violations will be handled according to the rules outlined in the Employee Manual.

A poster advertising tourism in Riccioli Islands

Discover Riccioli Islands, a hidden paradise nestled amidst Rinascita's turbulent waters.
Named after the renowned astronomer and seafarer of the Order, Sir Riccioli, this archipelago has been a sanctuary of natural wonders since its discovery during Rinascita's founding years. From the elusive Riccioli Black Pearls to the ethereal Stygian Phantoms and strange Yarn Eels, the archipelago is teeming with life and natural beauties thanks to the unique qualities of its geographic location with much more yet to be discovered.

Embark on adventures to encounter the mysterious ancient Echo of the sea in secluded coves and hunt for pearls washed ashore. As the tide recedes in the sunset, join friendly locals in nearby Riccioli settlements for a refreshing drink.
And last but not least, don't miss out on the signature Riccioli fishing experience!
There you have it, an enchanted wonderland filled with life where infinite possibilities are immersed in aromas of the sea.
Come to the Riccioli Islands and let your heart race as you discover life's new wonders.

About Fantasies of the Thousand Gateways

Past memories lie buried deep within dreams, and the key to exploration is in your hands. Please do not forget, only within dreams will the answers be revealed.

[Eligibility]
Reach Union Level 30, and activate the Resonance Nexus in Ragunna City during Main Quest "The Sacred Breeze So Often Breathes."

[Exploration]
- Choose three Resonators and embark on epic battles in the Illusive Realm. The Echo Skills, Stats, Levels, Resonance Chains, and Weapons of Resonators can be carried over in the event.
- In the Illusive Realm, you can gain powerful boosts from Metaphors. Metaphors marked with Dreamscape Power provide additional enhancements when Lucid Dream is activated through Dreamscape Aid.
- Each battle in the Illusive Realm brings you against different enemies. Complete these challenges to earn Illusive Points and reach milestones to claim bountiful rewards.

[Remnant Crystal]
A Remnant Crystal will appear in the Memory Zone after defeating the powerful enemies found in the deepest parts of the realm. Use Waveplates to collect its rewards.

[Difficulty]
Higher SOL3 Phases offer more challenging Exploration in the Illusive Realm with more Remnant Crystals and Illusive Points as rewards. The difficulty of the Illusive Realm is dependent on the SOL3 Phase you're in when the Illusive Realm resets (04:00 every Monday). Adjusting your SOL3 Phase during each exploration cycle does not affect the difficulty and rewards of the current cycle.

Fishing Rules

Fishing Spot Rules:

1. There are two types of Fishing Spots: Sea Life Fishing Spots and Material Fishing Spots, each offering different resources.

2. Each Fishing Spot requires a specific Fishing Ability to access. Check the Fishing Abilities page for details.

3. Each Fishing Spot has a limited number of catches. When depleted, the spot will disappear and automatically generate after a certain period, possibly at a different location.

Fishing Rules:

1. When the harpoon lands within a glowing area, {Cus:Ipt,Touch=tap PC=click Gamepad=press} the button to accelerate the Fishing Progress. Brighter areas grant greater acceleration.

2. Once the Fishing Progress reaches 100%, 1 Fishing Attempt will be consumed, and you will have a chance to catch the target.

3. When all Fishing Attempts are used up, no further fishing can be done, and you will proceed to handle the storage for the harvest.

4. During fishing, you can access the Cargo page to manage your catches. Doing so will interrupt the current fishing attempt.

Hi, {PlayerName}!
Thanks to you, we're finally back home, safe and sound!
And Jojo's fully recovered, too.
Ms. Rosemary at the Apothecary gave me this special medicine! Just a tiny dab, and the pain's all gone!
She said it was from Ms. Can… something… Oh, I can't remember. Grown-up names are always so hard to keep straight!
Anyway, it's from a very nice lady!
And anyone sick can use it, too! Yay!
We survived, but at what cost? Is it a blessing? Or is it just more to carry?
Sometimes, I wonder, when life is this heavy, could death be... an easier path?
But if you die, you lose everything. No more chances. No paths ahead.
Besides, as survivors, who are we to say whether the dead found peace?
Just being here, with thoughts and worries and even fears… That's its own kind of happiness.
Annis, O' Annis… the light in despair, the angel from the mirage…
Hello, ma'am. Do you know Annis?
Annis? Isn't that the name of Girl A?
Hmm? So, everyone's heard of Annis?
Girl A? No, no… Annis is Annis, no one else.
Annis is the angel sung about in hymns, a gentle light that appears to those lost in despair.
They take many forms, like someone dear, a flower, a bird… even a jellyfish, sometimes.
So Annis is just a legend?
Is there an Annis here in the town?
Oh, no, child. Annis is as real as hope itself.
Not in name, no. But the angel Annis is always near.
When someone is in a bind, yet clings to the faintest glimmer of hope, Annis appears in the form of things they're familar with, guiding them out of the tight spot.
If you're strong enough to hold on, Annis will come to you.
I've conducted over a hundred visits and interviews, traveling between Thessaleo Fells and Egla Town. Finally, I think I have a theory...
It seems that these regions are experiencing a phenomenon—mass hypochondria, if you will.
For example, many people claim to have seen an ancient knight they believe is still alive.
Others speak of an angel named Annis, said to answer the call of those with unbreakable wills. Annis appears in different forms, helping those in dire need.
From the records, she's often seen as a young girl, a flower, a bird… even a jellyfish.
Yet, after combing through records over the past few centuries, I have yet to find any concrete evidence for Annis's existence.
Medically speaking, it seems more likely that these are hallucinations brought on by intense mental strain.
When someone is under severe stress or endures deep trauma, the mind might create an external figure to ease the pain, like a survival mechanism.
Think of the pressures of strained family ties, the toll of years of competition, and hallucinations induced by toxins...
In extreme cases, one's own identity can fragment, conjuring up an imaginary figure.
So, when an entire community is facing intense pressure...
Hmm, but I'd say that angel or not, true salvation lies within ourselves. Don't you agree?
I never imagined life could feel this carefree.
Just look at this vast scenery... It brings much calm to my heart.
Yeah, I feel the same way. A simple and quiet life. There's a beauty in it.
We have Cantarella to thank for this peace.
I feel reassured with her as the head of our family.
She's… she's everything a Maiden should be, more so than I could ever be. And as the head of Fisalia? She's unmatched.
For us, I think it's our turn to make the most of the world she saved for us. Let's live every day to its fullest.
Yes, and let's capture the beauty we find along the way! I'm sure she'll be happy to receive these photos!

A Young Acolyte's Letter

Dearest Father, I am writing this letter to you from a corner of the library. Over time, I have slowly adjusted to life at the seminary. During my free time, I often come to this library to read the ancient texts it holds and study the doctrine of Unity. But the deeper I delve into the history of Rinascita, the more I sense that it is shrouded by an unresolved mist. There are too many unanswered questions about our faith, the grace we have received, and the disaster that once befell us. Fortunately, many publicly sensitive topics and even discussions of taboos are regarded as subjects of academic interest in the seminary. I will take time to study and explore them. Of course, I haven't neglected the swordsmanship Mother taught me. Recently, I applied for sparring practice with the Divine Envoys... Don't worry, I won't hurt myself. I remember you once told me that Avinoleum is so vast you'll always get lost. This year, I've walked everywhere in the seminary, except for those places where I'm not allowed to go. I've drawn a simple route map, which is easier to read than the one in the Order. I'll send it to you later. With my sword and lamp, I press on through the fog. My Lord Imperator from above, Rosalie

The Divine Trials are a hallowed Fisalia tradition, but the danger surrounding them has led some family members to seek out commoners who resemble their daughters, using them as substitutes.

You find the second Sea Apple and another note from Chloe that records why and how she participated in the trials.

To avoid the watchful eyes, the girls formed secret pacts in whispers, such as "hum a special tune," "use the right color," "knock on the door three times every two seconds"…

You find the third Sea Apple and another note from Chloe that reveals her change in mindset during the trials.

The Fisalia family is built on poison, and from a young age, every Fisalia child is introduced to it and learns to build up resistance.

The Fisalia bloodlines can develop poison-related abilities when exposed to poisons and pushed to the brink, but commoners rarely survive. However, a commoner girl named Annis also seemed to have awakened such an ability, though her throat was damaged by poison, leaving her forever voiceless.
A familiar door appears in front of you. Just knock on it three times as those girls used to do. Maybe something unexpected will happen.
Behind the door is another world where the jellyfish await your arrival.

They recorded these ideas on paper, each word melting into a sweet candy to soothe their sorrows.

You find notes in the sketchbook.
Though time has yellowed the pages, the girls' laughter and joy still dance vividly across each line.

It looks like a study room, but as you look up at the ceiling, the sparkling waves there make you feel this whole place is underwater.

While you know nothing of poisons, Cantarella, who is well-experienced in this field, extends her hand and volunteers to take the poison herself.

You hesitate, but she smiles and calls the jellyfish to her, explaining that she has long since become immune to all poisons.
A subtle shift seems to have taken place in this familiar room.
Behind the door is the deep water zone. Please be well-prepared beforehand.
A sketchbook scribbled with the lyrics of an eerie folk song.

The messages jotted on the sketchbook are like soundless screams.
You can feel the despair of those girls from these words.

A strange doll blocks your way and asks you to find a suitable round hat for her.

Meanwhile, Cantarella seems unwell but forces herself to stay collected for your sake.
The doll thrusts a Round Hat into your hands with no further explanation.
The doll thanks you for bringing her the Round Hat and invites you to the stage for the final performance.

You figure out who this girl with a red round hat is. She must be Annis, the silent Ghost Girl A who sent you that message. But why hasn't she aged over these years? There's no time to dwell on this question now. After all, saving Cantarella comes first.

Annis offers to help. She closes her eyes and holds the lamp. A brilliant light appears, reigniting the lamp's glow, yet Annis vanishes in its wake.

Years ago, Cantarella used illusions to deceive the late head of Fisalia, seizing his position and ending the cruel trials. But his remaining obsession, corrupted by the whispers, has lingered in the castle and turned the place into the Sea of Ghosts.
 
Together, you and Cantarella set his lingering will free.

As the lingering obsession of the late head of the Fisalias fades, the Sea of Ghosts vanishes.

With the hymns rising around you, you find yourself in the sanctuary, where the girls who are supposed to be dead stand in front of you, all safe and sound.

You learn from Cantarella that since the Threnodian's lies were uncovered, the frequencies and circumstances around Ragunna have shifted. The time had come for the girls to finally go home.

She admits that she never intended to involve you and had planned to handle everything herself. That's why for this year's Night of Remembrance, she took part herself and chose "ghost girls" as the theme.

She had meant to dive into the Sea of Ghosts alone, claim she had solved the riddles and obtain the elixir of revival. This would allow her to send the girls home during the midnight Dance of the Dead. 

But Annis's message led you to her side to complete the plan.

As you wonder how to find the Inverted Tower Imperator spoke of, Abby suggests taking to the air, noting that the cliff near Egla Town would make a perfect launch pad.

You encounter Ciaccona, a wandering bard sent by Carlotta to aid you. With her unique ability to recreate past experiences, she helps you relive your experience meeting Cartethyia. As you recount the meeting, you find yourself drawn into a strange realm conjured by her Resonance Ability.

Under the effect of Ciaccona's Resonance Ability, you begin to view your meeting with Cartethyia from a different perspective. To your surprise, Cartethyia also "enters" this memory.

In your conversation, she reveals that she has lost most of her memories and is uncertain about the nature of her resonance.

However, her words offer new insights. The Sonoro Sphere where her body currently resides may be the Inverted Tower the Sentinel once mentioned. A mysterious wandering figure has attempted to enter the Sonoro but has always been stopped by the barrier. Finding this person's identity may lead to new findings.

Ciaccona shakes you awake, and her reaction makes you realize that what happened wasn't entirely due to her Resonance Ability.

As you begin to consider your next steps, a butler from the Fisalia family arrives with an invitation to meet the head of the family.

You put off the meeting for now, opting to first learn more about the Fisalia matriarch. Ciaccona shares some of the most intriguing rumors about her, and a few details seem to match the wandering figure Cartethyia described.

Regardless of the matriarch's motives, this invitation could be the breakthrough you need. You say goodbye to Ciaccona and depart for the Fisalia estate.
The current head of the Fisalia family introduces herself as Cantarella. She seems to be well prepared for your arrival and invites you to her study.

Based on what you previously learned from Gilberto, you confront Cantarella about the Fisalia family's true allegiance to the Threnodian.

Yet Cantarella unveils a more daunting truth. The Threnodian Leviathan is an entity with powers of assimilation, devouring civilizations through the spread of spiritual plague. Its invasion of Ragunna has long since concluded.

Peace is all but an illusion, blinding the Ragunnesi to the abyss they are unknowingly walking toward.

As if everything were unfolding as planned, Cantarella offers to present more evidence to back her claims.

Cantarella shows you Sentinel Imperator's true form and the twisted truths behind its history.

The Sentinel was originally a majestic steed, not the half-horse, half-sea creature now worshipped by the Order. This form was assumed only after the Threnodian's corruption.

With the powers of separation, the Sentinel infused the Sword of Divinity—Tyrvine with part of Their power to ensure Their Resonator, the Blessed Maiden, could be chosen in the event of Their absence. For generations, the Fisalia family held trials to find the true Blessed Maiden who can resonate with Tyrvine through Overclocking. However, after her own failed attempt, Cantarella uncovered a chilling message: "The Maiden is dead."

Cantarella now asks you to persuade Jué to help rescue the trapped Imperator.

You decline her request, but not without alternative plans. Before acting, you must first verify the truth of Cantarella's claims.

After confirming that Tyrvine was indeed left by Imperator through your special permission, you tell Cantarella what you know about Cartethyia.

Given past events, Cantarella quickly believes you and suggests traveling to the barrier of the Sonoro Sphere. It turns out that Cantarella is the wandering figure Cartethyia mentioned before.

Using Tyrvine, you and Cantarella enter the Sonoro Sphere where Cartethyia has been waiting for your arrival.

The moment you brought Tyrvine into the Sonoro, Cartethyia recalled certain information she had previously forgotten.

The seal surrounding the Inverted Tower can be broken by bringing Tyrvine, Hognis, and Haultir to their respective pedestals.

Is this a clue from the Sentinel, or a trap set by the Threnodian? Only by continuing forward will you uncover the truth.

After being lifted into the sky, you finally view the Inverted Tower in its entirety, with the three seals clearly visible at the central spire.

With Cartethyia's help, you manage to keep your bearings despite the abnormal gravity conditions.

As soon as Tyrvine is placed on its pedestal, visions of Cartethyia's past flood your mind—moments from her coronation and the arrival of the Second Dark Tide. Cantarella, however, shares she witnessed a completely different vision.

Meanwhile, Abby detects Imperator's frequencies within your Tacet Mark, leading Cartethyia to grow even more suspicious of her own identity.

To ensure that these frequencies pose no danger to you, the three of you decide to rest for the night.

To verify her visions and improve the chances of saving the Sentinel, Cantarella decides to venture into the unknown alone.

After exchanging contact information, she sets off on a separate path with Tyrvine.

After placing Hognis on its pedestal, visions of Cartethyia's past resurface, showing her valiant struggle against the Threnodian in the wake of the Dark Tide.

A looming mystery finally has an answer. Cartethyia has always been on the side of humanity. With this revelation, the young maiden finally lets go of emotions long suppressed.

But new uncertainties arise. The frequencies of the Threnodian Leviathan glowing within your Tacet Mark...

Who split these frequencies? Was it the Sentinel or the Threnodian who gave Cartethyia these hints? It seems the answers will only be revealed once the third sword is placed.
You follow the singing and arrive at a floating garden where Cartethyia is saying goodbye to the lost companions of her past.
You and Cartethyia awaken in the garden. The final battle lies before you.

After placing Haultir on its pedestal, you witness a vision in which the Threnodian reveals the truth: Cartethyia was created by the Leviathan, intended to be"whole" and "perfect." The people's adoration of her served as the Threnodian's lifeblood, and it was Cartethyia's resonance that brought forth the Second Dark Tide.

The Cartethyia before you now remembers everything. The Sentinel's corrupted form had long since been destroyed, but the Threnodian's essence lingered within Its vessel, Fleurdelys.

Your journey with Cartethyia was part of her plan to destroy Leviathan for good, taking all the things the false Divinity had bestowed and using them against It. Not only to end Its life, but also to extinguish Its future.

The Cartethyia who has accompanied you these past three days is a fragment of consciousness—the part of her that wished to live in the face of the Leviathan's corruption.

After arriving at the site of Cartethyia's coronation, she makes a final request. Instead of directly confronting the Threnodian's vessel, Fleurdelys, she asks that you use the connection she and Fleurdelys share to bring the last fragments of consciousness from the vessel here, so they can reunite.

This is the only way to trap the Threnodian's essence in a powerless shell, ensuring It can never return. By doing this, the cursed Fleurdelys will finally find the peace she has long sought. She asks for your help in illuminating the final path of your journey together.

Cantarella approaches Cartethyia with the now restored Tyrvine in hand. Within it are fragments of the Sentinel's power, remnants of failed resonances from the Maiden candidates in the past.

"The real Blessed Maiden is dead." Cantarella sacrificed her Second Awakening with Imperator for a chance to destroy the Sentinel's corrupted form.

So now, why can't the "false" Blessed Maiden become the "true" one?

In a realm of pure white, you encounter Imperator's final consciousness and learn the truth behind Their transformation.

In order to understand the Threnodian's true nature, Imperator was forced to allow the Threnodian's assimilation. In doing so, They discovered that while the Threnodian is indestructible, it can be bound by a human Resonator.

The journey was fraught with difficulty. Without Cartethyia's determination and Cantarella's sacrifice of her Second Awakening, the situation would have been doomed.

With the last bit of Their power, Imperator awakens Cartethyia.

Cartethyia ultimately refuses Imperator's proposition to forget the past and reconciles with her true self.

Now, she realizes she is whole again.

As Cartethyia gradually awakens, you notice a slight shift in her personality. She has become more lively and carefree, as the legends described. 

Having faced the edge of life and death together, the two of you can now savor a moment of peace.

Once Cartethyia calms down, she makes an unexpected vow. She vows to surpass you, so that one day she may defy your wishes, ignore your pleas, defeat you, and be your savior. Just as you did for her.

But for now, she intends to take time to reflect on her future path, and also rediscover Ragunna as it is now.

Cantarella thanks you for bringing the Fisalias the peace they've long sought, offering you a symbol of the unbreakable pact between you and them.

My dearest sister, I cannot fathom anything more heart-wrenching than facing you in this trial, given all the years we have spent growing up together.

The head of our family has always taught us that to be born into the Fisalias is to embrace coldness, decisiveness, and ruthlessness.

Gather your strength and determination, so that when we face each other in the trial, we shall do so as equals.

Should I become the Maiden, I will honor your sacrifices. And if you are chosen, I hope you will do the same.

Yours,

Night of Remembrance specials! Feast well, for only a full belly will sharpen your wits for the riddles ahead!
Bread of the Lost, Pozo Soup, Coffin Tamale, Caramel Fruit Pie... Each is prepared to satisfy both your body and soul!

Take my soul, take my flesh, take everything! Take it all to bring back the lost souls.

I wonder if this warmth could cross the realm of illusion into reality, lasting beyond a single night... into eternity.
Take my soul, take my flesh, take everything! Take it all to bring back the lost souls.

A worn student handbook, its pages frayed and torn, revealing only snippets of information.

Welcome to Avinoleum. This handbook serves as a guide for new students.

 1. The academy consists of three towers. In addition to the classrooms used for daily lessons, one tower is specifically dedicated to student gatherings and social events. This tower also houses portraits of past Primuses. Both new and old students are welcome to visit and pay their respects. Afterward, visitors must leave in an orderly manner.
 2. The watchtower and garden are only accessible before curfew. Entry is prohibited outside of these hours. Students are strictly forbidden from feeding the dragons that inhabit the surrounding area. Violators will face confinement for a period of three to five days.

3. Students who have completed the knighthood curriculum may apply to participate in the trials. Applications must be submitted with the required materials at least seven days in advance. A review process will follow, during which instructors will ensure applicants are not carrying any prohibited weapons or Echoes before proceeding to the trials.
4. The Path of Bestowal is only open to faculty and students during divine services and the Carnevale. Outside of the Carnevale, students invited to attend divine services must wear the prescribed attire and be accompanied by a member of the Order to the Path of Bestowal for their studies.
 
By the Sentinel above, may every student find enlightenment in Avinoleum.

If you prove your worth, the family permits you to use any means necessary to rise. Even the position of family head is a treasure to be claimed at the right price. Betrayal is a tool, and greed is a virtue. But remember, always wield them with grace.

About Visiting: Every visit to the estate must be justified. For those who dare intrude without invitation, the Fisalias will show them the Fisalia way of hospitality. "Invite" them to leave, or "invite" them to stay permanently as a warning to others. When an invitation is extended, visitors must mind their manners and maintain discretion. Never allow curiosity or fear to lead to your undoing.

About the Castle: Visitors with matters to discuss must wait quietly in the reception room on the first floor until granted an audience with the family head. No wandering or departure is allowed during this time. Invited guests must present their invitations and proceed to the banquet hall on the right, where hospitality will be provided in accordance with their station. All other rooms in the mansion are off-limits for visitation, including but not limited to the study on the second floor and the surrounding garden.

About the Montellis: Fleeting brilliance. Remember, true glory belongs to the Fisalia family.

You receive a strange message from a "ghost girl." The twisted frequency within it affects both you and Abby. 

To uncover the mystery and lift its effects, you decide to attend the Night of Remembrance in Egla Town, as mentioned in the message.

The guide briefs you on what the Night of Remembrance is. It's an annual festival in Egla Town, dedicated to honoring those who have passed. People dress up like ghosts at night for various activities.

The guide tells you to wear a mask for the event, and you show him the mask of the Laureate, which works perfectly.
I am after a particular elixir myself.

Cantarella tells you that three riddles entwined with the tale of the "ghost girl" are hidden among the stalls set up for tonight.

Whoever solves all three riddles and uncovers the mystery of the "ghost girl" can ask the host for an elixir that grants any wish. You're skeptical, but Cantarella seems intrigued. You decide to join her.

Mammon, the owner of the first stall, says he will only give you the first riddle if you exchange something precious.

As the new Laureate, you offer a performance, which he gladly accepts.

Impressed by your performance, Mammon reveals to you the first riddle: The Siren's Song.

"Long ago, a group of girls followed the Siren's call out of town. They journeyed to the 'crown' atop the mountain and to the waterfall that cascaded into the depths below."

He also offers you a music box.

As Cantarella tinkers with the music box, you notice its shape resembles an apple.

Inspired by your observation, she solves the first riddle and leads you to the second stall.

The owner of the second stall is Beelzebul, who asks you to pick the freshest apple in the stall. After you find the correct apple, Beelzebul gives you a "lucky coin" and reveals the second riddle: The Red Apple.

"The girls lined up for their apples, each one in a vivid, glistening red… but why would apples appear in the deep sea?"

The coin isn't perfectly round, with its edges ribbed and uneven. The front of the coin features a doll in a red hat, while the back shows one in blue.

Cantarella picks up on the clue and leads you to the third stall... But, isn't collecting these riddles going a bit too smoothly?

Dolls wearing red and blue hats are placed in the third stall. The owner, Invidia, asks you to pick the most beautiful one. But no matter which one you choose, she insists on giving you the doll in the red hat, claiming that the red hat symbolizes divine will and brings luck.

She then tells you the last riddle: The Round Hat.

"A girl dons her red dancing shoes and wears a scarlet hat, ready for the final act of her performance."

You realize that the music box, the cog-like "lucky coin," and the doll in a red hat can be assembled into a ballerina music box.

Cantarella puts the parts together and you perform once again. This time, the music box plays.

After reading the strange message you received, Cantarella explains that the Night of Remembrance is centered around ghost-related themes. Tonight's theme happens to be the "ghost girl."

She senses the effect on you and invites you to join the event, promising that you'll recover once you solve the riddles prepared for tonight.

As the music box plays, the red hat doll materializes and dances, only to abruptly stop. You realize it was all an illusion, but the music reminds you of Porto-Veno Castle. A fleeting shadow crosses Cantarella's usually calm face.

A sharp headache interrupts your thoughts, the distorted frequencies intensifying. You seize the moment and ask Cantarella if you can rest at her castle, and she agrees.

The girl points at a crimson plant nearby. Its shape resembles an apple, yet it seems more like a peculiar marine creature.

You realize it's a poisonous Sea Apple, which may be the key to solving the riddle of the Red Apple.

Before you can question the girl, she runs to another part of the garden.

The girl points to a jellyfish-like plant, its crimson bloom resembling her own round hat.

Could the round hat from the riddle be a poisonous Jellyrose Medusa? If so, the "ghost girls" are tied to the Fisalias. You need to speak with Cantarella about this.

The girl seems to understand and runs off, gesturing for you to follow.

Cantarella lets you rest in her garden and brings you a potion to ease your nerves. You feel much better after drinking it.

Cantarella then leaves to attend to other business, giving you a chance to search around.
You spot a girl wearing a red round hat among the bushes. She tries to say something but can't speak, instead gesturing for you to follow her.

You follow the girl to the corner and find Cantarella dancing, her steps seemingly regulating certain frequencies. 

You share your thoughts with her, and she admits that the "ghost girl" refers to the cruel Divine Trials of the Fisalia family. The blood and tears from these trials have twisted Porto-Veno Castle into the <ano=Sonoro Sphere>the Sea of Ghosts</ano>.

To uncover the truth and lift the "curse" binding you, you must dive into this Sea of Ghosts.
You prepare to send the girls back to their homes. Before you leave, they say their final goodbyes to Cantarella, thanking her for everything she's done for them over the years.

The Night of Remembrance ends smoothly, and the girls return to their homes. The lingering influence over you and Abby is lifted, and everything returns to its usual calm.

It feels like nothing ever happened, as if it was just a fleeting night's dream. But you know it was real, because Cantarella stands right beside you.

She acknowledges that you're stronger than her, but that doesn't stop her from instinctively caring for you. She invites you to rest at her now peaceful castle.

It's just you and Cantarella in the castle now. She opens up to you, sharing her thoughts.
 
The Fisalias have always fought to resist the Threnodian's spiritual interference and hold fast to their faith in the Sentinel. The cruel trials were designed to find a Maiden with an unbreakable will, someone capable of withstanding the Threnodian's whispers.
 
Cantarella can't accept the so-called "necessary sacrifice" that strips others of their free will, but she understands it's the only solution. Therefore, she transferred her Second Awakening power to find a solution where no one else but her would be harmed.
 
She pretended to align with the Order to lull the Threnodian into complacency, all the while searching for a way to liberate the Sentinel and defeat the Threnodian once and for all.
 
And then, she found you. Alongside Cantarella, you shaped this peaceful, happy ending, a miracle born from both of you.

Its round canopy resembles a soft, plump jellyfish with long, graceful tentacles that seem to float effortlessly in the air. Drawing her enemies into this enchanting yet perilous sea of dreams is the signature art of Cantarella. Like its owner, the parasol may appear soft and fluid, yet when the need arises, it is always indestructible.

The light filtered through the stained glass, casting a speckled pattern across the crimson sofa. 

Dim lamps flickered softly in the misty purple room. Around the round table sat several indistinct figures. Some lounging in the light, others half-immersed in the shadows. The lady who arranged this gathering, or at least, by her position, that's what it seemed, spoke first. She had long, silky purple hair, and her indigo eyes, veiled in a soft mist, gave her an ethereal, dreamlike vibe. Lounging lazily on the sofa, she absentmindedly toyed with the sapphire pendant on her chest, a habit she indulged whenever lost in thought.

"I've gathered everyone today to discuss one thing: where should we stay? In the 'Illusory Dream,' or in reality?"

"Since we've been wandering the edge of dreams, should we remain here, in this illusion, where everything is familiar, light and delicate as bubbles? Or should we step forward, into reality, where we might face the unknown… but also see sights we've never known?"

A lazy but resolute voice cut through her words. "How weak of you, Cantarella. You may be head of the family now, but from what I see, you're far from being capable."

A figure emerged from the shadows, a woman with long hair cascading like a waterfall. She wore the same sapphire pendant and carried an air of grace similar to Cantarella's, but with the undeniable weight of experience and authority. Her deep purple eyes glinted with an unquestionable edge.

"This meeting is pointless. Just pour the 'Velvet Dream' into the waterfall behind the castle, and let all of Ragunna fall into a dream under your control. That way, we will be queen wherever we go."

"Invalid answer. Or, if you insist, it will be counted as a vote for 'Illusory Dream.' Though it sounds a little wild and impractical, I'll still write it down for fairness. This is our discussion, after all." A young girl sitting beside them answered, opening a notebook full of strange doodles. She found a small space nearly buried under potion recipes and seriously drew a neat line.

"I abstain," she said casually. "This discussion probably won't change anything. You already have your answer, don't you? For me, it doesn't matter where we stay." She closed the notebook with a soft snap and shook out her white shawl. The light caught her blue, hazy eyes.

"Why can't we just keep it simple and follow our hearts? Cantarella, you like watching the birds outside the window and long for a life of freedom, right? Then just do what feels right," said the youngest one, sprawled on the sofa, her hands lazily chasing the dust motes dancing in the light.

"This is an important decision and should be discussed seriously," Cantarella replied, her voice tinged with a hint of helplessness. "Let's start with you then. Please explain your choice and the reasoning behind it."

The deep purple, venomous crown, when first placed upon the brow, brings a sharp sting. Yet, the blood that seeps from the forehead nourishes it, making it shine ever brighter. Soaked in the blood and tears of countless souls, this crown of toxic thorns rises from the depths of the sea,  symbolizing those who work silently against the chaos to support the weight of the Celestial Steed's tail feathers.

Such is the glory of the Fisalia family, and its inescapable fate.

But what of each member of the family? In the dark, deep sea, they suffer the gnawing whispers, until the faintest glimmer of true faith in their hearts fades, lost to the abyss. The next in line to wear the crown will take up the duty, and so the cycle endures, unbroken, with no beginning or end.

Fragrant yet toxic blooms,
Colorless, flavorless tears of poisons,
Twisted organs and venomous breaths,
Neurotoxins,
Biotoxins,
Metallic toxins…

The poisons and toxins the Fisalias so pride themselves on and the abilities birthed from them will inevitably be undone by the whispers… In the end, they only come in handy when used to seek the end of life, either for the Fisalias themselves or their kin.

This had long been the norm until I developed the "Illusory Dream." When the thorned crown burrowed into my flesh, the blood flew in strange, shimmering hues. Black tea steeped in mercury tasted like rich, honeyed nectar, while scones soaked in Jellyrose juice had a delicate sweetness. The heat in my throat was searing, as if hastily swallowing an entire cherry, and the suffocating sensation was like drifting in an endless sea… Slowly, the pain faded, and both body and mind became light as air. The bottles of poisons shattered on the floor, and our expressions turned relieved. The whispers were powerless in the world woven by the sea of dreams, for it gently dissolved all discord. Amidst the colorful waves, the once harsh thorned crown was softened… So soft that it formed delicate folds, resting lightly on my head. It became light and pure, like the tail feathers of the Celestial Steed.

That's why I cast my vote for "Illusory Dream." After all, what harm is there in this illusion? Have we not all wandered here for so long? Pour the "Velvet Dream" into the waterfall behind the castle, and let the whole of Ragunna fall into a dream shaped by my hand… Rest assured, this is but a joke. I do not seek to control but only wish for all to live more peacefully.

You see, the "Illusory Dream" flows within our veins, and whether we like it or not, it's a permanent and inseparable part of us.

In the dimly lit room, heavy with a peculiar scent, a faint yellow light illuminated an old notebook and a strange cauldron. The young woman, wrapped in a white shawl, scribbled notes in the book while casually tossing ingredients into the cauldron. The smoke rising from it darkened her clothes, leaving patches of black and purple. Her once-clean apron was now speckled, but she wiped her face carelessly, unfazed by the mess.

Distilled water, peppermint, castor bean, barnacle fish leaves, rosemary… The scent was fresh, the toxicity mild, with soothing and analgesic effects. It could treat the common Infantile Gray Matter syndrome seen recently… I'll write this recipe on a small note and leave it for Chloe later.

Hilo grass, sea okra, barnacle fish leaves, sea apple juice… The scent was unpleasant, and the toxicity potent, though it could counteract some nerve paralysis reactions. Hmm, but the side effects… Never mind, I'll keep it.

Sea okra mucilage, barnacle fish leaves dried and crushed, a splash of sea apple juice, a touch of Jellyrose juice… The toxicity of Jellyrose is too strong. Effective, but too risky.

Crush the barnacle fish leaves, drizzle with Violacas juice, mix with sea okra mucilage, add a bit of sea apple juice, and let it ferment in a glass vial… Done. Once consumed, it soothes the spirit and neutralizes most poison reactions. I should distribute some to everyone to get through the trials in the coming days. And the name… okay, I'll call it Velvet Dream.

The ingredients, processing method, sequence of preparation, and environmental temperature… Handle each step at the right moment, and I can brew the perfect elixir. I believe the same applies to life. In the right moment, with the right steps, most problems can be solved. No matter how illogical the rules or how brutal the situation is, there is always a way to find the right approach.

Therefore, I stepped into the darkness with the lamp, facing my fears. The abyss mocked me—reclusive, weak, incapable of adapting. Its taunting howls echoed through the corridors, the twisted frequencies of past family heads surging forward, engulfing me. Serious, rigid, pale, gloomy, silent… They knew me too well, able to predict my every move and trap me effortlessly.

But still, I played my very first and last trick as I drank a large dose of Velvet Dream in advance. The moment the jellyfish's poisonous thorns pierced my skin, I pressed the Jellyrose Medusa to my head. The violent toxins clashed within my veins, nearly tearing me apart. My soul rolled between life and death, on the verge of spilling out through my burning throat. I couldn't tell if it was blood, tears, or sweat mixed with the remnants of the potion… It dripped onto the almost extinguished lamp.

A small jellyfish wobbled out from the faint light. When I raised my eyes, the darkness lifted, and my blurred vision filled with colorful, vivid illusions.

It worked.

So, like I said, any situation can be solved with the right steps at the right time, even if you're just one part of the process. Since then, I've remained in a perpetual state between life and death, between dreams and reality. I often catch glimpses of lingering illusions, like the girl in the red hat. Who is she? Is it me? Or someone else? I can't figure it out.

Anyway, I'll abstain from voting. It doesn't matter whether it's in the dream or reality. I've been used to it, and I can survive anywhere.

Since I could remember, I had always been in that big, empty house. I would walk from one end to the other, knowing every tile on the floor and every potion bottle on the shelves. The house was gray, dark, and quiet. The only time it ever felt alive was when a bird flew past the window. I would watch its white wings flutter up and down until it became nothing more than a tiny dot in the sky. Beyond that, the sky turned a clear blue, and the trees shone a bright green. It was such a beautiful sight. That was when I would wonder… what was happening in that thick forest? Maybe a princess was having an adventure. I imagined a clever princess who knew how to spot a poisoned apple. When a snake chased her, a little bird would swoop in to save her, carrying her high into the sky. There, she would find a girl in red shoes who couldn't stop dancing and save her. Then, they would dive into the sea to rescue a siren who was on the verge of turning into foam. In the end, the bird would carry them all, flying as far as it could until it could fly no more, finally landing in a castle… But what was the castle like? I only hoped it wasn't like the manor I lived in—big and boring. Sorry, that probably sounds all over the place, doesn't it? Well… Mother and Father always said that girls from the Fisalia family didn't need to read silly fairytales or have strange ideas like that. We were supposed to read books—books like The Complete Guide to Poison Recipes, The Fisalia Family's Secret Elixirs, and 108 Poisons You Never Knew About. They were interesting, but after reading them too many times, they became dull. Still, Mother and Father insisted that I memorize everything so that one day, I could save myself, or perhaps even become a Maiden or the family's leader. It sounded like a huge responsibility. I didn't really understand it yet, but I did what they told me. They were always busy, always rushing around. Whenever they left, they locked the door extra tight and checked it over and over again. I never understood why they grew busier and thinner. And why did they drink so much "water" and mumble strange words? I had learned to say those words too: "It's the glory and fate of the Fisalias." Eventually, I grew older and had to move to a different house. When I left, Mother and Father looked proud, but their eyes were full of tears. "Indeed, milord, our child has great talent, especially in brewing poisons." "Yes, becoming a candidate for the trials is the glory and fate of the Fisalias." That was the first time I ever left home. As I stepped outside, my footsteps startled the crows perched on the dead tree near the gate. They flapped their black wings and took off, flying toward a strange castle in the distance. Oh, sorry, I went off track again. What I meant to say was... after spending so long flying through dreams, you start to miss the feeling of your feet on the ground. Sure, you might step into mud or get pricked by sharp stones, but there was something comforting about taking each step on solid earth. So, when it came time to vote, I chose reality—The Other Side of the Dream, as the adults liked to call it. They always used fancy terms like that. But deep down, you already knew what your heart truly wanted, didn't you? Not just in dreams, but in reality, too. You could open the door, step outside, and go with everyone. Just fly alongside the white birds and chase after the happily-ever-after ending for everyone.

In the misty purple room, voices blended together—the majestic and enchanting, the cold and resolute, and the genuine and innocent. They intertwined, forming a dreamlike symphony. The sapphire light shimmered with quiet authority, the pages of a book rustled softly, and the scent of freshly baked pastries mingled with the warmth of the room, creating a sweet, ethereal atmosphere.

Cantarella lifted the delicate teapot and poured the tea, a change from the usual. No longer the alluring purple hues, but a cup of tea with a refreshing clarity.

"Thank you for your invaluable opinions," she said, setting the teapot down. The fresh aroma filled the room. "Now, I've made up my mind."

"I will continue to wear the crown of thorns, for the poison has already sunk deep into my bones, and the dream is a part of me I cannot remove."

"I will keep brewing potions, for they are needed not just by the Fisalias, but by all in struggle."

"I will step outside and follow the flight of birds, into the mountains and the streets. The whispers that once trapped us are gone, and now we are free."

"I am still within the dream, but I will strive to feel the ground beneath my feet… In that fleeting moment between dream and reality, I will hold on to what is real."

Cantarella took a deep breath, slowly opening her eyes. She had just woken from a brief afternoon nap, stepping out from a hazy yet lucid dream. The sunlight at three in the afternoon filtered through the glass window, casting a quiet glow over her lonely figure in the room. The only sounds left were the gentle bubbling of the tea and her steady breathing.

She picked up her cup and took a sip. The fresh aroma soothed the restless Tacet Mark in her mouth. It no longer draws power from illusion or pain. This was the tea she had bought earlier this morning in Ragunna, just ordinary tea. The faint sweetness and subtle fragrance reminded her of a breeze in the countryside, of dew drops hanging on fresh leaves…

So, this was the taste of peace and happiness after everything had settled.

The door creaked open. She poured another cup and offered it to the guest who had just arrived. The guest had black hair and golden eyes, a presence of calm and unwavering strength that grounded the room. This quiet, tranquil afternoon was a miracle granted by no other but {PlayerName}.

The soft sunlight brushed through the room, and the refreshing fragrance lingered between them, filling the space around the two teacups. She lifted her violet-blue eyes, the mist long faded, her gaze now like a calm sea, with just the ripple of gentle feelings.

Some see in dreams the scars of a troubled past, others see bleak futures. For those confined in reality, dreams offer a sweet reprieve. Tell me, what do you see in yours, if not nothing at all? Look at you, hehe... so peacefully asleep.

Dreams born of fevered escape lay bare our darkest desires and fears. The weak drown in their own fantasies until they fade into oblivion. But I know that's not you. You sip the poison like it's sweet nectar.
I like the way you look at me. In your eyes, even the darkest depths of the sea are made transparent. With you, I am no longer "The Bane." I am simply myself.

You see those delicate blooms in the garden? I shall pluck them and distill their essence into sweet concoctions. The toxins in their petals, once crushed, will be tempered, the poison dissolving like a fading nightmare leaving only a soft fragrance that beckons sweet dreams.
I've spent too much time in the depths of the sea. At times, I wish for a breath of fresh air above the surface.
Food, stripped of extravagant "seasonings." I can scarcely recall the natural taste of most foods.
Apples soaked in poison for too long. They become sickeningly sweet. Even the glossy sugar shell cannot mask the scent of decay beneath.
I've longed to craft a potion like no other. One born of my soul, to free the dreams buried deep below, and let them soar, singing through the waking world.

Tell me, what do you suppose goes into the Fisalia family's famed elixir? A rare herb, grown in secret? Tormented souls simmering in unseen cauldrons? Hehe... Or perhaps the delicate flesh of young girls?

Perhaps you've heard of this method for crafting poison? Seal venomous creatures in a jar, and let them battle until only one remains... Nourished by the venom of the dead, it will produce the deadliest poison, the vilest of all banes.
Even in shackles, she dances elegantly—a true Montelli, yet more than that. Where will her choices lead her family? How delightful to imagine how she might present herself when next we meet.
A lively Starfish and a gentle Sea Bunny... But I must admit, I can't tell them apart.
The little girl with a giant box who plays with fireworks? A fascinating child. I wonder if bringing her into this castle would liven it up a little. Oh relax, I'm only teasing.
She accomplished the impossible, reclaiming her humanity from the cage of a Divinity's vessel. When the Carnevale petals fall upon Ragunna's streets again, the Holy Maiden will at last be herself.

Hmm, what would be a fitting analogy... perhaps an immortal jellyfish? Like these delicate, shimmering creatures roving alone in the darkness, {Male=he;Female=she} dispels shadows with {Male=his;Female=her} gentle light, inch by inch, until the end of time.

Fine black pearl powder, the essence of Albizia flowers, and the petals of starfish blooms, all sealed in a glass vial bearing your name. For all the time we've shared, it has slowly fermented, ripening to perfection. Today, the moment has finally come. Unseal this birthday elixir, and look... Do you see? A fleeting moment in your long life, a private stretch of sea that belongs to only the two of us.
(Effort sound)
Hmmm... it tastes good.
(Effort sound)

The current head of Fisalia, Cantarella, the Bane. Whether I am the Bane of the wicked or the pure is yours to decide. Shh, no need to answer. The moment you arrived, the ripples that surrounded you told me all I needed to know.
Shall we take a walk?
With you? I'd be delighted.
Let's dive in.
I can feel that warmth, just like the caress of sunlight tracing the sea.
Mmm, how exquisite... Like a storm crashing into a still sea, stirring it to life with waves that reach for the sky.
Ah... Like a fierce undertow sweeping through the abyss, causing the sea itself to tremble.
Who can plumb the sea's depths, or uncover its secrets? Yet for those who brave its dark currents, the sea offers her truest, most tender gifts—her treasures, her deepest secret.

You rose from the ocean in the sky, wove through loops of time, and now you've reached the sea's depths. Remember, no matter how venomous the seabed, there will always be a place for you here. Here, the currents move slowly, and I long to... drift with you.
Surge of deep tides.
Call from the abyss.
Try not to blink.
Shh... silence.
Feel the tide pull.
Surrender to it.
Caresses of the waves.
Riptides claim you.
Crash forth in fury...
To sunken depths.
Suffocate.
Struggle.
Smother.
Sink, into the endless deep.
Engulfed, by sea's venom.
Sleep, in the whispers of sirens.
Take a breath, I'm right here.
I'll keep you company.
How rude.
The nerve...
Hehe, that tickles...
Quite the standard, I see.
I'm no stranger to this sensation...
From water, to water...
Like sea foam on the shore...
Come on out, little critter.
Oh, this will be fun.
Who will sink into the depths with me?
What a divine breeze...
Oh? A little treasure, perhaps.
Why not savor this, hm?
We desire, and so we find.
What we want has a way of appearing when least expected.
Luck does seem to favor you.

A real-time exchange rate, plus a 0.02% variable fee, plus 10% GST, and a courier fee… What the actual... Oh! If it isn't my old friend, {PlayerName}! Unbelievable, we meet again!
Well, if it isn't good old Maji!
Why the sudden change in tone?
Haha, call it the magic of Ragunna! The allure of classical aesthetics and culture is simply too tempting to resist!
So, do you still remember the trial "Lollo Navigator"? I navigated my way to Ragunna with it, and it turned out to be incredibly useful. It even sparked a new idea! Care to hear about it?
I'm all ears.

Alright, picture this: You see something you want, but it's unavailable where you live. Or maybe you find it, but the price is inflated beyond reason. Or maybe the price is acceptable, but you don't have the luxury of time to get it yourself…
Where there's a need, there's a market! That's why I came up with a new campaign called "Lollo Errand"!
Sounds very nice.
Sounds rather profitable.
Haha, exactly! The time I've spent on it has already paid off. I've already completed several orders!

Right now, I'm handling an order for some <color=yellow>flour</color> from Ragunna. An astute client discovered the price here is half of what they pay in Jinzhou, so they've been buying flour from Ragunna for quite a while!
Really?!
Your astute friend right here knew that a long time ago.
Amazing, right! They used to get the flour from a mysterious man wearing sunglasses, but he told them his ship was lent to someone else, so no errands for now…
Aha! As expected for someone as sharp as you!
This client said they used to get the flour from a mysterious man wearing sunglasses, but he told them his ship was lent to someone else, so no errands for now…

But later, they found out about Lollo Logistics's new service and reached out to me for help. That's how this all came together! Interested in joining me this time, {PlayerName}? Buy 10 bags of flour, and you'll earn a nice errand fee in return!
I never say no to bounties.
If you pay upfront, I'll handle it.
Wonderful! The customer has already made their payment, and I'll transfer it to you right away.
Haha, of course! The customer has already made their payment, and I'll transfer it to you right away.
By the way, you might want to check out the <color=yellow>Gondola Market</color>. I hear they've got a special <color=yellow>fortified flour</color>. I'll be waiting for you here!
Understood. I'll have two plans ready for you to review today.… Yes, everything on the list will be completed by the deadline.
And... Hm, {PlayerName}? When did you get here?
I've been here for a while.
Right when you said you'd send the two plans…
Sorry... I have a deadline tomorrow and things are tight. Do you need something?
I just wanted to ask you something.
Am I bothering you?
Go ahead. I'm waiting for things to move forward anyway. Ask me whatever you need.
No, it's fine. I'm waiting for things to move forward anyway. Ask me whatever you need.
You tell Zani about what happened...
So, you met an oven Echo that wants to visit the Vault's Echo Depository, right? Got it.
Every Echo or piece of artwork needs to be appraised to see if it's valuable enough for the Vault. Is there anything particularly notable about this Echo?
It's especially large.
{PlayerName}! How's it going? Any news on Bakethoven's chance to enter the Vault?
It needs to have something special, like a unique talent…
Your words seem to be dimming Bakethoven's spirit, causing it to lower its head. All it can do is bake, which probably doesn't count as a special talent.
I see… So, what should we do now?
Let's head to the Vault tomorrow. You said you'd prefer to live a short but meaningful life, right? From where I stand, making food for others seems like a pretty meaningful thing to me.
(Bakethoven lets out some grateful noises.)
Alright then! Let's meet at the Vault tomorrow! Thanks as always, {PlayerName}!
{PlayerName}, I've got some great news! Bakethoven has decided to demonstrate its best skill—baking pizza!
That sounds great!
I know, right! It's a bit nervous, but with all its years of experience, I'm sure it'll be just fine.
Before we get started, could you get some <color=yellow>flour</color> and <color=yellow>milk</color>? Can't bake pizza without the right ingredients, after all.
Leave it to me.
I always trust you to get things done! Once you've got the <color=yellow>flour</color> and <color=yellow>milk</color>, let's meet up in front of the bank.
No problem!
{PlayerName}, you're here! We're all set.
Nice.
Zani's here too?
Hope you don't mind if I watch too. I just finished up with work when you arrived, and I'm genuinely curious to see how this Echo performs.
I just finished up with work when you arrived. I'm genuinely curious to see how this Echo performs.
Haha, of course, you're more than welcome to watch Bakethoven in action!
The appraiser is here as well. Shall we get started?
Greetings, my dear friend! How wonderful to see you again.
Likewise, my friend.
You do sound like a real Ragunnesi now.

Haha, you flatter me. Unfortunately, today is my last day in Ragunna. But as people say: "There's always more to the journey!" There will be a next time. Life is long, and there's always something to look forward to.
Well, about Bakethoven, while it is a pity that the Averardo Vault declined its application...
...It still wanted me to thank you and Zani! The Vault staff seemed to really enjoy its pizza, saying it was a hundred times better than the canteen food. Bakethoven felt that it had found its value.
That's great news.
So tired… but I haven't found it. No, can't give up, can't go home...
Hey there, are you Dora?
W-who are you!
Don't worry, I won't hurt you. I was asked by an Echo to find you.
An Echo? C-could it be…?
Dora's eyes widen. Before she can say anything else, a small Tubpup runs over with a loud bark!
…Dumdum! Where have you been? I've been looking for you everywhere… Where did you go…
The Tubpup, Dumdum, clumsily licks the tears from the little girl's face, whimpering anxiously.
So it was trying to find its way back to its owner… and so secretly followed me the whole way?
Thank you, thank you so much! Sorry I was unfriendly earlier, {Male=sir;Female=miss}. Thank you for helping me find Dumdum… Dumdum, you should thank this {Male=gentleman;Female=lady}…
Woof!
You're welcome, just be sure to take good care of your pup from now on.
Thank you, Dumdum.
I'll take Dumdum home now. Mother has been so worried… I hope you have a wonderful day, {Male=sir;Female=miss}!
Be careful.
Welcome back, my dear friend!
Mission completed.
I've already heard the news! You reunited the Tubpup with its owner! A feat worthy of praise. Feels like we've done something good again.
Well, it's almost time for me to head back. Before I leave Ragunna, I want to know what you think of our Lollo Errand campaign.
It's fun.
It's profitable.

Ha, at one point it didn't even feel like an errand service anymore. But since everything worked out, all is well! This trip has really given me an appreciation for this Land of Echoes. Quite the fascinating place, wouldn't you say?
It is, indeed.
Your efforts never go unnoticed. It's always a pleasure working with you. I look forward to whatever adventure awaits us next!
You're back already? That was fast!
So you really can get 10 bags of flour for just 5,000 Shell Credits! The client wasn't exaggerating after all!
Ragunna might just win best city of the year.
Everyone should start selling goods like they do at the Gondola Market.
Well… I wouldn't go that far, but it's definitely the perfect place for my errand business...
Anyway, thank you for your help today! Keep the rewards, and I'll see you tomorrow!
Here you are, {PlayerName}!
Here I am.
Well, well, I didn't expect the esteemed Laureate to deliver my order in person.
{PlayerName}! Oh dear, you won't believe this!
What's wrong?
The freight insurance of the item we're delivering today is worth a billion! I can't even imagine how much the actual item must cost... probably a number I could never earn in my lifetime!
What could it possibly be...
No idea. Based on the tiny package, it could be a precious gem? We need to be extremely careful with this one...
Got it. I'll take care of it.
I wonder if my payment's going to be in the 10-digit range too.
Safe delivery!
Well, that's a bit beyond my reach... But maybe one day, when I strike it rich!
Oh, my package has finally arrived!
Here you go, the invaluable, precious package.
Yes, Mr. Super Duper Rich.
Let me check. Hmm, looks perfect, no damage at all...
Mr. Super Duper Rich eagerly opens his packages and pulls out a smooth, delicate egg.
Very well! This will be my dinner tonight!
Worth a great fortune, I guess.
Nice try, but not quite.
Anyway, we need to be extra careful when delivering them, {PlayerName}!
Leave it to me.
Such "jewelry" and "perfume" should be handled carefully...
Thank you for your... Oh, it's you, {Male=sir;Female=miss}. I remember seeing you with Lady Carlotta before.
Please take your package.
Excuse me, but you are...?
Thank you for the prompt delivery. It's exactly what Lady Carlotta needed.
Hehe, I'm just a butler from the Montelli family. Thank you for the prompt delivery. It's exactly what Lady Carlotta needed.
Oh, what should I do... Oh, {PlayerName}! Thank goodness you're here!
What's going on this time?
Why is there an Echo here?
I'm not sure. It was already here when I arrived, with this note...
Seems like this is the situation now... Any ideas?
...Maybe we should help it.
...That might be a little tricky.
Maybe... but are there any rules for this Averardo Vault when it comes to accepting Echoes? They can't just take in any Echoes off the street, right?
True... Are there any rules for this Averardo Vault when it comes to accepting Echoes? They can't just take in any Echoes off the street, right?

[About]
The Black Shores has developed a special training program that can simulate dangerous trials in Solaris by using Tethys system data. The program is a good measure of the challenger's combat capabilities under adverse conditions.
 
[Eligibility]
Reach Union Level 30.
 
[Crisis Trials]
As a member of the Black Shores, take on trials under a selection of Stress Modules.
Select a Stress Level for each trial. The Stress Level must meet the requirements to complete the trial.
Each trial has a default Stress Module. Support Modules are available to lower the trial's difficulty.
After completing a Crisis Trial, the corresponding Disaster Trial along with its Stress Module and Support Module will be unlocked.
 
[Disaster Trials]
To gather additional combat data and improve the Black Shores's crisis response plans, this training program also includes a Hard Mode.
As a member of the Black Shores, you will face <color=#c89a45>hard challenges</color> with various Stress Module combinations.
Disaster Trials have no required Stress Level. Data samples are gathered from participants pushing their limits.
Participating in a Disaster Trial will consume Support Modules, so select them carefully in advance.
Certain high-difficulty Stress Modules can only be unlocked after clearing a Disaster Trial.
<color=#c89a45>Warning: Equipping too many Stress Modules may make the trial excessively challenging.</color>
 
[Revival Mechanism]
If a participant is downed in a trial, they can consume Stress Levels to revive. This also gives a corresponding buff.
Please note that consuming Stress Levels will affect the completion and final result of Challenge Goals.

[Matrix Crystals]
Obtain Matrix Crystals by completing the Challenge Objectives in the Crisis and Disaster Trials. Matrix Crystals can be exchanged for rewards at the Supply Station. Completing certain Stress Level challenges in Disaster Trials will grant an <color=#c89a45>event-exclusive Title reward</color>.
<color=#c89a45>The Supply Station closes when this event ends. Please exchange your Matrix Crystals in time.</color>

The Resolve that Burns for All or Nothing

"He bent down and picked up the box, salvaged from the wreckage. Its surface, stained with blood, radiated a strange, captivating glow. This eerie luster seemed to beckon him, drawing him away from the tragic aftermath of the crew's violent fights. Without a glance back, he vanished into the depths of the island."

The traveler clung to the belief that the blood flowing through his veins was tied to a lineage from a land long forgotten by Rinascita. The visions of cold and fjords relentlessly plagued his mind. Finally, he poured all his savings into a ship, set sail, and never returned.

"Mary, by the time you read this letter, everything will have already settled. Do not mourn for me. I have given my life willingly, alongside my comrades, to defend the glory of the Sentinel. We will ascend to the heavens and stand beside Them."

He continued to roll the dice, silently praying that he wouldn't be forced to face the fate head-on. Yet, deep down, he understood that by continuing to roll, he had already made his choice. He was prepared to bring it all to an end.

Twisted frequencies permeate the castle, giving birth to a Sonoro Sphere where past and future intertwine. <color=#ffd12f>Use the lamp given to you by Cantarella</color> in certain areas to travel between different dimensions.

During combat, the lamp's energy can be charged <color=#ffd12f>by performing Dodge and Counterattack</color>.
